findings.title: IssueSync terminal-verification wrapper lost the joinable guard: nil/unjoinable-identity terminal tickets are retained and re-fetched forever
findings.description: The 'safely set terminal-verification pending' wrapper exists in four copies. Three (CommentWake, RetryEngine, Reconciler) return :ok without calling the store when the identity is not a joinable %TrackerIdentity{}. The IssueSync copy calls the store for every identity. The store's public function has a guard `when is_struct(identity, TrackerIdentity)`, so a nil identity raises FunctionClauseError (rescued to :error) and an unjoinable struct takes `terminal_verification_marker_failed`, which sets health degraded and terminal_verification_pending?: true. In `record_disappearing_idle_terminals`, a disappeared idle ticket that the refresh shows terminal goes MembershipLifecycle.record (returns :ok for nil/unjoinable) -> clear_refreshed_terminal_verification -> :error -> {:error, :terminal_verification_marker_failed} -> added to failed ids -> retained in last_polled_issues and `mark_reconciled(:unavailable)`. Next poll it is 'disappearing' again, so the loop never exits. Linear issues carry no tracker_identity at all (src/lib/aiur/linear/* never sets it), so on a Linear tracker every idle ticket that reaches a terminal state is retained forever, re-fetched in 25-id batches every poll, and keeps run membership 'unavailable'. On GitHub the same path fires for any issue whose identity is unjoinable and degrades CurrentRunMembership health. Second latch in the same code: a disappeared ticket the refresh does not return at all (deleted/transferred) is also retained with no age or attempt bound.
findings.recommendation: Replace the four wrappers with one function in a membership boundary module (e.g. Aiur.CurrentRunMembership.Safe.set_terminal_pending/3) that returns :ok for non-joinable identities, and use it from IssueSync, CommentWake, RetryEngine and Reconciler. Add an attempt or age bound (and a needs-attention alert) to the 'pending terminal verification' retention so a ticket the tracker never returns is released. Add a test with a nil-identity terminal issue that asserts it is dropped from last_polled_issues after one poll.

findings.title: CommentWake drops trusted review feedback on the deactivated-entry path with only a log line; terminal retry failures are log-only
findings.description: Three writers handle a trusted comment: the idle writer and the active-entry writer both route `{:error, reason}` to schedule_comment_rework_retry/6, but the deactivated-entry writer (transition_and_revalidate_comment_reactivation/5) and its follow-up revalidation just log and return state. A single 5xx/429/held read while an agent's entry is :deactivated (the common 'finished turn, waiting in human-review' shape) drops the feedback with no retry and no alert. The module's own comment (lines 822-831) says a review submission is delivered once and 'returning ... abandoned it'. Separately, when the retry chain is exhausted or the failure is classified permanent, schedule_comment_rework_retry only logs a warning, so the same once-only review is lost silently (only the {:skip, _} path raises review_rework_refused). mark_pr_merged_issue_done has the same gap: the comment at 91-98 says a failed `done` write 'still fails closed and the alert below still fires', but the alert is only emitted when the target cannot be determined; a failed `done` or remaining-open write is Logger.warning only (the poll-cycle MergedTicketReconciler backstop may recover the done case).
findings.recommendation: Route every `{:error, _}` outcome of all three writers through one retry scheduler, and make exhaustion/permanent failure raise a resolvable ticket attention (the same review_rework_refused family) carrying the review id. Emit merge_terminal_write_failed for a failed done/remaining-open write too, or fix the comment. Consider collapsing the three writers into one decision function returning {:write_rework | :wake_only | :skip | :retry, reason} with a single executor.

findings.title: Agent queue store never evicts items, and every digest enqueue scans all of them inside the Orchestrator
findings.description: AgentQueueStore.items is only ever added to (`Map.put(store.items, id, item)`); nothing in the module or elsewhere deletes consumed/failed/superseded items, and item_id_by_message_id / item_id_by_action grow alongside. The store lives in Orchestrator State for the life of the daemon. OperatorMessages.reject_already_queued_events/2 builds a MapSet of every event id of every events_digest item ever queued, on every enqueue_event_digest_item call (CI terminal events, dependency events, comment wakes, rewake handoffs), so enqueue cost grows linearly with daemon uptime and the GenServer state (and every status snapshot that copies queue_store) grows without bound.
findings.recommendation: Add retention to AgentQueueStore (evict terminal items older than N minutes or beyond K per target, keep a bounded seen-event-id index keyed by target) and make reject_already_queued_events consult that index instead of scanning items.

findings.title: Read-model projection drops State fields its own renderers read; dashboard and `aiur status` show struct defaults
findings.description: StatusReport.snapshot_input/1 builds the projected State from a hand-kept Map.take allow-list (23 keys plus 3 overrides). SnapshotStore then runs StatusReport.snapshot_payload/1 (dashboard) and, for fleet rows, StatusReport.agent_statuses/1 (`aiur status`/`watch`) on that projection. Several fields those renderers read are not in the allow-list, so on the steady-state read path they resolve to struct defaults: (1) orphaned_agent_reap_count is always 0; (2) startup_claim_reconciliation_complete? is always false, so an idle in-progress row always reads :orphaned_claim and the post-pass :stale_claim that WaitingReason documents can never reach an operator; (3) Slots.max_concurrent_agent_status reads dispatch_capacity_sample, so capacity.load is always :unavailable and load_threshold/schedulers are nil; (4) capacity.queued_demand? runs DispatchPolicy.dispatch_candidate?, which reads claimed, model_fallback_waiting and blocked_ticket_ids, all defaulted (nil blocked_ticket_ids means 'no gate'), so demand is over-reported. Only the pre-first-publish fallback (fleet_view_from_process -> full State) shows real values, so the two sources disagree. The comment at 211-213 records an earlier instance of the same omission (dispatch_recovery).
findings.recommendation: Short term: add the missing fields to snapshot_input and add a test that builds a State with non-default values for every field the renderers read and asserts snapshot_payload(snapshot_input(state)) == snapshot_payload(state) and the same for agent_statuses. Durable fix: replace the allow-list with an explicit projection struct (e.g. FleetProjection) consumed by both renderers, so a renderer cannot read a field the projection does not carry.

findings.title: Parked rate-limit-fallback safety entry has no :started_at; teardown paths crash the Orchestrator with KeyError
findings.description: RateLimitFallback.redispatch_safety_entry/2 builds a parked running entry from Map.take([:identifier, :worker_host, :retry_attempt, :prior_work]) plus control: %{status: :completed} and pid/ref nil. It has no :started_at and no :completion_totals_recorded. retain_redispatch_safety/3 leaves that entry in state.running whenever the redispatch did not produce a Task pid. TokenAccounting.record_session_completion_totals/2 (called by both AgentTeardown.terminate_running_issue and deactivate_running_issue) uses strict dot access `running_entry.started_at`, which raises KeyError on that entry inside a GenServer callback. Paths that reach it while the entry is parked: (a) the next poll's Reconciler.maybe_reactivate_or_refresh matches `%{control: %{status: :completed}}` -> PauseResume.replace_completed_issue -> replace_admitted_completed_entry_result -> AgentTeardown.terminate_running_issue once a slot is free; (b) the ticket closes -> terminal reconcile -> terminate; (c) the ticket moves to human-review -> deactivate, whose completed_provenance? branch also records totals. A crash restarts the Orchestrator with an empty registry (the #2699/#2705 class). Every other started_at reader in this unit uses Map.get.
findings.recommendation: Use Map.get(running_entry, :started_at) in record_session_completion_totals (State.running_seconds already returns 0 for nil) and set completion_totals_recorded: true on the safety entry. Add a regression test that parks a safety entry and drives Reconciler with the ticket closed, in human-review, and active with a free slot, asserting the call returns a State.

findings.title: Rate-limit fallback: one ticket with a failing label write starves fallback and revert for every other ticket
findings.description: reconcile/2 sorts running entries by issue_id and stops after @max_transitions_per_tick (1) transitions. engage_after_preflight/3 and revert_after_preflight/2 return {state, true} - counted as a transition - when the tracker label write fails. A ticket whose label write fails every tick (permission, deleted label, 422) and sorts first therefore consumes the only transition on every tick, so no other ticket is ever engaged, reverted or resumed. The failure is reported only by Logger.error (written nowhere without --debug); no alert, no backoff, and a failed rollback leaves the marker/model labels inconsistent on the ticket.
findings.recommendation: Count only successful transitions, record a per-ticket failure backoff on the running entry, and raise a needs-attention alert (with rollback outcome) on the first failure. Test: two engage candidates, first one's add_label_fun always errors; assert the second engages on the next tick.

findings.title: Pending blocker auto-resume retries forever with no log for non-capacity refusals
findings.description: drain_pending_auto_resume/3 runs on every reconcile tick for each entry holding a pending_auto_resume hint. Any resume error is dropped without a log line and the hint is kept, on the assumption that the cap is full. For a non-capacity refusal ({:control_rejected, _}, :control_id_unavailable, {:pause_override_clear_failed, _}) the blockee stays paused indefinitely and each tick reserves a durable control id, persists a new request, rejects and persists it again, and broadcasts both. The cleared-dependency path emits an info alert (needs_attention: false) saying the resume 'is waiting for a dispatch slot' for every error reason.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish :max_concurrent_agents_reached (keep hint silently) from every other error (log once, raise a needs-attention alert naming the reason, add an attempt counter with exit). Only claim 'waiting for a dispatch slot' when that is the reason.

findings.title: An unavailable decision count is fed to WaitingReason as 0, dropping waiting_for_human and emitting false `.resolved` alerts
findings.description: open_decision_count/1 returns {0, :unavailable} when SubscriptionStore cannot answer. The row carries open_decision_count_health: :unavailable, but every classifier receives the bare 0: WaitingReason.for_running/for_idle classify the row as if no decision were open, and human_wait_alert_candidate?/1 drops it. track_waiting_for_human_episodes/3 then treats a still-waiting ticket as no longer waiting and emits `ticket.<id>.agent.attention.waiting_for_human.resolved`; the attention is re-raised only after a fresh 600 s window. findings.title: agent.max_consecutive_noop_turns is declared and documented but never cast, so operator config is silently ignored
findings.description: The field is declared in the Agent embedded_schema with default 3, but it is missing from the explicit cast/3 permitted list. Ecto drops non-permitted keys, so any operator value (0 to disable, or a larger cap) never reaches the struct: every run always uses the default 3. The configuration reference documents the key as configurable with '0 disables the bound'. The only tests pass the cap through TurnLoop opts, never through Schema.parse, so no test can catch this.
findings.recommendation: Add :max_consecutive_noop_turns to the cast list and a validate_number(greater_than_or_equal_to: 0). Add a Schema.parse test that sets the key to 0 and to 7 and asserts the parsed struct. Derive the permitted list from `__schema__(:fields) -- __schema__(:embeds)` so the two lists cannot drift (see platform-misc-02).

findings.title: Config schemas silently drop unknown, misspelled and removed keys; obsolete-key policy is inconsistent (error tuple vs raise vs silent)
findings.description: Every embedded schema uses cast/3 with a hand-written permitted list. Keys outside the list are dropped with no warning, so a typo (agent.max_turn), a removed key, or a key that was declared but not added to the list (platform-misc-01) is silently ignored. The code base relies on this on purpose for removed build_order keys. At the same time, obsolete keys are handled in three different ways: a root `codex:` section returns an error tuple, `polling.interval_ms` raises ArgumentError from inside a changeset (Schema.parse/1 is specced to return {:error, {:invalid_workflow_config, msg}}, and Config.settings/0 does not rescue), and removed build_order keys are silently accepted.
findings.recommendation: Add one unknown-key pass in Schema.parse/1 that walks the normalized attrs against each schema's `__schema__(:fields)`. Emit a structured warning (and an alert at daemon start) for unknown keys, and a hard error for a registry of known-obsolete keys with rename hints. Replace the raise in Polling.changeset with add_error so parse keeps its error-tuple contract.

findings.title: Workspace ownership guardian can latch a ticket forever (survives restarts) with no timer, alert or operator exit, while status calls the wait 'self-clearing'
findings.description: When the owner dies with provider_expected?: true and no provider tracked, or with a remote provider, maybe_release_or_reap moves the lease to :reaping and loops with no retry timer. In :reaping, track_provider, expect_provider and mark_provider_cleanup_* are all refused by their `phase in [:provisioning, :active]` guards, and a `release` request re-enters the same clause, so the release waiter is never answered. The receipt is persisted in :reaping, and Guardian.restore/3 at boot re-runs maybe_release_or_reap on it, so the latch survives daemon restarts. The only exit is deleting the receipts file by hand. Ownership.call/2 turns the unanswered `release` into `:ok` after 5 s (timeout_result(_message) -> :ok), so the caller believes the release happened. The status surface classifies the resulting wait as 'a known, self-clearing wait'.
findings.recommendation: Keep the fail-closed default, but make it observable and exit-able: (1) emit a needs_attention alert naming ticket, generation and provider state when a lease enters an indefinite retain; (2) add an operator verb (aiur workspace release <ticket> --force) that deletes the receipt after confirmation; (3) answer release waiters with {:error, :retained} instead of timing out into :ok; (4) give WaitingReason a distinct :workspace_retained reason instead of the 'self-clearing' label.

findings.title: Every workspace-lease transition runs a host-wide `sync` subprocess inside one serialized GenServer, behind a 5 s call timeout
findings.description: Ownership.Store.persist/3 rewrites the whole receipts file with fsync and then calls sync_fun, which defaults to Fs.sync_filesystem/0 = System.cmd("sync"). `sync` flushes the dirty pages of every mounted filesystem. The guardian persists on claim, activate, every provider/host-lock update and every phase change, so one dispatch runs several host-wide syncs. All of them go through one GenServer, and each caller uses the default 5 s GenServer.call timeout. On a busy host with many dirty pages (agents compiling), a sync can take seconds: callers get {:error, {:store_unavailable, timeout}}, the guardian maps this to :workspace_ownership_lost, and dispatch fails. The Store may still complete the write afterwards. The same global-sync default is used by about 12 other durable stores.
findings.recommendation: Replace Fs.sync_filesystem with a directory-entry fsync (open the parent directory and :file.sync the fd, or :prim_file-based datasync) that makes only the rename durable. Keep the file fsync. Give Ownership.Store calls an explicit timeout above the worst measured write latency and separate 'store slow' from 'ownership lost'.

findings.title: Reconstruction.with_log_lock is a cluster-wide :global spin lock with no timeout, held for whole hook runs; every alert or event write for that workspace blocks behind it
findings.description: Reconstruction.run/3 takes the lock and holds it while prepare.(stage) runs. For after_create and before_run reconstruction, prepare is the operator's clone/compile hook (hooks.timeout_ms default 600 000 ms). The lock is :global.register_name, which takes a cluster-wide global lock on every attempt, and waiters poll every 10 ms with no deadline. AgentEventLog.write/3 takes the same lock for every transcript event. Alerts.emit calls AgentEventLog.write synchronously in the calling process, so any process that emits an alert for a ticket whose workspace is being cloned blocks for up to the full hook duration. That can be the orchestrator or a runner.
findings.recommendation: Use a local lock primitive (a per-workspace Registry or :ets owner with monitor-based waiting) with an acquisition timeout. Shrink the critical section to the promotion and log-merge step, not the whole hook. Make AgentEventLog writes asynchronous (a per-workspace writer process or buffer) so alert emission never blocks the caller on disk or lock.

findings.title: Hook timeouts kill the BEAM task but not the OS process; orphaned hooks keep running into workspaces that are then removed or rebuilt, and git lock repair deletes live locks
findings.description: run_local_hook runs System.cmd(sh, ["-c", cmd]) in Task.async and, on timeout, calls Task.shutdown(task, :brutal_kill). Killing the task closes the port but sends no signal to the `sh` process group, so a timed-out clone or compile keeps running. The same holds for SSH hooks in Remote.run_bounded (the remote side keeps running). After the timeout, provisioning calls cleanup_incomplete_workspace (rm_rf) or cold fallback while the orphan still writes into the path. The next before_run then runs GitMetadata.ensure_git_metadata_writable, which unconditionally deletes index.lock, FETCH_HEAD.lock, ORIG_HEAD.lock and the branch ref lock ('remove_stale_lock'), including a lock held by the orphan's live git process.
findings.recommendation: Run hooks through a port wrapper that starts the command in its own process group (setsid, or the existing pause_containment approach) and on timeout kill the whole group (TERM, then KILL) before cleanup. For SSH, run the remote command under `timeout --kill-after` or a remote setsid and kill it through the control path. Only remove git lock files older than a threshold, or after confirming no git process has the workspace as cwd.

findings.title: HostLock stale-lock reclaim has a TOCTOU race that lets two daemons both acquire, and PID-only liveness can strand a workspace after PID reuse
findings.description: The lock exists to stop two daemons from writing one working tree (moduledoc: 'silent corruption'). Reclaim reads the holder, decides it is dead, then File.rm(path) by path and retries the O_EXCL create. Two contenders that both read the same stale holder can interleave: A rm, A create (ok), B rm (removes A's fresh lock), B create (ok). Both then hold the lock. Separately, liveness is only alive_fun.(os_pid). After a reboot or crash the recorded pid can be reused by an unrelated process, and the lock is then honoured forever. The guardian already captures process identity (birth time and session) to detect PID reuse; HostLock does not.
findings.recommendation: Reclaim by atomic rename of the stale lock to a unique tombstone (rename fails for the loser), or use flock(2) through a small port so the kernel releases the lock on process death. Record the process identity (start time from /proc or ps, as RemoteControl.process_identity does) in the lock and treat a pid whose identity differs as dead.

findings.title: Logs.Retention can rm -rf another live daemon's session directory under the shared ~/.aiur/logs
findings.description: Every daemon launch creates ~/.aiur/logs/<utc>-<pid>. The directory is shared by all daemons on the host (several repos, aiurdev and aiur). Each daemon's Retention sweep sorts all session directories by directory mtime and rm -rf's the oldest until under cap. It protects only its own current session. Another daemon that is still running is deleted if its directory is older. Directory mtime changes only when entries are added or removed, not when log files grow, so a long-running live session looks 'oldest'. Its open logs (including daemon-owned evidence such as log/event-publications.ndjson, which AGENTS.md says must survive) are unlinked while it writes. The root is hard-coded to ~/.aiur/logs and ignores AIUR_LOGS_ROOT. The moduledoc still refers to `.aiurconfig`, which is now rejected.
findings.recommendation: Have each daemon hold a liveness marker in its session directory (a pid file plus process identity, or an flock). Skip any session whose marker is live. Order candidates by the newest mtime of the files inside, not by the directory mtime. Read the root from the launcher (AIUR_LOGS_ROOT parent) instead of a literal. Fix the moduledoc.

findings.title: CurrentRunMembership.Store latches writable?: false on one transient write failure for the rest of the run; terminal verification can never clear afterwards
findings.description: Any append, checkpoint, directory-sync or journal-compaction error sets writable?: false. No code path sets it back to true while the process lives (the only true assignment is at boot in Recovery.load). A degraded marker written for checkpoint or journal corruption also keeps the store unwritable across restarts for the same run. From then on every observe/3 returns {:error, {:membership_unavailable, _}}. The orchestrator's terminal path then takes retain_terminal_retry_claim and sets terminal_verification_pending, and Runtime.reconciliation_status turns every later :fresh into :unavailable while anything is pending. One ENOSPC blip or slow sync therefore degrades membership, and the run summary built on it, for the rest of the run.
findings.recommendation: Split transient persistence faults from integrity faults. For append or sync failures, keep the in-memory projection authoritative, retry the journal append with backoff, and restore writable? after a successful checkpoint of the full projection. Keep the permanent latch only for integrity faults (corrupt checkpoint or journal). Emit an alert on entering and leaving the degraded state.

findings.title: Usage ledger idempotency set grows forever and latches the ledger into permanent capacity_exhausted
findings.description: CounterPolicy keeps one idempotency key for every envelope ever accepted (MapSet.put on every apply, nothing ever deletes). Every append serializes the full policy, including the sorted idempotency list, into the checkpoint, and Store.capacity/4 refuses the append once the encoded checkpoint exceeds max_checkpoint_bytes (1 MiB) or the set exceeds 50,000 entries. Retirement/compaction drops raw records but never touches policy.idempotency or the checkpoint, so once the cap is crossed every later append returns {:error, :capacity_exhausted} for the life of the ledger, across restarts (recovery reloads the same policy). The Emitter discards the append result, so usage accounting silently stops. Threshold estimate derived from the code, not measured: an idempotency key is base64(term_to_binary({provider, backend, transport, generation, counter_epoch(~106 B), source(~35 B), idempotency_key(~100 B)})) = roughly 395-480 bytes of JSON, so the 1 MiB checkpoint cap is reached after roughly 2,200-2,700 lifetime envelopes (plus the absolute/streams maps), far below the 50,000-entry cap. I could not locate the live ledger state directory to census it (the only .aiur-state ledger found was an empty 2026-08-15 one), so the live count is unverified.
findings.recommendation: Bound the dedup window by epoch: keep idempotency keys only for counter epochs/sessions that can still produce duplicates (e.g. per counter_epoch, dropped when the epoch is retired or older than the retired floor), or store dedup keys beside raw records so compaction retires them with the range. claim.title: Usage ledger idempotency set grows forever and latches the ledger into permanent capacity_exhausted
claim.description: CounterPolicy keeps one idempotency key for every envelope ever accepted (MapSet.put on every apply, nothing ever deletes). Every append serializes the full policy, including the sorted idempotency list, into the checkpoint, and Store.capacity/4 refuses the append once the encoded checkpoint exceeds max_checkpoint_bytes (1 MiB) or the set exceeds 50,000 entries. Retirement/compaction drops raw records but never touches policy.idempotency or the checkpoint, so once the cap is crossed every later append returns {:error, :capacity_exhausted} for the life of the ledger, across restarts (recovery reloads the same policy). The Emitter discards the append result, so usage accounting silently stops. Threshold estimate derived from the code, not measured: an idempotency key is base64(term_to_binary({provider, backend, transport, generation, counter_epoch(~106 B), source(~35 B), idempotency_key(~100 B)})) = roughly 395-480 bytes of JSON, so the 1 MiB checkpoint cap is reached after roughly 2,200-2,700 lifetime envelopes (plus the absolute/streams maps), far below the 50,000-entry cap. I could not locate the live ledger state directory to census it (the only .aiur-state ledger found was an empty 2026-08-15 one), so the live count is unverified.

findings.title: Codex tokens are counted twice: thread (absolute) and turn (delta) envelopes from one payload are both summed
findings.description: The codex provider registers both ThreadUsage and TurnUsage (coding_agent.ex:143), and the Normalizer runs every adapter for the provider on every payload. A Codex token-count payload carries both total_token_usage and last_token_usage, so it yields one absolute thread envelope and one delta turn envelope for the same tokens. The ledger turns the absolute stream into deltas, and the aggregate folds both streams into cells that differ only by relationship_revision. Both the dashboard query (GroupedScopes.totals) and UsageAggregate.Query sum tokens over all selected cells regardless of relationship_revision or counter scope, so codex token totals (and any priced estimate) are roughly doubled. Moduledocs assert the opposite ("the two overlapping streams are never summed as if independent"), but no layer implements that exclusion.
findings.recommendation: Pick one authoritative stream per provider for additive totals (e.g. mark relationship definitions with `additive_rollup: true|false`, or have the aggregate fold only the turn/delta stream and keep the thread stream as a reconciliation check). Enforce it in one place (Key.cells or a projection filter) rather than in each query layer, and add an aggregate-level test that feeds the real token-count fixture through Normalizer -> CounterPolicy -> Projection -> GroupedScopes and asserts total input == the payload's single-turn value.

findings.title: API-equivalent pricing is inert for Codex and headless Claude: price-table revisions never match adapter revisions and retained tiers are ignored
findings.description: PriceTable.lookup filters on exact relationship_revision. findings.title: Usage aggregate stops refreshing forever if the ledger store restarts (subscription lost, no poll, freshness frozen)
findings.description: The aggregate subscribes to the ledger exactly once, in bootstrap, and only a {:usage_ledger_delta, _} message triggers catch_up. The ledger keeps subscribers in its in-memory GenServer state, and Aiur.UsageLedger supervises its Store one_for_one, so a Store restart (the top-level rest_for_one tree does not see it) starts with `subscribers: %{}`. From then on the aggregate never re-scans, and because freshness is only recomputed inside catch_up, it keeps reporting the last computed status (often :fresh) while the ledger advances. There is no periodic reconciliation tick. The subscribe result is also discarded at boot (`_ = safe(...)`), so a failed first subscribe has the same effect.
findings.recommendation: Monitor the ledger process (or subscribe via a Registry/PubSub topic that survives restarts) and re-subscribe + catch_up on :DOWN; add a low-frequency reconciliation tick comparing projection.source_position with UsageLedger.generation(); compute freshness at read time from the live ledger position instead of caching it.

findings.title: UsageCompaction.Coordinator halts permanently on any transient failure and can latch the aggregate unavailable
findings.description: halt/2 sets health {:degraded, reason}; run_cycle then skips every cycle and schedule/1 stops re-arming the tick unless health == :ok, so a single retire timeout, manifest write error or ledger unavailability disables compaction until the daemon restarts. The only signal is a Logger.warning, which is written nowhere without --debug. If the halt happens after the manifest reached :source_retired, Floor.load returns {:error, :destructive_phase_in_flight}, and any aggregate rebuild in the meantime latches base_health_override {:unavailable, :compaction_floor_unavailable}, which is also only cleared at boot. Reconciliation (roll_forward) exists but runs only in init.
findings.recommendation: Keep ticking while degraded and retry reconcile_pending (roll_forward is already idempotent) with backoff; emit a durable alert/attention on halt; let the aggregate re-attempt Floor.load when the coordinator finalizes (publish a compaction-finalized event) instead of latching until restart.

findings.title: Headless usage coverage facts and ledger append errors are discarded; source drift silently stops accounting
findings.description: Adapters carefully return bounded coverage ({:coverage, %{class: :unsupported_source_revision | :ambiguous_measurement_semantics ...}}) instead of envelopes, and the Normalizer returns them in outcome.coverages, but the only production caller (agent_runner/message_handler.ex:90-93) ignores the outcome, and the Emitter publishes only envelopes. When a Codex/Claude app-server upgrades its protocol version (drifted?/1) or a payload lacks a required partition, zero envelopes are produced and nothing records, counts or alerts it. Emitter failures log at warning only.
findings.recommendation: Publish coverage facts to a bounded counter (per provider/source/class) that the dashboard and alert feed read, and raise an attention when coverage-only outcomes persist for a provider; count and surface non-:ok ledger acknowledgements the same way.

findings.title: About 44 tests start a named Orchestrator whose first poll makes a real HTTPS call to api.linear.app
findings.description: Orchestrator.start_link/1 defaults to initial_poll?: true (Lifecycle schedules a tick at 0 ms). The default TestSupport workflow fixture is tracker_kind linear with endpoint https://api.linear.app/graphql and token "token", and Linear.Client posts with Req and a 30 s connect timeout. So every test that starts a named orchestrator without initial_poll?: false and without overriding the tracker performs a live network request from inside the orchestrator GenServer. 42 of the 98 tests in orchestrator_status_test do this, plus the start_orchestrator/1 helper in orchestrator_max_agents_test. The test file already records one flake this caused. Offline hosts fail fast; slow networks block the GenServer that the test then calls with 1-5 s timeouts.
findings.recommendation: Add a shared start_orchestrator!/2 test helper that defaults to initial_poll?: false and registers on_exit cleanup. Change the default fixture to tracker_kind "memory", or to an injected request_fun, so no test can reach a real tracker by default. In the test env, make outbound Req calls fail fast, for example with a Req plug or a :linear_request_fun override that raises, so a new network dependency is caught at once.

findings.title: Tests stop, terminate and restart children of the production rest_for_one Aiur.Supervisor
findings.description: Unit tests use the running application tree as their fixture. They stop app children to test the degraded paths. read_cache_test deletes the ETS tables of the live Aiur.GitHub.ReadCache and calls GenServer.stop on it. Aiur.Supervisor is :rest_for_one, and ReadCache (aiur.ex:342) starts before Quota, BrokerTimeout, ElevenLabs.Quota, BuildOrder, Events.IdGenerator, Exchange, BranchRefStore, OpenIssueSnapshot and ResourceStore. So this one test restarts about ten unrelated app children and adds to the supervisor's restart intensity. Three unit files terminate ResourceStore with Supervisor.terminate_child(Aiur.Supervisor, ResourceStore); suite-wide the count is six (also deposit_test, webhook_poll_reconciliation_test and shared_resource_store_test). Sibling files add defensive 'restart it if a sibling left it down' blocks in setup (resource_events_test:20-22, mutation_write_through_test:52-54). This is the known #589/#2397/#2740 cascade family.
findings.recommendation: Let ResourceStore and ReadCache take name/table options, as Quota (`name: nil`) and CacheHistory already do. Then each degraded-path test can start a private instance with start_supervised!. Remove every terminate_child/GenServer.stop against Aiur.Supervisor children from unit tests. Add a lint check that fails when a test file other than test_support_test matches `Supervisor.(terminate|restart)_child(Aiur.Supervisor`.

findings.title: Tests rewrite the live application Orchestrator/DecisionStore/registries and leave the singleton Orchestrator with a dead tick
findings.description: Three test modules take the application-supervised singleton `Aiur.Orchestrator` (and `Aiur.DecisionStore`) with `Process.whereis/1` and rewrite 12-16 internal State fields with `:sys.replace_state`. Their setup cancels the singleton's pending tick timer, and on_exit restores the *original* state snapshot, which still carries the cancelled `tick_timer_ref` and old `tick_token`. After restore no `{:tick, token}` is in flight; `Lifecycle.wake_tick/1` only moves an already-scheduled tick (returns state unchanged when `next_poll_due_at_ms <= target`), so the singleton stops polling until something calls `request_refresh`. This is a latch in the shared suite state, order-dependent for every later module that relies on the app Orchestrator. Other shared singletons are mutated the same way: dispatcher_test creates blocking Decisions on the global DecisionStore via `ToolExecutor` emit_event and never answers them (4 per run, lines 2810-2817 and 3049-3055); slot_policy_test `setup` kills every process in the app-global SlotRegistry and two tests `:sys.suspend` the registry partitions; token_registry_test writes/deletes (`delete_stale(1, 2)`) in the live TokenRegistry with inline (not on_exit) cleanup; session_writer_registry_test calls `delete_all()` on the live registry.
findings.recommendation: Never rewrite application singletons from tests. Give each such case its own named Orchestrator/DecisionStore (the pattern correlated_replay_wake_test.exs:94 and global_pause_test already use: `Orchestrator.start_link(name: name, initial_poll?: false)`, `DecisionStore` with `name: nil, state_dir: ...`). If a singleton must be touched, restore by calling `Lifecycle.schedule_tick/2` (or `request_refresh`) in on_exit instead of reinstating a stale timer ref. Answer or delete every Decision a test files; inject a registry name into SlotPolicy/TokenRegistry/SessionWriterRegistry so tests use a private registry.

findings.title: Fabricated OS pid 424242 is registered with the real workspace guardian and can be SIGKILLed on the test host
findings.description: The 'workspace containment' test claims a real Ownership lease (default guardian options) and tracks sessions whose provider pid is the literal 424242 (root_pid via os_pid / claude_app_server_pid / codex_app_server_pid). session_provider/2 turns that into %{root_pid: 424242, descendant_pids: RemoteControl.process_tree(424242)}; the guardian captures the process identity with the real RemoteControl.process_identity/1 and on Ownership.release/1 goes maybe_release_or_reap -> maybe_reap_descendants -> live_provider_processes, which treats an identity-matching live pid as :live and start_reap(:processes, ...) with the real RemoteControl.reap_process/2 (pidfd kill). If any process on the developer/CI host holds pid 424242 (well inside Linux pid_max 4194304) during the test, it and its children are killed. The identity check does not help: identity is captured from the same real process moments earlier. This is exactly the 'fabricated OS pids that reach real kill' family.
findings.recommendation: Pass guardian options through Ownership.claim/3 (it already accepts opts) with stub process_identity_fun/process_alive_fun/process_reap_fun that record calls, or use a pid obtained from a real spawned `sleep` port (as engine_control_test.spawn_sleeper does) that the test owns. Add a suite-level guard in test/support that refuses integer pids > 0 not owned by the test when the default reapers are in use.

findings.title: Answerable-status sets diverged: UI offers "Change choice" on a selected dismissed Command, the command adapter rejects it with a false "not loaded" error
findings.description: DecisionAction renders the answer form for `status in [:open, :deferred, :dismissed]` and labels the submit "Change choice" for dismissed Commands; DecisionDetail always renders DecisionAction for the selected Command. DecisionCommands.selected_open_decision/2 accepts the *selected* decision only when `status in [:open, :deferred]`, and its second clause (which does allow :dismissed) is guarded by `decision_id != selected_id`. So submitting "Change choice" on a dismissed Command's detail page (or its expanded History row) always returns "This Command is not loaded on this page; return to the Commands list.", and `change/3` silently drops every phx-change for it, so selecting "Custom response" never reveals the textarea. The same action works from the inbox card (non-selected). No test covers answering a selected dismissed Command (dashboard_live_test.exs only covers the non-selected case at 2088-2130). Same file: `acknowledgeable?` is always false (see web-occ-29).
findings.recommendation: Define the answerable/dismissible/deferrable status sets once (e.g. `Aiur.Decision.answerable_statuses/0` or a DecisionPolicy module) and use it in DecisionAction, DecisionCard, DecisionInbox.open?/1 and both selected_open_decision clauses. Add a LiveView test that answers a dismissed Command from /commands/:id and asserts the store records the answer.

findings.title: Decision writes collapse a GenServer timeout into "storage unavailable" and discard the idempotency key, defeating retry dedup; RevisionCommands does the opposite
findings.description: DecisionStore.answer/dismiss/defer/revise are GenServer.calls with @request_timeout. Every `safe_*` wrapper catches any `:exit` (including a call timeout, where the store may still commit the write) and returns `{:error, :store_unavailable}`, rendered as "Command storage is currently unavailable." That names a specific cause for an unknown outcome (the AGENTS.md collapsed-cause rule; AgentLogModal already has an explicit `{:outcome_unknown, _}` message for the same situation in operator messages). Worse, DecisionCommands.put_error/3 deletes `:idempotency_key` on every error, so the operator's retry after a timeout carries a fresh key: if the first write landed, the retry hits `{:conflict, {:already_decided, _}}` / stale_version and is told "Another durable answer already won" about their own answer. RevisionCommands.put_revision_error keeps `:revision_idempotency_key` across errors, so the two adapters already disagree about the same mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish `{:exit, {:timeout, _}}` as `{:error, :outcome_unknown}` with copy that says the answer may have been recorded and to retry (same key) or refresh. Keep the idempotency key until a definitive success or a definitive non-retryable rejection; clear it only on success or on a validation error that changes the payload. Share one wrapper (`DecisionWrite.call/2`) between DecisionCommands and RevisionCommands so the two cannot drift again.

findings.title: 46 rescue/catch fallbacks and zero logging in the unit; several swallow real faults, drop records, or relabel them as a different cause
findings.description: `grep Logger` over the 82 files returns nothing; `grep -cE '^\s*(rescue|catch)'` returns 46 sites in 15 files. Most return a neutral 'unavailable' view, which is reasonable for a renderer, but with no log, metric, or alert the cause is lost (and without --debug the daemon writes no Logger output anyway). The harmful cases: (1) DecisionPresenter.present/1 rescues any error and returns `[]`, so a Decision that fails to present disappears from the Commands inbox while AwaitingCommands' counts (read directly from DecisionQuery) still include it; a blocking Command can be invisible in the list. (2) DecisionProvider.detail maps that same presenter failure to `{:error, :store_unavailable}`, naming the wrong cause. (3) Analytics.Presenter.load wraps the whole load in `rescue _error -> {:unavailable, :error}`, and BuildOrderAnalytics renders any such bug as "The durable telemetry stream could not be read." (4) DecisionCommands discards the result of `resolve_legacy_attention/1` (which returns `{:error, :attention_registry_unavailable}` on exit) after a successful dismiss/defer, so a stale legacy attention stays up with no signal.
findings.recommendation: Introduce one `AiurWeb.SafeRead.call(source_name, fun, fallback)` that returns the fallback *and* emits a telemetry event / rate-limited alert with the exception class, and use it at every site. For DecisionPresenter, return `{:error, decision_id, reason}` rows and render an explicit 'N Commands could not be displayed' notice instead of dropping them; DecisionProvider.detail should return `{:error, {:presentation_failed, reason}}`. Analytics.Presenter.load should rescue only around the I/O calls and report `{:unavailable, {:exception, module}}`.

findings.title: Analytics substitutes the local config cap (or a hard-coded 10) when the effective cap is unknown, and the concurrency chart draws it as the real cap
findings.description: When no capacity snapshot is available, `cap_facts/1` returns `cap: safe_cap()`, where safe_cap/0 reads `Aiur.Config.max_concurrent_agents()` (the local .aiur/config) or falls back to @default_cap 10. The comment directly above says the local config "is NOT substituted here" because it "would put a confident number under an admitted unknown". cap_label/1 correctly prints "unknown cap" and wasted_slot_hours/3 returns nil, but Charts.concurrency/1 reads `model.cap` unconditionally and draws the cap line, the "cap N" label, and the shaded wasted-capacity band from it. The KPI tile and the chart beneath it therefore disagree, which is the #1564/#2241 failure this module's docs describe. compute_kpis also copies the substituted value into `kpis.cap`.
findings.recommendation: Carry `cap: nil` when `cap_available?` is false and make every consumer handle nil: Charts.concurrency omits the cap line and wasted band and titles the chart 'cap unknown'; KPIs render the em dash. Add a test that builds the model with an unavailable capacity reading and asserts the concurrency SVG contains no "cap " label.

findings.title: Stream Deck channel bypasses the dashboard read-only (dashboard_writable) gate for every write
findings.description: observability.dashboard_writable: false is the documented authorization gate for write controls. It is enforced by the router (:require_writable), DashboardLive (handle_writable_event), the Stream Deck browser emulator (dashboard_writable? before key-press/command-press/mic-hold) and VoiceChannel/VoiceSocket at join. The physical deck's StreamdeckChannel never checks it: pause/resume, implement (queue a ticket via AgentControlCLI.todo), answer_command (a durable operator decision) and say (message to an agent) all run on a read-only dashboard. guide/stream-deck.md states 'Read-only Dashboard | Pause and Mic are disabled'; the sidecar has no read-only handling either (grep of packages/streamdeck/src for writable/read-only finds nothing) and no channel test covers read-only.
findings.recommendation: Gate every mutating handle_in (control, answer_command, say, voice_start) on one shared authorization function (e.g. AiurWeb.WriteGate.writable?/0) and reply {:error, %{reason: "read_only"}}; carry `writable` in the join snapshot so the device can disable keys; add channel tests for read-only mode.

findings.title: ControlCenterCache runs the whole dashboard loader inside its GenServer, under the daemon's top-level rest_for_one ahead of the Opencode supervisors
findings.description: fetch/4 and fetch_event/4 do GenServer.call(..., :infinity) and execute loader.() inside handle_call. The loader is PayloadLoader.load_uncached, which runs ControlCenterPresenter.state_payload, DecisionProvider.counts, UnitsPresenter.load (UnitsRow.snapshot join, not wrapped in rescue) and TicketsPresenter.load (not wrapped). (1) Every connected dashboard serializes behind one process with no timeout, so one slow provider stalls all dashboards. (2) Any exception in that presentation code crashes the cache process. The cache is a direct child of Aiur.Supervisor, which is :rest_for_one; the children after it are FinancialData.Supervisor, Aiur.HttpServer, Aiur.Opencode.TokenRegistry, ActiveTurns, PaneSupervisor, SessionSupervisor, BridgeSupervisor and the CLI children. A dashboard presenter bug therefore restarts the HTTP server and the agents' Opencode session and bridge machinery. Several dashboards crashing on the same event can exceed default restart intensity (3 in 5s) and stop the daemon. FinancialData.Cache already solves this correctly: it runs loaders in a Task.Supervisor with per-key waiters.

findings.title: Durable model-usage meter parsing duplicated verbatim in two surfaces; both raise FunctionClauseError on a window the writer can persist
findings.description: durable_observation/1, durable_percent_entry/1 and the ISO-parse helper are copied between StreamdeckProjection and RunSummaryStrip (the Stream Deck comment even says it mirrors the dashboard). Both use a single-clause anonymous function with a guard inside Enum.map. ModelAvailability.maybe_add_bucket stores normalize_window(value) for any bucket that has a window length, and normalize_window drops nil keys. A provider bucket with a window length but no used/used_percent is therefore persisted as %{"reset_at" => ...}. A limit of 0 also fails the guard. Either shape raises FunctionClauseError. The `with` in durable_observation does not rescue it, and StreamdeckProjection.provider_meters/0 wraps only the fetch, not the normalization. The branch runs only for providers still :unknown this boot, which is right after a restart. Possible blast radius: StreamdeckLive mount (refresh_grid), the StreamdeckChannel join snapshot, and the DashboardLive render through RunSummaryStrip. Each call also re-reads and JSON-decodes model-usage.json once per unobserved provider.
findings.recommendation: Move the durable reading into one domain function (e.g. Aiur.ModelAvailability.governing_percent/1 returning {:ok, %{percent, observed_at}} | :none) with a total clause set (Enum.flat_map with a catch-all). Call it from both surfaces and load the ledger once per projection.

findings.title: Rescue-everything with no logging is the default error strategy across the web unit (83 rescue/catch lines, 2 Logger calls)
findings.description: Counts of rescue/catch lines versus Logger calls per file: dashboard_live 18/0, github_cache_live 14/0, streamdeck_live 11/0, analytics_live 10/0, streamdeck_channel 7/0, streamdeck_projection 5/0, change_bridge 4/0, decision_api_controller 4/0, control_center_presenter 4/0, voice_channel 4/2. Concrete harms: (a) DecisionApiController.invoke turns any exception, including a FunctionClauseError from a malformed payload, into 503 decision_service_unavailable with no log, so a bug reads as an outage. (b) StreamdeckLive.update_logs `rescue _ -> socket` hides every StreamdeckLogs.scroll bug. (c) DashboardLive.refresh_open_tickets swallows OpenTicketSource and orchestrator refresh failures, so add-agent reports success while the panel stays stale. (d) ChangeBridge.safe_subscribe returns :error at init, but the bridge never retries or reports, so dashboards stop refreshing financial data. (e) Generation.subscribe returns :ok when the Generation server is down, so callers such as StreamdeckChannel.join (`:ok = FinancialDataAccess.subscribe_to_configuration_changes()`) believe they will be told about credential rotation. Without --debug, Logger output goes nowhere, so even the 2 Logger calls are weak.
findings.recommendation: Adopt one helper (e.g. AiurWeb.Safe.call(fun, fallback, tag)) that emits an Aiur.Alerts/telemetry event with the tag and exception class before returning the fallback. Narrow rescues to expected failures (:exit from GenServer.call, noproc). Make Generation.subscribe return {:error, :unavailable} and make ChangeBridge retry subscription with backoff. Reserve 503 for real store exits and return 500 with a logged error id for exceptions.

findings.title: Aiur.Claude.RemoteControl is a 726-line generic OS-process toolkit that the whole system depends on, under a Claude-RC name
findings.description: The moduledoc says 'stateless helpers shared by the Claude Remote Control path'. Only parse_session_url/1, ensure_workspace_trusted/2 and reap_orphaned_servers are RC-specific. The rest is generic process management: graceful_kill, graceful_kill_tree, process_tree, process_group_alive?, process_group_for_pid, graceful_kill_process_group, reap_process_group/tree/process through the pidfd helper, reap_workspace_agents, and Claude transcript-path resolution. Outside the Claude namespace it is called from Codex.AppServerPort, AppServer.Adapter, Workspace.Ownership.Guardian, PauseContainment, Orchestrator.AgentTeardown, Shutdown, ProcessReaper, Git, AgentResourceGuard and AgentRunner.SessionLifecycle. A Codex-only or core package therefore cannot be carved without dragging Aiur.Claude.* along. The module mixes five responsibilities: URL parse, ~/.claude.json trust edit, transcript discovery, signal/reap primitives, and a /proc cwd sweep.
findings.recommendation: Split into (1) Aiur.OsProcess (kill/kill_tree/process_group/pidfd reap/identity/alive) in the core package, (2) Aiur.OsProcess.WorkspaceSweep (reap_workspace_agents, used by Shutdown), (3) Aiur.Claude.Transcripts (workspace_slug, resolve_transcript_path, newest_transcript, session_transcript_path), and (4) a small Aiur.Claude.RemoteControl that keeps only parse_session_url and ensure_workspace_trusted. Keep defdelegates during migration.

findings.title: Claude telemetry publishes events and usage envelopes on two PubSub topics that have no production subscriber
findings.description: Every accepted OTLP event is broadcast on "claude_telemetry:events". For claude-repl it is also normalised through UsageAdapter/Validation into a UsageEnvelope and broadcast with coverage facts on "claude_telemetry:usage". Neither subscribe/0 nor subscribe_usage/0, nor either topic string, is referenced anywhere in src/lib outside the module. Only src/test/aiur/claude/telemetry_test.exs subscribes. health/1 has no production caller either. The only production effect of the ingest path is the {:session_resolved_model, ...} message to the orchestrator. About 380 lines (UsageAdapter + Validation + publish/broadcast code) are computed per event and discarded. This is the 'instrumentation that measures zero' shape AGENTS.md warns about: readers will assume Claude usage is accounted.
findings.recommendation: Either wire a consumer (the usage ledger / grouped scopes that already import Relationship) with a test proving an envelope lands, or delete the broadcast plus UsageAdapter/Validation and keep only resolved-model reporting. Expose health/1 on a status surface or remove it.

findings.title: The telemetry contract pins an exact Claude Code version, so every auto-update silently rejects all events (latched)
findings.description: Event.authenticated_resource/2 requires service.version == Contract.emitter_version() ("2.1.210") exactly. Claude Code auto-updates often, and after an update every OTLP batch is rejected as {:coverage, :unsupported_version, ...}. The only trace is a counter in state.rejections (reachable only through health/1, which nothing in production calls) plus an unconsumed coverage broadcast. The orchestrator's resolved-model reporting (report_resolved_model -> {:session_resolved_model,...}) stops without any signal, and nothing un-latches it except shipping a new aiur with a bumped pin. This is the 'fix by raising a limit' shape.
findings.recommendation: Accept a version range (a major.minor compatible set) validated by attribute shape, not by exact version string. Emit one alert or attention (not a counter) the first time a new emitter version is rejected. Surface rejection counts on the status board.

findings.title: Claude and Codex AccountGeneration duplicate the binding life-cycle wrappers and have diverged in error handling and auth_mode type
findings.description: Both modules wrap ProviderAccountGeneration.bind/confirm/replace/invalidate/retire/recover_binding with the same arguments except the provider atom and the source (:claude_app_server vs :codex_app_server). Both copy meter_ingester/meter_failure_recorder. The copies have drifted. (1) Claude stores auth_mode in the context as an atom (:subscription | :api_key). Codex stores it as the raw string ("chatgpt", "apikey") and converts at every use through RateLimitAdapter.auth_mode/1. (2) Claude.observe checks the bind result and returns {:error, :unknown_account_generation}. Codex with_recovered_binding/2 discards the transition result and always returns :ok, so a rejected bind/confirm/invalidate is silent. (3) Claude.AccountMeters logs when the failure recorder rejects. Codex.record_rate_limit_failure/3 ignores the recorder's return value entirely.
findings.recommendation: Extract Aiur.ProviderAccountGeneration.SessionBinding parameterised by {provider, backend, source}, with one transition helper that returns and logs the result, one meter ingest/failure path, and a normalised auth_mode atom. Each backend then keeps only its notification-to-transition mapping.

findings.title: Unknown provider-meter failure causes are collapsed into specific causes (:transport, :malformed)
findings.description: AGENTS.md rule 2: 'collapse an unknown cause to a cause-neutral atom ... never to a specific cause'. Both rate adapters end failure_reason/1 with `_reason -> :transport`, so a port crash, an unknown_account_generation or any unexpected tuple is recorded as a transport failure. AccountMeters maps `_other` (for example an AccountGeneration.observe mismatch returning a different binding) and every ingester rejection to :malformed. Codex.ingest_rate_limit_update/3 does the same for both {:error, reason} and `_other`, and drops the reason. These atoms go into ProviderMeters failure records and the dashboards.
findings.recommendation: Use :unknown for the fallthrough, and add a distinct :meter_rejected (carrying the ingester's reason in a separate `reasons` field) instead of :malformed. Share one failure_reason/1 between the adapters.

findings.title: The Codex `rateLimits` payload is parsed by five independent parsers with different validation and epoch units
findings.description: Parsers: (1) RateLimitAdapter.rate_window requires usedPercent to be an integer in 0..100 and resetsAt to be epoch *seconds* (DateTime.from_unix/1). (2) RateLimits.redact accepts any number for usedPercent and any integer up to @max_epoch_millis (4.1e12, a *millisecond* bound) for reset fields. (3) ExhaustedReset.limit_resets accepts any number >= 100 and reads resetsAt as seconds. (4) EventNormalizer.rate_limits_map? detects the shape heuristically, and falls back to RateLimits.safe?. (5) ModelAvailability.normalize_window/parse_time reads the redacted feed, and parse_time treats integers as seconds, so a millisecond value that RateLimits accepted becomes nil. Each fix to the Codex payload shape has to be made five times. The unit disagreement (millis bound vs seconds consumers) has already crept in.
findings.recommendation: Parse the payload once into a typed struct (Codex.RateLimitSnapshot: windows with used_percent, reset DateTime and duration) at the notification boundary. Derive the meter update, the redacted legacy map, the exhausted resets and model availability from that struct.

claim.title: The Codex `rateLimits` payload is parsed by five independent parsers with different validation and epoch units

(2) RateLimits.redact accepts any number for usedPercent and any integer up to @max_epoch_millis (4.1e12, a *millisecond* bound) for reset fields. (3) ExhaustedReset.limit_resets accepts any number >= 100 and reads resetsAt as seconds. (4) EventNormalizer.rate_limits_map? detects the shape heuristically, and falls back to RateLimits.safe?. (5) ModelAvailability.normalize_window/parse_time reads the redacted feed, and parse_time treats integers as seconds, so a millisecond value that RateLimits accepted becomes nil. Each fix to the Codex payload shape has to be made five times. The unit disagreement (millis bound vs seconds consumers) has already crept in.
claim.evidence: rate_limits.ex:20 `@max_epoch_millis 4_102_444_800_000`, 89 `defp safe_reset_value(value) when is_integer(value) and value >= 0 and value <= @max_epoch_millis`; rate_limit_adapter.ex:258-259 `%{"usedPercent" => used_percent} ... when is_integer(used_percent) and used_percent in 0..100`; exhausted_reset.ex:79 `%{"usedPercent" => used} = window ... is_number(used)`; model_availability.ex:405 `defp parse_time(value) when is_integer(value), do: DateTime.from_unix(value)`.
claim.recommendation: Parse the payload once into a typed struct (Codex.RateLimitSnapshot: windows with used_percent, reset DateTime and duration) at the notification boundary. Derive the meter update, the redacted legacy map, the exhausted resets and model availability from that struct.
claim.refactor_hint: Codex backend package: one wire-format parser module. Consumers outside the backend take the typed struct.

findings.title: Usage-limit pause construction and reset-time parsing are implemented twice (Claude and Codex) with different policies
findings.description: Both backends build %{kind: :usage_limit_exhausted, reason, reset_hint, reset_at} pauses with their own ResetTime parser. They differ in behaviour. Codex rounds up to the end of the minute, accepts dates and yearless dates, and moves a past or just-passed reset to now + reset_min_delay_seconds (#2737). Claude's parser accepts only 'H:MMam (Zone)' with a mandatory parenthesised IANA zone, returns nil for a past ISO time, and has no min-delay floor. A Claude banner such as 'resets 11:40pm' without a zone, or a reset that just passed, yields reset_at: nil. The recovery scheduler (auto_resume.ex recovery_due_at_ms) then treats that as due now. The #2737 fix reached only one backend.
findings.recommendation: Extract Aiur.ProviderPause (pause payload builder + reset resolution policy: numeric reset > parsed text > now+min_delay). Give it provider-specific text grammars as small parser modules. Apply the min-delay floor to all providers.

findings.title: Codex usage-limit detection and reset-hint extraction regex over `inspect(payload)`
findings.description: usage_limit_exceeded?/1 and usage_limit_reset_hint/1 call inspect/1 on the whole payload and substring or regex match the result. inspect escapes quotes and newlines, changes key rendering, and truncates by default (binaries after printable_limit 4096, collections after 50 items). A 'usage limit' marker or a 'try again at' phrase deep in a large error payload can therefore be missed, and the match depends on Inspect formatting rather than on data.
findings.recommendation: Match structured fields (codexErrorInfo, error.message, params.message) or, at most, a bounded join of binary leaf values, like Claude's payload_text but without keys. Never match against inspect output.

findings.title: EventHumanizer doubles 35 lookups and 32 path-list entries with atom-key variants that map_path already covers
findings.description: EventHumanizerHelpers.map_path/2 resolves every segment through fetch_map_key/2, which tries the given key and then alternate_key/1 (string <-> existing atom). Every `map_path(payload, ["params", ...]) || map_path(payload, [:params, ...])` pair is therefore redundant. delta_paths (34 entries), reasoning_focus_paths (24) and token_usage_paths (6) are exactly doubled. Codex's humanizer has 60 lines containing `[:params` and Claude's has 7. (Codex.EventNormalizer's doubled paths are *not* redundant, because MapAccess.dig does no fallback. The two map-access helpers have different semantics, which invites this confusion.)
findings.recommendation: Delete the atom-key variants (about 100 lines). Pick one map-access helper (map_path with fallback, or MapAccess.dig without) and use it everywhere so the doubling habit dies.

findings.title: Test-only public functions in production modules, including a remote-spawn branch that production never takes
findings.description: Codex.CodingAgent.run/4 (which needs a @dialyzer nowarn), Handshake.establish/5 and send_initialize/2, AppServerPort.start_port/4 and start_port/5, and codex_command_for_test/2 have no callers in src/lib. Only app_server_port_test.exs, handshake_test.exs and coding_agent_test.exs call them. start_port/5's remote clause (86-94) duplicates open_port/5's SSH spawn but does not close the port when the callback fails, unlike open_port (100-111). Tests therefore exercise a spawn path production never uses, and the production path (start_port/6 -> open_port) gets less coverage.
findings.recommendation: Delete run/4, establish/5, send_initialize/2 and start_port/4 and /5, and point the tests at start_port/6 and establish_with_rate_limits/5. Replace codex_command_for_test with a test through start_port and a fake command, or make codex_command/2 @doc false public.

findings.title: reap_orphaned_servers sweeps `rc-<pid>-<n>.debug` files that nothing creates any more, using `pkill -f`, on every boot
findings.description: Remote Control now runs as a `--remote-control` flag on the REPL pane. No code in src/lib launches `claude remote-control --debug-file <tmp>/aiur-rc/rc-<pid>-<n>.debug` any more. The only references to 'debug-file' and 'aiur-rc' are in this module's doc and debug_dir/0. Boot still calls cleanup_stray_remote_control_servers -> reap_orphaned_servers, which lists the directory, probes owner pids with `kill -0`, and runs `pkill -f "remote-control.*<escaped path>"` for dead owners. The rescue-all wrapper would hide a failure. `pkill -f` matching on command lines is the hazard class the operator notes warn about.
findings.recommendation: Delete reap_orphaned_servers/0,1, maybe_reap_orphan, kill_orphan_server, os_process_alive? and debug_dir, and drop the call from cleanup_stray_remote_control_servers. Keep Reaper.reap_orphaned_panes, which covers the live REPL design.

findings.title: Approvals.maybe_handle_approval_request has 10-, 9- and 8-arity overloads with positional booleans and suppresses Credo's arity check
findings.description: The public API is maybe_handle_approval_request/10 (port, method, payload, payload_string, on_message, metadata, tool_executor, auto_approve_requests, context, paused?). It re-dispatches to /9, which pattern-matches on a trailing `true|false` paused flag and, when paused, re-calls itself with `false` for id-less payloads. /8 exists only to default paused?=false. The /10 head also special-cases item/tool/call before delegating, so tool calls are routed in two places (lines 37-38 and 92-104). The file disables Credo.Check.Refactor.FunctionArity, and every helper threads the same 7-8 values.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a %Request{port, method, payload, raw, on_message, metadata} and a %Policy{tool_executor, auto_approve?, paused?, context}. Route on method in a single function, and remove /8 and /9.

findings.title: Thirteen hand-rolled sleep-until-deadline polling loops across the REPL and process-kill code
findings.description: Each loop re-implements `deadline = now + budget; cond do done? -> ...; now >= deadline -> timeout; true -> Process.sleep(n); recurse`. There are 13 Process.sleep call sites and 10 `>= deadline` checks in this unit. Budgets and poll intervals are scattered module attributes (15_000, 10_000, 5_000, 20_000, 2_000, 200, 150, 100, 25, 10 ms). transcript_turn.ex and hook_turn.ex say 'Deliberately duplicated ... do not create a shared constants module'. Several loops block the calling process and poll tmux via capture-pane on each tick.
findings.recommendation: Add Aiur.Poll.until(fun, timeout: ms, interval: ms) returning {:ok, value} | :timeout, with an injectable clock for tests, and convert the loops to it. This keeps the one-way dependency the comments ask for, because it is a utility, not shared constants.

findings.title: graceful_kill_tree kills descendants one at a time with up to about 4 s each, and walks the tree with one `pgrep` per node
findings.description: graceful_kill_tree/1 snapshots descendants with a recursive `pgrep -P` (one OS spawn per process in the tree). It then calls graceful_kill/1 on each descendant in sequence, and each call waits up to @kill_grace_ms (2 s) after TERM and 2 s more after KILL. A wedged tree of N processes blocks the caller for up to about 4N seconds. Callers include AppServer.Adapter.terminate_uncontained_port, Codex AppServerPort.stop_port (in the runner), Repl.Reaper.stop_session, Orchestrator.AgentTeardown.kill_repl_session, ProcessReaper and Git. The same module already fixed this for reap_workspace_agents by moving to Task.async_stream, citing #453. graceful_kill/1 also signals raw pids with no identity check. That is the pid-reuse hazard the pidfd path (369-386) exists to avoid.
findings.recommendation: TERM all snapshotted pids at once, wait on the set with one deadline, then KILL the survivors. Read the tree from one `ps -eo pid,ppid` snapshot. Prefer process-group signalling when a verified group exists.

findings.title: DisplayTailer can latch 'unavailable': retarget happens only on the next hook, with no timer retry
findings.description: When a hook names a transcript_path that is not on disk yet (the moduledoc notes Claude's lazy flush), maybe_retarget/3 stops any tailer, logs a warning and sets tailer: nil and path: nil. When the inner tailer exits, the same happens. In both cases the moduledoc says it 'waits for the next hook to retarget'. Nothing schedules a retry. If the agent's next hook never comes (a long single tool-less turn, a Stop that was the last hook, or a hook stream interrupted by a dashboard restart), the chat pane stays empty for the rest of the turn. The only record is a Logger.warning, which is not persisted without --debug.
findings.recommendation: Keep the last known path. On :enoent or an inner EXIT, schedule a bounded exponential retry (for example 0.5 s to 10 s) that re-attempts start_tailer for that path until a new hook supersedes it.

findings.title: Three backend-side state stores live in the process dictionary, so session maps work only in the process that created them
findings.description: The account-generation binding (via Claude and Codex AccountGeneration.Context), Codex exhausted-reset epochs keyed by port, and the per-turn progress quota are all kept with Process.put/get. A session map passed to another process (a Task, a GenServer call, a future package boundary) silently sees no binding, so fetch returns :error. AccountMeters then returns {:error, :unknown_account_generation} and ExhaustedReset.latest returns nil, which falls back to text parsing. The progress quota must be reset by DynamicTool.reset_turn_quotas in the same process as the tool call (called from agent_runner/turn_loop.ex:117 and queue_drain.ex:670). Context.clear/3 writes a `:cleared` tombstone instead of deleting, so entries accumulate for the life of the runner process.
findings.recommendation: Carry this state explicitly in the session map (or turn state), returned and threaded like other session fields. If process-local storage is kept, assert the owner pid on access and fail loudly instead of returning :error or nil.

findings.title: The two REPL turn loops handle pause differently, and HookTurn's pause-confirm knob is dead
findings.description: HookTurn documents @pause_confirm_ms as 'how long to wait for the tailer to observe the turn closing before parking the agent as paused anyway'. It reads the option and stores it in the loop map, and then never uses it. interrupt_for_pause/2 returns {:paused, payload} as soon as Ctrl+C is sent, without waiting for a Stop hook. TranscriptTurn does wait (confirm_pause, returning :pause_confirmation_timeout on expiry). HookTurn's paused payload also drops session_id, while TranscriptTurn's comment says the runner's {:paused,_} branch reads payload[:session_id] and so the payload must carry the ids.
findings.recommendation: Make HookTurn confirm the pause by waiting for :stop or :stop_failure up to pause_confirm_ms, and merge acc.session_id into the pause payload. Extract the shared pause and operator-queue receive clauses (duplicated verbatim in both loops) into one helper.

findings.title: The prompt-echo check matches anywhere in the pane, so a previous turn's echo or paste chip satisfies it at once
findings.description: input_echoes?/2 joins the whole captured pane and returns true if it contains the first 24 characters of the prompt *or* the literal "[Pasted text". After one multi-line prompt, the chip stays in the visible scrollback, and repeated continuation prompts share a prefix. send/3's retype guard, which exists so a dropped paste is never submitted as a blank line, can then pass immediately and press Enter even though the new paste was dropped. findings.recommendation: Check only the input box region (the lines after the last prompt glyph), or snapshot the pane before pasting and require a *new* occurrence. Add a test whose pane already contains the chip from a previous turn.

findings.title: Several backend paths drop failures with no log or alert
findings.description: (1) register_pause_containment/3 returns nil, without logging, when the pid/pgid metadata is missing or PauseContainment.register errors. The Codex session then runs with no pause containment, and a later pause cannot be enforced at the OS level. (2) Claude.CodingAgent discards AccountMeters.handle_notification's result (`_ = ...`), so {:error, :unknown_account_generation} and {:error, :provider_meter_failure_unrecorded} disappear. findings.title: Transcript reads are unbounded: whole-file pread on backfill, and whole-file reads to test cwd during discovery
findings.description: TranscriptTailer.consume/3 preads [offset, size) in a single call with no cap, then decodes and emits every line inside one GenServer callback. DisplayTailer starts it with `from: :start`, so opening a pane mid-run reads the whole session jsonl (often tens of MB) into memory and floods on_message synchronously. RemoteControl.newest_transcript/3 checks each candidate file newest first with transcript_matches_cwd?/2. That calls File.read on the whole file and JSON-decodes every line, only to find one record whose cwd matches. It runs on every cold-start poll (every 100 ms for up to 15 s in TranscriptTurn.await_transcript).
findings.recommendation: Read in bounded chunks (for example 256 KiB per tick) and carry a partial-line remainder. For cwd matching, stream only the first N lines (File.stream!/1 |> Enum.take) and stop at the first record that has a cwd.

findings.title: UsageApi serves an arbitrarily old reading as fresh after repeated 429s, and the reading carries no age
findings.description: On {:error, :rate_limited}, put_cache/3 re-stores the previous good reading with a new fresh_until of now+5 min. Each further 429 extends it again, so a reading hours old keeps coming back from fetch/1 as {:ok, reading}. The reading type has no observed_at or age field, so no surface can show that the number is stale. AGENTS.md: 'If a surface computes an age, it renders the age'. Here the age is not even computed.
findings.recommendation: Add observed_at to the reading and keep it from the original fetch. Let callers render age or freshness. Keep the backoff separate from freshness (backoff_until vs observed_at). Consider ETS instead of :persistent_term for a value that is rewritten every few minutes.

findings.title: Provider-process metadata ({root_pid, process_group_id, descendant_pids, remote}) is built four ways, and the copies have diverged
findings.description: Each backend hand-builds the provider map that Workspace.Ownership.Guardian and containment consume. Codex's maybe_put_provider_pid and maybe_put_provider_group accept both binary and integer ids. AgentRunner.SessionLifecycle's maybe_put_provider_group accepts only integers, so a string pgid from Codex metadata is silently dropped there. Claude's provider_metadata trusts os_pid as the process group without verification. The launcher only sets process_group_id when process_group_for_pid confirmed it.

findings.title: A timed-out sensitive RPC permanently discards every later non-JSON stream line on that port
findings.description: When a sensitive request times out (for example Codex account/read, handshake.ex:148-164), its id is retained per port. From then on, any malformed line on that port that does not mention the retained id is still discarded, because the fallback is `retained_for_port?(port)`. That fallback does not remove the id. TurnLoop runs discard_late_sensitive_response? before StreamDiagnostics.record. The retained set is cleared only in cleanup_port at session end. So after one unanswered sensitive request, the provider's stderr refusal banners never reach StreamDiagnostics. The #2607 quota classification (Adapter.classify_stream_failure) then sees an empty string.
findings.recommendation: Bound the retention. Discard malformed lines only while a partial sensitive line is pending, or expire retained ids after N lines or T ms. For discarded non-sensitive lines, still record a redacted placeholder in StreamDiagnostics. Test: retain an id, feed a quota banner line, and assert StreamDiagnostics.recent_text/1 contains it.

findings.title: Dead modules and dead protocol paths: EventConsumer, PaneSupervisor, WarmthReport, stream-marker Replay, ActiveTurns subscriber displacement

findings.title: TurnState keeps an unreachable legacy 'active_turn_ids without accepted_turn_ids' state shape, dispatched by map-shape pattern matching
findings.description: TurnState chooses among three behaviors by the shape of the state map. (1) With accepted_turn_ids, it delegates to ProviderTurnLedger; Codex, via loop_state_extras -> ProviderTurnLedger.start_turn, which always sets both sets. (2) With active_turn_ids only: the legacy path. (3) With neither: an outstanding_turns counter; Claude, whose loop_state_extras returns %{}. No production code builds shape (2); only tests in app_server/*_test.exs and codex/*_test.exs do. That dead variant accounts for 5 clauses plus retire_legacy_provider_turn and put_active_turn_ids. Using the state's shape as polymorphism doubles the combinations every function must handle.
findings.recommendation: Delete the legacy active-only branches. Make the turn-tracking strategy explicit: a :tracking field (:ledger | :counter) or a behaviour implemented by the backend, instead of matching on which keys exist.

findings.title: The opencode backend reaches directly into Orchestrator, AgentChat, IssueLog and Config, including a sleep-poll inside a GenServer callback

findings.title: A SessionWriter restart re-replays up to 500 history events into the same opencode session
findings.description: Writers are :transient children started with a fixed session_id. After any crash, the DynamicSupervisor restarts the writer with the same session_id. handle_continue(:boot) then calls replay_history, which inserts a fresh root message and rewrites the last 500 IssueLog events as new rows. Nothing checks which rows already exist, so the chat pane shows the history twice.
findings.recommendation: Make replay idempotent: persist the last replayed event id or check for existing rows in the session. Or use restart: :temporary and let SessionWriterRegistry.ensure create a new session on the next attach.

findings.title: Slot does long blocking I/O inside GenServer callbacks while callers probe it with 2 s snapshots on hot paths
findings.description: Inside Slot callbacks: ServeLifecycle.boot waits up to 30 s in Server.await_ready plus the 3 s orchestrator sleep-poll. do_attach_known and do_select call SessionWriterRegistry.ensure, which is an HTTP create_session with a 30 s receive timeout, followed by SessionWriter.await_replay with a 10 s timeout. Meanwhile three hot paths call Slot.snapshot/1 (2 s timeout, returns %{status: :unavailable}): Caller.base_url on every bridge request, which silently disables segmentation when it fails; SlotSupervisor.acquire_slot_or_grow, serially over all slots; and AttachPool.do_seed, serially over all slots inside the pool GenServer.
findings.recommendation: Publish slot status and base_url into the SlotRegistry value, as pane_state already does, so readers never call the Slot process. Move serve boot and session ensure into Tasks whose replies arrive as messages (a gen_statem with :postpone for queued selects).

findings.title: OpenAI-compat conversation grows unbounded, read_file is uncapped, and the tool-round limit was fixed by raising it
findings.description: The session's messages list only ever grows (`state.messages ++ [...]`, which is also O(n) per append), and the whole history is resent on every request for the session's lifetime. Nothing compacts it or caps it by tokens. exec_command output is truncated at 100_000 bytes, but read_file returns the entire file, so a single read of a large log or build artifact enters the context permanently. @max_tool_rounds went from 32 to 256 because complex tickets hit :tool_round_limit_exceeded, which is the known 'fix by raising a limit' pattern.
findings.recommendation: Cap read_file (offset and limit arguments, plus the same 100 KB truncation or ToolResultSpill). Add context compaction or token budgeting keyed on usage.prompt_tokens. Replace the fixed round cap with a spend or elapsed budget that raises an Executor alert, not a silent error.
