findings.title: OpenAI-compat run_turn snapshots and then wholesale-overwrites the session Agent, which would lose concurrent send_operator_message writes
findings.description: run_turn reads the Agent state once with Session.get, runs the whole tool loop (minutes) on that copy, and then writes it back with `Session.update(pid, fn _ -> state end)`. send_operator_message/2 appends a user message and bumps next_request_id inside the Agent through get_and_update. Any append made during a turn is overwritten, and request ids can collide. It is latent today: the only path to this callback is Aiur.CodingAgent.send_operator_message/2, which has no callers in src/lib. OpenAI-compat receives mid-turn operator text through Checkpoint instead.
findings.recommendation: Delete send_operator_message for this backend (return {:error, :unsupported}, since the checkpoint path is the delivery mechanism), or have commit_turn merge messages appended since the snapshot. Replace the Agent with a plain struct owned by the runner process.

findings.title: RPC await restarts its full timeout on every notification; with_timeout_response/handle_response arity explosion and Rpc<->Await mutual recursion
findings.description: When Rpc.handle_response/7 receives a non-matching JSON frame (a notification) or a non-JSON line, it re-enters with_timeout_response with the original timeout_ms. So the deadline is really 'time since the last line', and a provider that keeps streaming notifications never times out an awaited response. Rpc has 3 arities each of with_timeout_response and handle_response just to default two optional arguments. Await.response calls back into Rpc.handle_response, which calls Await.response again: mutual recursion across two modules.
findings.recommendation: Compute a monotonic deadline once and pass the remaining time. Collapse the arities into one function taking an opts keyword. Move the decode and route step into Await so Rpc only delegates.

findings.title: A second pause request during a pending pause is silently dropped; the reply carries the old request id
findings.description: Clause 2 of handle_pause_request returns {:continue, state} for any new request while pause_request_id is set, with no log and no reply. When the interrupt finishes, the pause payload uses state.pause_request_id, the first request's id and generation. The newer control request (a re-issued pause with a new generation) gets no evidence for its own id. Clause 1 (same id) is fully covered by clause 2 and is redundant.
findings.recommendation: Collect the superseding request ids (or the latest control) and include all of them in the pause result, or reply {:worker_control_state, :superseded, ...} for the dropped one. At minimum, log it at warning level.

findings.title: Callbacks, meter updates, notification handlers and account-generation binds fail silently
findings.description: TurnState.safe_invoke_success_callback and safe_invoke_failure_callback turn any exception into :ok without logging. These callbacks carry operator-message delivery bookkeeping. MeterAdapter.observe rescues and catches everything into :ok, so a broken meter ingest never surfaces. Rpc.maybe_route_notification logs a crashing notification handler at debug level only. AccountGeneration.bind/1 and process_stopped/1 are `with` chains with no else, and they discard ProviderAccountGeneration.bind/retire results (`_ =`), always returning :ok. SlotPolicy.resize_for_cap rescues every exception and keeps only the new cap. The magic fallback `3` appears 6 times (slot_policy.ex:137,139,340,352,358; hidden_window.ex:143).
findings.recommendation: Log at warning with the exception and a counter, and raise an alert where the lost effect is operator-visible (delivery callbacks, account-generation binding). Replace the `3` fallbacks with one documented default in Aiur.Config.

AccountGeneration.bind/1 and process_stopped/1 are `with` chains with no else, and they discard ProviderAccountGeneration.bind/retire results (`_ =`), always returning :ok. SlotPolicy.resize_for_cap rescues every exception and keeps only the new cap. The magic fallback `3` appears 6 times (slot_policy.ex:137,139,340,352,358; hidden_window.ex:143).
claim.evidence: turn_state.ex:226-227 `rescue _error -> :ok`; meter_adapter.ex:36-39 `rescue _error -> :ok catch _kind, _reason -> :ok`; rpc.ex:122-123 `rescue _ -> Logger.debug("Notification handler failed ...")`; account_generation.ex:31-38 `_ = ProviderAccountGeneration.bind(...)` then `:ok`; slot_policy.ex:372-373 `rescue _ -> %{state | max_concurrent_agents: cap}`.
claim.recommendation: Log at warning with the exception and a counter, and raise an alert where the lost effect is operator-visible (delivery callbacks, account-generation binding). Replace the `3` fallbacks with one documented default in Aiur.Config.
claim.refactor_hint: Cross-cutting. Adopt one 'best-effort with telemetry' helper in core.

findings.title: TurnStream subscribes every live stream to the global DebugLog firehose, undoing #409 for the bridge
findings.description: SessionWriter moved to the per-identifier DebugLog.subscribe/1 (#409) because the global topic 'fanned every mark to all M×N writers'. The two consumers of the same data have diverged.

findings.title: Slot workspaces, debug pipes and the session GC are not keyed by Aiur instance; the bridge token file uses default permissions
findings.description: Aiur instances are keyed (node and socket `aiur-$USER[-KEY]`, per AGENTS.md), but slot workspaces are `~/.local/share/aiur/opencode-slot-N` for every instance. The same is true of the debug pipe log `/tmp/aiur-debug/slot-N-attach.log` and the opencode DB `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`. Two instances on one host each write opencode.json (bridge URL and token) into the same directory. Slot 1's boot-time SessionGC deletes every providerID=='aiur' session whose title is not in *this* instance's active set. Whether that reaches another instance's sessions depends on opencode's GET /session scoping, which could not be verified from this repo. opencode.json holds the bridge bearer token and is written with File.write and default umask, unlike ToolCallLedger.Storage and ToolResultSpill, which chmod to 0600.
findings.recommendation: Derive slot and debug paths from the instance key, as the node and tmux names already are. Scope SessionGC to sessions whose directory is under this instance's workspace root. Write opencode.json with mode 0600.

findings.title: Env and config parsing duplicated: AIUR_DEBUG x5, trim-or-default x5, two read paths for opencode config
findings.description: The same 8-line AIUR_DEBUG truthiness parse (`String.downcase(String.trim(v)) in ["1","true","yes"]`) exists in 5 modules, although LogFile.debug_enabled?/0 is already public. AIUR_PREWARM_DISABLED uses a different rule (`in ["1","true","yes"]` with no trim or downcase), so ` TRUE` enables one flag and not the other. findings.title: Bridge port selection probes by listen-then-close (TOCTOU), publishes the choice via Application.put_env, and duplicates parse_ip
findings.description: BridgePort.available?/2 opens a listen socket, closes it, and reports the port free; Bandit binds later. Opencode.Server's own comment rejects this pattern: 'Pre-allocating via gen_tcp.listen + close races'. The selected port is published by mutating global app env (:opencode_bridge_port_override), which Config.bridge_port reads back. The Bandit child is restart: :temporary, so a lost race leaves the bridge dead for good. parse_ip/1 is duplicated verbatim in both files. num_connections: 50 caps concurrent SSE streams, each held for a whole turn per attached slot.
findings.recommendation: Let Bandit bind port 0 (or retry on :eaddrinuse), then read the bound port from ThousandIsland.listener_info and store it in a dedicated registry or persistent_term owned by BridgeSupervisor. Use restart: :permanent. Move parse_ip into BridgePort. Make num_connections configurable, sized from max_slots × max_concurrent_agents.

findings.title: Opencode.Server re-implements process-group reaping (TERM, poll kill -0, KILL), which Claude.RemoteControl already provides with a different liveness check
findings.description: Server has its own pgid probe (`ps -o pgid=`), group and single-pid TERM-wait-KILL, and a liveness check that shells out to `kill -0` every 50 ms, which can spawn 20 processes during terminate/2. Claude.RemoteControl provides graceful_kill_tree, process_group_for_pid and process_alive? (via Aiur.ProcessIdentity.alive?, which is identity-aware). BuildGate has a third pgid reader (build_gate.ex:638). The copies differ: Server's liveness check is a bare pid, subject to pid reuse, and RemoteControl's is identity-aware.
findings.recommendation: Extract Aiur.OsProcess (group_of/1, alive?/1, terminate_group/2, terminate_tree/2) built on ProcessIdentity, and use it from Server, RemoteControl, Adapter and BuildGate.

findings.title: exec_command timeout kills the Elixir task, not the sandboxed process; each command also shells out to `git config` twice
findings.description: On the 300 s timeout, Task.shutdown(task, :brutal_kill) kills the task that is blocked in System.cmd. No signal reaches the bwrap process or its children. --die-with-parent only fires when bwrap's parent exits, and that parent is the BEAM's port machinery, which stays alive. So a timed-out build or test keeps running, and holding locks, in the workspace after the model has been told 'command timed out'. Separately, every exec_command runs `git config --global --get` twice to build the identity env, and falls back to the operator's global git identity.
findings.recommendation: Launch bwrap through a Port with :exit_status and record the os_pid. On timeout, signal the process group (use the helper from finding 33). Compute the git identity once per session.

findings.title: Two copies of the turn-execution pipeline (TurnLoop vs QueueDrain) have already diverged
findings.description: run_supported_turn (124 lines) and run_supported_queue_item_turn (128 lines) each rebuild callbacks via TurnCallbacks.build with the same Keyword.put chain, send :working, TurnStreams.open, DynamicTool.reset_turn_quotas, call coding_agent_run_turn(opts).(...) with the same callback set, close the stream, then settle {:ok|:paused|:error}. Drift already present: (1) TurnLoop confirms PauseContainment on pause, QueueDrain does not (agent-runtime-01); (2) TurnLoop records RunTelemetry Lifecycle :implement start/end, QueueDrain records nothing, so operator-message turns are invisible in lifecycle telemetry; (3) TurnLoop emits more-tokens and route-failure alerts on error, QueueDrain does not; (4) bookkeeping error policy differs (agent-runtime-02); (5) QueueDrain restores on -32_003 provider active-turn and on :response_timeout/:turn_timeout, TurnLoop does not; (6) codex recovery check expressed differently (backend == "codex" vs a "codex" function-head).
findings.recommendation: Extract one TurnExecutor.run(app_session, issue, input, ctx) -> {:ok, session} | {:paused, payload} | {:error, reason} that owns callbacks, streams, quotas, telemetry, alerts and settlement; TurnLoop and QueueDrain keep only what differs (prompt building and item-specific delivery acknowledgement). Put the settlement table (restore vs fail vs recover) in one function with a test per row.

findings.title: tmux pane-died notification channel is dead: Tmux.Protocol and PaneManager event handling are unreachable in production
findings.description: Aiur.Tmux moduledoc says control mode (tmux -CC) was abandoned and every command shells out via System.cmd. Nothing in src/lib sends {:tmux_event, _}: the Tmux GenServer keeps a subscribers MapSet (subscribe_events/1, :DOWN pruning) but never broadcasts. Tmux.Protocol (a 183-line control-mode parser) is referenced only by its own test. PaneManager's moduledoc still says it 'Consumes tmux notifications via Aiur.Tmux.subscribe_events/1 and treats %pane-died ... as authoritative pane-closed signals', and its pane_died handler plus Reconcile.handle_pane_closed are exercised only by tests that send the event by hand. In production a dead chat pane is noticed only lazily, by reconcile_visible_panes on the next open request, so identifier_to_pane stays stale and the AgentList keeps showing the pane as open (no :pane_closed broadcast) until the user opens something else.
findings.recommendation: Delete Tmux.Protocol, the subscriber set and subscribe_events, and the tmux_event handlers; replace with an explicit liveness source that actually exists (a periodic list-panes reconcile tick in PaneManager, or a tmux `set-hook -g pane-died` that calls the control endpoint). Fix the PaneManager moduledoc. Rewrite the pane-died tests against the new source.

findings.title: Generic runner code reaches into backend packages and orchestrator internals
findings.description: The backend-agnostic runner imports Codex- and Claude-specific modules and orchestrator internals directly: Aiur.Codex.SessionRecovery (recovery classification), Aiur.Codex.DynamicTool (tool execution and turn quotas), Aiur.Claude.RemoteControl.process_tree (generic process-tree walk used for every local provider), Aiur.Claude.DisplayTailer and Aiur.Claude.Telemetry; hardcodes backend names ("codex" in three recovery sites, ["claude", "claude-repl"] for telemetry launch) and a Codex JSON-RPC error code (-32_003, matched in two different shapes); CodexUpdateRelay depends on Aiur.Orchestrator.TokenAccounting.Payloads and a list of Codex notification method names; LiveConversation.Normalizer depends on Aiur.BuildOrder.TicketDetail.Sanitizer. CodingAgent already has a registry with capability fields (runtime_report, fallback_backend, rc_display_tail, remote_transport), so these are capability gaps rather than necessities.
findings.recommendation: Add registry callbacks/capabilities: recoverable_error?/2, active_turn_rejection?/2, telemetry_launch?/1, streaming_notification?/1. Move process_tree into a neutral Aiur.Process (or Os) module. Move the projection sanitizer into a shared text-safety module. After that the runner depends only on CodingAgent (behaviour + registry) and a queue/orchestrator client behaviour.

claim.title: Provider active-turn error code is recognized in two queue recovery paths
claim.description: Both paths recognize JSON-RPC code -32,003 as a provider active-turn rejection and restore durable queue work, but they receive different outer error tuples and call different restoration APIs. findings.title: Control-message receive loops duplicated with legacy 2-tuple variants that have diverged
findings.description: drain_operator_messages and wait_for_operator_message each handle {:pause_agent, id, gen} and legacy {:pause_agent, id}; wait_for_operator_message also handles {:resume_agent, id, gen}, legacy {:resume_agent, id}, and both 3- and 4-tuple {:agent_queue_updated, ...}. The same families are re-matched in agent_runner.ex wait_for_before_run_resume, app_server/turn_loop.ex, claude/repl/hook_turn.ex and transcript_turn.ex. findings.title: MessageHandler mixes per-message fan-out, live-conversation bridge and control protocol; warns on every message for non-GitHub tickets
findings.description: The moduledoc says it 'Handles one normalized backend message', but ~470 of its 671 lines are a LiveConversation projection bridge (source resolution, operator delivery buffering, degradation, activation/replacement) and ~80 are orchestrator control messages. with_live_source/5 logs a Logger.warning whenever live_source/3 fails; for any ticket whose TrackerIdentity is not a joinable GitHub identity (Linear, memory, or an unjoinable GitHub identity) that happens on every transcript event, because TrackerIdentity.joinable?/1 and github_key/1 are GitHub-only.
findings.recommendation: Split into MessageFanout (the 9-step per-message pipeline), LiveConversationBridge (everything that talks to Aiur.LiveConversation) and WorkerProtocol (agent-runtime-12). Resolve live-conversation eligibility once per session and skip (with a single log/metric) when the tracker cannot join, instead of warning per message.

findings.title: Every backend message (including streaming deltas) takes a :global lock and two file appends on the hot path
findings.description: The on_message closure calls AgentEventLog.write/3 synchronously for every normalized message. For a local workspace that wraps mkdir_p plus appends to agent.ndjson and agent.md inside Reconstruction.with_log_lock, which does :global.register_name/unregister_name per call (spin-sleeping 10ms on contention). :global name registration is serialized through global_name_server for the whole node, so all agents' per-message writes contend on one process. CodexUpdateRelay's moduledoc documents Codex streams 'hundreds of messages per second' of deltas; those deltas are coalesced for the orchestrator mailbox but not for the log. Failures are Logger.debug only, and remote workers are a silent no-op.
findings.recommendation: Replace the :global lock with a per-workspace writer process (or a local :ets/Registry lock) and buffer/coalesce stream deltas before writing (write completed items and control events eagerly). Measure messages/sec and lock wait before and after on a live run as AGENTS.md requires.

findings.title: AgentList controls mislabel failures: pause errors flash the max-agents alert, max-agent errors are silently ignored
findings.description: handle_control_result/3 is used for both pause and resume. Any error other than :globally_paused logs '[user-action] resume_failed' (even for a pause), rings the bell and sets max_agents_alert? - which renders the Agents: N/max chip in red reverse video - so a failed pause is reported as a concurrency-cap problem. Conversely adjust_max_concurrent_agents/2 - the control the max-agents alert belongs to - maps every result to the unchanged state (both handle_max_adjust_result clauses return state), so a failed cap change gives no feedback.
findings.recommendation: Give each control its own feedback channel: pause/resume failures set a per-row or footer hint naming the action and reason; cap-change failures set max_agents_alert?. Log the actual action. Add tests that assert which state field changes for each failing control.

findings.title: AgentList maintains and re-renders for state that no renderer reads (debug footer, slot warmth, visible sessions)
findings.description: RenderState.build threads perf_summary, warmth_events, started_slots, fully_warmed_slots, visible_sessions, warm_status_dark_mode?, debug_mode? and agent_kind into the renderer, but grep over agent_list/renderer* finds no reader for any of them except agent_kind, which Chrome.agents_row ignores (`_kind`). PerfIntake (the 'compact 3-row debug footer') is therefore entirely dead, WarmthIntake returns changed?=true for slot events and triggers full re-renders that draw nothing new, and ConvoPaint polls capture-pane every 100ms for up to 30s after every open only to feed that footer (its PaneManager message handler is a no-op). attach_state is also never pruned (grows by one entry per ticket ever attached).
findings.recommendation: Delete PerfIntake, the unused WarmthIntake branches and RenderState fields, the agent_kind lookup, and gate ConvoPaint behind the debug flag (or delete it). Prune attach_state in Roster.fold alongside agents_with_content. Update State's field comments that describe the removed footer and bottom-nav glyphs.

findings.title: TUI computes activity freshness and ages but never renders them; unavailable attention counts render as zero
findings.description: ActivityIntake builds activity_status_by_identifier (snapshot status plus per-field freshness for progress, stage and evidence) and stores the latest evidence timestamp; the renderer threads activity_status_by_identifier into the layout map and no cell ever reads it, and latest_event_message renders only the message (plus a 'Stale:' prefix). This violates AGENTS.md rule 1 ('If a surface computes an age, it renders the age'). Separately Roster uses SubscriptionStore.open_attention_count/1, which collapses {:error, :unavailable} to 0, although the store offers open_attention_count_result/1 precisely to avoid 'collapsing a missing or restarting store to an exact zero'; the TUI then shows no attention marker, the plausible-default pattern AGENTS.md forbids.
findings.recommendation: Render the evidence age in the LATEST cell (e.g. '3m ago') and a freshness glyph for stale/unknown progress; use open_attention_count_result/1 and render an explicit unknown marker (e.g. '?') when unavailable. Add tests that fail when the unknown branch is replaced by 0 or blank.

findings.title: Blocking GenServer calls on the AgentList render and keypress paths reintroduce the documented input freeze
findings.description: App renders synchronously on almost every message (1s tick, every PubSub event, every debug event). Each render calls RenderState.build, which performs ProviderMeterProjection.snapshot/0 (GenServer.call with a 5s timeout), Tracker.project_identity/0, HttpServer.base_url/0, Config.agent_kind/0 and :io.columns/rows. RenderState's own comment records that a 5s Orchestrator call on this path 'froze arrow-key input during poll cycles' and was replaced by a cached broadcast; the provider meter call has the same shape. Keypress handlers (Controls) make 5s synchronous Orchestrator calls from handle_cast; running_changed triggers a PaneManager.list_open_panes call plus one Tmux.set_pane_border call per change and one SubscriptionStore lookup per visible agent, all inside the TUI process.
findings.recommendation: Cache provider usage, project label, dashboard URL and agent kind in App state, refreshed by PubSub or a slow timer; coalesce renders (dirty flag + at most one render per 50-100ms); run orchestrator control calls in a Task that reports back with a message; move RcPaneBorders tmux writes to PaneManager.

findings.title: PaneManager open-success bookkeeping copied five times with drift

findings.title: Production-dead GenericOpen path puts the Erlang cookie on a tmux command line and carries most PaneManager tests
findings.description: OpencodeOpen.do_open routes any command not starting with '__aiur_opencode__ ' to GenericOpen. Every production caller builds '__aiur_opencode__ <id>' (Activation.default_command_template, Conversations.default_command) and Conversations.open has no callers, so GenericOpen is reachable only from tests. It wraps the command with ERL_AFLAGS containing '-setcookie <cookie>' read from AIUR_ERLANG_COOKIE or ~/.erlang.cookie; the cookie then appears in the tmux pane start command and process arguments, readable by other local users via /proc/<pid>/cmdline, which is sufficient to connect to the distributed aiur node on 127.0.0.1. Meanwhile pane_manager_test.exs drives titles, bookkeeping and queueing through 'echo <id>' commands, i.e. through the path production never takes, leaving the opencode path's bookkeeping (agent-runtime-19 drift) untested by those cases.
findings.recommendation: Delete GenericOpen and the non-opencode branch (or keep a test-only fake transport outside lib). Rewrite the affected pane_manager tests against the opencode path with SlotRegistry/AttachPool fakes. If a generic pane is ever needed again, pass the cookie via a 0600 file or environment inherited from the parent, never argv.

findings.title: Queue claim errors collapsed to :empty; a consumed wake leaves pending items with nothing polling
findings.description: Four wrappers map {:error, _reason} from the orchestrator claim RPCs to :empty with no log. In wait_for_operator_message the {:agent_queue_updated, ...} wake has already been received, so a transient claim error returns the runner to waiting with the item still pending and no further wake until some other queue event or resume arrives. In drain_queued_operator_messages an error ends the drain and the turn loop proceeds as if the queue were empty. The collapse also makes 'queue empty' and 'orchestrator unavailable' indistinguishable in logs.
findings.recommendation: Return {:error, reason} distinctly; on error in the paused wait, schedule a self-wake (send_after :retry_claim with backoff) and log/metric the failure; in the drain path, retry once and otherwise leave a marker so the next turn boundary re-drains.

findings.title: Decision-attention open/resolve failures are logged and dropped while the agent is told the request is pending
findings.description: When an agent emits blocked/pause.request with reason operator_decision (or attention.<slug>), enqueue_agent_event opens a decision attention and then publishes the event. If the attention open fails, log_decision_projection_failure writes a Logger.warning and publication continues; the tool call already returned {:ok, %{"status" => "pending"}}. The operator may never see the decision the agent is waiting on. On attention.resolved, a failed DecisionAttention.resolve is likewise only logged, leaving the attention open (latched) although the agent reported it resolved.
findings.recommendation: Record projection/resolve failures in the event publication record (it already has a failed status) and emit a system needs-attention alert naming the ticket and slug; retry resolution on the next safe checkpoint. Add tests with a failing attention_opener that assert an alert is emitted.

findings.title: Turn stream registration is not released if a turn raises; ActiveTurns entry stays :active
findings.description: TurnStreams.open/1 inserts {identifier, turn_id} as :active in the ActiveTurns ETS table and posts turn markers; TurnStreams.close/3 is called only after run_turn returns normally. Neither TurnLoop nor QueueDrain wraps the turn in try/after, and ActiveTurns has no owner monitor or TTL for :active entries (cleanup is scheduled only by mark_closed). If run_turn raises or the runner is killed, the entry stays :active for the life of the node and the opencode bridge waits on a broadcast that never comes (its 10-minute watchdog is the only exit).
findings.recommendation: Wrap open/run/close in try/after inside the extracted TurnExecutor (agent-runtime-03) closing with {:failed, :runner_crash}; have ActiveTurns monitor the registering pid and close entries on DOWN.

findings.title: Oversized modules and functions in agent_runner
findings.description: SessionLifecycle (1095 lines) mixes session option resolution, workspace-ownership containment, telemetry launch/revoke, backend fallback, display-tailer wiring and live-conversation source handlers, RC chat naming, RC trust seeding, unsupported-model alerts and backend labels; its private pipeline passes the same 8 arguments through start_expected_session/run_contained_session/run_session_turn_loop. ToolExecutor (908 lines) mixes alert namespacing, blocker coordination with reconciliation, ticket-state writes, event publication with durable records, and the decision request/lifecycle flow. Largest functions (approximate, including clause groups): QueueDrain.run_supported_queue_item_turn ~128 lines, TurnLoop.run_supported_turn ~124, QueueDrain.wait_for_operator_message ~110, ToolExecutor.build ~93, SessionLifecycle.run_session ~79. TurnLoop.run_turns has arity 10 and QueueDrain.run_queue_item_turn arity 7, both with credo FunctionArity disables.

Replace positional context with a %RunContext{} struct (the code already builds session_context and turn_context maps ad hoc).

findings.title: Turn alerts classify causes by substring of inspect(reason) and name a re-resolved route instead of the session's backend
findings.description: maybe_emit_more_tokens_alert decides 'token budget or context limit was exhausted' by searching the lowercase inspect/1 of the error for a fixed list that includes 'rate limit exhausted', so a rate-limit error is reported as token/context exhaustion (a collapsed, mislabelled cause). maybe_emit_route_failure_alert passes CodingAgent.backend_for(issue) - re-resolved from labels/config - rather than the backend the session actually ran on, although SessionLifecycle documents that fallback (claude-repl -> claude) and RC promotion change the real backend and that alerts 'must not invent a backend'.
findings.recommendation: Classify exhaustion from structured reasons produced by the backends (a CodingAgent.classify_failure/2 capability) and pass SessionLifecycle.session_backend_label(app_session) into the route-failure alert.

findings.title: tmux driven through interpolated command strings, a hand-rolled argv splitter and stderr substring matching
findings.description: Aiur.Tmux.command/2 takes one string that Exec.split_command re-tokenizes by splitting on whitespace and re-joining double-quoted runs with a single space (lossy for repeated spaces, no single-quote or escape support). 27 call sites across src/lib build these strings with interpolation (e.g. "swap-pane -s #{real_pane_id} -t #{placeholder_pane_id}", "capture-pane -p -t #{pane_id}"), while a structured run_args path exists. tmux failures are classified by substring of stderr in four places ('no server running' twice, "can't find pane", 'source and target panes must be different'). The placeholder pane command embeds the identifier into a bash -c string with only single quotes stripped, so $() or backticks in an identifier would execute.
findings.recommendation: Replace Tmux.command/2 with typed functions over argv (kill_pane/2, select_pane/2, swap_pane/3, capture_pane/2 already partially exist in Query/Layout) and delete split_command; centralize error classification in Tmux.Error.classify/1 returning atoms; pass the placeholder identifier as an environment variable or printf argument rather than inside the script text.

findings.title: Containment test passes a fabricated OS pid that reaches real pgrep and a real ownership lease
findings.description: 'accepts every valid session shape ...' feeds sessions with os_pid 424_242 and provider pids "424242" into SessionLifecycle.track_session_containment/3 with a real Ownership lease. For local shapes, session_provider/2 calls RemoteControl.process_tree(424242), which shells out to pgrep -P recursively on the host and records any real descendants of whatever process owns that pid into the lease that the workspace guardian reaps on owner death. This is the 'fabricated OS pids that reach real kill/kill -0' family: the test's outcome depends on host state and can register a foreign process tree for reaping.
findings.recommendation: Inject the process-tree function (opts or application env) and use a stub in tests; if a real pid is required, spawn a sleep process owned by the test and use its pid.

findings.title: Catalog metric derivation is copied three times (CatalogStore, GitHubGraph.Normalizer, PlanningSource) and has already drifted
findings.description: CatalogStore says its metric rules 'deliberately mirror' the normalizer and are 'written out rather than shared'. Copied verbatim in both files: the progress cond (resolved_count == 0 / == total / partial), metric_count/2, member_state_digest/1, validate_root_label/1, append_diagnostics/2 and @root_label "build-order". PlanningSource.progress/2 is a third copy of the progress cond. They have diverged. For a root with more than 100 members, the normalizer reports member_count = the true totalCount with progress nil and :unresolved (root_metrics requires has_next? false and length == total). CatalogStore instead runs Enum.take(member_numbers, 100), reports member_count 100, and computes a percentage and a :resolved/:partial resolution over the 100 lowest issue numbers, with no overflow diagnostic. The store path is now the steady-state catalog source (Options.catalog_reader defaults to &CatalogStore.fetch/1), so the page shows a capped member count and a biased percentage as resolved.
findings.recommendation: Extract a pure Aiur.BuildOrder.RootMetrics module that takes lifecycles and optional label sets plus a declared total, owns progress, metric_count, digest and the overflow rule, and is called by all three sources. CatalogStore must pass the true edge count and report :member_overflow / :unresolved exactly as the normalizer does.

findings.title: Pack manifest parsing is duplicated between PlanningSource, PackStatus and PackPaths, and ticket-number parsing has diverged
findings.description: Three modules each parse the same build-order.json. The 'repository' split appears three times: PlanningSource.repository/1, PackStatus.pack_repository/1 and PackPaths.foreign_repository?/1. Ticket numbers are parsed twice, and the two parsers disagree. PlanningSource.ticket_number/1 accepts `"ticket"` or `"github": {"number": n}`. PackStatus.ticket_number/1 accepts only `"ticket"`. For a pack whose tickets carry only github.number, PlanningSource marks the ticket materialized, so pack_status_facts/1 sets requires_projection? to true. PackStatus never fetches or writes that ticket's lifecycle, so status_lifecycle/2 is nil for it indefinitely. project_pack_status_health/2 then reports the pack :stale/:unavailable with failure :pack_status_incomplete on every cycle, and no refresh clears it. Lifecycle strings are parsed a third way: PlanningSource.status_lifecycle/2 accepts 'COMPLETE'/'complete'/'CANCELED' variants, while PackStatus writes only lowercase 'completed'/'cancelled'/'open'.
findings.recommendation: Create Aiur.BuildOrder.Pack (a struct plus a parser) that owns manifest decoding, repository, ticket numbers, drafts and status.json reading. Have PlanningSource, PackStatus and PackPaths consume it. Add a contract test with a github.number-only pack that asserts PackStatus fetches it and the health reaches :healthy.

findings.title: GraphProjection.Policy.failure_class/1 matches a GitHub classification the transport never emits and misses the one it does emit
findings.description: failure_class/1 maps `{:github, c, _} when c in [:auth, :forbidden]` to :permission. The GraphQL transport emits {:github, :permission, detail} for a non-rate-limited 403 (Errors.graph_status_classification/2) and for a FORBIDDEN GraphQL error (GraphQLErrors line 124). It never emits :forbidden (grep: :forbidden appears only in auth_preflight.ex). {:github, :permission, _} matches no clause except the fallback `_ -> :provider_unavailable`, so a token that cannot read the repository is reported as 'GitHub planning data is unavailable', and count_resolution_failure/1 then maps it to nil. The same GitHub error tuple has four hand-written classifiers with different taxonomies: Policy.failure_class, TicketDetail.Normalizer.failure_from (no :permission-class clause, so {:github, :permission, _} becomes :transport), PackStatus.failure/1, and GraphProjection.count_resolution_failure/1.
findings.recommendation: Give Aiur.GitHub.Errors one exhaustive classifier from GitHub error tuples to a small shared cause enum (:auth | :permission | :rate_limited | :timeout | :unreachable | :schema | :unknown), and have every Build Order consumer map from that enum. Add a property test that feeds every classification Errors can produce through each consumer and asserts that none lands on a specific wrong cause.

findings.title: The 'labelled catalog read' cadence (about 200 lines, 6 state keys) is keyed on a flag the catalog reader now ignores
findings.description: GraphProjection still decides every catalog read as labelled or cheap (catalog_labels_due?/2). It passes `member_labels:` in the reader options and runs the #1766 machinery on completion: record_catalog_labels_read/failure, labels_penalty_ms geometric backoff, carry_catalog_counts via Catalog.carry_forward_counts, put_catalog_count_resolution, count_resolution_failure and failure_reset_at, with six state keys (catalog_labels_read_ms, _ok_ms, _failure, _failure_reset_at, _failures, _penalty_ms). The production catalog reader is CatalogStore.fetch/1 (Options line 115). It reads only :repository and always makes the same zero-cost store read. The flag therefore changes nothing about the read, but it does flip semantics: on a 'labelled' tick a nil epic/phase count is shown as Unresolved (:incomplete), and on the next 'cheap' tick the same nil is filled from the previous generation. Identical inputs render differently on a 10-minute cycle. The budget and rate-limit classes cannot occur, because CatalogStore reports calls: 0. The labelled GraphQL variant now runs only inside Reconciliation, which always sets member_labels? true. GitHubGraph.fetch_catalog/1, Result.catalog/3 and Client.fetch_build_order_catalog/1 have no production callers; grep finds them only in tests.
findings.recommendation: Delete the labelled-read cadence from GraphProjection, Options and Cadence (graph_catalog_labels_refresh_ms). Keep count carry-forward only if the store genuinely lacks label sets, and key it on store completeness rather than a timer. Delete GitHubGraph.fetch_catalog, Result.catalog and Client.fetch_build_order_catalog, or move them to test support. Update the stale cost comments in Queries and Options.

findings.title: GraphProjection is a 1,825-line GenServer that owns catalog, selected roots, demand monitors, debounce, reconciliation, the labels cadence and PubSub
findings.description: The module has 161 defp and 32 def, 19 handle_* clauses, and a 45-key state map built in Options.new/1. Its responsibilities include: catalog scope, selected-root scopes with LRU eviction, demand registration with monitors, forced and pending queues, per-root member-change debounce timers, retry scheduling, the GraphQL reconciliation lifecycle, delivery-mode subscription, the labelled-read cadence (build-order-08), configuration reconciliation, and broadcast. 18 of the handle_* paths begin with `reconcile(state)`. reconcile/2 calls Configuration.snapshot/2, which re-reads the workflow store, Settings.limits, Aiur.Config.build_order_graph_projection_options and Aiur.Config.settings. On the unchanged-fingerprint path it then cancels and re-arms every timer (reschedule_active_scopes/1). Every message, including each webhook-driven :github_resource_changed, pays for that. The comment at 1293-1297 admits the pattern once produced a lost-retry bug: 'this runs on almost every message: it cancels all timers, so without restoring the retry a root whose read failed would lose its backoff timer'.
findings.recommendation: Split along the existing seams: (a) a Scope/Entry state machine as a pure struct plus functions (request_scope, start/complete, retry, eviction, demand), (b) a ReconciliationWorker GenServer (build-order-03), (c) MemberChangeDebouncer, (d) a thin GraphProjection GenServer that routes messages. Reconcile configuration only on :workflow_config_updated and at init, not on every message, and stop cancelling and re-arming all timers per message.

findings.title: AdHocSource and OpenTicketSource are near-copies of one event-sourced overlay and have diverged on paging
findings.description: OpenTicketSource (509 lines) says it is 'modelled on AiurBuildOrder.AdHocSource'. It re-implements the same functions under the same names: reconcile_issue/5, label_names/1, fetch_pages, apply_result/2, do_apply_result/2, rebuild_snapshot/1, snapshot_status/1 (identical baseline_ok? rule), meaningful/1, broadcast/1, subscribe_to_events/0, maybe_relist/2, resolve_repo/1 and safe_label_prefix/0. The two have already diverged. OpenTicketSource.fetch_pages/7 carries a `pages_left` cap and returns a truncated? flag. AdHocSource.fetch_pages/7 follows Link headers with no cap, lists `state=all` (closed issues keep accumulating forever), and runs synchronously inside the GenServer (build-order-13).
findings.recommendation: Extract a generic `Aiur.GitHub.LabelledIssueOverlay` behaviour or module: a baseline listing with a page cap, store-event reconciliation, degraded, recovered and diverged re-listing, and snapshot status. AdHocSource and OpenTicketSource then become configurations of it: a label or filter, a member projection and a topic.

findings.title: Blocking GitHub, file and store I/O inside GenServer callbacks that callers reach with the default 5 s call timeout
findings.description: AdHocSource runs the full paginated REST listing inside handle_info(:poll), handle_cast(:refresh) and the three webhook-mode handlers, deliberately, for ordering. ModeRegistry re-publishes :webhook_degraded 'on every sweep while the repo stays degraded', so every sweep during an outage blocks the server for a whole unbounded listing, and AdHocSource.snapshot/1 callers time out. TicketHistoryProvider calls history_fun, which defaults to IssueLog.event_history/2. That function File.read!s and JSON-parses every line of the issue's event log, however large, before taking the last 101. It runs inside handle_call({:request, _}), inside handle_info({:ticket_activity_changed, _}) for an unseen identity, and in init/1 once per seeded activity entry, which delays supervisor boot. PackStatus.refresh_sync/1 runs GraphQL batches in handle_call. GraphProjection.debounce_roots_containing/2 lists every :sub_issue store entry on each label or dependency event while any root is watched.
findings.recommendation: Move the listings into supervised tasks with a monotonic listing sequence. To keep the 'events win over the listing' rule, apply a listing result only if no store event for that issue arrived after the listing's start marker. Tail-read the issue log (seek from the end, bounded bytes). Seed history lazily on the first request instead of in init/1. Keep the parent-to-members index incrementally in CatalogStore instead of re-listing the store.

findings.title: One slow AdHocSource.snapshot/1 blanks execution and activity for the whole Build Order page
findings.description: DataSource.load_sources/1 builds %{activity, execution} and then calls AdHocSource.snapshot inside the same expression. SourceRuntime.schedule_reload/1 wraps the whole load_sources call in Runtime.safe_source_call(..., Runtime.unavailable_sources()). A GenServer.call exit from AdHocSource, which is likely while it runs a synchronous listing (build-order-13), therefore replaces all three sources with :unavailable. The execution overlay (StatusReport) and activity (TicketActivity) had loaded successfully. Separately, the only trace of the failure is a Logger.warning.
findings.recommendation: Guard each source independently: `%{activity: safe(TicketActivity.snapshots), execution: safe(StatusReport.snapshot_api), adhoc: safe(AdHocSource.snapshot)}`, and show per-source health on the page.

findings.title: AdHocSource resolves its repository once in init, while listings re-resolve it each time
findings.description: state.repo comes from repo_fun exactly once, in init. fetch/1 calls state.repo_fun.() on every listing. The event filter reconcile_issue/5 and maybe_relist/2 pattern-match on the frozen state.repo. There is no :workflow_config_updated handler. If configuration was unreadable at boot (state.repo = nil), every store event and every degraded, recovered or diverged notice falls through to the no-op clause for the life of the daemon, while the boot listing still succeeds and reports :available. After a repository change, the listing and the event filter follow different repos.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the repository once per listing and store it together with the baseline. Subscribe to WorkflowStore and reset the projection on a repository change, as TicketHistoryProvider does. Report :unavailable while repo is nil instead of silently ignoring events.

findings.title: Three coordinator GenServers copy the same skeleton (start_link, options, epochs, topics, LRU, task handshake, PubSub guard)
findings.description:
The GraphProjection, TicketDetailCoordinator and TicketHistoryProvider families (plus AdHocSource and PackStatus) duplicate the following:
- start_link with `nil -> GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, opts)`: 5 files in this unit, 18 in lib.
- `Keyword.pop(opts, :runtime_config?)` option merging: 3 copies.
- Bounded-integer option helpers: positive/non_negative in GraphProjection.Options, bounded_positive_option in TicketDetailCoordinator.Options, bounded_positive in TicketHistoryProvider.Options.
- reset_epoch with positive_epoch or valid_epoch_or_default: 2 identical copies. GraphProjection uses new_authority_epoch instead.
- Topic encoding `term_to_binary |> url_encode64`: 3 copies with 3 different identity keys (Policy.root_key = github_key, cache_key = {kind, downcase owner, downcase repo, provider_id}, github_key).
- LRU eviction: GraphProjection.eviction_candidate and TicketDetailCoordinator.Policy.make_room use min_by last_access_ms after rejecting inflight entries. TicketHistoryProvider.make_room uses an access_sequence counter instead.
- Task start with a `{:start, owner}` receive handshake plus terminate_child catch: 2 copies. The coordinator also calls Process.link on an async_nolink task.
- Configuration repository_opts/maybe_put: 2 copies.
- `if Process.whereis(Aiur.PubSub)` broadcast guards: 8 in this unit.
findings.recommendation: Extract `Aiur.Projection.Runtime` with: an Options DSL (bounded ints, runtime_config merge), `Epoch.new/1`, `Topic.for/2`, `LruEntries` (a struct with touch, evict and insert that respects inflight), `SupervisedRead` (start, terminate, timeout, generation guard), and `Broadcast.safe/2`. Migrate the three coordinators onto it.

findings.title: Unknown failures are collapsed into specific causes (:transport, :provider_unavailable, :connection_overflow)
findings.description:
The AGENTS.md rule 'a collapsed cause names the collapse at the source' is broken in several places:
- TicketDetail.Normalizer.failure_from/1 maps `{:github, _, _}` and `_` to :transport.
- The coordinator maps an unexpected reader return, and a crashed task (:DOWN), to :transport.
- GraphProjection maps a crashed read task, which is usually an Aiur exception in normalization, to {:error, :transport}. count_resolution_failure/1 then turns :transport into :unreachable, so the operator is told the tracker is unreachable when Aiur crashed.
- UsageRuntime rescues any exception or exit as :provider_unavailable, and apply_result/4 renders every error as health {:unavailable, :provider_unavailable}.
- GitHubGraph.Dependencies maps an invalid, schema-broken connection to :connection_overflow. That code is in Member.@invalidating_codes, so a missing field marks the whole selected root structurally invalid as an 'overflow'.
findings.recommendation: Add :unknown or :crashed to each failure taxonomy (TicketDetail.Failure, projection failure, Diagnostic) and use it in these clauses. Keep the original reason in a bounded `reasons` field, as analytics_cli does. Use Diagnostic :invalid_dependency or :provider_schema for an unparsable connection.

findings.title: PlanningSource silently drops unreadable or malformed packs, and a single bad ticket drops the whole pack
findings.description: load_pack/2 returns :error on any File.read, Jason.decode, repository or ticket failure. tickets/3 halts on the first ticket that fails ticket/3, for example a doc path outside tickets/ or an unexpected 'ticket' type. load_packs/1 then flat_maps :error away. No log, diagnostic or catalog entry is produced, so an operator whose pack has one typo sees the Build Order disappear from the catalog with no reason given. PackStatus, by contrast, records {:error, :invalid_pack} for the same file and reports it through health.
findings.recommendation: Return {:error, path, reason} and surface it as a catalog diagnostic (Catalog.new/3 already carries diagnostics and search_paths). Keep valid tickets and mark invalid ones as member diagnostics rather than dropping the pack.

findings.title: PlanningSource re-reads and re-parses every pack, status.json and draft body from disk on every catalog, selected or demand call
findings.description: catalog/0 calls membership_snapshot (CurrentRunMembership.snapshot plus StatusReport.snapshot_api), load_packs (File.read and Jason.decode of every discovered pack, File.read of each sibling status.json, and a sha256 of each body), and PackStatus.health (a GenServer call). selected_snapshot/1 calls load_packs(include_drafts?: true), which additionally reads up to 64 KB of draft body per draft ticket in every pack, only to find one pack by root. BuildOrderLive calls refresh_live_state on every :current_run_membership_changed and :build_order_pack_status_changed broadcast, which runs catalog/0 and selected/1 for each connected socket. In PackPaths.tracked_planning/0, foreign_repository?/1 reads and decodes each pack again.
findings.recommendation: Make the planning source a small GenServer or ETS cache keyed by path and mtime (or content hash) that re-parses only changed files, and load a draft body only for the selected pack.

findings.title: Workspace pack mirrors share a single status.json, which contradicts PlanningSource's stated invariant
findings.description: Workspace mirrors are flat files at `.aiur/build_orders/<slug>.json`, and status_path/1 is `dirname/status.json`, so every mirror maps to the same `.aiur/build_orders/status.json`. PackStatus writes that file, because tracked_planning -> planning -> discovered includes workspace packs, and merges each mirror's members into it. PlanningSource reads it back for every mirror. status_completed?/1 reads the top-level 'state'/'completed' keys, which the planning contract keeps as operator annotations, so one mirror's completion marker makes every workspace mirror render as completed. The comment on retain_state_projection/2 claims 'the daemon writes status.json only beside the repository-state manifest', and the code does not do that.
findings.recommendation: Key status by pack: `<slug>.status.json` for flat mirrors, or skip PackStatus writes for workspace mirrors and resolve their status from the matching state pack by build_order_id. Fix the comment.

findings.title: PackStatus writes each pack all-or-nothing within a per-repo 200-number window, so large or interleaved packs never converge
findings.description: One reconcile cycle fetches at most planning_call_budget (at most 4) x 50 = 200 issue numbers per repository. These are the sorted union of every tracked pack's numbers, rotated by retry_count x budget x 50. reconcile_fact/3 writes a pack only if every one of its member numbers is in this cycle's fetched map. As a result: a pack with more than 200 promoted members can never be written, and packs whose members interleave across a union larger than 200 may never fall inside one window. Completed packs stay in discovery, so the union grows over time. Their status.json freezes, which the moduledoc accepts ('a stale completion fact is strictly better'), but the health failure :planning_call_budget_exhausted recurs indefinitely and looks transient. Rotation also depends on retry_count, which resets to 0 on any fully successful cycle.
findings.recommendation: Merge partial lifecycles per member (status.json is keyed by member already), and track a per-pack cursor instead of requiring the full set in one cycle. Exclude completed packs, whose status says complete, from the poll union.

findings.title: Synthetic planning identities reuse real-looking issue numbers in the tracked repository
findings.description: For draft tickets, PlanningSource derives the issue number from the ticket id ('CT-101' becomes 101) or from phash2(id, 8000) + 1, and builds a joinable TrackerIdentity in the real configured repository with url `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/101`. The provider_id ('PLAN_CT-101') keeps github_key distinct. However, every consumer keyed on the bare identifier or the URL aliases a real, unrelated issue #101. Member.url becomes a valid-looking link to that issue. AnalyticsScope joins telemetry by the bare `identifier` string, so the analytics pane for a pre-ticket pack can attribute real ticket #101's telemetry to draft CT-101. Plausible; not reproduced end to end.
findings.recommendation: Give draft members an explicitly non-joinable identity kind (for example :planning) with no GitHub URL, or a number range that GitHub cannot assign. Make UsageScope and AnalyticsScope reject planning identities.

findings.title: The GitHub infrastructure layer depends on Build Order internals, and Build Order hosts general-purpose utilities
findings.description: The dependency arrows run the wrong way for a carve. Aiur.GitHub.Issues uses Aiur.BuildOrder.Bounded to validate repository components. Aiur.GitHub.IssueRelationships aliases Aiur.BuildOrder.TicketDetail.DestinationNormalizer only for a page-size constant. Aiur.GitHub.ViewStateSweep hard-codes `@sources [Aiur.BuildOrder.PackStatus]`. Aiur.GitHub.Client aliases GitHubGraph and ProviderResult. Aiur.Config aliases Aiur.BuildOrder.Cadence. Bounded, a generic GitHub URL, identifier and route validator, is also used by global_config_startup.ex and several OperatorControlCenter components. TicketDetail.Sanitizer, a generic secret and local-path redactor, is used by Aiur.LiveConversation.Normalizer and AiurWeb.Markdown. In the other direction, AiurWeb.BuildOrder.PlanningSource is a web module holding domain logic: pack parsing, lifecycle precedence and progress.
findings.recommendation: Before carving: move Bounded to Aiur.GitHub.Validate (or the identity package), move Sanitizer to Aiur.Redaction next to SecretRedactor, give IssueRelationships its own limit, turn ViewStateSweep sources into a registered behaviour, and move the Cadence derivation that Aiur.Config needs behind a config-side function. Move PlanningSource's domain parts into Aiur.BuildOrder.Pack (build-order-06).

findings.title: Several modules and functions have no production callers (tests only)
findings.description:

- TicketHistoryProvider.snapshots/0,1.
findings.recommendation: Delete these, or move them to test support if they document a contract. If a client-side highlight really needs DependencyChain, wire it in. Otherwise remove it and its test.

findings.title: GraphProjection scheduling has no-op and unreachable clauses left over from removed cadences
findings.description: Both clauses of schedule_after_completion/3 return state unchanged, yet complete_success/5 still computes `scope_interval(state, scope)` to pass in. The second clause of schedule_from_success/2 (1227-1246) is unreachable: schedule_active_scope/2 is called only for :catalog, where schedule_from_success(:catalog) is a no-op, and from restore_selected_retries/1 only when next_retry_at is non-nil, which skips the success branch. findings.title: Planning bounds and cadence ceilings are hard-coded in 4 or more places, and the member caps disagree
findings.description: The root, page and call limits 100/4/4 appear as literals in Settings (@member_limit 100, @max_page_budget 4, @max_call_budget 4), in Configuration.valid_limits?/1 (`valid_limit?(roots, 100) and valid_limit?(pages, 4) and valid_limit?(calls, 4)`), in Options.new/1 (`positive(opts, :root_limit, 100, 100)` and the rest), and in the tracker schema. Cadence ceilings of 3_600_000 and 300_000 appear in Cadence, Options.@maxima and Schema.BuildOrder. Cadence says its values 'mirror' the schema. The 120_000 fallback is repeated in Cadence (@fallback_interval_ms) and GraphProjection (@catalog_on_demand_fallback_ms), whose comment says 'mirroring Cadence's own fallback'. The member cap is 100 in GitHubGraph, CatalogStore, Normalizer and Dependencies, but SelectedRoot uses @max_members 1000, which no provider can reach. The 'build-order' label literal appears in Queries, CatalogStore and Normalizer. The schema rejects an explicit graph_catalog_refresh_ms of 0 (greater_than: 0), while Cadence and Options treat 0 as the on-demand sentinel.
findings.recommendation: Add an Aiur.BuildOrder.Limits module (or schema-exported constants) as the single source, referenced by the schema, Settings, Options, Configuration and Cadence. Remove the unreachable 1000 cap.

findings.title: Each graph read task closure captures the entire GraphProjection state and copies it to the task process
findings.description: TaskLifecycle.start/3 spawns `fn -> receive do {:graph_projection_start, ^owner} -> read(state, scope, reader_options) end end`. The closure closes over the full state map: the catalog, up to max_selected_roots (32, max 100) SelectedRoot graphs of up to 100 members each, all monitors and all timers. The BEAM copies all of it into every read task, up to max_inflight concurrently, when only the reader function is needed. TicketDetailCoordinator.TaskLifecycle.start_task/4 likewise captures `state` (all detail snapshots) to read reader, max_description_bytes and freshness_ms.
findings.recommendation: Bind only what the task needs before spawning: `reader = reader_for(state, scope)` and a small opts keyword list.

findings.title: PlanningSource generation comes from a resettable counter under a constant authority epoch, which can freeze a live page
findings.description: PlanningSource publishes authority_epoch: @epoch = 1 always, and a generation equal to 1 + CurrentRunMembership generation, Cantor-paired with the PackStatus generation. CurrentRunMembership.Projection.new/1 starts generation at 0 on a new run, and PackStatus's moduledoc says membership 'is rebuilt from an empty journal whenever a new run starts'. If a run rotates while a Build Order LiveView stays mounted, the published generation falls. RouteState.catalog_update/2 and selected_update/2 then return :ignored, because the incoming generation is neither newer nor equal. Since the epoch never changes, SourceRuntime.reset/2 never fires, and the page ignores updates until the counter climbs past its old value. Plausible; depends on whether a run can rotate without a daemon restart.
findings.recommendation: Derive the epoch from run_id (bump the authority epoch when the membership run_id changes), or publish a monotonic generation owned by PlanningSource (System.unique_integer monotonic) instead of arithmetic over foreign counters.

findings.title: A single unacceptable linked pull request fails the whole ticket detail
findings.description: DestinationNormalizer.normalize/3 reduce_while's over the linked PR nodes and halts with :error on the first one that fails pull_request/2. The whole ticket detail then fails with Failure :validation. closedByPullRequestsReferences can include pull requests in other repositories that reference this issue, and Bounded.github_pull_request_url_for/3 rejects those because the repository differs. Such a PR, or any node with an unexpected state such as a new GitHub enum value, makes the detail drawer unavailable. It also feeds the loop in build-order-01. Plausible; depends on cross-repository references existing.
findings.recommendation: Drop and count invalid PR nodes (for example pull_requests_rejected: n) instead of failing the snapshot. Treat a foreign-repository PR as an external destination.

findings.title: File and module layout is inconsistent: files named after one module define another, and namespaces are flat
findings.description: lifecycle.ex defines Aiur.BuildOrder.ProviderHealth first, then Lifecycle, and there is no provider_health.ex. edge_state.ex also defines Readiness. ticket_detail_destinations.ex defines TicketDetail.DestinationNormalizer. The *_contract.ex files bundle 2 to 6 modules; ticket_detail_contract.ex holds Failure, State, IssueDestination, PullRequestDestination, Destinations and Snapshot. findings.recommendation: Own bounded text, permitted controls and collision-rejecting key normalization in decision validation; retain the recent-merge adapter as a separate domain policy.

findings.title: The generic event bus core embeds GitHub policy and calls into the Orchestrator, which blocks carving Aiur.Events into a standalone package
findings.description: Publisher is documented as the shared publish boundary for every source, but it hard-codes GitHub concerns. These are bot self-loop via GitHub.Config.daemon_account and AgentMarker, single-account provenance, ResourceStore processed marks, and Webhooks.record_activity corroboration. It also depends on Aiur.IssueLog and TicketObservation. SubscriptionStore delivers by GenServer.call to the globally named Aiur.Orchestrator. The Aiur.Events namespace mixes the generic bus (Exchange, Topic, IdGenerator, Publisher, SubscriptionStore, DebugLog) with GitHub producers (firehose, comments and CI pollers, webhook normalizer and deposit, ls-remote ticker, BranchRefStore, PrCommandScanner, Sanitizer). The GitHub producers in turn reach into Orchestrator modules (ReadyForReviewTransitions, request_refresh, a named-process send). None of these can move into separate packages without cycles.
findings.recommendation: Split Publisher into a generic publish pipeline (id, envelope, dedup window, Exchange fan-out) plus a list of injected gates. Implement GitHubGates (self-loop/provenance, resource-processed suppression, webhook activity) in the GitHub package and register them at boot. Give SubscriptionStore a sink behaviour ({module, fun}) configured by the orchestrator instead of Process.whereis(Aiur.Orchestrator). Move the GitHub producers to Aiur.GitHub.Events.* (or a github_events package) that depends on the bus, not the other way round.

findings.title: Closing-keyword ticket parsing has diverged: the webhook normalizer uses a loose first-match regex while RecentMerge deliberately uses a narrow line-anchored one
findings.description: For an issue_comment on a PR, the normalizer routes the comment to the first `\b(close[sd]?|fix(e[sd])?|resolve[sd]?)\s+#N` anywhere in the PR body, including quoted text and mid-sentence prose. RecentMerge documents why it deliberately accepts a keyword only where it opens a line, list item or clause, and why it skips quoted lines. A PR body such as 'This does not fix #12. Closes #34' routes the comment to ticket 12. The comment is published with bypass_contamination: true, so it can reach a ticket the PR never claimed.
findings.recommendation: Expose RecentMerge's closing-reference parser (or move it to Aiur.GitHub.ClosingReferences) and use it in the normalizer, taking the first same-repo reference. Better still, resolve PR to ticket via the delivered PR head ref (DeliveredPullRequest store) when it is available.

findings.title: Webhook check-run normalizer and poll-batch normalizer disagree on check_suite_id type despite the 'change one, change both' contract
findings.description: Both files say the normalized keys are the contract between delivery and poll snapshots. The GraphQL batch selects `checkSuite { id }`, a global node id string, while the REST delivery writes check_suite.id, a numeric database id. After PollSnapshots.merge_check_run replaces one run in a polled snapshot, that run's check_suite_id is a different type from its siblings in the same suite. GithubCIPoller keys 'latest run per workflow' on {:suite, check_suite_id}, so a merged run and a polled run of the same workflow would no longer collapse. The damage is latent today: CIPollBatch serves delivered snapshots as inert ('delivered: true') and they are never evaluated for a verdict. It becomes live the moment anyone evaluates a merged snapshot.
findings.recommendation: Select checkSuite { databaseId } in the GraphQL query so both sides are numeric. Move both normalize_check_run/1 functions into one module with two entry points (from_graphql/1, from_rest/1) and a test asserting identical key sets and value types.

After PollSnapshots.merge_check_run replaces one run in a polled snapshot, that run's check_suite_id is a different type from its siblings in the same suite. GithubCIPoller keys 'latest run per workflow' on {:suite, check_suite_id}, so a merged run and a polled run of the same workflow would no longer collapse. The damage is latent today: CIPollBatch serves delivered snapshots as inert ('delivered: true') and they are never evaluated for a verdict. It becomes live the moment anyone evaluates a merged snapshot.

Change one, change both.`
claim.recommendation: Select checkSuite { databaseId } in the GraphQL query so both sides are numeric. Move both normalize_check_run/1 functions into one module with two entry points (from_graphql/1, from_rest/1) and a test asserting identical key sets and value types.

findings.title: Deposit's function-wide rescue also skips ReadCache invalidation; fixed per raise-site instead of structurally
findings.description: deposit/4 computes bodies, writes them, then calls invalidate_read_cache/3, all inside one rescue/catch that logs a warning and returns []. Any raise in body extraction, for example get_in on a malformed nested field inside Normalizer.comment_shape, skips the invalidation. The ReadCache then keeps serving stale entries whose TTLs the moduledoc says were raised 'from seconds to hours' on the strength of this invalidation. Two raise sites were patched individually, and their comments name exactly this hazard.
findings.recommendation: Run invalidate_read_cache/3 in its own try (or in an `after`) so it happens whether or not the deposit raised. Emit a counter or alert for deposit exceptions instead of only a Logger.warning, since Logger output is dropped without --debug.

findings.title: EventKey semantic dedup collides for genuinely new events (review edits, check-suite re-runs), dropping them at admission for 72 h
findings.description: The moduledoc promises that a key 'changes when the event genuinely changes'. The pull_request_review key is [id, action, state] with no timestamp, so a second 'edited' of the same review is a duplicate_event and is dropped before Deposit and record_delivery run. The check_suite/check_run/workflow_run key is [id, status, conclusion]. The CI poller documents that 'GitHub re-runs of the same workflow reuse the suite id', so a re-run that ends with the same conclusion (failure after failure) produces the same key. Its completed delivery is dropped, and the CI reconcile wake is lost until the next scheduled poll.
findings.recommendation: Include updated_at for check_suite/check_run/workflow_run (all three carry it) and run_attempt for workflow_run. For reviews, include a hash of the body plus submitted_at, or omit the semantic key for 'edited'. Add tests for a re-run with the same conclusion and for two review edits.

findings.title: Webhook wake coalescing window lives in :persistent_term with a non-atomic get/put and an unsupervised sleeping process per window
findings.description: Each delivery that wakes or first coalesces calls :persistent_term.put with a new tuple. Replacing a persistent term triggers a global GC scan of every process, which is the documented anti-pattern for frequently changing values. Up to two puts per window, and the window can be as short as 2 s. Deliveries run in concurrent Task.Supervisor children, so claim_reconcile_window/0 is a racy read-modify-write: two tasks can both claim the leading edge, and generation numbers can be lost. arm_trailing_wake/2 uses bare spawn plus Process.sleep, so the timer process is unsupervised and survives code reloads and test boundaries. The test seam reset_reconcile_window/0 is public production API.
findings.recommendation: Move coalescing into the Orchestrator's request_refresh handling (it already coalesces) or into a small GenServer or :atomics-backed module. Use Process.send_after for the trailing wake. Delete the persistent_term state.

findings.title: Publisher replay dedup is a non-atomic check-then-insert on a public ETS table; the moduledoc wrongly says mutations go through the GenServer
findings.description: deduped?/1 runs seen?/1 and then record_seen/1 in the caller's process. Callers include up to four concurrent comment-poller tasks, concurrent webhook delivery tasks, the firehose and CommandScan. Two concurrent publishes of the same dedup key both observe 'not seen' and both publish. The durable resource gate has the same check-then-mark gap, since it marks only after the publish. The table is also a fixed :named_table, so the start_link :name option cannot actually support a second instance.
findings.recommendation: Use :ets.insert_new/2 as the atomic claim, and for an expired entry use a match-spec compare-and-swap or :ets.select_replace. Fix the moduledoc. Derive the table name from the server name, or drop the :name option.

findings.title: A third, divergent CI classifier lives in TakeoverAlert.Snapshot
findings.description: Snapshot.summarize_ci/2 reclassifies check runs and statuses for the takeover advisory with its own failure list. That list omits startup_failure. It also skips the non-blocking filter ('(non-blocking)' suffix) and the latest-run-per-(suite, name) collapse that GithubCIPoller.evaluate applies. The advisory can therefore say 'failing (N checks)' for a head whose gate verdict is :passed, for example after a superseded failed run or a failing non-blocking check. It can also say 'unknown' where the gate says failed (startup_failure).
findings.recommendation: Make GithubCIPoller.evaluate/2 public (as Aiur.GitHub.CIClassifier.evaluate/2, replacing evaluate_for_test/2). Have the snapshot render its decision and failures instead of re-deriving them.

findings.title: GithubCIPoller (816 lines) mixes CI classification, PR base-branch repair and journaling, and its 4-arm base-repair case is copied three times
findings.description: The module has 69 def clauses and three responsibilities: a pure classifier (evaluate plus helpers, about 250 lines), base-branch repair with a crash-safe journal (ensure_pull_request_base, recover/persist/journal, repair_error, base_branch_failure/repaired, about 300 lines), and the fetch/fan-out orchestration. The ensure_pull_request_base result case ({:ok,:unchanged} / {:ok,{:unchanged,rec}} / {:ok,{:repaired,inv}} / {:error,reason,inv}) is handled by three near-identical case blocks. The invalidation marker is matched in both atom-keyed and string-keyed shapes (lines 430-446 and 643-653), which is the 'duplicated parsing of a persisted shape' family. evaluate_for_test/2 is a test-only public function.
findings.recommendation: Split into CIClassifier (pure), BaseRepair (ensure, journal, recovery, returning one tagged result), and GithubCIPoller (fan-out plus one with_base_repair/3 helper consumed by the batch, REST and recheck paths). Normalise the invalidation marker to one struct at the CIApprovalStore load boundary.

findings.title: The conditional-list (ETag plus held body) read protocol is copy-pasted in GithubCommentsPoller (3 call sites) and Orchestrator.CommandScan
findings.description: The correctness-critical validator/body contract with the ResourceStore is implemented twice, and CommandScan says it mirrors the poller. The contract covers where the validator came from (cycle or store), depositing the list and the ETag together only after publish, dropping the ETag on nil, and 'a 304 against a store validator with no body is unusable'. The pieces are request_etag and durable_etag, remember_list x2, unchanged_list and command_scan_unchanged_list, forget_validator and drop_validator. Inside the poller, the fetch then 200/304/error then publish then remember flow is written out three times (issue comments, PR conversation comments, reviews), with three near-identical unchanged_* functions. Their return tuples have 4 or 6 positional elements ({count, newest, result, etag} and {count, newest, results, etags, review_seen_at, draft_obs}).
findings.recommendation: Extract Aiur.GitHub.ConditionalList with read(resource, cycle_etag, fetch_fun, publish_fun) returning a result struct (count, newest, etag, error). Use it from all four sites. Replace positional tuples with a %TargetResult{} struct.

findings.title: The two pollers' per-target fan-outs are duplicated and have diverged (supervision, option validation, trap_exit)
findings.description: Both pollers normalise targets identically (normalize_targets/1 copied verbatim), then fan out with max_concurrency 4 and a 60 s kill_task timeout, then zip results back to targets and map {:exit, reason} to a per-target error. They differ in ways nobody chose. The comments poller uses unsupervised Task.async_stream and flips trap_exit. The CI poller prefers Task.Supervisor.async_stream_nolink and falls back to the trap_exit variant. The comments poller validates max_concurrency and timeout through positive_integer_option/3; the CI poller passes Keyword.get values through unvalidated.
findings.recommendation: Extract Aiur.GitHub.TargetFanout.run(targets, fun, opts) (supervised, validated options, results keyed by target, plus max_duration_ms/2) and use it from both pollers.

findings.title: SubscriptionStore failure handling is inconsistent: attach reports :ok on failure, base-branch reconcile swallows errors after a partial Exchange mutation, and some persist failures crash while others are ignored
findings.description: (1) attach/1 turns {:error, reason} from DynamicSupervisor.start_child into Logger.warning plus :ok. The caller (UniversalSubscriptions.attach) proceeds, every add_subscription exits with noproc, and each exit is caught and logged. The agent receives no events and nothing surfaces to the operator. (2) reconcile_base_branch_auto/1 rescues and catches everything and returns the old state with no log. reconcile_exchange_bindings/2 may already have unsubscribed old topics before the failure, so Exchange bindings and subscribed_to diverge silently. (3) persist/1 returns :error on failure. Six handle_call sites match `:ok = persist(new_state)`, which crashes the per-ticket store on a disk error, while advance_cursor_inline, reconcile and terminate use `_ = persist(...)` and continue with durable state behind memory.
findings.recommendation: Return {:error, reason} from attach/1 and emit an alert (Aiur.Alerts) when a ticket's subscription store cannot start. In reconcile_base_branch_auto, log and alert, and recompute Exchange bindings from the retained state on failure. Choose one persist policy (retry with backoff as BranchRefStore does, plus an alert) and apply it everywhere.

findings.title: SubscriptionStore does an fsync'd atomic file rewrite for every consumed event, per subscribing ticket
findings.description: Every successfully enqueued event calls advance_cursor_inline, which calls persist, which calls JsonStore.write!. That write is mkdir_p, encode, write a tmp file, fsync and rename. Universal topics such as system.<base>.branch.push are bound by every running ticket, so one main-branch push produces N fsync'd rewrites at once. The cursor is monotonic and replay is already at-least-once and deduped downstream, so per-event durability buys little.
findings.recommendation: Debounce cursor persistence (for example, persist at most every 1 s or every N events, and always in terminate/2). Subscription and attention changes stay synchronous. Document the replay window this adds.

findings.title: Executor.Principal stops renewing forever, with no log or alert, on revoke, release or a corrupt claims file
findings.description: If renew returns an entry whose role is not owner or observer (revoked), or returns {:error, :unknown_consumer}, the Principal returns {:noreply, state} without rescheduling. It never re-registers and never logs. Claims.read_at/2 maps any unreadable or corrupt claims file to %{}, which makes every renew answer :unknown_consumer. One truncated write therefore permanently ends the declared Executor's lease renewal with no signal, and the lease lapses 10 minutes later. This is a latch that nothing polls.
findings.recommendation: On :unknown_consumer, re-register (claim, then observe). On revoked, log at warning and emit an Executor alert. In read_at/2, distinguish a corrupt file (alert, and refuse to overwrite other daemons' entries) from an absent one.

findings.title: BranchRefStore pending final-unblocks are never pruned: an unblock for a superseded or deleted SHA is latched on disk forever
findings.description: register_unblock/3 durably retains a pending unblock until acknowledge_unblock/3 removes that exact ref:sha. It is removed only if recipients later consume it. If the agent pushes again (new SHA) or the branch is deleted, the pending entry can never match. replace/2, called with every ls-remote baseline, prunes nothing, so entries accumulate across tickets in branch_refs.json. The push_routing caller also treats the bare :error return (a persistence failure) as 'do nothing' with no log.
findings.recommendation: In replace/2, drop pending unblocks whose identifier is absent from the new baseline or whose SHA differs from the baseline SHA. Add a TTL for anything older than N days. Return {:error, reason} rather than bare :error, and log or alert at the caller.

findings.title: LsRemoteTicker keeps its own in-memory ref map and ignores the durable BranchRefStore baseline, so pushes made while the daemon was down are never published
findings.description: BranchRefStore exists to hold 'restart-durable validated remote refs'. The ticker starts with refs: %{} and bootstrapped?: false. On its first successful tick after boot it overwrites the durable baseline with the current refs and publishes nothing. A push that happened during downtime is never emitted as ticket.<id>.branch.push, even though the durable previous SHA needed to detect it was on disk. The same ref map exists twice (ticker.refs and BranchRefStore.refs). Separately, publish_push/4 builds the same payload map in both the :ticket and :system branches.
findings.recommendation: At init, seed the ticker's refs from the BranchRefStore baseline and mark bootstrapped? when one exists, so the first tick diffs against durable state. Keep the silent bootstrap only when no baseline exists. Drop the ticker's private refs and read the store's. Build the payload once.

findings.title: Webhooks.EventSource (and its Polling/Webhook implementations) is unused in production and bypasses Publisher; its contract tests cover a path that does not exist
findings.description: grep finds no reference to EventSource anywhere in src/lib outside its own three files. It is used only by test/aiur/webhooks/consumer_equivalence_test.exs, webhook_mode_contract_test.exs and test/support/webhook_mode_contract.exs. The production webhook path is Aiur.Events.GithubWebhook, which goes through Normalizer, Sanitizer and Publisher. EventSource.publish/2 calls Exchange.publish directly, with no id, no sanitizer, no dedup and no contamination filter. findings.title: Ingest's LabelState output (full label list, refresh_required?) is computed and never consumed
findings.description: Ingest.accept/4 returns admission.label_state = %{labels: [...], refresh_required?: bool}, and LabelState's doc says a refresh_required? result means 'the issue should be re-read from the API'. The only consumer, the webhook controller, passes only (event_type, payload, delivery_id) to GithubWebhook.handle_delivery. grep finds no reader of label_state or refresh_required? outside webhooks/. Only the {:drop, :stale_state} side effect is live.
