findings.title: Executor.Roster turns an unavailable wake inbox into cursor 0 and pending 0, so a consumer reads 'idle' instead of 'unknown'
findings.description: The Roster's contract is that missing evidence yields :unknown, never a healthy state. safe_cursor/1 and safe_pending_count/1 catch every failure and return 0. With pending_count 0, stalled? is false and derive_state returns :idle for any live claimed consumer, even a wedged one. The fabricated 0/0 is also written into the durable observation (record_observations), which corrupts the next build's 'grew?' and cursor_moved comparisons. This is the collapsed-cause pattern that AGENTS.md ('Computed ages and collapsed causes') calls out.
findings.recommendation: Return nil (unavailable) from both helpers. Have derive_state yield :unknown when the cursor or pending count is nil, and skip record_observations when the inputs are unavailable. Add a test that makes the inbox raise and asserts :unknown.

findings.title: BudgetMap re-implements agent-cache.tsv discovery and parsing: its glob never matches in production and its parser has drifted from AgentCacheMetrics
findings.description: The same /github-cache page renders two agent-cache hit rates from two independent readers of the same files. (1) BudgetMap.agent_cache_files/0 calls Path.wildcard/1 without match_dot: true. Quota documents (#1805) that this matches nothing through the .aiur-runtime dot directory, and I verified it: the default call returns [] while match_dot: true finds the file. The BudgetMap agent-cache panel therefore always reports available?: false in production. (2) The parser has drifted. BudgetMap accepts exactly 5 columns and the actions hit/miss/store/refused. The writer emits 6-column miss rows with a reason and a coalesced action (AgentCacheMetrics accepts both; agent_github_guard_test asserts both). BudgetMap therefore undercounts misses and over-reports hit rate. It has no time window, reads only .tsv and .tsv.1, and has no read-byte cap. AgentCacheMetrics uses a 24h window, all rotated archives and an 8 MiB cap. (3) The test injects glob_fun and uses only 5-column rows, so the fixture cannot reach either defect.
findings.recommendation: Delete BudgetMap.agent_cache/1, agent_cache_files/0, read_workspace_cache/1 and parse_agent_cache_row/1. Have the budget map read AgentCacheMetrics.snapshot() (the cached sampler), adding a per-workspace breakdown to AgentCacheMetrics if the page needs one. Extract the workspace-glob builder shared by Quota (x2), AgentCacheMetrics, BudgetMap and AlertFeed into one Layout helper that always passes match_dot: true.

findings.title: The OS process-tree walk and kill is copied in three places, and one copy keeps the String.to_integer bug that Config.kill_os_process documents fixing
findings.description: GitHub.Config (a configuration module) contains about 150 lines of OS process management: a recursive pgrep -P walk, TERM-then-KILL of every descendant, and a shell fallback for a missing kill binary. Its comments describe a shipped regression: parsing pgrep's stderr-merged output with String.to_integer/1 raised on a non-numeric byte, and the rescue swallowed the whole kill. Config fixed that locally with Integer.parse. The copy in Claude.RemoteControl.collect_descendants still uses String.to_integer on the same stderr_to_stdout pgrep output. AgentResourceGuard has a third copy (defensive, but with no kill sequencing). Budget.terminate_port has a fourth, pid-only kill.
findings.recommendation: Extract an Aiur.OsProcessTree module (descendants/2 with defensive parsing, signal_tree/3 with walk-before-TERM, re-walk, then KILL, never process groups) and replace all four call sites. Move the keyring shell-out itself out of GitHub.Config into Aiur.GitHub.KeyringToken.

findings.title: The GitHub.Client facade depends on BuildOrder (a package cycle) and carries more than 10 pass-through delegates with no production caller
findings.description: Client is a 388-line module with 53 public functions, almost all one-line delegates into 16 aliased modules. It aliases Aiur.BuildOrder.GitHubGraph (fetch_build_order_catalog/selected_root), and BuildOrder.GitHubGraph aliases Aiur.GitHub.Transport. That creates a github <-> build_order dependency cycle that will block splitting them into packages. The BuildOrder delegates are called only from tests. Other delegates have no lib caller (checked via direct calls, Tracker.client_module() dynamic dispatch and GitHubClient aliases): fetch_recent_repo_review_comments/1, fetch_recent_repo_issue_comments/1, fetch_pull_request_changed_paths/2, fetch_pull_request_review_comments/2, fetch_pull_request_head_ref/2, fetch_pull_request_head_ref_conditional/2, fetch_open_pull_request_conditional/2, fetch_build_order_catalog/1, fetch_build_order_selected_root/2. Client is also dispatched dynamically through Application.get_env(:aiur, :github_client_module) in tracker.ex, human_review.ex and rework_gate.ex, so the facade doubles as an untyped mock seam.
findings.recommendation: Delete the BuildOrder delegates (tests call GitHubGraph directly) and the other unused delegates. Replace the Client facade plus Application.get_env mock seam with a Tracker-side behaviour (the Aiur.Tracker callbacks already exist) implemented by domain modules. Callers alias the domain module they need (Issues, PullRequests, Comments, ReviewThreads).

findings.title: GitHub login normalisation is repeated in about 11 places with divergent case handling; BotIdentity.agent_login? is case-sensitive while its twin is not
findings.description: The question "is this login one of ours / allowed" is answered by hand-rolled trim, downcase and uniq code at each site. The sites disagree: Config.trusted_accounts and normalize_logins preserve case (uniq_by downcase). CodeOwners downcases into a MapSet. DispatchAuthorization.allowed_users downcases but does not trim, while member?/2 trims. BotIdentity.codeowners_classification_opts trims but never downcases, and agent_login?/2 uses exact Enum.member?. Aiur.Codeowners.agent_login? downcases. So BotIdentity.agent_login?("aiur-bot", bot_account: "Aiur-Bot") is false while the Codeowners twin answers true. Config.ex:448 claims "Case-insensitive, matching every consumer of bot_account". The same trim/reject-empty/uniq pipeline is copy-pasted twice inside config.ex alone (trusted_accounts vs normalize_logins).
findings.recommendation: Introduce Aiur.GitHub.Login with normalize/1 (trim, strip leading @, downcase, nil for blank), normalize_set/1 and member?/2. Replace all listed sites, and make BotIdentity.agent_login? and every allowlist compare through it. Add one property test asserting that case and whitespace variants are equivalent for every trust predicate.

findings.title: CIPollBatch and CommentPollBatch duplicate branch-candidate discovery, GraphQL alias building and PR-node normalisation, and their overflow semantics have already diverged
findings.description: Byte-identical private copies exist in both files: branch_target_entry/2, guessed_branches/2, known_branch/2, open_pull_request_head_ref/2 (2 clauses), escape_graphql_string/1 and open_pull_request_node?/1, plus the same @pull_requests_per_branch 2 constant and a roughly 40-line rationale comment repeated almost verbatim. The branch-alias GraphQL string, candidate-connection lookup and GraphQL-to-REST PR normalisation ("head" => %{"ref","sha"}, "base" => %{"ref"}, downcased state) are near-copies. The divergence is real. CommentPollBatch answers :unknown if ANY candidate connection overflowed. CIPollBatch checks hasNextPage only on the chosen (first non-empty, else first) connection, so the two batches can answer the same target differently. The normalised PR payloads also carry different field sets (draft/review_decision/head_committed_at vs merge_queue). Branch names are interpolated into the GraphQL document with a hand-rolled escaper instead of being passed as variables.
findings.recommendation: Extract Aiur.GitHub.PullRequestDiscovery with target_entries/4 (delivered number / known branch / guessed branches), aliases/3 (with GraphQL variables for headRefName), resolve/3 (one overflow policy) and normalize_node/2 (one base shape, with callers adding their extra fields). Both batches then own only their field selection and post-processing.

claim.title: CIPollBatch and CommentPollBatch duplicate branch-candidate discovery, GraphQL alias building and PR-node normalisation, and their overflow semantics have already diverged

Group into the complete CI/comment branch selection subroutine, retaining malformed/non-map fallback; no separate extraction count.
claim.evidence: 10 distinct definition spans in 5 assessed exact/renamed candidate groups. Body hashes and every candidate site are preserved in evidence_groups and the census/triage ledgers. Group membership is syntactic evidence; the description states verified semantic differences.
claim.recommendation: Own ordered branch candidates in TicketBranch and poll-input normalization in GitHub polling; preserve known-branch precedence including current empty-string behavior.

findings.title: Every metered GitHub request forks at least two python3 processes synchronously in the calling process (acquire and release, plus reconcile or hold)
findings.description: Budget.acquire, release, the 304 reconcile, hold and the disagreement meter each call command/3. That spawns a fresh python3 interpreter via Port.open against priv/github_budget.py and SQLite. Transport.budget_request runs acquire before the request and release in the after block on the CALLER's process (often an orchestrator or poller GenServer), with a 1.5s admission deadline and Process.sleep retries. CredentialSelector's own moduledoc rejects exactly this cost for usage/1 ("would trade an API-budget problem for a fork-per-request problem"), yet the request path already pays it twice per request. Each call is also another place a slow host turns into github_budget_broker_timeout (see BrokerTimeout).
findings.recommendation: Run the broker as one long-lived port (a line protocol over stdin/stdout) owned by a supervised Budget.Broker process, or move daemon-side admission into Elixir (Exqlite is already a dependency; BudgetLedger uses it) and keep python only for the shell wrapper. Make release asynchronous (cast) so it does not extend the caller's deadline. Measure calls per hour before and after using the ledger.

findings.title: Budget (915 lines) mixes broker process management, settings resolution, response observation and alerting; its settings defaults duplicate the config schema
findings.description: Budget holds at least five responsibilities: (a) the Port/guardian/kill machinery for the python broker (542-640), (b) settings resolution with 11 near-identical positive/nonnegative(Keyword.get(opts, k, Map.get(github, k, @default_k)), @default_k) stanzas (settings/1 is 51 lines), (c) admission retry and hold parsing, (d) response observation and rate-limit hold derivation with its own header parsing, (e) meter-disagreement alerting via CredentialHeadroom (a Budget <-> CredentialHeadroom call cycle). All ten @default_* budget constants are duplicated in Config.Schema.Tracker, while BrokerTimeout reads its defaults from the schema struct ("keeps one source of truth"), so the codebase uses both approaches.
findings.recommendation: Split into Budget.Broker (port and command transport), Budget.Settings (table-driven: one list of {key, kind} reading defaults from struct!(Schema.Tracker.Github)), Budget.Admission (acquire/retry/hold), and Budget.Observer (response -> holds). Move token_key/identity_key/request_resource into a small leaf (e.g. Budget.Keys or EndpointPolicy) to break the Budget <-> CredentialHeadroom cycle.

findings.title: GitHub.Config (1090 lines) is a grab bag on the per-request hot path: repo resolution, token resolution, keyring shell-out plus process killing, identity, allowlists, PR watch/health settings, and a /rate_limit probe
findings.description: Config.token/0 is called on every GitHub request, yet the same module owns about 375 lines of keyring shell-out, Task bounding, pgrep walking and kill signalling (621-996), plus a separate /rate_limit validity probe with its own header parsing (998-1080) that bypasses Transport and Budget. The module also exposes pr_watch/pr_health accessors that read non-GitHub settings (Aiur.Config.settings!().pr_watch/.pr_health), and its allowed_users fallback calls the CodeOwners GenServer (github-a-02). Many functions route through section_value/1 -> Aiur.Config.settings!(), which raises when config is unavailable, so callers such as CredentialRegistry and AppTokenRefresher wrap it in rescue/catch.
findings.recommendation: Split into GitHub.Config (typed section accessors only), GitHub.RepoResolution (explicit vs origin, diagnostic), GitHub.TokenResolution (App vs PAT vs keyring, cached), GitHub.KeyringToken (bounded gh auth token, using OsProcessTree from github-a-05), and GitHub.Identity (bot/app/daemon/identity_mode). Move pr_watch/pr_health accessors to the orchestrator's config. Validate tokens through Transport with AppToken.rate_limit_usable?/2 (one probe).

findings.title: CiReadiness (1148 lines) combines HTTP inspection, a GitHub Actions workflow and matrix interpreter, ruleset evaluation, a two-tier cache and operator copy, and re-implements Transport's bounded request
findings.description: Responsibilities: (1) cache and persistence of assessments in :persistent_term plus a JSON file, with fingerprint, TTL and encode/decode (106-347); (2) its own spawn_monitor deadline wrapper, await_request_result, around a request_fun that already goes through Transport.off_process_request with request :timeout_ms. That is a second, weaker bound: not linked to the caller, and it drops $callers and logger metadata. (3) Two copy-paste paginators (workflow states and rulesets) differing only in URL prefix and error atoms. (4) A pure interpreter for Actions YAML: triggers, branch globs, matrix include/exclude expansion and job if-conditions (850-1094). (5) Token-type-specific operator guidance text. glob_matches?/2 compiles a Regex on every call.
findings.recommendation: Split into CiReadiness (orchestration and result type), CiReadiness.WorkflowAnalyzer (pure YAML semantics, highly testable), CiReadiness.Rulesets, CiReadiness.AssessmentStore (memory plus file cache) and CiReadiness.Messages. Delete bounded_request_fun/await_request_result and pass timeout_ms/deadline through Transport. Use one Transport paginator (github-a-16).

findings.title: DispatchAuthorization rewrites a 1000-entry :persistent_term map on every new decision and lazily creates a named public ETS table owned by whichever process calls first
findings.description: The module comment says only small caches stay in :persistent_term, because each put triggers a global literal-area GC scan. But cache_decision puts a map holding up to 1000 fingerprints and decisions (each decision carries a list of prefix appliers) every time a timeline is evaluated, i.e. on every issue whose updated_at moved. maybe_alert_once rewrites the same term. At 1000 entries the whole cache is dropped at once. The timeline ETS table is created on first use by whatever process calls authorize (the orchestrator, an RPC handler in agent_control_cli, decision_revision_dispatch, ...). If that process is short-lived, the table and its held ETags vanish with it. Two first callers racing between :ets.whereis and :ets.new raise ArgumentError (named table exists) inside issue normalisation. The same lazy-owner pattern appears in opencode/active_turns.ex:173, orchestrator/snapshot_publisher.ex:136, opencode/token_registry.ex:128, orchestrator/tracked_set.ex:109 and workflow_store/cache.ex:36.
findings.recommendation: Create both caches in init/1 of a supervised owner (e.g. a DispatchAuthorization.Cache GenServer that owns an ETS table with a bounded LRU by insertion time) and keep decisions and alerts in ETS, not :persistent_term. Replace the wholesale reset with per-entry eviction. Apply the same fix to the other lazily created named tables.

findings.title: Dispatch-authorization causes are collapsed: every non-transport failure is labelled "transient", and a missing token becomes a provenance denial that revokes agents
findings.description: deferral_cause/1 maps everything other than truncation or the page limit to "transient" (`_reason -> "transient"`). That includes permanent responses: timeline 403/404/410 (`{:timeline_fetch_failed, ...}`), `:timeline_unexpected_304` from a proxy, and `:invalid_timeline_response`. Such a ticket is deferred on every cycle with only Logger.warning and no alert, so it is never dispatched and nothing surfaces it. This is the AGENTS.md rule 2 anti-pattern: collapsing to a specific cause rather than :unknown. Conversely, a missing token is a "could not check" condition, yet fetch_decision returns {:ambiguous, :missing_github_token}. That becomes :denied, which Reconciler treats as revoked (terminating running agents), and it raises one needs_attention alert per issue.
findings.recommendation: Classify deferrals as transport_limit | rate_limited | transient_network | permanent_http | unknown, and alert with dwell on anything other than transient_network and rate_limited. Return {:deferred, :missing_github_token} instead of :ambiguous. Keep :denied strictly for verdicts derived from a fetched timeline.

findings.title: Link-header pagination is re-implemented in about 7 places with divergent safety (page cap, cycle detection, origin check); DependenciesApi does not paginate at all
findings.description: The implementations differ. CiReadiness has a page cap (20), cycle detection (seen list) and a same-origin prefix check. DispatchAuthorization has a page budget but no cycle or origin check. Comments.fetch_repo_comment_stream and Teams.fetch_member_logins have no cap, no cycle check and no origin check, and accumulate with acc ++ body (quadratic). Transport.fetch_json_list silently takes page 1 (github-a-04). The DependenciesApi blocked_by and blocking GETs send no per_page and never follow Link, so they return at most GitHub's default of 30 entries. An issue blocked by more than 30 issues is gated on a truncated list, and the store caches that truncated list as the full answer. parse_next_page_url is called at 22 sites across 10 files.
findings.recommendation: Add one Transport.paginate(request_fun, request, max_pages:, same_origin?: true) returning {:ok, list, meta} | {:error, :pagination_limit | :pagination_cycle | ...} with iodata/reverse accumulation, and migrate every call site. Give dependency reads per_page=100 and pagination. Where a page-1 ETag is used, have the helper report single_page? so callers stop re-deriving it.

findings.title: x-ratelimit-* header parsing is implemented four or five times with different strictness, and there are two separate token-usability probes
findings.description: Remaining, limit and reset are parsed by: Config.header_remaining/body_remaining/parse_integer (lenient Integer.parse, keeping the rest, plus list-and-map header forms re-implemented despite Transport.header/2 existing); Budget.remaining/parse_integer (strict {int, ""}) and nonnegative_parse; CredentialHeadroom.integer_header (lenient); and GraphQLErrors.rate_limit_remaining (canonical, re-exported as Errors.rate_limit_remaining). A header like "5000 " parses in some and not others. Separately, AppToken.rate_limit_usable?/2 (through request_fun/Transport) and Config.valid_github_token?/2 (Req.get against a hard-coded URL, bypassing Transport, Budget and Quota attribution) are two implementations of "is this token usable". AppToken's doc says it "Mirrors the daemon's existing PAT posture (#678) exactly".
findings.recommendation: Create Aiur.GitHub.RateLimitHeaders.parse(response) -> %{limit, remaining, used, reset_at, resource} using Transport.header/2 with one integer policy, used by Budget, CredentialHeadroom, Quota, Config and GraphQLErrors. Delete Config.valid_github_token? and validate PAT candidates with AppToken.rate_limit_usable?/2 (renamed TokenProbe.usable?/2) through Transport.

findings.title: The rate-limit pool vocabulary is duplicated in 6 lists, and CredentialHeadroom still attributes unmodelled pools to the request's resource (the #2409 misattribution Budget fixed)
findings.description: The resource lists disagree: ["core","graphql","search"] in Budget (twice), ["core","graphql"] in CredentialHeadroom and CredentialUsage, ["graphql","core"] in BudgetMap, and ["core","graphql","search","none"] in EndpointPolicy. Budget.response_resource returns nil for a header naming a pool it does not model (integration_manifest, code_scanning_upload, ...) and skips the hold, per #2409. CredentialHeadroom.resource/2 instead falls back to Budget.request_resource(request) for any unrecognised header. A response from another pool on a /repos/... URL is therefore recorded as the credential's CORE window, and CredentialSelector will then bench that credential as :blocked on remaining == 0. Search windows are never recorded because "search" is not in its list.
findings.recommendation: Put the pool list and the header -> pool mapping in EndpointPolicy (pools/0, response_pool(headers, request) -> pool | :unmodelled) and have Budget, CredentialHeadroom, CredentialUsage and BudgetMap call it. CredentialHeadroom must skip :unmodelled, exactly like Budget.

findings.title: A configured app_installation credential aliases the one daemon App token under a second accounting identity; the docs claim it "mints its own"
findings.description: Credential.token/1 resolves every kind: :app_installation credential through AppTokenRefresher.current_token(), and there is only one refresher and one App (the GITHUB_APP_* env). With App auth configured, the legacy credential is already kind :app_installation using that token. Adding a tracker.github.credentials entry with kind app_installation yields a second pool member holding the SAME token but a different identity_key (the id is part of stable_identity). CredentialSelector then scores two budgets that are really one (an unobserved one gets the optimistic 5000). The broker keys admissions by --identity-key, so the per-actor hourly ceilings are split and effectively doubled. With the App not configured, such an entry silently resolves to nil and is dropped. The configuration reference and schema comment say the credential "mints its own" token, which is false.
findings.recommendation: Either reject kind: app_installation entries in the changeset until per-credential App config (app_id, installation_id, key path) and per-credential refreshers exist, or implement that properly. At minimum, dedupe pool members by resolved token_key and fix the docs row.

findings.title: The /github-cache page recomputes the whole budget map (SQLite, tsv reads, read-cache twice) and a full store projection on every ResourceStore change; the projection ceiling does not bound the work
findings.description: Each {:github_resource_changed, _} message makes the LiveView call load/1 in its own process: CacheInspector.project(), then BudgetMap.snapshot. The latter opens the broker's SQLite and runs 5 queries (two LEFT JOINs) with a 5s busy_timeout each, reads every agent-cache.tsv, and calls read_cache/1 twice (snapshot line 123 and caller_rows line 166). ResourceStore changes happen many times per poll cycle. CacheInspector's comment says @projection_ceiling exists because "building a struct for every one of them on every re-render would make an open inspector expensive", but project/1 builds an Entry for EVERY raw row (up to the store's 100,000), sorts them all, and only then takes the ceiling. Each Entry keeps raw_data (the cached body), so up to 5000 bodies sit in every viewer's socket assigns. CacheHistory repeats the full tab2list plus classification every 30s. by_family and by_consumer in BudgetLedger are derivable from rows, so 3 of the 5 queries are redundant.
findings.recommendation: Debounce store-change reloads (e.g. at most once per second per socket) and refresh the budget map only on the quota sampler tick. Build the projection from a cheap tuple view (key, sizes, timestamps) and load raw_data lazily for the one entry being displayed. Derive the family and consumer totals from a single GROUP BY query. Fix the comment, or bound the work with a selection before building structs.

findings.title: BudgetMap's static caller classification has drifted from the caller names Quota emits and is time-blind
findings.description: @free_by_nature keys the exact string "agent-shell:gh" as free by nature (pool :free, "costs no quota"). Since #2299, Quota names agent rows "agent-shell:gh <subcommand>" (e.g. "agent-shell:gh pr view"), so current rows fall through to :unclassified. Legacy rows that still match are wrong the other way: agent-requests.tsv rows are gh API calls that GitHub metered, and Quota bills them (cost: 1), yet the map labels them "costs no quota". @wasted_callers pins ci_poll_batch, comment_poll_batch and review_threads_unaddressed as :wasted from the #2265 measurement. Later changes (#2310 delivery displacement, #2355 thread-page cut, #2326 comment inversion, DeliveredPullRequest) changed those callers, but the verdict is declared "authoritative" and cannot move. This is a fixed, provenance-blind list of string literals with no link to the producers.
findings.recommendation: Classify by prefix for agent-shell rows and remove the :git/free label for them (they are metered). Make callers declare their reuse class where they declare caller: (e.g. a caller registry module used by Transport.put_caller and BudgetMap), or compute the verdict from live read-cache and ETag counters and treat the static list as a hint that expires. Add a test that every caller name in the classification is emitted somewhere.

findings.title: CacheInspector.ResourceStoreSource reads ResourceStore's private ETS table and entry map shape directly
findings.description: The source hard-codes Module.concat([ResourceStore, Table]), the store's private @table, and the internal field names (:data, :data_source, :source, :fetched_at_ms, :processed_at_ms, :recorded_at_ms, :data_version). Its moduledoc concedes that the store exposes no enumeration API. Any change to the store's representation silently breaks the inspector and the CacheHistory charts, with no compile-time link. Reading the table also copies every body into the reader process (see github-a-20).
findings.recommendation: Add ResourceStore.stream_entries/1 (or fold/3) that yields a documented projection struct (without bodies, plus body?/byte_size) and have the source call it. It remains an ETS read, so the "viewing never fetches" property holds.

findings.title: The GitHub API base URL is hard-coded in 11 places despite Transport.base_url/0
findings.description: Transport defines @base_url and exposes base_url/0, but other modules redeclare "https://api.github.com" or build full URLs from literals, including the App token exchange and both token probes. findings.title: Request boilerplate is copy-pasted in every domain module: 59 request_fun defaults, 48 parse_repo calls, 51 identical error-mapping arms
findings.description: Almost every GitHub call repeats the same preamble and tail: with {:ok, {owner, repo}} <- Transport.parse_repo(), {:ok, token} <- Transport.require_token(opts), request_fun = Keyword.get(opts, :request_fun, &Transport.default_request_fun/1), then {:ok, %{status: _} = response} -> {:error, Errors.github_status_error(response)}; {:error, reason} -> {:error, Errors.classify_error({:error, reason})}. Sites differ in whether they pass opts to require_token (comments.ex:14 and 128, dependencies_api.ex:65, 102 and 236, teams.ex:18 ignore opts[:token]) and whether they set caller: (DependenciesApi and Comments.create_comment do not, so their spend is unattributed in Quota and BudgetMap).
findings.recommendation: Add Transport.request(opts, method, path, extra) that resolves repo, token and request_fun, stamps caller: (required), and maps errors, returning {:ok, response} | {:error, classified}. Migrate modules incrementally, and make a missing caller a compile-time or test failure.

findings.title: Async tests mutate the process-global environment, and negative assertions rely on sleeps
findings.description: Three `async: true` suites call System.put_env/delete_env, and System env is VM-global. CredentialRegistry and Credential.token read it, so concurrent suites can see each other's tokens. Several negative tests use Process.sleep(50..120) and then refute. On a loaded CI runner the message may not have been processed yet, so the refute passes vacuously; a `:sys.get_state(pid)` barrier would make them deterministic. cycle_fetch_cache_test uses a bare assert_receive :fetch_started (100ms default) on a Task-driven message. See also github-a-03: BudgetMap's test injects glob_fun and 5-column rows, so it cannot reach the production defects.
findings.recommendation: Inject env via a :env_fun/:token_fun seam (or unique env names plus async: false), replace sleep-then-refute with :sys.get_state/1 synchronisation, and give assert_receive explicit timeouts where the message comes from another process.

findings.title: ResourceStore is a 2,191-line god module and the cross-package shared mutable state
findings.description: One module owns seven responsibilities: a closed registry of every consumer's resource types, an ETS compare-and-swap engine, the validator/body invariants, event-dedup 'processed marks' (an Events.Publisher concern), the retention sweep and body shedding, JSON checkpoint persistence and decoding, and a PubSub facade (defdelegates to ResourceEvents). Measured: 811 code lines, 512 comment lines, 656 doc lines (the moduledoc alone is 250 lines). The table is a public named ETS table written directly from callers' processes in at least five would-be packages (events, orchestrator, build_order, github read paths, github write-through). Any consumer adding a resource type must edit @resource_types in the store; the comments on that list name CommandScan, Build Order, DependenciesApi, CommentPollBatch and the Client lookup, so the store encodes other packages' vocabulary and cannot be carved without them.
findings.recommendation: Split into ResourceStore.Key (key/key_for_repo/normalize_id plus an open type registry that each package contributes to at compile time), ResourceStore.Table (lookup, update_cas, pace, swapped?, announce), ResourceStore.Entry (pure transitions: deposit, deposit_etag, apply_processed_mark, held_body, storable_data), ResourceStore.Retention (sweep, shed_bodies, expired_body_keys, reload_entry) and ResourceStore.Checkpoint (encode_*/decode_*/load/write). Move processed?/mark_processed to an events-owned ProcessedMarks module (Events.Publisher is the only production caller). Move the design narrative out of @moduledoc into a design doc and keep the module doc to the contract.

findings.title: Request classification (resource, direction, consumer, cost) is implemented in five places and the copies disagree
findings.description: Quota and RequestLog carry copies of request_resource, request_direction, request_consumer, ticket_number_from_url/variables, find_ticket_number, valid_ticket_number and request_cost, with a comment saying 'the two must agree'. They already disagree: for a transport error on core, Quota records {1, :reported} and RequestLog records {1, :assumed}. There are four definitions of 'this GraphQL document is a mutation': Quota and RequestLog use ~r/^\s*mutation\b/i (start of string only, case-insensitive), ReadCache.Identity uses ~r/(\A|\n)\s*mutation\b/ (any line start, case-sensitive), CredentialSelector uses ~r/(\A|[\s{])mutation[\s({]/, and GraphQLCost.query_root? strips comment trivia first. A document that starts with a '#' comment line and then 'mutation' is a read for attribution (Quota, RequestLog) but a write for cache invalidation (Identity) and for credential choice (CredentialSelector). 'Is this GraphQL' has two forms: URI path == "/graphql" (Quota, RequestLog, CredentialSelector) and a prefix match against a hard-coded base URL (Identity). Budget.request_resource is a fifth resource classifier via EndpointPolicy.
findings.recommendation: Extract Aiur.GitHub.RequestClass with resource/1, direction/1 (one mutation detector built on GraphQLCost's trivia stripping), consumer/1, cost/2 and graphql?/1. Compute it once in Transport and stamp the result on the request map, so Quota, RequestLog, ReadCache.Policy/Identity, CredentialSelector and Budget read the same fields.
findings.merge_reason: Request attribution and cost classification are subsets of the five-owner GitHub request-classification drift.

findings.title: The GitHub layer depends upward on Orchestrator, BuildOrder, Workspace, Webhooks, CodingAgent and AgentGitHubGuard
findings.description: Lower layers call higher ones. Transport identifies the Orchestrator process by registered name to pick its deadline. Quota sends :github_quota_recovered to Aiur.Orchestrator and derives workspace paths from Workspace.Layout and Config.workspace_root. Issues calls Orchestrator.DispatchPolicy (terminal_issue_state?/2, terminal_state_set/0, resolve_state_labels/1) and BuildOrder.Bounded. IssueRelationships uses BuildOrder.TicketDetail.DestinationNormalizer. ViewStateSweep hard-codes Aiur.BuildOrder.PackStatus as a source and calls its reseed_demand/demanded?/refresh. Labels builds its label set from CodingAgent, HostCommand depends on AgentGitHubGuard, and Policy depends on Webhooks.ModeTable. PullRequests and ReviewThreads call Codeowners. These become dependency cycles once github/ is its own package.
findings.recommendation: Invert each edge: carry the deadline class on the request (deadline: :interactive) instead of comparing pids; publish quota recovery on PubSub; inject terminal-state sets and the multi-label resolver into Issues (or move them into StatePolicy); have ViewStateSweep read its sources from config and a ViewStateSource behaviour; move label-set composition (Labels.label_set/2) to the init/CLI layer that knows the backends; pass the paths Quota needs through start_link; take the webhook transport mode as a function injected into Policy.

findings.title: REST boilerplate, status mapping and Link pagination are hand-written at every call site
findings.description: Each reader repeats the same lines to resolve repo, token and request_fun and to build the URL, then the same two error arms. Counts in the snapshot: `Keyword.get(opts, :request_fun, &Transport.default_request_fun/1)` appears 59 times in lib (17 in pull_requests.ex, 7 in issues.ex, 3 in issue_state.ex); `Transport.parse_repo()` 17 times in pull_requests.ex; `Errors.github_status_error(response)` 14/8/5 times and `Errors.classify_error({:error, reason})` 14/4/5 times in pull_requests/issues/issue_state. Link-header pagination is written as separate recursive functions: PullRequests fetch_open_ticket_pull_request (159-185), fetch_open_ticket_pull_requests (218-240), fetch_open_ticket_pull_request_pages (318-347), fetch_check_runs (412-429), fetch_all_open_pull_requests (487-501), fetch_labeled_open_pull_requests (898-913); Issues fetch_label_issue_pages (682-701) and fetch_conditional_page (582-608); Teams.fetch_member_logins (27-42); plus GraphQL cursor loops in ReviewThreads and IssueDependencies. findings.title: The repo-wide open-PR listing is revalidated once per ticket per cycle and paginated by five separate functions
findings.description: GET /repos/:o/:r/pulls?state=open&per_page=100 is built in five functions, each with its own paginator and filter. The per-cycle caller, Client.fetch_open_pull_request_for_branch, runs once per human-review target (up to 25 per cycle, per the PullRequests doc) and keys the conditional read by ticket number. So the same page-1 URL is revalidated N times per cycle under N different validators, and any change on page 1 (any PR update) turns all N into full 200 reads of up to 100 PRs each. HumanReviewGate reads the same listing unconditionally on every gate check, and fetch_open_pull_requests_for_branch (merged-ticket reconciler) paginates it to exhaustion per ticket.
findings.recommendation: Read the open-PR listing once per cycle into one per-repo entry (CycleFetchCache or a store key such as {:open_pull_requests, repo}) with a page-1 validator, and answer the per-ticket, per-label and all-PR questions as pure filters over that list. Keep one paginator.

findings.title: Issues keeps parallel conditional and unconditional pipelines for three fetch families
findings.description: fetch_candidate_issues, fetch_issues_by_states and fetch_issue_states_by_ids each exist in an unconditional and a conditional form (six entry points). The unconditional ones are live (AgentControlCli, DecisionStore, SessionLifecycle, IssueContext). The module has two pagination engines (fetch_label_issue_pages and fetch_conditional_page), three copies of the same ctx map (398-405, 532-539, 651-658), two implementations of '304 with no held body: retry once without the validator' (serve_not_modified_raw_issue 259-275 and materialize_not_modified_issue 825-860), and a private response_header/2 that duplicates Transport.header/2. Its 1,246 lines mix fetch, normalization (normalize_issue has 7 references in 4 other lib modules) and blocked-by hydration.
findings.recommendation: Keep only the conditional pipeline (an empty cache map is the unconditional case), build ctx once, share one 'conditional GET with a single retry' helper, and use Transport.header/2. Split into Issues.Fetch (listing and by-id), Issues.Normalize (normalize_issue, extract_state*, priority, label flags) and Issues.BlockedBy (hydrate_blocked_by, normalize_blockers).

findings.title: State-label parsing is spread over five modules and has already drifted on case and whitespace
findings.description: Issues.extract_state_labels/2 trims and down-cases both the label and the prefix before matching. IssueState.remove_state_labels/8 and remove_active_state_labels/7 filter with a case-sensitive String.starts_with?(&1, "#{prefix}:"), and StatePolicy.terminal_state_label?/2 uses a case-sensitive replace_prefix. A label that differs from the configured prefix only in case or surrounding whitespace is therefore counted as a state label by the reader but never removed by the writer, so a swap leaves two state labels. normalize_label_name/1 is defined twice (public in IssueState, private in Issues), paused_label?/2 and parked_label?/2 are two copies of one function, and the terminal list ["done", "cancelled", "canceled"] is duplicated in StatePolicy.terminal_state_name?/1 and IssueState.maybe_close_issue/4.
findings.recommendation: Create one Aiur.GitHub.LabelCodec owning normalize/1, state_suffix/2, marker?/1, paused?/2, parked?/2, state_labels/2 and terminal?/1. IssueState filters with LabelCodec.state_suffix/2 so reader and writer agree. maybe_close_issue/4 uses StatePolicy.terminal_state_name?/1.

findings.title: Test seams live in production paths, and production code has to defend against them
findings.description: Transport.require_token/1 returns the literal "test-gh-token" whenever opts contain :request_fun and no token, so a production caller that injects a request_fun without a token sends a fake bearer token. IssueState has a helper and a comment whose only job is to avoid that seam. findings.title: ViewStateSweep's divergence watermark drops every failed head read with no log or alert
findings.description: The head read is the only corroboration signal left for detecting lost 'issues' webhook deliveries; the moduledoc says that without it the projections 'would sit frozen reporting :available forever'. Any non-200 answer (401, 403, rate limit, 5xx), any {:error, _} including a local quota hold, and a missing token all fall into ':ok' branches with no log. Only raised exceptions are logged, with Logger.warning, which is not persisted without --debug. A credential that lacks permission therefore disables delivery-loss detection silently.
findings.recommendation: Count consecutive failures in state. After N ticks emit an Alerts.emit_system alert naming the status or classification, and a resolved alert on recovery. Expose the last successful head time for the dashboard.

findings.title: Quota latches with no exit: the anonymous-quota alert and hold file, and the request log after one write error
findings.description: (1) The 'core:anonymous' window is updated only by an anonymous response (Codeowners public reads); the /rate_limit refresh ingests only core and graphql. reconcile_resource_alerts/3 and sync_hold_file/3 run only when that resource's window is written. So a system.github.quota.core:anonymous.exhausted alert (needs_attention: true) and the core:anonymous-hold file stay after reset_at until another anonymous read happens. (2) log_request/4 sets request_log_io to nil on the first write error and nothing reopens it, so the durable request log stops for the life of the process with no log line. (3) write_hold_file/3 swallows every failure in a bare rescue, so the agents' gh guards never see a hold the daemon believes it wrote.
findings.recommendation: On every observe and refresh, evaluate each held window against the clock and clear alerts and hold files once reset_at has passed, whatever the resource. Retry open_writer on a timer and emit one alert when the log is disabled. Log and alert on hold-file write failure.

findings.title: The store's 'loud' refusals and write-through faults are Logger-only
findings.description: The ResourceStore docs repeatedly promise that dangerous states are 'loud': an unknown type, a refused body, an abandoned compare-and-swap write, a failed checkpoint, an entry that cannot be checkpointed. Every one is only Logger.error or Logger.warning, which is not persisted without --debug; there is no counter, metric or alert. WriteThrough swallows every exception at Logger.debug; that loses the processed mark which stops a webhook echo from waking an agent for its own write. ResourceEvents drops broadcast failures at Logger.debug.
findings.recommendation: Add a ResourceStore metrics table (refused_unknown_type, refused_body, cas_abandoned, checkpoint_failed, write_through_failed) shown by the existing CacheInspector and github-cost surfaces, and emit a system alert when a checkpoint fails or CAS abandonments exceed a rate.

findings.title: ResourceStore.with_table rescues ArgumentError around caller code, so a raising merge function silently drops the write
findings.description: with_table/2 wraps its whole callback in 'rescue ArgumentError -> default'. update_resource/3 and update_reply/3 run the caller-supplied merge function inside that callback. An ArgumentError raised by the caller's function (String.to_integer/1, String.to_existing_atom/1, :binary functions and so on) becomes the storeless default (:ok): the write is dropped with no log and looks like a successful deposit.
findings.recommendation: Narrow the rescue to the ETS calls only (lookup, select_replace, insert_new). Let exceptions from the caller's function propagate, or log them with the key and count them.

findings.title: ReadCache invalidation markers are max-merged non-atomically and can move backwards
findings.description: mark/2 does :ets.lookup and then :ets.insert. Two concurrent invalidations of one identity with stamps a < b can interleave so that b is written and then overwritten by a. The {:collections, owner, repo} identity is marked by every numbered write (write_identities/1) and every webhook delivery (invalidate_number/2), so concurrent marks of it are routine. After the regression, an entry whose fetch started between a and b is no longer retired and can be served for the rest of its TTL (1 h on webhook-backed repos). That is the write-after-invalidate race the module says its start stamp closes.
findings.recommendation: Make the max atomic: :ets.insert_new when the marker is absent, otherwise an :ets.select_replace loop guarded by {:<, :"$1", at_ms}.

findings.title: Two GitHub error taxonomies coexist, and the retry classifier recognises only one of them
findings.description: Transport code returns {:github, class, detail}. Labels.ensure/5 returns {:github_api_status, status, label} 3-tuples and {:github_api_request, reason}; Codeowners, Init.Github and GlobalConfigStartup (outside this unit) return {:github_api_status, status} 2-tuples. retryable_github_error?/1 matches only the 2-tuple, so a 502 or 429 during label creation is permanent. findings.title: Distinct failures are collapsed into specific, wrong causes
findings.description: IssueDependencies.post_dependency_error/1 maps every 422 to :cycle_detected, although GitHub also returns 422 for other validation failures. The REST BFS returns :rate_limited when its own 200-call cap is spent, the same atom used for GitHub rate limiting. HumanReviewGate.approved?/2 maps any failed reviews read (transport error, 5xx, local hold) to false, so the caller reports {:unverified_review_threads, ...} instead of the read error: the ticket is told to fix threads when the real cause is an unreadable review list. The gate also passes ({:ok, _pr} -> :ok) a PR body whose "number" is not an integer. AGENTS.md: collapse an unknown cause to a cause-neutral atom, never to a specific cause.
findings.recommendation: Return {:error, {:dependency_rejected, detail}} for a non-cycle 422 (inspect the message) and :cycle_check_budget_exhausted for the BFS cap. Have approved?/2 return {:error, reason} and propagate it from verify_pr_review_threads_clear/3. Treat a non-integer PR number as {:error, :invalid_pull_request}.

findings.title: Tracker dispatches through a runtime-configured client with function_exported? duck typing, guarded inconsistently
findings.description: Aiur.GitHub.Tracker delegates to Application.get_env(:aiur, :github_client_module, Client). Client (53 defs, 44 lines of the form 'do: Module.fun(...)') delegates again to Issues, PullRequests and the rest. Optional capabilities are probed with function_exported?/3 at five sites. Four call Code.ensure_loaded?/1 first, because (per the comment at 89-92) function_exported?/3 is false for a module not yet loaded in a release. auth_preflight/0 does not, and its fallthrough is 'true -> :ok'. Under the condition the module itself documents, the auth preflight is skipped silently.
findings.recommendation: Define an explicit Aiur.GitHub.ClientBehaviour with required callbacks and call through it; drop the fallbacks. Collapse Tracker -> Client -> domain into Tracker -> domain, or make Client the behaviour implementation and delete the pass-through layer.

findings.title: Issues' 304 handling follows a rationale the store has invalidated, and contradicts itself
findings.description: On a 304, Issues calls put_etag/2 and deliberately does not move fetched_at_ms, arguing that put_resource and update_resource 'both take the version as a fixed option'. The store now accepts a version function and offers revalidate/3, which ResourceFetch uses on the same 304 path to move the clock atomically. So the two readers of the :issue key follow opposite policies, and Issues pays an extra conditional request every freshness window. The comment at 834-836 in the same file says the opposite ('the shared entry's freshness clock has to move'). The comment at 284-291 says the store's change test includes :source, but observable/1 excludes it. The ResourceEvents moduledoc (line 48) also lists source as a publishing change.
findings.recommendation: Route Issues' 304 through ResourceStore.revalidate/3 (or ResourceFetch.need/3 with a freshness), delete retain_validator/2 and refresh_stored_issue/3 with the stale comments, and fix the ResourceEvents doc list.

findings.title: ResourceStore has two listing APIs with different expiry rules, and one documents the wrong shape
findings.description: list/3 returns raw ETS entries from match_object, including bodies past retention that fetch/1 and list_type/2 decline, and using internal field names (:version is the processed mark, not the body version). The one production caller of list/3 (BuildOrder CatalogStore) reads :data directly, so between sweeps it can build the graph from expired bodies.
findings.recommendation: Keep one list API that returns fetch-shaped, expiry-filtered entries; migrate CatalogStore; delete the other.

findings.title: ResourceStore checkpoints copy the whole table every 30 s and keep a second full copy in process state
findings.description: Each checkpoint runs :ets.tab2list/1 over up to 100,000 entries (bodies up to 256 KiB), re-checks every body with json_round_trips?/1, builds a map, deep-compares it with the previous document and keeps that whole map in last_written. The GenServer heap therefore holds a copy of every checkpointed body. shed_bodies/2 also tab2lists and sorts the full table. The checkpoint and sweep timers are rescheduled with the module constants, ignoring the :checkpoint_interval_ms and :sweep_interval_ms options that init uses.
findings.recommendation: Track dirtiness with a write counter bumped in update_cas and skip clean cycles; keep only a hash of the last document; stream-encode with :ets.foldl. Store the intervals from opts in state and reuse them.

findings.title: Quota filters its whole hour of observations on every observed request
findings.description: attribute_request/4 prepends the observation and immediately calls prune_observations/2, which runs Enum.filter with DateTime.compare over the whole list. findings.recommendation: Keep observations in a queue or in per-minute buckets keyed by resource, caller and consumer, drop from the old end on a timer, and store integer stamps instead of DateTime structs.

findings.title: ResourceStore.clear/3 is an unversioned whole-type delete that lets set reconciliation erase newer deliveries
findings.description: clear/3 match_deletes every entry of a type in a repo, with no time bound. Reconciliation fetches the catalog (multi-page GraphQL), then clears :sub_issue, then put_resource's each fetched edge unconditionally. A sub_issue_removed tombstone deposited by the webhook during the fetch is deleted by the clear, and the older fetched edge is re-deposited as present: true; an add delivered during the fetch is wiped. Separately, reconciliation deposits with source: :reconciliation, which known_source_atom/1 does not decode, so the body's source is lost after a restart.
findings.recommendation: Replace clear/3 with clear_older_than(type, owner, repo, cutoff_ms) (select_delete on recorded_at_ms) and pass the reconciliation's fetch start time. Deposit through the guarded primitive from github-b-02. Derive the known sources from one attribute that includes :reconciliation.

findings.title: Aiur.DecisionStore is a 4,826-line god module on the Decision hot path
findings.description: One GenServer module owns at least ten separate responsibilities: (1) the public API and call serialization (lines 131-523), (2) boot, replay, corruption and projection repair (524-765), (3) Executor escalation (766-852), (4) request intake, legacy-attention projection/enrichment and creation-time fuzzy dedup (1583-1738, 2047-2475), (5) answer/revise/supersede/moot/dismiss/defer/expire command handling (1158-2045), (6) the transport delivery gate, handoff marks and queue settlement (2655-3164), (7) delivery-failure alert projection (3166-3454), (8) dispatch scheduling, fences, retry ladders and the DecisionDispatchTasks monitor (3456-4600), (9) Executor notification fan-out (4603-4665), and (10) audit read models and the recent-decision gb_sets index (4667-4826). Every mutation, every read and every background settlement goes through this one process, so a change in any area (for example the #2711 withdraw rules or the #2717 orphan adoption) edits the same file and risks the others.
findings.recommendation: Keep one serialized writer, but split the module by responsibility: Aiur.Decisions.Store (GenServer shell: API, handle_* dispatch, state struct), Aiur.Decisions.Boot (replay/repair/corruption), Aiur.Decisions.Commands (answer/revise/supersede/moot/dismiss/defer/expire as pure `state -> {reply, state}` functions), Aiur.Decisions.Intake (request, attention projection, creation dedup), Aiur.Decisions.DeliveryGate (validate_delivery/handoff/transport transitions), Aiur.Decisions.DispatchScheduler (fences, retry ladders, monitor), Aiur.Decisions.Alerts (every Alerts.emit_custom and topic builder), Aiur.Decisions.ReadModel (audit windows, gb_sets index). Replace the ad hoc state map with a %State{} struct so the 30+ keys are declared once.

findings.title: Every Decision mutation rewrites the whole decisions.json; the audit log and in-memory history grow without bound
findings.description: repair_projection serializes the entire `current` map, fsyncs a temp file, renames it and chmods it, all inside the single serialized writer, for every accepted event (answer, handoff, delivered, consumed, failed, ...). The cost grows with the total number of Decisions ever retained. There is no retention or compaction: decisions.ndjson is only appended to, boot replays it by reading the whole file into memory (File.read), and the store keeps `history` and `audit_history` for every Decision forever. The store has no bound on its memory or its per-event write cost.
findings.recommendation: Write the projection on a debounce (coalesce bursts, write at most every N ms) or only at checkpoints, since the ndjson is authoritative. Add a retention policy: snapshot plus truncate for terminal Decisions older than a horizon, and stream replay line by line. Keep only the bounded windows the read APIs actually use in memory, and serve full audit history from disk on demand.

findings.title: Pending-answer redelivery (#2713) is silently dropped when the dispatch-task coordinator is momentarily down
findings.description: schedule_pending_answer_delivery logs "Redelivering Decision answer to the new worker", resets the retry count, then calls maybe_start_dispatch directly. maybe_start_dispatch's `with` returns the state unchanged when `decision_dispatch_monitor_live?` is false, so while DecisionDispatchTasks is restarting the redelivery does nothing: no reschedule, no alert, and a log line that says the opposite happened. Every other dispatch entry point goes through with_decision_dispatch_monitor, which reschedules the message after @decision_dispatch_monitor_retry_ms. This is the silent-refusal family on the exact path #2713 added to stop answers from being stranded.
findings.recommendation: Schedule the redelivery as a `{:dispatch_action, fence, true}` message via schedule_dispatch/4, so it gets the same monitor-retry wrapper as every other dispatch. Log after admission, not before. More generally, make maybe_start_dispatch return a reason for every refusal and log or alert the non-fence ones.

findings.title: Queue-settlement facts are dropped with a warning or with no log at all
findings.description: record_transport_batch_async is the Orchestrator's only way to report restored/consumed/failed queue settlements. In the batch path, a settlement whose attempt is missing or whose correlation is rejected is dropped with only Logger.warning. When the store is read-only, the `:transport_transitions` and `:deliver_pending_answers` casts are dropped with no log at all. The cast wrapper also swallows `:exit` to `:ok`. A `:failed` settlement that is dropped leaves the attempt `:queued`, so the failure alert and the transient retry ladder never fire for it.
findings.recommendation: Count dropped settlements in store state and expose the count in health. Emit one deduplicated needs-attention alert per decision/action when a `:failed` or `:consumed` settlement cannot be recorded. While read-only, buffer settlements in a bounded queue and replay them when the store becomes writable, instead of discarding them.

findings.title: Notify-after-persist has four different failure policies inside one module
findings.description: After a durable append, notification is a side effect with inconsistent handling. (a) A request's Exchange publish failure is Logger.warning with no retry, but its Executor notification retries on a 3-step ladder and then gives up with only Logger.warning (no alert; recovery happens only at the next boot reconcile). (b) A lifecycle Exchange publish, a deferred-Executor notification and an escalation resolution each fail with Logger.warning and no retry. (c) Lifecycle and enrichment notifications are skipped entirely when the projection write failed (loose-1-03). #2558 established that an exhausted delivery ladder must raise an alert. The Executor-notification ladder does not follow that rule.
findings.recommendation: Introduce one outbox for post-commit side effects: each durable event records the notifications it owes, a single retry scheduler drains the outbox, and exhaustion raises one deduplicated alert. That removes the four ad hoc paths and makes publication at-least-once for every event type.

findings.title: 16 copy-pasted read-only guard clauses, with two different error shapes for the same condition
findings.description: Every mutating operation has its own `%{writable?: false}` handle_call clause that returns `{:error, {:store_unavailable, state.health}}`, and three casts have their own no-op clause. The client wrappers for validate_delivery, record_delivery, blocked_ticket_ids and open_blocking_decision_ids catch exits and return a bare `{:error, :store_unavailable}`. Callers have to match both shapes, and every new operation needs a new guard clause (forgetting one would let a mutation through while read-only).
findings.recommendation: Tag mutating messages as `{:mutate, op, args}` (or keep a module attribute list of mutating ops) and guard once: `def handle_call({:mutate, _, _}, _, %{writable?: false} = s)`. Pick a single error shape (`{:error, {:store_unavailable, health}}`) and make the exit-catching wrappers return it too.

findings.title: Three hand-written copies of 'apply an accepted event to the in-memory indexes' have drifted
findings.description: persist_enrichment, persist_and_notify and build_and_append_event each rebuild current/decision_index/retained_index/audit_history/recent_audit by hand. They already differ: `history` is updated by two of the three (build_and_append_event skips it), and notification gating differs (see loose-1-03). audit_history appends with `&1 ++ [event]`, which is O(n) per event, while the boot comment claims histories are kept newest-first "so every accepted append is O(1)". accept/2 calls IdGenerator.reserve_durable_id() directly and bypasses the injected state.event_id_reserver seam that the other two paths use, so a test cannot inject a non-durable ID for requests.
findings.recommendation: Extract `apply_event(state, prior, updated, event, opts)` as the single function that updates every index, and `reserve_event_id(state)` as the single reservation path. Store audit_history newest-first (or as :queue) and reverse on read, as `history` already does.

findings.title: An event-ID reservation exit crashes the single Decision writer instead of rejecting the request
findings.description: The moduledoc says a request is "rejected outright ... if ... the durable ID reservation itself fails". The reservers are GenServer.call to IdGenerator with the default 5 s timeout and no catch. A slow or restarting IdGenerator therefore exits the DecisionStore process, whether the call came from a client request or from a background settlement in handle_info. The in-memory dispatch bookkeeping (dispatching, retry_counts, lifecycle_append_failures) is lost with the process, and any in-flight callers get exits.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the reserver in a `safe_reserve/1` that catches :exit and returns {:error, :event_id_unavailable}, and map it to a rejection or background retry like the other append failures.

findings.title: DecisionStore depends upward on Tracker, Orchestrator policy, Executor journal and Alerts, which blocks a clean decisions package
findings.description: Of its 28 aliases, 12 are outside the Decision domain. They include Aiur.Tracker (the default terminal-ticket resolver does a live tracker batch read), Aiur.Orchestrator.DispatchPolicy (terminal-state policy), Aiur.ExecutorEvents and Aiur.ExecutorCommandAttention (Executor journal and alert markers), Aiur.Alerts, Aiur.Events.Publisher/IdGenerator, Aiur.Boot, Aiur.Config.Paths and JsonStore. Some are injected via opts (configure_dispatch). Others are called directly (Tracker/DispatchPolicy in default_terminal_ticket_resolver, ExecutorEvents.publish_deferred, ExecutorCommandAttention.resolve, Alerts.emit_custom x13, Publisher.publish_persisted). As a result the decisions core cannot be compiled or tested without the orchestrator, tracker and executor layers.
findings.recommendation: Define ports owned by the decisions package: TerminalTicketResolver, Notifier (Exchange + PubSub + Executor journal), AlertSink and IdSource. Make DecisionStore depend only on those behaviours and inject the implementations from the application supervisor. Move the terminal_identities/1 helper (3263-3283) to the adapter side.

findings.title: Decision attention topic grammar is built in 4 places and classified by string prefix in 3 others
findings.description: Whether a legacy attention counts as an operator Command (and therefore gates dispatch) is decided by `String.starts_with?(slug, ["decision-delivery-", "decision-lifecycle-persistence-"])`, copied three times (DecisionStore.open_blocking_command?, RetainedIndex.operator_command?, AlertFeed.internal_decision_alert?). The strings are produced by separate builders in DecisionStore (two), QueueDrain ("decision-delivery-correlation-", which matches the prefix only by accident), DecisionAttentionSignals (three kinds, sha256-16 digest) and ExecutorCommandAttention (another sha256-16 digest copy). Adding a new internal alert kind, or renaming one, silently changes dispatch gating.
findings.recommendation: Create Aiur.Decisions.AttentionTopics with one builder per kind and a single `internal?/1` classifier (or better, carry an explicit `internal: true` field on the alert instead of parsing the slug). Replace the three prefix checks and the two local digest helpers with calls to it.

findings.title: DecisionApi reports every exception, exit and unexpected reply as :store_unavailable
findings.description: safe_store_call turns any raise inside DecisionStore client code (a FunctionClauseError from a guard, for example) and any exit (noproc, the 60 s timeout, a store crash) into the atom :store_unavailable. Each write_* then also maps any unexpected reply shape to {:error, :store_unavailable}. AGENTS.md ("A collapsed cause names the collapse at the source") forbids collapsing heterogeneous causes into a specific one. Here a programming error and a timeout (where the answer may actually have been accepted) are both reported to the supervising agent as "store unavailable". The module also has three near-identical write_* functions and three trusted_*_actor functions that differ only in the error tag.
findings.recommendation: Return {:error, {:store_call_failed, :exception | :timeout | :noproc | :unexpected_reply}} and preserve the reason in a `reasons` field. Map a timeout to an explicit "outcome unknown, retry with the same idempotency key" reply. Collapse the three write_* functions into one with a result validator, and the three actor checks into `trusted_actor(opts, error_tag)`.

findings.title: unsafe_control_chars? has 9 copies with 2 different definitions
findings.description: Two incompatible rules are used for the same check. DecisionApi, Config.Schema.Decisions and DecisionQuery.Params reject every C0 control plus DEL (0x7F), including newline and tab. DecisionAnswer, DecisionEvent, DecisionRevision, DecisionValidation, DecisionDelegation and RecentMerge allow \n \t \r and allow DEL. As a result an identity field (for example an action_id checked by DecisionRevision.bounded_identity) accepts newlines and DEL, while the API layer rejects the same characters in a decision_id.

findings.title: CoordinationTasks and DecisionDispatchTasks are two implementations of the same keyed FIFO lane scheduler
findings.description: Both are GenServers that admit work per key with global and per-key pending bounds (per-key default = max_pending - 1 in both), keep a runnable-key queue plus MapSet for fairness, run one task per key under Aiur.TaskSupervisor, enforce per-task timeouts, and look up active tasks by linear scan on ref. They have drifted apart. CoordinationTasks retries task-start failures with exponential backoff and supports synchronous `run/5`. DecisionDispatchTasks fails the job on start failure, monitors owners and purges their work, and emits saturation alerts. CoordinationTasks hardcodes Aiur.TaskSupervisor for termination even when task_starter is injected (line 162).
findings.recommendation: Extract one Aiur.KeyedLanes library (admission, fairness, timeouts, owner monitoring, saturation hook, start-failure policy as options) and make both modules thin configurations of it.

findings.title: CODEOWNERS team membership is cached in the process dictionary forever, so a removed team member stays authoritative
findings.description: team_members/3 memoizes `@org/team` expansion with Process.put and has no TTL and no invalidation. The cache lives as long as the calling process: the agent runner (via Tracker.fetch_classified_issue_comments -> Comments -> Codeowners.repo_ownership), or any long-lived poller that classifies review threads. A user removed from a CODEOWNERS team keeps being classified `authoritative: true`, so their comments stay trusted instructions to the agent for the rest of that process's life. Additions are not seen either (the fail-closed direction). The process dictionary also grows with every team looked up.
findings.recommendation: Move team expansion into a shared cache with a short TTL (minutes). The existing GitHub ReadCache/Teams module is the natural owner, since the comment at 428-432 already calls this "a second, unpaginated copy of Teams.fetch_team_members/3". Never cache authority data in the process dictionary.

findings.title: Codeowners has two unpaginated copies of GitHub reads; PRs with more than 100 files or teams with more than 100 members are truncated
findings.description: fetch_team_members and fetch_pr_changed_paths are documented (#2298 item 7) copies of Teams.fetch_team_members/3 and PullRequests.fetch_pull_request_changed_paths/2, kept because the error contract differs. Both request `per_page=100` and never follow Link pagination. For a PR touching more than 100 files, owners are computed only from the first 100 paths. For a team with more than 100 members, later members are not trusted. The module also hardcodes `@base_url "https://api.github.com"` instead of Transport.base_url().
findings.recommendation: Call the canonical paginated readers and adapt their error shape in a 5-line wrapper (map 429 -> :quota_hold, status -> {:github_api_status, s}). Delete the private copies.

findings.title: Codeowners' default request function drops the :caller tag, so its GitHub spend is never attributed
findings.description: fetch_team_members and fetch_pr_changed_paths pass `caller: "codeowners_team_members"` / `"codeowners_pr_files"`, and the comments say they "now declare [their] caller so the read is attributed". But default_request_fun pattern-matches only method/url/token and builds a new map without :caller before calling Transport.default_request_fun. Quota attributes observations with GraphQLCost.derive(request), which uses request.caller when present and otherwise falls back to a route shape. In production these two call sites are therefore reported under anonymous route shapes, and the attribution the comment claims is inert.
findings.recommendation: Pass the incoming request map through (`Map.put_new(req, :anonymous, true)` when the token is blank) instead of rebuilding it. Add a test that asserts the request reaching Transport carries :caller. This one should also fail with the production hunk reverted, per AGENTS.md.

findings.title: The tmux event-subscription path is dead: nothing sends tmux_event, so PaneManager's pane_died handler is unreachable
findings.description: The moduledoc says control mode (`tmux -CC`) was abandoned for shell-outs. The subscription API was kept: Tmux.subscribe_events/1 monitors and stores subscribers, but no code anywhere in lib sends `{:tmux_event, ...}`. PaneManager subscribes at init and has a detailed `{:tmux_event, {:notification, :pane_died, pane_id}}` handler (with Perf events and logging) that can never run. Aiur.Tmux.Protocol, a 183-line control-mode parser, has no caller in lib. A reader of PaneManager would believe externally killed panes are detected by notification, when in practice only list_panes polling catches them.
findings.recommendation: Delete subscribe_events/1, the subscribers set, the DOWN handler, Aiur.Tmux.Protocol and PaneManager's tmux_event handlers. If pane-death detection is wanted, implement it explicitly (for example tmux `set-hook pane-died` running a CLI callback) and test it end to end.

findings.title: Every tmux operation for every agent runs through one GenServer with unbounded System.cmd calls
findings.description: Aiur.Tmux is a singleton GenServer whose state is only {transport, session, dead subscribers}. Every call (capture_pane for REPL readiness, paste_text, send_keys, split/move/kill) runs System.cmd("tmux", ...) inside handle_call, and that System.cmd has no timeout. One wedged tmux invocation blocks the process for every agent. Callers time out at 5-10 s and receive {:error, :timeout}, while the GenServer keeps working through a growing backlog. Serialization is not needed for correctness, because the tmux server serializes commands itself. Each of the 23 public functions also repeats the same catch block (26 copies of `:exit, {:noproc, _} -> {:error, :no_tmux}`).
findings.recommendation: Make the tmux API plain functions over a config stored at init (socket, session, transport) and execute through a bounded runner (Port with kill-on-timeout, or Task with yield/shutdown), so concurrent agents do not queue behind each other. Keep a GenServer only if ordering between specific pane operations must be guaranteed, and then per pane. Collapse the catch boilerplate into one `safe_call/3`.

findings.title: PauseContainment.paused? is a synchronous singleton call on every Codex turn method and fails open
findings.description: The Codex turn loop passes `pause_latched?(session, state)` as an eager argument to Approvals.maybe_handle_approval_request for every turn method. That is a GenServer.call into the PauseContainment singleton (1 s timeout) per streamed method, across all agents. call/2 turns any exit into :ignored, so paused?/2 returns false (`:ignored == true`) when the containment server is slow or restarting, which is fail-open for a pause latch. The same :ignored leaks out of arm/confirm/release/unregister, whose specs promise {:ok, handle} | :not_registered or :ok. The Orchestrator calls arm/1 synchronously from inside its own process and ignores the result.
findings.recommendation: Publish the latch state in an ETS table (or :atomics per registered generation) written by PauseContainment and read lock-free by the turn loop. Evaluate it lazily only when an approval decision needs it. Treat "containment unknown" as latched (fail closed) or at least report it distinctly, and make the API return its declared types (for example {:error, :containment_unavailable}).

findings.title: Storage primitives are misnamed and bypassed: DecisionLog is a generic durable log, and 16 writers hand-roll their own atomic writes
findings.description: Aiur.DecisionLog (fsync'd append, torn-tail repair, validating replay) is the codebase's only crash-safe NDJSON primitive, and EventPublicationLog, ExecutorEvents and ExecutorWakeInbox use it under a "Decision" name. EventPublicationLog and ExecutorEvents also call DecisionLog.prepare/3 on every append, although the doc says prepare is a one-time setup step kept off the hot path. Aiur.Fs.atomic_write is the shared temp+rename primitive, but at least 16 sites implement temp+rename themselves with different semantics (no fsync, no temp cleanup on failure, a fixed `.tmp` name that races). JsonStore's doc says it writes to `path <> ".tmp"` (actually `.tmp.<unique>`) and lists only two users.
findings.recommendation: Create a small storage package: Aiur.Storage.DurableLog (renamed DecisionLog), Aiur.Storage.AtomicFile (Fs.atomic_write plus mkdir and mode options) and Aiur.Storage.JsonFile (JsonStore). Migrate the 16 hand-rolled writers, and document which ones intentionally skip fsync. Call prepare once at owner init.

findings.title: PollCadence is a :persistent_term global registry shared by the Orchestrator, web, CLI and Stream Deck; an explicit option is ignored for on-demand classes
findings.description: The Orchestrator writes the per-class effective interval into :persistent_term, and every reader derives staleness from it. That is shared mutable state across what will become separate packages, and each change of value triggers a global GC scan on write. The fleet flips between idle and busy widening often, so the value does change. effective_interval_ms/1 documents precedence "1. an explicit :effective_interval_ms option", but when the published class value is 0 it returns 0 before looking at the option. forget_effective_interval_ms/0 erases the bare @effective_key, which nothing writes (dead line).
findings.recommendation: Move the published cadence behind a small owner process (or the Orchestrator snapshot) with a read API. If persistent_term is kept for read speed, keep it private to one module and document the write frequency. Honour the explicit option first, and delete the dead erase.

findings.title: Persisted content hashes are computed from Erlang external term format of Elixir maps/structs, so an OTP upgrade or a new struct field invalidates every stored record
findings.description: RecentMerge.with_content_hash hashes `Map.from_struct(merge) |> :erlang.term_to_binary([:deterministic])`; DecisionValidation.content_hash does the same for Decision/Answer content. decode_record/from_json_safe recompute and compare to the persisted hash, and a mismatch is treated as corruption. OTP documents `deterministic` as stable only within one release, and Map.from_struct includes every struct field, so adding a field to RecentMerge (or any hashed map) changes every hash. The result is RecentMergeStore going permanently read-only at boot (apply_corruption sets writable?: false and alerts), and Decision answers/revisions/events failing to decode, with no automatic exit short of an operator deleting data.
findings.recommendation: Introduce one Aiur.CanonicalHash that hashes a canonical JSON encoding (sorted keys, explicit field list taken from the to_record/to_json_safe shape, schema_version included). Migrate verifiers to accept the legacy hash once and rewrite. Never hash Map.from_struct of an evolving struct.

findings.title: SupervisionHealth commits the new `missing` set before alert delivery, so a failed degraded/resolved alert is never retried
findings.description: evaluate/1 computes `changed?`, stores `missing` into state, then calls notify/3, which rescues any delivery failure into a Logger.warning. The next check sees `missing == state.missing` and never re-emits, so a supervision degradation whose alert write failed stays invisible in the alert feed for as long as the degradation lasts.
findings.recommendation: Track `last_notified_missing` separately and update it only when notify succeeds; retry on the next tick otherwise.

findings.title: Process liveness probes are duplicated with opposite failure semantics; BuildGate deletes slots when its probe fails
findings.description: ProcessIdentity.alive? returns true when the probe raises because `A probe failure is not evidence that a process is gone`. BuildGate.owner_alive?/process_group_alive? return false when `sh` is missing or System.cmd raises, and active_count then `File.rm_rf(slot_path)` on the pid strategy, reaping a possibly-live lease. All copies use `kill -0`, which also reports EPERM (process owned by another user) as dead. Five more ad-hoc `kill -0` shell-outs exist in Claude/opencode code.
findings.recommendation: Give ProcessIdentity a tri-state `probe(pid | {:group, pgid}) :: :alive | :gone | :unknown` backed by /proc (falling back to `kill -0` that distinguishes ESRCH from EPERM) and make every destructive caller treat :unknown as alive.

findings.title: `aiur watch --changes` keeps one node-global baseline, so concurrent watchers (supported multi-Executor setups) consume each other's deltas
findings.description: The watch baseline is a single persistent_term key shared by every caller on the node. Multiple Executors are documented as `a supported configuration, not a fault`; when two consumers (or an Executor and a human) run `watch --changes`, whichever runs first advances the baseline and the other sees `(no changes)` for rows that did change. persistent_term.put also triggers a global scan of all processes on each update.
findings.recommendation: Key the baseline by consumer id (Claims.resolve_consumer_id/1 already exists) in an ETS table owned by a long-lived process, or return an opaque cursor the caller passes back.

findings.title: Many control-RPC entrypoints bypass `guarded/2`, reintroducing the empty-output crash mode it was added to prevent
findings.description: guarded/2 exists because an unexpected raise/exit inside a command `used to kill the RPC evaluator outright, and the operator saw a non-zero exit with an empty buffer` (#1684). units/1, executor_emit/2, executor_subscribe/1, executor_unsubscribe/1, executor_subscriptions/0, executor_wait/1, executor_fast_forward/2, executor_roster/1, executor_claim/1, executor_release/1 and executor_revoke/2 are not wrapped, so any raise (e.g. Roster.build, JsonStore.write! inside a rescue-less path, Claims errors) produces no exit marker.
findings.recommendation: Dispatch every public command through a single `run(command, fun)` that applies guarded/2 and exit_marker/1, so a new command cannot forget it.

findings.title: Credential and provider env-var name lists are duplicated outside Env.Schema (including the bash launcher)
findings.description: Env.Schema already tags variables with groups (:github_app, :provider_keys), yet env.ex hard-codes the GitHub credential group and provider key names, AgentEnvironment keeps its own provider/App/GitHub token lists, and the launcher keeps GITHUB_CREDENTIAL_ENV_NAMES. findings.recommendation: Expose Schema.names_in_group/1 and derive all Elixir lists from it; generate the launcher constant (or test that it equals the schema group).
