findings.title: PromptBuilder mojibakes the whole prompt when any byte is invalid; four divergent UTF-8 repair strategies exist
findings.description: ensure_utf8/1 reinterprets the entire rendered prompt as latin1 if it is not valid UTF-8, which double-encodes every valid multibyte character (em dashes and arrows in the shared instructions and operator template) instead of repairing the bad bytes. AgentEventFeed drops invalid bytes, Events.Sanitizer re-encodes as latin1 then falls back to replace_invalid, and TicketDetailSanitizer uses String.replace_invalid.
findings.recommendation: Add Aiur.Text.scrub_utf8/1 = String.replace_invalid/2 (replacement char) and use it in all four places.

findings.title: The Tracker behaviour mixes issue-tracker and code-host (PR) concerns; its conditional fallback is duplicated and the CLI bypasses it
findings.description: Tracker callbacks include fetch_open_pull_request(s)_for_branch, fetch_classified_pr_review_comments and fetch_unaddressed_pr_review_thread_comments; Linear and memory adapters stub them to `{:ok, nil}`/`{:ok, []}`, so a Linear-tracked repo hosted on GitHub silently never sees its PRs. The `function_exported?(..., :fetch_issue_states_by_ids_conditional, 2)` fallback is implemented both in Aiur.Tracker and again in Aiur.GitHub.Tracker. AgentControlCLI.todo calls Aiur.GitHub.Tracker directly and refuses non-GitHub trackers rather than going through the behaviour.
findings.recommendation: Split into Aiur.Tracker (issues, labels, states, comments) and Aiur.CodeHost (branches, PRs, reviews); keep the conditional fallback in one layer; make `--todo` use Tracker.add_label/remove_label.

findings.title: Tests for this unit are serial, global-state-driven and sleep-timed
findings.description: agent_control_cli_test.exs (4,052 lines) has 75 Application.put_env calls and no async; ordering depends on Process.sleep (e.g. sleeping 30ms before enqueueing a wake against a 300ms executor_wait timeout, which can race on a loaded CI runner). build_gate_test.exs (3,231 lines) uses real bash/python holders with wall-clock sleeps of 1.5s and 2s to assert idle windows. Neither file runs async, so both add directly to suite wall time.
findings.recommendation: After the Deps refactor (loose-2-18), make CLI tests async with injected deps; synchronize on explicit signals (e.g. a claim-acquired message) instead of sleeps; keep a small tagged set of real-process build-gate tests and unit-test the rest against a fake scanner.

findings.title: Core (non-web) modules depend on AiurWeb: AnalyticsCLI builds on the OCC web presenter, and Alerts/RecentMergeStore broadcast through AiurWeb.ObservabilityPubSub
findings.description: The `aiur analytics` CLI path loads its model through AiurWeb.OperatorControlCenter.Analytics.Presenter, ScopeResolver and Charts. The alert pipeline and the merge store call AiurWeb.ObservabilityPubSub.broadcast_update/0 directly. The dependency points from core to web, so aiur_web cannot be carved into its own package, or made optional for headless/CLI builds, without first moving these pieces.
findings.recommendation: Move the analytics data model (Presenter.load, ScopeResolver, time-domain windowing) into core as Aiur.Analytics, and keep only HTML/chart rendering in AiurWeb. Put a core Aiur.ObservabilityEvents module (topic constant plus broadcast_update/0) in place, have AiurWeb.ObservabilityPubSub subscribe to or delegate to it, and point Alerts and RecentMergeStore at the core module.

findings.title: Decisions and Orchestrator depend on each other: DecisionDispatch/DecisionRevisionDispatch call Orchestrator.OperatorMessages, which calls back into DecisionStore

findings.title: RepoBase (1,539 lines) is a god module: per-repo state-path layout used by 18 modules, the prewarm GenServer, legacy-layout migration with an SQLite lease, findings/asks ledger transfer, and git auth
findings.description: The module mixes five responsibilities that change for different reasons. (1) Pure path functions (repo_path, builds_path, findings_path, asks_path, handoff_path, executor_path, ...) are the dependency most callers need. (2) The prewarm GenServer (status/refresh_for_dispatch/probe/watchdog). (3) One-shot migration of the legacy layout (rename-parking, SQLite exclusive-transaction lease, recovery). (4) Exactly-once NDJSON ledger transfer with checksum markers, specialised for findings and asks. (5) git auth env construction. Eighteen modules outside it call RepoBase, almost all for paths, so any package that needs a state path would drag in the GenServer, Exqlite and the migration code.
findings.recommendation: Split it into: Aiur.RepoState.Paths (pure, no deps), Aiur.RepoState.Tree (ensure_state_tree + path-safety checks), Aiur.RepoState.LegacyMigration (deletable once no pre-migration nodes remain; it needs a removal criterion), Aiur.RepoState.LedgerTransfer (generic over a ledger-schema behaviour), Aiur.Prewarm.Base (GenServer + build worker) and Aiur.Git.AuthEnv.

findings.title: Alerts.emit_alert does heavy synchronous IO in the caller: it re-reads and parses the alerts YAML and re-sorts patterns on every emit, then fans out to five durable sinks
findings.description: Each emit runs the following in the calling process: definition_for_topic → definitions() → alerts_path() (Config.alerts_settings + File.exists?) → Aiur.Yaml.read_from_file → normalize → sort_by specificity; alert_settings() a second time; for `.resolved` topics, AlertFeed.duplicate_resolution?, which reads and sorts the whole ledger; Publisher.publish (IdGenerator call, Exchange, and the IssueLog synchronous call from finding 04); AgentEventLog.write under a workspace lock; AlertLedger.append (possibly the compaction from finding 02); the central alerts.ndjson append; sound playback; and two PubSub broadcasts. There are 63 emit_system/emit_custom call sites, and several run inside GenServer callbacks: Orchestrator.handle_info({:emit_system_alert, ...}), WorkflowStore's reload commit, and RecentMergeStore.
findings.recommendation: Cache the parsed and sorted definitions in :persistent_term keyed by {path, mtime}, or refresh them on WorkflowStore's configuration broadcast. Keep only the metadata/message computation in the caller and cast the durable fan-out to an Alerts.Dispatcher process (or a small pool), with the ledger write done by its single writer.

findings.title: IssueLog and AgentEventLog each re-implement json_safe instead of using Aiur.JSONSafe.normalize; the copies have drifted and both raise on structs, so records are dropped
findings.description: Aiur.JSONSafe.normalize/1 already handles DateTime, structs (Map.from_struct), tuples, atoms and nil/booleans. AgentEventLog added its own tuple clause after #708. IssueLog's copy has no tuple clause, so a tuple in a transcript payload reaches Jason.encode! and raises. Both copies match structs with `%{} = value` and call Map.new/2 on them; a struct is not Enumerable, so that raises too. IssueLog's failure path rescues, reopens and retries (which fails the same way) and logs a warning, losing the transcript record. AgentEventLog rescues and logs at debug, losing the agent.ndjson line that the moduledoc says must never be dropped.
findings.recommendation: Delete both private copies and call Aiur.JSONSafe.normalize/1. If IssueLog needs string keys, JSONSafe already stringifies atom keys. Add a regression test with a struct and a tuple in the payload for each writer.

findings.title: Per-workspace and per-issue log write failures are invisible: AgentEventLog logs at debug, IssueLog.write_line rescues with no log at all, and the central alert feed logs at debug
findings.description: agent.ndjson is documented as the only structured per-event record and the crash-reason sink (#708), yet mkdir/write/encode failures go to Logger.debug. The .log and .events.log writes in IssueLog swallow every exception with `_ -> :ok` and no log line. Without --debug, debug output never reaches a file (and there are no handlers at all), so a full disk or a revoked directory permission produces no signal while evidence stops being written.
findings.recommendation: Track per-sink write-failure counters in a small health registry, emit one rate-limited `system.logging.write_failed` alert, and use Logger.warning at minimum. Treat the transcript and event-log sinks with the same reopen-and-retry policy.

findings.title: Decision text validators are copy-pasted across ~10 modules with three different semantics (control characters, slug regex, JWT regex, bounded-string trim/redact)
findings.description: unsafe_control_chars?/1 exists in 10 modules. Seven reject codepoints below 0x20 except newline, tab and carriage return. decision_api.ex and config/schema/decisions.ex reject every codepoint below 0x20 plus DEL (0x7F). decision_query/params.ex uses a regex over [\x00-\x1F\x7F]. As a result a DEL character is accepted by DecisionValidation/DecisionEvent but rejected by DecisionApi, and newlines are accepted in one place and rejected in another, with no named policy. The attention-slug regex `\A[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{0,63}\z` is duplicated in decision_event, decision_validation and decision_attention, and embedded in alert_feed. The JWT regex is duplicated in decision_provenance and decision_sanitizer, which also duplicate the ≤256-byte/redact==value identity check. The bounded_required/bound_string trim→length→control→SecretRedactor.redact pipeline is duplicated between DecisionEvent and DecisionValidation.
findings.recommendation: Create Aiur.Decisions.TextPolicy with bounded_text(value, max, field, multiline?: bool), control_chars?(text, :multiline | :single_line), attention_slug?/1, jwt?/1 and safe_identity?/2. Replace every copy and decide deliberately whether DEL is allowed (see the tests).

findings.title: DecisionEvent (1,057 lines) spreads per-type logic across parallel clause tables, copies actor encoding eight times, and builds the provenance hash material twice
findings.description: Adding an event type means editing @types, the @type union (which lists :dispatch_outcome_unknown separately even though @types is later redefined to include it), 18 normalize_data/5 clauses, 15 data_to_json_safe/2 clauses and possibly @transport_types/@actor_types. `%{"kind" => Atom.to_string(data.actor.kind), "id" => data.actor.id}` appears at lines 565, 573, 577, 582, 590, 597, 621 and 638. The provenance hash material is built once in provenance_material/4 (write side) and again inline in verify_provenance_hash/4 (read side). Any drift between the two makes every persisted snapshot fail replay with :provenance_hash_mismatch, which is the fail-closed latch the moduledoc warns about. decode_typed_provenance/8 has five clauses of eight positional arguments, and decode_versioned_snapshot_provenance/1 has a clause (line 782) with the same result as the catch-all.
findings.recommendation: Give each event type its own codec module implementing a DecisionEvent.Codec behaviour (normalize/3, to_json/1, schema_versions/0), registered in one map. Extract actor_to_json/1. Have one provenance_material(context, provenance, state) used by both hash and verify. Pass a context struct instead of eight arguments. Delete the redundant clause at 782.

findings.title: AgentQueueStore keeps every queue item and idempotency index forever in Orchestrator state; several operations scan all items, and callers reach into its internals
findings.description: Consumed, failed and superseded items are never removed from `items`, and item_id_by_action and item_id_by_message_id only grow. list_visible_operator_messages/2, consume_delivered/2, restore_delivered/2 and fail_delivered/2 (via update_delivered_items/3) iterate Map.values(store.items), as does OperatorMessages.reject_already_queued_events/2, which also depends on consumed items being retained for dedupe. On a long-running daemon the Orchestrator's state and per-call cost grow with total history. StatusReport builds %AgentQueueStore{items: ..., pending_ids_by_target: ...} directly, and OperatorMessages reads queue_store.items, so the internal representation is a de facto public API.
findings.recommendation: Add per-target indexes for delivered items. Move terminal items into a bounded per-target ring, and keep a bounded seen-event-id set for the digest dedupe. Expose snapshot/1 and seen_event_id?/2 instead of letting callers read .items. Give StatusReport a constructor (from_snapshot/1).

findings.title: Five different repository-identity derivations key durable state files: IssueLog base64, SessionHandle last-segment, AlertLedger hashed project name, RepoBase slug, Workspace.Layout segment

findings.title: RecentMergeStore latches read-only until restart after a boot-time compaction failure, while the same failure at runtime is retried
findings.description: compact_replayed_log/1 sets writable?: false when compaction fails during init (for example a transient ENOSPC or EACCES). handle_call({:upsert, _}) then refuses every write with {:store_unavailable, health}, and nothing retries: there is no timer, and only a restart re-runs init. The runtime path (persist_compaction/3) keeps writable? true and retries on the next upsert. The alert fires once. A transient disk condition at boot thus permanently disables merge recording for the daemon's lifetime (latch with no exit).
findings.recommendation: Treat a boot compaction failure like the runtime one: keep the store writable with health {:compaction_failed, reason} and retry compaction on the next upsert or a backoff timer. Reserve writable?: false for interior corruption.

findings.title: ProcessReaper reaps serially inside handle_call (up to 4 s per pid and per descendant), and the 25 s call timeout is swallowed so shutdown proceeds as if the reap finished
findings.description: The kill_tree killer is RemoteControl.graceful_kill_tree/1, which walks descendants and, for each one, sends TERM, waits up to @kill_grace_ms (2 s), then sends KILL and waits up to 2 s more. With N entries this runs sequentially inside the reaper's handle_call. reap/3 uses safe_call with a 25 s timeout that catches :exit and returns :ok, so Shutdown.cleanup continues while the reaper is still killing, and the caller cannot tell that the sweep was incomplete.
findings.recommendation: Do the TERM phase for all pids first, then one shared grace wait, then KILL the survivors, which bounds total time to about 2×grace. Return {:ok, %{killed:, skipped:, timed_out:}} and log or alert when the call times out instead of returning :ok.

findings.title: IssueLog writers never exit: each ticket ever attached keeps a GenServer and three open file descriptors for the daemon's lifetime
findings.description: The moduledoc states that the writer 'stays alive until the BEAM exits; there's no automatic detach when the issue completes'. Each writer opens the .log, .events.log and .agent_events.jsonl files in append mode and holds them. A long-running daemon that works many tickets accumulates file descriptors without bound. The codebase already documents an `:emfile` BEAM death (ProcessReaper moduledoc) as a real failure mode.
findings.recommendation: Add an idle timeout: close the files (or stop the writer, since restart is :transient) after N minutes with no events, and reopen lazily on the next event. Alternatively open per write with O_APPEND for the low-rate .events.log.

findings.title: IssueLog.event_history/2 and disk_history/2 read and regex-parse the entire per-issue log on every call, although read_tail/2 was deliberately bounded
findings.description: Per-issue logs are uncapped ('capped by disk'). event_history/2 is called by AgentEventFeed.bus_events (dashboard/Stream Deck), BootstrapDigest (agent resume) and ticket_history_provider. Every call File.reads the whole .events.log, splits it, runs a regex on every line, and only then applies limit and since_id. disk_history/2 does the same over the human .log. read_tail/2 exists because 'a busy or historic transcript cannot turn a Stream Deck refresh into a full-log scan', but the same reasoning was not applied to these two readers.
findings.recommendation: Reuse the tail-chunk reader (pread from EOF backwards) for both. For since_id queries, scan backwards until id <= since_id or the limit is reached.

findings.title: Findings and Asks are twin append-only NDJSON ledgers with different durability disciplines, and RepoBase hard-codes both in its migration
findings.description: Findings appends with O_APPEND and no lock (it relies on the 4 KiB atomic-append bound). Asks goes through Store.with_lock. Both live in meta/*.ndjson and both do validate-per-line and latest-by-key reads. RepoBase's migration special-cases each: merge_findings/merge_asks, two transfer-marker suffixes, transfer_error_tag and transfer_inconsistent_tag with a clause per ledger, validate_ledger/3 dispatch, and merged_findings_suffix/2 (named for findings but also used for asks). A third ledger would need edits in all of these places.
findings.recommendation: Define an Aiur.RepoState.Ledger behaviour (path/1, validate_record/1, key/1) plus a generic append/read_with_diagnostics/transfer implementation, and make Findings and Asks schema modules. Pick one locking discipline for both.

findings.title: TestReset --force ignores the result of `git stash push` and then runs a destructive `git checkout HEAD --` over the sandbox files
findings.description: restore_baseline/1 calls stash_sandbox_if_dirty/1 when --force is set, 'so destructive checkout doesn't silently lose work'. stash_sandbox_if_dirty discards the System.cmd result of the stash and returns :ok, and the checkout runs regardless. If the stash fails (index lock, a stash conflict), uncommitted edits to the sandbox files are overwritten with no stash entry. That is a latent data-loss path in the dev harness, and the one thing the comment promises cannot happen.
findings.recommendation: Match {_, 0} on the stash and abort the restore (return an error) otherwise. Also check that `git stash list` gained the entry.

findings.title: ExecutorWakeInbox re-reads and re-validates the whole journal several times per operation; trim write failure is ignored
findings.description: The journal is capped at @default_max_records 10_000 lines, and each DecisionLog.replay/2 reads the whole file and runs every line through the validator. One flush does durable_wake_ids/1 (replay), trim_consumed/1 (replay) and serve_waiters/1 -> unread_records/1 (replay); every wait, stats, pending and cursor call also re-reads the cursor file (current_cursor/1). All of this runs inside the GenServer, so producers queue behind it. The replay-and-case block is copied three times (durable_records, durable_wake_ids, journal_summary). trim_records/2 discards the Fs.atomic_write result, then advances the cursor and alerts that unread wakes 'were evicted' even when the file was not rewritten, so the file keeps growing past the bound.
findings.recommendation: Replay once at init and keep an in-memory ordered index (wake_id -> record) plus the durable id set; append updates the index. Read the cursor file only on an explicit refresh or a file-change signal. Extract one replay_journal/1. Check the atomic_write result and alert on failure.

findings.title: Two process-tree observers poll the host independently: one pgrep spawn per tree node per second, plus two ps snapshots every 2s even when idle
findings.description: AgentResourceGuard ticks every 1s and, for every registered agent root, recursively runs `pgrep -P <pid>` once per process in the tree (System.find_executable + System.cmd per node). With 20 agents running Mix builds (tens of processes each) that is hundreds of process spawns per second on the host whose load the dispatcher throttles on. AgentProcessLog separately runs `ps -eo pid=,ppid=,comm=,args=` and `ps -eo pid=,lstart=` every 2s unconditionally: observe_tree/1 snapshots the whole process table even when roots_fun returns [] and even when the log path resolved to nil at init (non-GitHub tracker or unresolvable repo), in which case append(nil, _) discards every row. Two more recursive pgrep walkers exist (Claude.RemoteControl.collect_descendants/1, GitHub.Config.child_os_pids/2). append/2 and rotate/2 also rescue everything to :ok.
findings.recommendation: Create one Aiur.ProcessTree snapshot service: a single `ps` (or /proc scan) per tick, a children index, shared read access for the resource guard, the process log, the reaper and remote-control teardown. Skip the tick entirely when there are no agent roots, and do not start the process log when its path is nil.

findings.title: Aiur.Config is a god accessor (1462 lines, 114 public functions, 147 dependent files) that also performs filesystem side effects
findings.description: One module owns: the memoized settings read and env-epoch hashing, ~100 one-line accessors across every domain (tracker, polling, events, workspace, build order, hooks, agent load/admission, codex, decisions, observability, telemetry retention, server), base-branch resolution with its own error formatting, Codex sandbox policy assembly, semantic validation, legacy config preparation, and error-message formatting. codex_runtime_settings/2 reaches into Budget, BuildGate and AgentEnvironment and creates directories (Budget.ensure_state_dir, BuildGate.prepare_writable_root) as a side effect of a config read. @implicit_env_vars must be hand-synchronised with every env read in the schema path or the memo goes stale. Every would-be package imports this module, so it becomes the dependency hub of the carve.
findings.recommendation: Keep Aiur.Config.settings/0 (+ memo) as the only core API. Move accessors into per-domain modules that take a %Schema{} (Config.Agent, Config.Polling, Config.BuildOrder, Config.Observability ...), move codex_runtime_settings/turn-sandbox assembly into the Codex package, and validation into Config.Validation. Derive the implicit env list from the schema instead of a hand-kept attribute.

findings.title: Config accessors have four different failure behaviours chosen per function
findings.description: About 70 accessors raise through settings!(). A handful fall back silently to a default on any config error, each with a different default (0, true, %{}, nil, 300, :local), and poll_intervals/0 rescues ArgumentError into %{} (all per-class cadences dropped). telemetry_enabled?/1 and upgrade_check_enabled?/1 default their argument to settings_uncached/0, so each call re-reads and re-parses the file. Three accessors use Map.get 'so a config cached before this field existed' works while every other accessor uses dot access, which is the same risk. A caller cannot tell from the name whether a read can raise or will quietly substitute a value.
findings.recommendation: Pick one policy per accessor class and encode it in the name (fetch!/get_or_default), or have callers receive a settings struct once per operation instead of re-reading. Remove the 'cached before this field existed' special cases (the memo is keyed per generation).

findings.title: Backend registry creates dependency cycles and mixes core dispatch capabilities with web presentation, pricing, usage and telemetry
findings.description: CodingAgent.backends/0 is a 187-line function returning one map per backend that holds the adapter and transcript modules, delivery flags, CSS colours and asset paths (presentation), pricing dimension tables, usage adapters, run-telemetry decoders and meter-probe callbacks. The result is bidirectional module dependencies: CodingAgent -> Config (agent_kind, agent_backend_configs, switch_model_on_ratelimit) and Config -> CodingAgent (default_backend, rate_limit_fallback_targets, complexity_level, dispatchable_backends, configurable_backends, known_backends); CodingAgent -> ModelDiscovery (cached_models, catalogue, source_key) and ModelDiscovery -> CodingAgent (backends, seedable_models, family_for); CodingAgent -> ProviderMeterProbe (registry entries capture &ProviderMeterProbe.probe_session/3) and ProviderMeterProbe -> CodingAgent (provider_meter_probe); CodingAgent <-> ModelAvailability. These cycles prevent carving agent backends, usage/pricing, meters and the dashboard into separate packages.
findings.recommendation: Split the registry: a core Backend behaviour/capability struct (adapter, transcript, delivery flags, resumable, remote transport) owned by the agent-runtime package, and facet registries (presentation in the web package, pricing/usage in the usage package, meter probes in the meters package) keyed by backend id. Pass configured backends and discovered catalogues in as arguments instead of calling Config/ModelDiscovery from CodingAgent.

findings.title: CodingAgent rebuilds the full registry on every accessor call; 11 accessors repeat the same Map.fetch/default body
findings.description: backends/0 allocates every entry map and merges OpenAICompat.Registry.entries() each time; it is called at 44 sites inside the module and by 14 external call sites. The per-issue dispatch path (backend_for, select_for_dispatch, model_for, effort_for) reaches override/2, which calls dispatchable_backends(Config.agent_backend_configs()) and label_opts/1 -> known_backends() for every label, so one issue per poll rebuilds the registry many times. The capability accessors family_for, efforts, control_application_confirmation, remote_control?, remote_worker?, resumable?, remote_transport, fallback_backend, rc_display_tail?, runtime_report and immediate_delivery? are the same 6-line `case Map.fetch(backends(), backend)` body with a different key and default.
findings.recommendation: Build the registry once (compile-time module attribute: remote captures are literals, or :persistent_term at boot) and expose one `capability(backend, key, default)` helper. Parse an issue's labels once per dispatch into a struct (override, variant, effort, remote flag, complexity) instead of re-running the regex in four functions.

findings.title: complexity:N label parsing is implemented three times and the implementations disagree
findings.description: CodingAgent.complexity_level/1 accepts any integer (including 0 and multi-digit values) and takes the highest of several labels; routing, max_turns_by_complexity and complexity prompts use it. BuildOrder.Metadata accepts only a single digit 1..5 and reports several labels as ambiguous. The dashboard units row accepts any positive integer and takes the first label. A ticket with complexity:2 and complexity:4 is routed as 4, shown as 2, and flagged ambiguous in the build order; complexity:7 routes (no table entry, so default) but is invalid to the build order.
findings.recommendation: Create one Aiur.Labels.Complexity module (parse/1 returning {:ok, n} | :ambiguous | :invalid | :none with the 1..5 domain) and use it in all three places; decide once whether multiple labels are an error or max-wins.

findings.title: Atomic tmp+rename file writes are re-implemented at least 11 times, most without fsync, despite Aiur.Fs.atomic_write and JsonStore.write!
findings.description: Aiur.Fs.atomic_write/3 (fsync + rename, mode option) and Aiur.JsonStore.write!/2 exist, yet each of these modules writes its own temp file and renames it. The copies differ: ModelAvailability and ModelDiscovery ignore the File.mkdir_p result and never fsync; AgentGitHubGuard opens with :exclusive and chmods; TakeoverAlert.Store uses a fixed `.tmp` name (two writers collide); CurrentRunMembership has its own atomic_write.
findings.recommendation: Extend Aiur.Fs.atomic_write/3 with :mode, :exclusive and :encode options and replace every hand-rolled copy; add a credo check or a grep in the lint job for `.tmp"` outside fs.ex.

findings.title: ModelAvailability and ModelDiscovery are two hand-rolled JSON ledgers beside the workflow config with copied load/write/time helpers
findings.description: Both modules compute a path next to `.aiur/config` (Path.dirname(Workflow.workflow_file_path())), permissively decode a whole JSON document, merge one backend entry, and write it back with identical code; ModelDiscovery's moduledoc even says its decode is the 'same as Aiur.ModelAvailability.load/1'. They each carry a private parse_time/1 with different accepted inputs. Runtime state therefore lives in the operator's config directory (with a global ~/.aiur/config it is shared across repositories), while CIApprovalStore was deliberately moved to Paths.decision_state_dir/0 for #2716. ModelDiscovery additionally memoizes through :persistent_term put/erase, which triggers a global GC on each replacement.
findings.recommendation: Extract a small keyed JSON ledger (load/update-entry/write under one lock, stored under the state dir) and build both modules on it; move the files to Paths state dir with a one-time adoption like CIApprovalStore; replace the persistent_term memo with an ETS entry.

findings.title: ModelAvailability reads model-usage.json on every call even when the caller passes :state (eager Keyword.get default)
findings.description: Keyword.get/3 evaluates its default argument before the lookup, so `Keyword.get(opts, :state, load(...))` reads and decodes the file even when :state is present. first_available/2 loads once and passes :state to available?/2 for each candidate precisely to avoid re-reading, but each available?/2 call still reads the file; recovery_confirmed?/2 reads it twice. These run on the dispatch path (CodingAgent.select_for_dispatch/2, Orchestrator.RateLimitFallback, DispatchPolicy).
findings.recommendation: Use Keyword.get_lazy/3 (or Keyword.fetch) at all three sites; add a test with a :path pointing at a missing/unreadable file plus a supplied :state and assert the state is used.

findings.title: ISO-8601 timestamp parsing and key stringification are re-implemented per module with differing semantics
findings.description: A private parse_time/parse_timestamp/parse_datetime/parse_iso8601 is defined in 12 lib files (alert_feed, build_order/ticket_history_normalizer, current_run_membership/projection, decision_metrics/event/fields, decision_metrics/sample, decision_query/cursor, events/github_comments_poller, executor/takeover_alert/snapshot, linear/client, model_availability, model_discovery, run_telemetry/dataset). They differ: ModelAvailability also accepts DateTime structs and unix integers, the others only binaries. stringify_keys/1 is defined in 5 files; decision_projection's is shallow and model_availability's is recursive under the same name.
findings.recommendation: Add Aiur.Time.parse_iso8601/1 (+ explicit parse_unix/1) and Aiur.MapKeys.stringify/2 (depth option) in a shared utility module and replace the private copies.

findings.title: AlertFeed answers every query by reading, decoding and sorting the full alert ledger; it is called on every resolution emit and from the Orchestrator
findings.description: list/1 and condition_states/2 read every ledger path (each capped at 8 MiB), JSON-decode each line, sort by timestamp string and fold. Alerts.do_emit/3 calls duplicate_resolution?/2 -> condition_state/2 on every emission, so each alert write costs a full ledger scan in the emitting process. active_system_attention?/2 is called from the Orchestrator process (dispatcher.ex:695, 786; issue_sync.ex:1861, 1943, 2073; comment_polling.ex:107) and active_ticket_attention?/2 from status_report.ex:1337 before emitting waiting-for-human alerts. Sorting ISO-8601 strings lexically also mis-orders records whose timestamps differ in offset or fractional precision.
findings.recommendation: Maintain an ETS index of condition state and active attention keys updated by AlertLedger.append/2 (rebuilt once at boot from the ledger), and serve condition_state/active_*_attention? from it. Parse timestamps to DateTime before sorting.

findings.title: AlertFeed turns any ledger read error into 'no alerts' with no log; two public predicates are identical
findings.description: read_alerts/2 and read_legacy_alerts/1 `rescue _ -> []`. A malformed or unreadable ledger therefore makes condition_state/2 return :unknown and active_*_attention?/2 return false, which re-arms emitters (they re-emit firing alerts and resolutions) and hides every attention from the dashboard, with nothing logged. backfill_locked/1 likewise drops {:error, _} from append_legacy_alerts silently (retried on the next boot only). active_system_attention?/2 and active_ticket_attention?/2 have byte-identical bodies (both filter agents to ["system"]), so the name promises a distinction the code does not make.
findings.recommendation: Return {:error, reason} from the read layer and let callers choose fail-open vs fail-closed explicitly; log and alert on a ledger read failure. Collapse the two predicates into active_attention?(topic, agents: ...) or give the ticket variant the ticket agent filter it implies.

findings.title: OpenTicketSource and BuildOrder.AdHocSource mirror 13 private helpers and have already drifted; both page GitHub synchronously inside GenServer callbacks
findings.description: The moduledoc says OpenTicketSource is 'modelled on Aiur.BuildOrder.AdHocSource'. Both define reconcile_issue, fetch_pages, apply_result, do_apply_result, rebuild_snapshot, snapshot_status (identical 3 clauses), meaningful, broadcast, now, maybe_relist, resolve_repo. They drifted: OpenTicketSource caps the listing at 10 pages and 4 MiB per response, AdHocSource paginates without a page or byte cap (acc ++ issues). Both run the whole multi-page listing inside handle_cast/handle_info, so OpenTicketSource.snapshot/1 (5s call) exits during a slow relist and returns an empty :unavailable snapshot. repo is resolved once in init: if repo_fun fails at boot, every store event is ignored by the catch-all reconcile_issue/5 and maybe_relist/2 clauses while a later successful refresh still marks the projection :available. GlobalConfigStartup has a third pagination loop (page=N, 10-page cap) instead of Transport.parse_next_page_url/1.
findings.recommendation: Extract an event-sourced GitHub listing behaviour (baseline listing + store-event reconcile + degraded/recovered relist + snapshot/broadcast plumbing) parameterised by a filter and a row mapper; run the listing in a Task with a generation fence so the server keeps answering; share one bounded paginator.

findings.title: AgentLog reads the entire agent.ndjson into memory to show 80 messages, and re-parses Codex app-server protocol that three other modules also parse
findings.description: read_structured_messages/1 does File.read of the full transcript and decodes every line before Enum.take(-@message_window). Transcripts grow for the life of a ticket, and the dashboard agent-log modal calls it (aiur_web/components/operator_control_center/agent_log_modal.ex:148-159). parse_json_log_entry/4 is a 77-line case over Codex notification methods (item/started, item/completed, item/agentMessage/delta ...) with eight explicit `-> nil` arms that duplicate the catch-all; the same methods are interpreted in codex/transcript.ex, codex/event_humanizer.ex and agent_runner/codex_update_relay.ex. summarize_prompt/1 and issue_prompt_text?/1 couple the renderer to literal prompt-template text ('You are an agent for this repository.', '## Workspace setup').
findings.recommendation: Read only the tail (reuse AlertLedger's Tail reader), and render from Codex.Transcript.extract/2 output instead of a parallel protocol switch. Mark prompt sections with explicit markers in the template rather than matching prose.

findings.title: Aiur.Application starts ~90 children in one flat :rest_for_one supervisor from a 246-line child_specs/1, with unguarded host side effects before it
findings.description: Every child sits in one :rest_for_one list, so a crash of any early child restarts every later child: e.g. ProcessReaper (308), AgentResourceGuard (310), BuildGateHoldMonitor (313) or any GitHub table owner restarts Orchestrator (449), DecisionStore, TicketActivity and HttpServer (475, which also regenerates secret_key_base). The comments justify rest_for_one by PubSub links, but most children do not depend on their predecessors. child_specs/1 mixes ordering rationale, feature flags read from Application env and conditional children in one 246-line function. start/2 writes the agent token file and installs host wrappers into ~/.aiur/bin (lines 60-61) with no env == :test guard, while maybe_validate_environment/0 (141) and GlobalConfigStartup.prepare/0 have one. log_base_branch/1 is named as a log helper but raises (Config.base_branch/2) and so gates boot.
findings.recommendation: Group children into per-domain supervisors (Core: ModeTable/PubSub/Registries; Host; GitHub; Usage; Decisions; Executor recording; Orchestrator; Web; TUI), use :rest_for_one only inside the Core group and :one_for_one between independent groups. Move boot side effects into an explicit Boot pipeline with an env guard, and make base-branch validation an explicit validation step.

findings.title: DecisionProjection (1039 lines) mixes record decoding, the lifecycle state machine and JSON serialization; three attempt constructors have diverged
findings.description: transition/2 has 24 clauses over ~250 lines; decode helpers (fetch_map/fetch_string/fetch_timestamp) and a ~160-line serializer live in the same module. Dispatch-attempt maps are built in three places: the :dispatch_outcome_unknown attempt omits :handed_off_at while the queued and failed attempts include it, contradicting the dispatch_attempt type in decision.ex:79; readers compensate with Map.get (to_json_safe 926, Decision.attempt_in_flight?/1 decision.ex:262, public_lifecycle_projection.ex:82). reserve_event_identity/2 has two identical clauses for DecisionEvent and Unrecognized. History, revisions and attempts are appended with `list ++ [x]`.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a DispatchAttempt struct with one constructor; split into DecisionProjection.Decode, DecisionProjection.Reducer (transitions) and DecisionProjection.JSON; merge the duplicate reserve clauses.

findings.title: DecisionExpiry skips the whole sweep whenever the Orchestrator does not answer a GenServer.call within 1s
findings.description: The sweep, and with it the stale-blocking and expired-unanswerable attention reconciliation, is abandoned when Orchestrator :list_active_identifiers takes longer than 1s. The Orchestrator is the busiest GenServer in the system, so under load expiry and attention reconciliation can starve indefinitely with only a Logger.warning per minute, which is written nowhere without --debug. A failed DecisionStore.expire result is silently not counted. sync_reconciliation_with_legacy_injections/5 keeps test-only injection branches (classification_sync_fun, attention_sync_fun) in production code.
findings.recommendation: Read active identifiers from the published orchestrator snapshot (Orchestrator.SnapshotStore / ETS) instead of a call; count consecutive skips and raise a system alert after N; drop the legacy injection seams and update the tests to inject attention_reconcile_fun only.

findings.title: OpencodeTheme overwrites the user's opencode kv.json with only {theme: aiur} when the file is unparsable, using a non-atomic write
findings.description: decode_kv/1 maps invalid JSON to {:enoent, %{}}; theme_action(:enoent) is :set; write_kv writes merge_theme(%{}) = %{"theme" => "aiur"}. Any other state opencode keeps in ~/.local/state/opencode/kv.json is discarded, for example after a torn read while a running opencode serve is rewriting it. The write is a plain File.write, so a crash mid-write truncates the user's file. The module reads the real XDG/HOME paths by default.
findings.recommendation: Treat an unparsable kv.json as {:error, :invalid_kv} and skip activation (report :skipped); write through Aiur.Fs.atomic_write/3.

findings.title: HttpServer uses Application env as a mutable global to wire runtime dependencies and regenerates secret_key_base on every start
findings.description: start_link/1 writes :dashboard_url_fun into the :aiur app env and merges orchestrator/decision_api/decision_store modules, auth flags and a freshly generated secret_key_base into the Endpoint's app env before starting it. Other code reads these globals implicitly, so tests and a second instance share them, and every HttpServer restart (which happens whenever an earlier sibling crashes under the flat :rest_for_one tree) rotates the secret and invalidates existing signed sessions/LiveView tokens.
findings.recommendation: Pass dependencies to the Endpoint via its child spec/init config and a registry lookup rather than app env; generate secret_key_base once per boot (Aiur.Boot) or persist it in the state dir.

findings.title: Token-usage key aliases are listed three times in TokenUsage with two different integer parsers, and token normalization exists in four other modules
findings.description: canonicalize/1, token_field?/1 and format_counts/1 each spell out the input/output/total alias lists (atoms and strings). canonicalize uses parse_token_value/1, which accepts trailing garbage ("12abc" -> 12 via `{n, _}`), while format_counts uses EventHumanizerHelpers.parse_integer, so the same payload can canonicalize and display differently. Other normalizers of the same provider fields: orchestrator/token_accounting/payloads.ex, usage/headless/claude/request_usage.ex, usage/headless/codex/tokens.ex, usage/headless/open_ai_compat/request_usage.ex.
findings.recommendation: Define the alias table once (module attribute of {canonical_key, [aliases]}) and one strict parser; have the usage adapters and token accounting call it.

findings.title: Command classification is hand-maintained in six places and has diverged
findings.description: Six lists record which subcommands exist and what each needs (rebuild, tmux, opencode, control-plane only): the engine dispatch, usage(), aiurdev targets_release_deliberately, pure_control_command, requires_pinned_opencode, and aiur.js isForegroundOneShot. They disagree. (1) usage() omits `usage` and `reset-budget`, both of which dispatch and are documented in cli.md. (2) pure_control_command omits commands, units, build-orders, analytics, usage, watch and executor-*, so under aiurdev those rebuild the release first. That matters for `executor-wait`, which the Executor runs in a loop, and it is the rebuild-under-a-live-daemon pattern that AGENTS.md says control commands avoid. (3) targets_release_deliberately omits `upgrade`, so it falls into the 'deliberate' branch. (4) aiur.js treats only `--version` and `init` as one-shots. Every other command (status, stop, executor-wait, findings, ask) runs `tmux -V`, `opencode --version`, and a global `npm install -g opencode-ai@<pin>` whenever the installed opencode does not match the pin.
findings.recommendation: Create one command registry, for example `libexec/commands.tsv` with columns name, kind (run|control|stream|oneshot), needs_tmux, needs_opencode and rebuild_policy. Generate usage() from it, source it from the engine and aiurdev, and read it from aiur.js. Add a test that every dispatch arm has a registry row.

findings.title: aiur-engine.sh is a 4,179-line god script with a 351-line run_session
findings.description: One bash file holds nine responsibilities: identity and distribution, dotenv loading, tmux launch and attach, the BEAM-death watchdog and process reaping, control-RPC transport and diagnostics, 32 cmd_* argument parsers (947 lines), restart build verification, npm upgrade and channel logic, and stale manual-smoke hygiene. findings.title: Control commands are parsed twice: bash cmd_* parsers generate Elixir source strings that the Elixir *CLI modules validate again
findings.description: Each control subcommand has a bash option parser that validates flags and builds an Elixir keyword-list literal (`Aiur.AgentControlCLI.units([scope: Base.decode64!(...)])`) sent through `bin/aiur rpc`. The Elixir side (CommandsCLI, UnitsCLI, ExecutorCommandCLI, GitHubCostCLI, ...) then validates again. Measured in the engine: 28 '--x requires a value' branches, 107 `exit 64` sites, and 11 inline `printf ... | base64 | tr -d '\n'` copies although encode_control_value exists. cmd_executor_answer, cmd_executor_escalate and cmd_executor_moot are three roughly 35-line near-copies. Run, init, findings and ask use a second transport (the argv file) and a third parser (Aiur.CLI OptionParser). Every new flag means editing bash, the Elixir CLI module, usage() and the docs.
findings.recommendation: Send raw argv as a base64 list to one entry point, `Aiur.AgentControlCLI.main(argv)`, that uses OptionParser. Bash keeps only transport, timeout and exit-marker handling. This removes about 900 lines of bash and makes the Elixir side the only validator.

findings.title: A trailing valued option exits 1 silently, breaking the engine's no-silent-failure contract
findings.description: In executor-wait (`--timeout`, `--as`), executor-claim (`--as`), executor-release (`--as`) and executor-emit (`--payload`), each option does `shift; x="${1:-}"` and then the loop does an unconditional `shift`. When the option is the last argument, the second shift fails and `set -e` ends the script with exit 1 and no output. I verified this under set -euo pipefail. The engine's own contract (2311-2331, #1684) says a non-zero exit always carries a stderr line. Other parsers, such as cmd_commands, guard with `[ "$#" -gt 1 ] ||`.
findings.recommendation: Add a shared `take_value <cmd> <opt> "$@"` helper that checks $# and prints '<cmd> <opt> requires a value' (or move parsing to Elixir, see -06).

findings.title: Nightly versions (<base>-nightly.<sha>) cannot be ordered, so upgrade and notice logic misjudges newer nightlies; the comparator is also duplicated in bash and Elixir
findings.description: resolve-version publishes nightlies as `<base>-nightly.<7-hex sha>`. SemVer orders prerelease identifiers lexically (numerically when all digits), so between two nightlies of the same base the 'newer' one is decided by sha spelling. Bash version_is_older compares the whole prerelease with `[[ a < b ]]`, so cmd_upgrade reports 'already up to date' whenever the newer nightly's sha sorts lower, and maybe_print_upgrade_notice suppresses the notice. Elixir Upgrade.notice uses Version.newer? and has the same flaw. The two also disagree when a sha is all digits: Elixir treats it as numeric, which sorts below alphanumeric, while bash compares it as text. The upgrade policy is implemented twice, and each copy says it mirrors the other: env opt-outs (3793-3795 vs env_disabled?/ci?), dev-launcher detection by path, channel resolution (3920-3935 vs channel/2), and the no-repeat marker.
findings.recommendation: Make nightlies orderable, for example `<base>-nightly.<YYYYMMDDHHMMSS>.<sha>` or `nightly.<run_number>`. Keep one comparator and one channel resolver: have `aiur upgrade` call into the release (`bin/aiur eval Aiur.Upgrade...`) or port the whole policy to one place.

findings.title: The analytics reducer exists twice (Python analytics/reduce.py and Elixir RunTelemetry.Dataset), and daemon materialization silently no-ops outside the aiur checkout
findings.description: reduce.py says it 'produces the same consumable dataset shape as the Elixir Aiur.RunTelemetry.Dataset reducer'. The two share the same constants (RESOURCE_METRICS/@resource_metrics, RESOURCE_EVIDENCE, 5,000 ms interval, 1.5 gap multiplier, 300 s review grace) and function-for-function copies: parse_line, dedupe_records, sequence_warnings, reduce_actors, statistics, resource_gaps, lifecycle_intervals, review_findings, active_review_pause, response_window and in_boot?. No test checks that the two agree. The daemon also shells out to the Python copy: Summaries.reduce_dir looks in `RepoBase.base_path(repo)/analytics` or `Path.expand("analytics")` relative to the BEAM cwd. The npm package does not ship analytics/, and other tracked repos do not contain it, so materialize_async returns `:unavailable -> :ok` with no log. Run summaries silently never exist for npm users and for non-aiur repos. This is the silent-refusal bug family.
findings.recommendation: Keep one reducer. The daemon already has Dataset, so materialize in-process (Dataset.build, then Jason-encode run-summary.json), remove the Python shell-out, and keep Python as a thin offline reader of materialized JSON if Executors need it. If both must stay, add a golden parity test that runs both on src/test/fixtures/analytics. Log when materialization is unavailable.

findings.title: Python and Elixir compute run KPIs differently: an unknown cap becomes 10 in Python and an em dash in Elixir, and the sample cadence is hard-coded in both
findings.description: The Elixir presenter documents that wasted slot-hours must be nil (rendered as an em dash) when the effective cap is unknown: 'an unknown cap must not produce a precise-looking hour count'. The Python renderer substitutes `fallback_cap`, which is the --cap CLI default of 10, both in _sampled_waste and in the legacy _concurrency path, and prints 'Wasted capacity: X slot-hours'. AGENTS.md names exactly this anti-pattern: an unknown value replaced with a plausible default. Both implementations hard-code a 5 s sample cadence for CPU-seconds (Python SAMPLE_SECONDS=5; Elixir `* 5`), while the sampler interval is only a default (@default_interval_ms 5_000). They also round differently (Python to 0.1, Elixir to an integer).
findings.recommendation: Record sample_interval_ms in the telemetry and summary and compute from it. Return None and render 'unavailable' when the cap is unknown. Keep one KPI implementation (follows from -10).

findings.title: build-report crashes on its documented non-materialized path because build_summary_for returns a path, not a summary
findings.description: The docstring says build-report 'reads the materialized build-summary when present, otherwise reduces the raw stream on the fly'. On the fallback path, _load_or_reduce returns `reducer.build_summary_for(...)`. That function writes the file and returns `str(target)`, and main then calls render.render_build_report(summary), which calls `summary.get(...)` on a str and raises AttributeError. The fallback also writes into the state node as a side effect of a read-only report. The only integration test materializes first, so the crash path is never exercised.
findings.recommendation: Split a pure `build_rollup(dataset, slug, build_order) -> dict` out of build_summary_for and use it in build-report. Add a test with no materialized summary.

findings.title: Materialized summaries embed the full raw stream, the daemon re-reduces every boot on every segment, and run-summary parses everything before checking the cache
findings.description: boot_summary and _rollup_build put `records` (every raw record) and actors[].samples (every resource sample again) into each JSON file, so a 'cheap' summary is at least as large as the raw telemetry. The daemon runs `reduce --all --all-builds --telemetry <file>` on every telemetry segment boundary. That re-parses and rewrites every boot's summary and every build rollup, so the cost grows with retained telemetry. run-summary's docstring promises to read the materialized file when present, but main() calls reduce_files over the whole stream first (line 37), only uses the dataset for boot ids, and never checks provenance for staleness. The `--current` flag is parsed and never read.
findings.recommendation: Materialize incrementally: only boots whose source_bytes changed, using the provenance already recorded. Drop raw records from summaries or put them behind --with-records. List boots from the runs/ directory before parsing the stream. Remove --current or implement it.

findings.title: The launcher↔BEAM environment and tempfile contract is implicit and mostly missing from the env schema
findings.description: The pane launcher re-exports 29 variables, and the BEAM depends on four launcher-minted handoff files (AIUR_SESSION_TMPFILE, AIUR_AGENT_TMPFILE, AIUR_WORKSPACE_ROOT_FILE, AIUR_ALERT_LEDGER_PATH_FILE). The engine also writes alert-ledger JSON by printf (1608), duplicating the Elixir alert schema. check-env-example.py calls env/schema.ex 'the single source of truth for every environment variable Aiur reads', yet 48 of the 69 AIUR_* names in the engine are absent from it. That includes operator-facing knobs: AIUR_NODE_GRACE_TICKS (the startup error at 1935 tells operators to raise it), AIUR_CONTROL_RPC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, AIUR_TMP_REAP_MINUTES, AIUR_WORKSPACE_REAP_SWEEPS, AIUR_REPO_ROOT (documented in AGENTS.md) and AIUR_TMUX_CONF. It also includes two names Elixir itself reads: AIUR_UPGRADE_CHECK_DISABLED and AIUR_NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER. Internal shell globals (AIUR_CONTROL_*, AIUR_RECORD_*, AIUR_STOP_FOUND_NOTHING) use the same prefix, so env and locals cannot be told apart. AIUR_LAUNCH_LOCK_TICKS falls back to the unrelated AIUR_NODE_GRACE_TICKS (1466).
findings.recommendation: Declare a :launcher group in env/schema.ex for every operator-settable launcher knob and every handoff variable. Rename internal shell state to lower-case (`_ctl_adopted_record`). Collect the handoff files into one per-instance directory whose path is a single variable.

findings.title: probe_control_liveness reports 'down' when the Orchestrator is merely slow, and several guards depend on it
findings.description: The probe runs `bin/aiur rpc` with no timeout wrapper (unlike probe_dashboard_status) and calls Aiur.Orchestrator.status/2 with a 100 ms deadline, which returns :timeout under mailbox load. Anything other than READY prints 'down'. Consequences: (a) bare `aiur` refuses to attach to its own live session when the Orchestrator is busy ('control plane is not ready; leaving the running session intact'), although attaching needs only tmux; (b) `aiur upgrade` fails open and replaces the binary under a live daemon without --force; (c) the startup budget counts ticks, but each tick boots a full Erlang VM for the rpc, so the 1,200-tick budget is not 120 s and the '$(max_ticks/10)s' message misreports elapsed time; (d) without a timeout, a wedged node can hang any of these callers. The budget was raised from 100 to 1,200 ticks (comment 1901-1905), which fits the 'fix by raising a limit' family.
findings.recommendation: Return three states (ready, alive-but-busy, down), combining epmd liveness with a timed rpc (run_release_rpc_with_timeout). Use a wall-clock deadline (`date +%s`) instead of ticks. Attach whenever tmux has-session and the node is up. Make destructive guards such as upgrade fail closed on 'busy'.

findings.title: Five different TERM→wait→KILL implementations with inconsistent grace periods
findings.description: kill_beams_matching (30 ticks by default, 300 on stop), kill_pid_with_escalation (20 ticks), reap_aiur_agents (20), reap_workspace_cwd_agents (10 ticks per sweep × 6 sweeps) and kill_control_rpc_process (a fixed 0.2 s) each implement signal, poll and escalate separately. agent_pid_tree says it mirrors Aiur.RemoteControl.collect_descendants, and Aiur.ProcessReaper has its own graceful kill tree, so the same policy also exists across languages.
findings.recommendation: Use one `signal_with_grace <grace_ticks> <pid...>` helper plus one tree snapshot helper. Document the grace policy in one place.

findings.title: Dev and manual-test hygiene is shipped in the product engine and runs on every launch and stop
findings.description: The npm-installed engine carries dev-harness knowledge: `*/aiur-workspaces/*` path scoping, wrapper sockets `codex-driver-*|codex-aiur*|claude-driver*`, `aiurdev --test` start commands, and the `/src/_build/dev/rel/aiur` release layout. preflight_stale_manual_smoke scans every same-user BEAM, every tmux socket and every opencode attach on every launch. findings.title: Platform tables and tmux/opencode provisioning are copied across the npm scripts, have diverged on darwin-x64, and the drift check misses most copies
findings.description: platforms.mjs calls itself the single source of truth ('everything ... must derive from here') and excludes darwin-x64. aiur.js PLATFORMS, verify-install.sh's inline map, assemble-platform-package TARGETS and launcher.test HOST_TRIPLE all still include darwin-x64, and postinstall has its own SUPPORTED_PLATFORMS. check-platform-drift only checks package.json pins and the workflow. On an Intel Mac installed with bun or pnpm (which skip postinstall, as aiur.js 89-96 notes), aiur.js reports 'platform package ... is not installed ... optional dependencies were skipped' instead of 'unsupported platform'. MIN_TMUX, tmuxVersion/tmuxSatisfiesMin, tmuxHint, installTmux (identical package-manager list), opencodeMatchesPin and installOpencode are copied between aiur.js and postinstall.mjs. The 'parity' test only asserts `MIN_TMUX == [3,3]`. postinstall's manual hint installs unpinned `opencode-ai`, which then fails the pin check on every launch.
findings.recommendation: Put platforms and provisioning in a CommonJS module (lib/platforms.cjs, lib/provision.cjs) that aiur.js requires and the .mjs scripts import (ESM can import CJS, so the comment that the launcher 'cannot import the .mjs counterpart' does not rule this out). Derive every table from PUBLISH_TARGETS and extend check-platform-drift to cover them.

findings.title: The bun test suites under packaging/ never run, and launcher.test.mjs has rotted
findings.description: Every packaging test imports `bun:test`: launcher.test.mjs (945 lines), postinstall.test.mjs (239), and packaging/scripts/test/*.test.mjs (512). At the snapshot, neither ci.yml nor release-npm.yml runs `bun test`. The root package.json has only `setup`, and the Makefile only runs rename-preflight. The launcher suite has drifted from the engine. It expects 'control rpc to aiur-test@127.0.0.1 timed out after 1s' and "for example, 'aiurdev stop'", but aiur_engine_main always sets AIUR_CONTROL_COMMAND to the subcommand, so the label is 'status', and 'for example' appears nowhere in the engine. 'launcher loads global provider credentials before repo-local dotenv' asserts that the global .env beats the repo .env, which is the inverse of load_dotenv. It exercises this through `--todo`, a control path that never loads dotenv.
findings.recommendation: Add a CI step (`bun test packaging/`) or port the suites to `node --test`, which CI already uses for capture-dashboard. Repair or delete the rotted cases. Deduplicate them against the ExUnit engine tests so each behavior has one owner.

findings.title: Saturation repro watches the wrong crash-dump path for background daemons and so cannot report REPRODUCED
findings.description: resolve_dump_path uses AIUR_LOGS_ROOT only if the operator's shell has it; otherwise it takes the newest existing erl_crash.dump under ~/.aiur/logs or falls back to ~/.aiur/logs/erl_crash.dump. A background daemon's ERL_CRASH_DUMP is `$AIUR_LOGS_ROOT/erl_crash.dump`, with AIUR_LOGS_ROOT created per run inside the engine, exported only to the pane, and not stored in the instance record or in `aiur __identity`. A real #852 crash therefore shows up as exit 4 'DAEMON DOWN, NO DUMP'. epmd_node_state is a stated mirror of probe_node_liveness. GNU-only stat -c and find -printf are used without a guard.
findings.recommendation: Write AIUR_LOGS_ROOT and ERL_CRASH_DUMP into the instance record and print them from `aiur __identity`. Have the repro read them from there.

findings.title: Repo-slug to state-node parsing differs between Python analytics and Elixir RepoBase
findings.description: Python _repo_segments splits only on '/' and drops 'https:', 'http:', 'ssh:', 'git@' and 'github.com'. Elixir slug splits on `[/:]`, drops a different token set, takes the last two segments, and raises on '..'. They diverge: `git@github.com:o/n.git` gives owner `git@github.com:o` in Python and `o` in Elixir; a single segment `n` gives `local/n` in Python and `n` in Elixir; '..' is accepted by Python and rejected by Elixir. Without --state-node, state_node_root silently picks the only repo node, or writes into ~/.aiur/repo itself when there are several.
findings.recommendation: Have the Python tools require --state-node or --repo and exit with an error when the node is ambiguous. Port the Elixir rule exactly and share a fixture table between the two test suites. Better, remove the need through -10.

findings.title: The human-only merge ruleset verifiers duplicate each other, and the admin verifier hard-codes what the live verifier reads from the declaration
findings.description: The ruleset lookup (`gh api rulesets --paginate | jq select(.name==...)`) appears three times. The target/main, exclude and pull_request jq checks are byte-identical in verify and verify-live. The admin verifier assigns `declaration=` (line 7) and never uses it. Instead it hard-codes the 13 required check contexts, strict=false, do_not_enforce_on_create=false and bypass actor 1020682, while the live verifier derives the same values from docs/security/human-only-merge-ruleset.json. The two agree today but can drift silently, and a new required check means editing two places. apply-* does not guard against duplicate names; verify-* does.
findings.recommendation: Merge into one script with `--admin`, which additionally checks bypass_actors. Read every expectation from the declaration JSON. Share the lookup function with apply-*.

findings.title: verify-workflow-security.sh is a raw-text YAML security scanner that has grown one special case per incident
findings.description: It grep-scans workflow YAML for triggers and `uses:` pins. Each bypass found so far has become another rule: escaped double-quoted keys (61-72), explicit `? ` mapping keys (74-85), quoted and flow-mapping `uses` with a hand-written tokenizer (99-156), and symlink refusal. This is the 'growing cond of special cases' family applied to a security control, and the next YAML feature (anchors or aliases, multi-line flow) is another bypass.
findings.recommendation: Parse the YAML (python3 -c with PyYAML, or yq) and walk jobs[].steps[].uses and `on:` structurally. Better, adopt pinact, actionlint or zizmor, which already implement these rules.

findings.title: The engine auto-detects Tailscale and overwrites AIUR_DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_HOST, contradicting AGENTS.md and the env schema; usage() is also stale

findings.title: Dotenv parsing and precedence are implemented three times with different rules
findings.description: The launcher parser rejects keys containing any character outside [A-Za-z0-9_], so `export KEY=v` lines are silently ignored. It strips only a matched pair of quotes and keeps trailing whitespace, and it treats an env var that is set but empty as set. Aiur.Init.Dotenv trims both ends, strips every leading and trailing quote independently (`String.trim("\"")`), keeps `export KEY` as the key, and overwrites empty env values. Aiur.Env.precedence_conflicts re-implements the launcher's precedence and GitHub credential grouping to produce warnings, and its docstring says it 'Mirrors GITHUB_CREDENTIAL_ENV_NAMES in the launcher'. So the warnings can disagree with what the launcher actually exported, for example on values with trailing whitespace. The launcher also reads `./.env` relative to cwd, while identity is keyed by the walked-up repo root (-08), so a launch from a subdirectory misses the repo .env.
findings.recommendation: Define one dotenv grammar, preferably with a shared fixture file tested by both bash and ExUnit. Load `.env` from the resolved project root. Have the BEAM receive the launcher's resolution (which file supplied each name) instead of recomputing precedence.

findings.title: guard-pr-deletions is advisory and uses a two-dot diff that counts files added on base as 'deletions'
findings.description: `git diff --diff-filter=D $base_sha..HEAD` compares the base tip with HEAD, so files that main added after the branch point show as 'deleted' and 'untouched', and a branch that is merely behind is refused with a message about deletions. The agent skill frames this as 'repair the wrong or stale base', but the refusal text does not say so. The guard only runs when the agent remembers to run it; the skill cites an audit that found 70 of 289 agent pushes where it never ran.
findings.recommendation: Install the guard as a pre-push hook in workspace bootstrap (Aiur owns after_create/before_run), so it cannot be skipped. Report 'branch is N files behind base' separately from real deletions (`merge-base...HEAD` diff), or use a three-dot diff if staleness is not meant to be part of this guard.

findings.title: Capture readiness deadline does not bound an in-flight HTTP request
findings.description: The 30-second deadline is checked only before fetch. Neither fetch nor response.text receives a cancellation signal, so a stalled response prevents reaching the deadline check and the finally cleanup until that operation settles or its underlying transport fails. A successful response arriving after the deadline is accepted. The application-level deadline therefore does not enforce its advertised bound.
findings.recommendation: Apply an abort signal using the remaining deadline to the request and body read, and recheck the deadline before accepting readiness. Cover a connected response that never finishes, not only connection refusal.

findings.title: A failed monitor spawn forks two recovery chains
findings.description: spawnLineSource forwards both error and close to onEnd. The runtime treats each as a separate terminal event, schedules a restart twice, and retains only the newest timer and child. When a monitor executable is absent, Node actually emits ENOENT followed by close(-2). The two timers create two replacements; stopping the runtime kills only the last replacement. If stopped before either timer runs, the overwritten timer remains and can spawn a child after stop. The normal main-process signal path calls process.exit after cleanup, so the post-stop survival claim applies to the exported runtime stop API; duplicate monitors while running do not depend on that API.
findings.recommendation: Make termination idempotent per monitor generation, retain one restart timer, and guard spawnOnce against stopped state. Test the error-then-close sequence through the composed source/runtime, including stopping before and after replacement.

findings.title: Removing another Elgato product takes the active deck offline
findings.description: Device discovery/open selects VID and PID, but udev filtering accepts any usb_device with vendor 0fd9. A remove for another product therefore becomes device-removed for the connected Stream Deck +. The reducer closes the healthy handle and enters absent; there is no retry timer, so it waits for a later matching-vendor add event or restart despite the intended deck remaining plugged in. The trigger requires another same-vendor device; no prevalence is claimed.
findings.recommendation: Match the selected device identity across discovery and hotplug. At minimum check product as well as vendor; for multiple identical devices, correlate the owned physical device path or serial. Add composed add/remove tests for other products and other instances of the same model.

findings.title: Send discards spoken text before delivery is accepted
findings.description: sendTranscript optional-chains the channel call and then unconditionally clears the voice buffer. With channel=null during reconnect, no frame is sent and the only buffered text is discarded. With a connected channel, say refs are not tracked, so a server error or outcome_unknown reply has no callback and cannot preserve/recover the already-cleared message. main.ts retains the live grid on disconnect and voiceSession.dispose stops capture without clearing committed text, so the offline case is reachable with a retained Send affordance.
findings.recommendation: Represent an outbound message as pending until a correlated server receipt, keep text and a stable message ID through disconnect/unknown outcomes, and expose failure without consuming the buffer. Reject offline sends visibly. Do not regenerate the message ID for a retry of the same intended message.

findings.title: Implement shows QUEUED when no request was sent or a request failed
findings.description: The Implement handler sets implementQueued after an optional channel call, even when the channel is null. The rendered key derives QUEUED from that flag. When connected, control replies are untracked and errors are ignored; the flag clears on any grid update rather than on an operation result. A physical press can therefore claim queued before any daemon acceptance, and during reconnect can claim it without a request at all.
findings.recommendation: Keep a sending state separate from accepted queue state, disable or visibly reject offline control attempts, and correlate the control reply to the ticket/action before rendering QUEUED. Cover daemon rejection and disconnect as well as successful method invocation.

findings.title: Command history cannot advance beyond the server first page
findings.description: The server defaults to eight history items and supplies has_next/next_cursor. The channel exposes commandsPage(cursor), but the controller never calls it: both knob turning and pressing only clamp or cycle within commandsPage.items.length. An eight-item first page has maximum local offset zero, so the control advertised as history paging cannot reach older Commands. Merely retaining the unused channel method does not provide paging.
findings.recommendation: Consume the opaque cursor when navigation reaches the loaded-page boundary, keep page/focus identity and a previous-page strategy, and distinguish loading/error from end-of-history. Test using the server default eight-item page plus a next cursor, not a single oversized in-memory page.

findings.title: Key release discards the final transcript it asks the server to commit
findings.description: Release flushes audio and calls relay close, which removes the transcript handler before port.stop. The host sends voice_stop then clears its session ID. The server commits asynchronously and forwards the settled final, but both client layers have already stopped accepting it. Text settled before release survives; the remaining partial is dropped even if its final arrives successfully. This concerns the tail not already settled by provider VAD, not every utterance.
findings.recommendation: Separate ending audio input from completing transcription. Retain generation-scoped handlers until final/closed or a bounded failure deadline; retain unsettled text with an explicit state. Test release followed by final through the composed host/relay/session.

findings.title: A delayed voice start reply consumes audio from the next hold
findings.description: If hold A is released before its start reply and hold B begins before that reply arrives, start resets the only queue and stop intent. The reply for A is accepted as the currently open hold, and queued B audio is labelled session A. The later B reply changes the ID again. Ordered replies are sufficient; no network reordering is required. The channel tracks refs but omits request identity from voiceStarted. The server replaces its active session on each start, so mislabelled frames may be discarded rather than transcribed.
findings.recommendation: Carry a hold/request generation through voiceStart and its callback, and preserve or explicitly cancel each pending hold. Route audio, stop intent and completion to the matching generation; test overlapping holds with delayed ordered replies.

findings.title: Capture discards recorder bytes flushed by its requested stop
findings.description: The Node adapter sends SIGINT specifically to flush buffered recorder audio, but capture sets stopped before signalling and drops every later stdout chunk. Session release immediately flushes only already-delivered bytes and closes transcription. Bytes buffered before key release are therefore discarded if they arrive during recorder shutdown. This is distinct from rejecting a final transcript after successful upload (finding 09).
findings.recommendation: Represent stop-requested and drained as separate capture states. Deliver buffered bytes through recorder exit, then flush the aggregator and commit transcription, with bounded forced cleanup and hold identity. Replace contradictory isolated expectations with a composed drain-before-commit test.

findings.title: Provider meters discard the server semantic window contract

findings.title: Log refresh captures old header offsets after replacing them
findings.description: setLogs replaces eventStarts and then assigns previousStarts from the replacement. For a non-live reader, its old-header/new-header delta therefore cancels back to the old absolute chat offset. When a bounded transcript drops older rows, the same offset points at different content and moves the reader without a navigation action. Stable event identities and ordering are sufficient; this finding does not depend on event reordering.
findings.recommendation: Capture previous event identity, header offset and within-event position before replacing the projection; resolve that identity in the new projection and define the fallback when it leaves the tail. Test shifted transcript starts, shifted event indices and expired selections, alongside live-follow and unchanged-refresh controls.

findings.title: Lifetime dispatch-latch check copied 8 times with diverged semantics (config-reinterpreted vs memory-authoritative)
findings.description: 'Is the lifetime latch enabled/active' is written out as `case Config.agent_max_dispatches_per_ticket() do max when is_integer(max) and max > 0 -> ...` in record_dispatch_committed, active_trip?/2, lifetime_exhausted?/1, persisted_lifetime/1, dispatch_latch_status/2, plus a `max > 0` variant in dispatch_latch_statuses/2, plus IssueSync's own lifetime_latch_status/2 and persisted_latch_status/2. The copies disagree: Dispatcher.active_trip?(%{tripped: :lifetime}) re-checks `lifetime >= max` against the CURRENT config, so lowering or disabling the cap reopens dispatch; IssueSync treats an in-memory trip as authoritative ('do not reinterpret an already-recorded latch through the current cap') and refuses to resolve the error attention while it is not :inactive; AutoResume uses Dispatcher.dispatch_latch_status (config-based). After a config change the dispatcher re-dispatches a ticket while IssueSync still reports 'lifetime latch is still active; Executor action is required'. Every copy also reads the whole dispatch-budgets.json file (DispatchBudgetStore.lifetime -> JsonStore.read) per call; IssueSync reaches it for every polled issue on every poll when the latch is enabled.
findings.recommendation: Extract Aiur.Orchestrator.DispatchBudget (thrash window + lifetime latch) owning one `latch_status(state_budget, issue_id, config, persisted)` with a single, documented rule for config changes; make IssueSync, AutoResume and StatusReport call it. Read the persisted lifetimes once per poll (the batch `lifetimes/0` already exists) and pass the map in.

findings.title: Needs-attention alerts with no resolution path latch in the attention feed forever
findings.description: AlertFeed keeps an attention active until a matching `<topic>.resolved` alert is written (AlertTopic.resolved_attention_key). In this unit these needs_attention topics have no resolver anywhere in src/lib: ticket.X.agent.attention.merged_pr_reconciliation_failed, .merge_terminal_write_failed, .review_rework_refused, .lifetime_latch_write_failed, .stranded-requeued, .state-label-missing, .state-label-missing-no-evidence; ticket.X.agent.model_fallback_waiting, .thrash_circuit_open, .review_feedback_delivery_deferred, .provider_delivery_failed, .auto_resume_exhausted, ticket.X.github-budget.escalation; system.ci_readiness.not_ready / .unavailable; system.dispatch.todo_capacity_exceeded (sync_todo_capacity_alert only flips the flag back); recent_merge_store.persistence_failed (outside the ticket./system. namespaces, so attention_key/1 returns nil and it can never be collapsed or resolved). Two resolvable alerts leak too: choose_issues prunes dispatch_declines with Map.take/2 without emitting the .resolved that clear_dispatch_decline would emit, so a ticket that leaves the candidate list keeps its dispatch-declined attention; and stranded-requeued is deduped against 'already active', so once it fires a second strand of the same ticket never alerts. Result: the Executor's attention list accumulates stale entries that no code path clears, and a real recurrence can be hidden behind the stale one.
findings.recommendation: Give every needs_attention emit an owner that resolves it: a small AttentionLatch helper (emit/resolve/reconcile-against-feed) used by all sites; resolve per-ticket attentions when the ticket leaves the poll or reaches a terminal state; emit .resolved from the dispatch_declines prune; rename recent_merge_store.persistence_failed into the system. namespace and resolve it on the next successful persistence. Add a CI check that every literal topic emitted with needs_attention: true has a .resolved counterpart or an explicit allowlist entry.

findings.title: Submodules call back into the Aiur.Orchestrator facade, which only forwards to their siblings (dependency cycles)
findings.description: Aiur.Orchestrator aliases and calls these modules, and they call back into Aiur.Orchestrator: CommentPolling 9 call sites (note_github_connectivity_*, note_github_poll_interval -> TrackerHealth), CommentWake 7 (clear_session_handle -> WorkspaceCleanup, terminate_running_issue -> AgentTeardown, reactivate_issue -> PauseResume, enqueue_event_digest_item -> OperatorMessages, schedule_poll_cycle_start -> Lifecycle), IssueSync 7 (running_worker_host), OperatorMessages 3 (reactivate_issue, resume_paused_issue), AgentTeardown 2 (cancel_ci_wait_rewake -> CiLifecycle, refresh_tracked_set -> TrackedSet), GithubBudgetPause 1, Dispatcher 2 (retry_candidate_issue? is a defdelegate to DispatchPolicy, which Dispatcher also calls directly at line 1896). The facade entries are one-line forwards, so every such call is a cycle through the top module. Some siblings bypass the facade for the same function (CiLifecycle calls OperatorMessages.enqueue_event_digest_item directly; CommentWake calls it through the facade).
findings.recommendation: Make the facade a pure GenServer boundary: callbacks delegate down, submodules never call up. Replace each back-call with a direct call to the owning sibling (TrackerHealth, WorkspaceCleanup, PauseResume, OperatorMessages, CiLifecycle, TrackedSet). Add `mix xref graph --format cycles` (or a boundary lint) to CI for lib/aiur/orchestrator.

findings.title: Debounced/latched alert state machine hand-copied at least ten times, already drifted
findings.description: Each of prewarm_blocked, tracker_preflight, contradictory_state_labels, dependency circular wait, fleet capacity starved, decision_store_unavailable, capacity_starved, firehose truncation, draft-stall and parked-ready alerts re-implements: since-timestamp debounce, `*_alert_active` flag, `*_resolution_emitted` flag, check AlertFeed for a restart-surviving attention, emit on :ok else keep state, emit .resolved.
