findings.title: Full alert-ledger reads inside the Orchestrator on every poll; read errors silently read as 'no alerts'
findings.description: AlertFeed.list/1 reads every ledger path from disk, parses JSONL, sorts, collapses and filters. It runs inside the Orchestrator GenServer at least twice per poll: IssueSync.sync_polled_issue_state rebuilds active_attention_topics from a full list, and the firehose truncation reconcile calls AlertFeed.active_system_attention?/1 (another full list) on every non-truncated tick. Other clear_* helpers call it on state transitions. read_alerts/2 wraps parsing in `rescue _ -> []`, so a corrupt or unreadable ledger looks like an empty feed: active_attention? turns false everywhere and dedupe-by-active-attention sites re-emit, while restart-surviving resolves are skipped.
findings.recommendation: Keep an in-memory index of active attention topics in the alerting service (updated on emit/resolve, rebuilt once at boot) and expose active?(topic) as an ETS read. Surface ledger read failures as a system health condition instead of an empty list.

findings.title: Three cross-process file-lock implementations with different stale-lock safety
findings.description: ControlLifecycleStore hand-rolls a ~160-line lock: hard-link publish, owner record with host/OS pid/process identity, stale break only when the owner is dead, fingerprint re-check before removing an invalid lock. Executor.Claims has its own File.open(:exclusive) lock whose stale break removes any lock older than @lock_stale_after_seconds by mtime alone, which can remove a live but slow holder's lock. AlertLedger uses :global.register_name, which only serializes processes in one BEAM cluster. The safer algorithm exists but is private to one store.
findings.recommendation: Extract the ControlLifecycleStore algorithm into Aiur.FileLock.with_lock(path, fun, opts) and use it for Executor.Claims and any other JSON store with read-modify-write.

findings.title: Best-effort stores always return :ok, so `:ok =` call sites are inert and durable-state loss is log-only
findings.description: CIApprovalStore.save/3 and ControlLifecycleStore.save/1 rescue every error, log a warning and return :ok. Callers write `:ok = CIApprovalStore.save(...)` / `:ok = ControlLifecycleStore.save(...)`, which reads as a durability assertion but can never fail. A persistently unwritable state dir therefore loses CI approved heads (the human-review replay guard ci_head_approved?/3 depends on them after restart) and the control-request audit journal with no alert; without --debug the warning is written nowhere. GlobalPauseStore, by contrast, returns {:error, _} and its caller surfaces it.
findings.recommendation: Return {:error, reason} from both stores, track consecutive failures in the store, and raise a resolvable system attention (e.g. system.persistence.<store>.failed) after N failures; remove the misleading `:ok =` matches.

findings.title: Orchestrator init hard-matches GlobalPauseStore.save, which can fail: --pause with an unwritable state dir crashes boot
findings.description: initial_global_pause/1 does `:ok = GlobalPauseStore.save(next)` whenever the --pause launch flag is set, in both the load-ok and load-error branches. save/1 returns {:error, {:path_unavailable, _}} when the decision state dir cannot be resolved and {:error, {:write_failed, ...}} on a write error, so a MatchError aborts Orchestrator.init and the supervisor restart loop takes the app down. Without --pause the same failure deliberately boots globally paused, which is the intended fail-safe; with --pause the operator asked for exactly that state and gets a crash instead.
findings.recommendation: Treat a failed save in init as 'paused, persistence degraded': keep the paused state, record the error, raise a system attention, and never MatchError in init.

findings.title: CommandScan drops commands beyond the per-cycle cap while advancing the cursor past them; publish results ignored
findings.description: do_scan_pr_commands computes `newest` over every PR comment seen and advances github_command_scan_since to newest-1s, but publish_command_hits keeps only the first @command_scan_pull_requests_per_poll (25) commanded PRs sorted by PR number and logs the rest. Commands on dropped PRs that are older than the new cursor are never read again (the next request uses a different `since`, so the held-body 304 replay described in the moduledoc does not cover them). Publisher.publish/3's result is discarded by Enum.each, so a filtered or refused publish is also lost once the cursor moves. Separately, command_scan_review_comments/3 and command_scan_issue_comments/3 are the same function with a different fetcher key and log label, and remember_list/3 is a copy of GithubCommentsPoller.remember_list/3.
findings.recommendation: Advance the cursor only to the newest comment that was actually published (or keep a per-PR backlog), check Publisher results, and collapse the two stream fetchers into one parameterized function. Move remember_list/unchanged_list into a shared ResourceStore helper used by both CommandScan and GithubCommentsPoller.

findings.title: CiLifecycle duplicates the draft-stall and parked-ready alert machinery and four tracker-transition functions
findings.description: Draft-stall and parked-ready alerts each have their own reconcile/emit/resolve/put/log_error/ensure_seeded functions that differ only in topic suffix, message text and the classifier; about 250 lines where one parameterized PR-alert latch would do. transition_ci_ticket/3, transition_ci_pass/3, transition_ci_failure/3 and transition_ci_wait_fallback/2 each repeat 'fence check -> Tracker.update_issue_state(to_string(issue.id || issue.identifier), X, expected_state_opts(issue)) -> on error Logger.warning and keep state'. The tracker key prefers issue.id while ci_target_for_issue/1 (used for every lifecycle map key) prefers identifier, so the module mixes two identities for the same ticket.
findings.recommendation: Extract `transition(state, issue, to_state, on_ok)` used by all four; extract a PrAlert latch parameterized by {name, classify_fn, message_fn} (or reuse the latch from orch-a-09); pick one ticket key (identifier) for both tracker writes and lifecycle maps.

findings.title: ci_lifecycle is an untyped grab-bag map that also stores the Dispatcher's candidate-list cache
findings.description: state.ci_lifecycle holds approved_heads, test_failure_heads, base_repair_invalidations, rewakes, draft_stall_alerts, parked_ready_alerts and poll_cache. poll_cache mixes per-target projections (string keys) with two atom-keyed list caches, one of which (:candidate_list_cache) belongs to Dispatcher's candidate fetch and has nothing to do with CI. prune_ci_lifecycle_state has to special-case both atoms (keep_shared_list_caches/2) so a CI prune does not wipe the dispatcher's ETag cache. base_repair_invalidations is read in both atom-key and string-key shapes (`%{repair_state: :repairing}` and `%{"repair_state" => "repairing"}`) because the in-memory and reloaded forms differ.
findings.recommendation: Define %CiLifecycle.State{} with typed fields; move :candidate_list_cache to a Dispatcher-owned field (or a per-poll cache struct); normalize base_repair_invalidations to one shape at load time in CIApprovalStore.

findings.title: Four dependency-injection styles, including functions smuggled inside event payloads and :persistent_term test hooks
findings.description: Test seams are injected four different ways: (1) keyword `*_fun` options (mark_pr_merged_issue_done reads 10 of them; sync_polled_issue_state has 5 arities to thread injected funs); (2) Application env read in production code (:build_gate_status_override, :github_quota_status_override, :human_review_ready_verifier, :github_client_module, :comment_rework_max_attempts, :comment_rework_retry_delay_ms, :operator_message_call_timeout_ms, :github_budget_wake_jitter_ms, :control_lifecycle_store_path, :global_pause_store_path), which forces the whole test suite onto non-async cases; (3) :persistent_term.put hooks in AutoSubscriptions (each put triggers a global literal-area GC scan); (4) functions carried inside the event map itself: CommentWake reads :issue_state_fetcher, :open_pr_fetcher, :unresolved_threads_fetcher and :emit_alert_fun off the incoming event, so production event payloads are part of the test API. AutoResume.schedule/4 is overloaded twice at the same arity (keyword list vs function), and OperatorMessages exports coalesce_for_test/2.
findings.recommendation: Adopt one style: a behaviour-backed deps struct (e.g. %Orchestrator.Deps{tracker:, alerts:, membership:, clock:}) held in State and replaced in tests, or Mox behaviours for Tracker/Alerts/Membership. Remove functions from event payloads and Application-env overrides from production modules.

findings.title: Dispatch functions return only State; callers infer outcomes by diffing claimed/retry maps, and worker-capacity refusals are silent
findings.description: do_dispatch_issue/5 and dispatch_issue/5 return State. dispatch_prevalidated_issue/2 reconstructs the outcome with a 5-branch cond over next_state (claimed? latch? retry_attempts? model_fallback_waiting? thrash trip?) and falls back to :dispatch_not_started; AutoResume.do_resume/5 and the startup-todo alert repeat the claimed-before/after diff. Any new refusal branch silently maps to :dispatch_not_started. dispatch_to_worker/5 returns state unchanged for :no_worker_capacity (Logger.debug) and :preferred_worker_unavailable (Logger.warning) without recording a dispatch decline, so the status board shows no reason.
findings.recommendation: Have the dispatch pipeline return {outcome, state} with an explicit outcome type ({:started, entry} | {:declined, reason} | {:deferred, reason}); record declines for worker-capacity refusals.

findings.title: CommentPolling hand-rolls a ~400-line process-ownership protocol with unbounded receives in the Orchestrator
findings.description: The async comment poll uses an owner process registered in a Registry, a poll process started on a :start message, a guard handshake ({:github_comment_poll_started, ...}, {:start_owned_poll, ...}, {:github_comment_poll_guarding, ...}, {:release_owned_poll, ...}, {:stop_owned_poll, ...}), trap_exit toggling, and reap_process_tree/2 which walks Process.info(:links) recursively and kills every linked process. terminate_poll/1 runs in the Orchestrator (via abandon_poll on the dispatch path and in terminate/2) and blocks in `receive` with no `after` clause. The protocol exists to bound a Task.async_stream fan-out, which Task.Supervisor.async_nolink + Task.shutdown(task, :brutal_kill) and a per-request timeout already provide.
findings.recommendation: Run the poll under a dedicated DynamicSupervisor/Task.Supervisor with `async_nolink`, keep only {ref, pid, started_at} in State, use Task.shutdown/2 for abandonment, and add `after` bounds to any receive left in the Orchestrator.

findings.title: Blocking I/O and synchronous calls inside Orchestrator callbacks on the poll path
findings.description: Inside the GenServer: every CI result that changes approved/test-failure/base-repair maps calls persist_ci_lifecycle_state -> JsonStore.write! (several writes per poll are possible), and each CI poll reads the whole approval store (merge_journaled_base_repairs -> CIApprovalStore.load). Idle-terminal verification calls MembershipLifecycle.observe -> CurrentRunMembership.observe with a 5,000 ms timeout for up to 25 issues per poll. Every control-request transition persists the journal through a file lock that can Process.sleep for up to 5,000 ms. The merged-PR route runs LocalHold.run around a tracker read and write, which waits out local budget holds in the Orchestrator process.
findings.recommendation: Batch CI lifecycle persistence to once per poll (dirty flag), move journal writes to a writer process (cast + periodic flush), make membership observations async casts with a reconciliation retry, and run LocalHold-waiting work in a Task that reports back.

findings.title: ControlLifecycle keeps its own pause-reason enum that is missing live reasons, so restored rejection conditions are dropped
findings.description: PauseResume records a rejection condition with `pause_reason: Map.get(running_entry, :paused_reason)`. ControlLifecycle.restore only accepts pause reasons from its private pause_reasons/0 list, which lacks :github_budget_hold, :agent_pause_request and :input_required (all set as paused_reason elsewhere: PauseResume.@input_pause_reasons, OperatorMessages.pause_clearance/1, GithubBudgetPause). After a daemon restart, restore_rejection_condition/1 returns nil for those rejections and the audit journal silently loses why the control was rejected. Pause reasons are enumerated separately in at least four places (ControlLifecycle, PauseResume, OperatorMessages.pause_clearance, State.@non_reserving_pause_reasons).
findings.recommendation: Define one Aiur.Orchestrator.PauseReason module (list, classification: input/operator/system/reserving, clearance text) and derive the ControlLifecycle allowlist from it; add a test that every reason PauseResume can set round-trips through ControlLifecycle.dump/restore.

findings.title: Atom/string dual-key reads repeated at every consumer instead of normalizing at the boundary
findings.description: Event payloads, subscriptions, persisted JSON and GitHub PR maps arrive with atom keys in-process and string keys after a JSON round trip. Instead of normalizing once, at least 14 consumers read both (`Map.get(x, :k) || Map.get(x, "k")`), and each new field needs another pair. The comments at comment_wake.ex:1378-1380 and auto_subscriptions.ex:307-309 acknowledge the pattern. A missed pair fails silently (nil).
findings.recommendation: Decode events into structs (%Aiur.Events.Event{}, %CommentPayload{}) at the Exchange/SubscriptionStore boundary and decode persisted JSON with explicit schemas at load; consumers pattern-match on atoms only.

findings.title: CI terminal event 'filtered' after the tracker transition is only logged: the agent resumes without the CI verdict
findings.description: transition_ci_pass/3 and transition_ci_failure/3 write the tracker state first, then publish_ci_terminal_event/4. If Publisher returns :filtered the digest item is never enqueued and only a Logger.warning is written; the ticket is already in in-progress or rework, so the agent is resumed/redispatched without the failing checks and excerpt. The dedup key is per head SHA, and the CI poll no longer covers the ticket after the transition, so nothing re-derives the event.
findings.recommendation: On :filtered, enqueue the digest item directly (the payload is already built) or raise a ticket attention; add a test that a filtered publish still leaves a queue item for the agent.

findings.title: Test layout does not mirror modules; some modules are effectively untested in isolation; cross-process assert_receive with 100ms default
findings.description: CiLifecycle (1708 lines) and OperatorMessages (1148) have no mirrored test file: CiLifecycle is tested by a 1733-line test/aiur/orchestrator_ci_lifecycle_test.exs outside the module path, and OperatorMessages behaviour is spread over ten files (core_test, decision_store_test, dashboard_live_test, operator_send_timeout_test, ...). AgentTeardownTest is 9 lines and asserts only terminate_task(nil) == :ok; terminate_running_issue/3 and deactivate_running_issue/2 are covered only indirectly. dispatcher_test.exs:426 and :499 use `assert_receive {:agent_runner_run, ...}` with the 100 ms default for a message sent from the runner function, which Dispatcher starts under Task.Supervisor.start_child (a different process), so the assertion races the task scheduler under load. findings.recommendation: Mirror test files per module before the carve (tests move with their module), add direct AgentTeardown tests for terminate/deactivate, and give cross-process assert_receive an explicit timeout (e.g. 1_000).

findings.title: Correlated resume keeps paused_reason for reasons outside a hard-coded list; the next worker pause is misattributed
findings.description: When a resume request is applied and the worker reports :working, paused_reason is cleared only by maybe_clear_control_owned_pause/3 (9 listed reasons), clear_agent_pause_on_work/2 (:agent_pause_request) and reset_duration_clock_if_capped/4 (:max_agent_duration). :usage_limit_exhausted (resumed by RateLimitFallback :resume), :rate_limit_fallback_recovery, :before_run_failure, :worker_pause_unknown and :automatic_pause survive on a :working entry, so status rows show a pause_reason for a working agent. worker_pause_reason/4 prefers the entry's stored paused_reason over the worker-reported payload kind, so the next uncorrelated worker pause (for example kind :input_required) is recorded as :usage_limit_exhausted. put_usage_limit_reset/4 then drops the reset time, and RateLimitFallback.usage_pause_recovered?/3 can auto-resume an agent that asked for human input as soon as ModelAvailability confirms the backend.
findings.recommendation: On an applied resume to :working, clear paused_reason unless the reason is explicitly owned by another subsystem, and let the worker-reported kind win over a stored reason when no request correlates. Test: usage-limit pause -> correlated resume -> worker pause with kind :input_required -> assert paused_reason == :input_required and RateLimitFallback.decide/3 == :noop.

findings.title: Orchestrator control-call client copied 7 times; the #1634 fix exists in only one copy
findings.description: Every control surface wraps GenServer.call to the Orchestrator with its own whereis/catch helper. PauseResume's copy distinguishes a crash inside a live Orchestrator ({:orchestrator_call_failed, reason}) from a missing daemon (:unavailable), because laundering every exit to :unavailable told operators the daemon was down when it was not (#1634). The other copies still map every non-timeout exit to :unavailable (and StatusReport.list_*_api maps even timeouts to []). Timeouts also differ: configurable :control_api_call_timeout_ms (PauseResume), hard-coded 5_000 (Slots, PriorityControl, Interrupts), 10_000 (RemoteControlMode), caller-passed (OperatorMessages).
findings.recommendation: Extract Aiur.Orchestrator.ControlClient.call(server, request, opts) with the PauseResume exit taxonomy and one configurable timeout; replace all copies. The client-side functions (pause_agent/1, set_remote_control/2, prioritize_agent/1, max_concurrent_agents/0, status_api/0 ...) move with it.

findings.title: Local GitHub budget-hold error shapes are parsed in five places with different coverage
findings.description: The same set of error terms (raw {:aiur, :locally_held, hold}, {:github, :local_hold, _}, legacy {:github, :transport, %{reason: ...}}, {:workspace_github_connectivity_failed, _, inner}, {:github_auth_preflight_failed, %{classification: :local_hold}}) is recognised by separate hand-written clauses. findings.title: Retry exhaustion of agent failures is recorded and alerted as a tracker failure
findings.description: schedule_issue_retry/4's give-up branch (agent crashed/startup failed max_retry_attempts times) releases the claim through record_claim_release/3 and emit_claim_released_alert/6, which were written for the retry-poll path. claim_release_reason/1 collapses every non-rate-limit cause to :tracker_retry_exhausted, which is stored in state.released_claims and rendered by StatusReason as 'claim released: tracker retry exhausted'. The alert text hard-codes 'after 3 tracker failures' (@max_retry_poll_failures) even though the caller passes the agent failure count. This is the 'collapse to a specific cause' pattern AGENTS.md forbids: the atom flows into the JSON envelope and logs.
findings.recommendation: Pass the release origin explicitly (:agent_retry_exhausted vs :tracker_poll_exhausted) and classify unknown reasons to a cause-neutral :unknown with the raw reason kept in details; format the alert count from the actual origin. Test both paths and assert released_claims[issue].cause.

findings.title: Backend-swap redispatch implemented four times; the lifecycle-fence safety exists in only one
findings.description: Four flows tear down a running agent and redispatch the same issue: RateLimitFallback.redispatch, RemoteControlMode promote/demote, PauseResume completed-entry replacement, and RetryEngine.handle_active_retry. Each has its own admission adapter, 'did it start' check and retry fallback. RateLimitFallback keeps a parked copy of the entry (with lifecycle_fence) until the replacement is admitted, 'so a failed fallback never turns an authoritative queue claim into an unfenced, unrecoverable ticket'. RemoteControlMode deletes the entry (drop_redispatch_entry) before dispatch, so a failed RC redispatch loses the fence exactly as the RateLimitFallback comment warns. Private helpers are literally copied: live_running_entry?/1 (3 copies), redispatch_admission (2 copies with different arity), ensure_redispatch_started (2 copies).
findings.recommendation: Extract one Redispatch.swap(state, running_entry, relabeled_issue, opts) that owns admission, teardown ordering, staged safety entry, start verification and retry fallback; make the four callers supply only the relabel and the reason.

findings.title: Submodules call back through the Orchestrator facade, creating dependency cycles the carve must break
findings.description: Orchestrator delegates to the unit's modules, and those modules call back into Orchestrator for functions that are themselves one-line delegations to siblings (e.g. Reconciler -> Orchestrator.resume_paused_issue -> PauseResume.resume_paused_issue, although Reconciler already aliases PauseResume). Counts of `Orchestrator.<fun>` calls: reconciler 20, push_routing 4, retry_engine 4, remote_control_mode 3, pr_anchored 2, status_report 1, tracker_health 1; orchestrator.ex references PauseResume 30x, StatusReport 22x, Slots 10x. Callers are inconsistent: TrackerHealth.note_github_connectivity_failure is called via the facade (comment_polling.ex:60,165,964) and directly (ci_lifecycle.ex:390,465,540; dispatcher.ex:531). State, the data module, calls StatusReport.notify_dashboard and PauseResume.reset_last_codex_timestamp, so it cannot be a leaf.
findings.recommendation: Make Orchestrator a GenServer shell only: submodules call siblings directly, never the facade. Move State's handle_* callbacks (handle_worker_runtime_info, handle_live_conversation_restart, handle_session_execution_info, note_agent_activity) out of State into a RuntimeInfo module so State has no outbound dependencies. Enforce with a boundary check (e.g. xref graph --fail-above or the boundary library).

findings.title: State is a ~100-field god struct and the running entry is an untyped map with ~60 keys written by 16 modules
findings.description: State carries about 100 top-level fields spanning polling, capacity, CI lifecycle, comment polling, GitHub connectivity, alert latches, decision gating, rework bounds and control lifecycle; Credo's StructFieldAmount check is disabled for it. The @type has drifted from defstruct (contradictory_state_label_tickets and contradictory_state_label_alert_active are in the struct but not the type). Running entries are plain maps; across the unit roughly 60 distinct keys are read or written (identifier, issue, pid, ref, control.{status,generation,version,application_confirmation,can_interrupt}, paused_reason, pending_pause_reason, paused_at, started_at, pending_auto_resume, blocker_pause, blocker_pause_generation, consumed_unblocks, github_budget_pause*, usage_limit_reset_at, interrupted_turn_observed_at, runtime_terminal_failure, runtime_health_sample, rate_limit_fallback_*, redispatch_safety, lifecycle_fence, label_divergence_*, before_run_resume_*, last_codex_*, agent_*_tokens, session_execution, live_conversation*, repl_*, headless_*, telemetry_attempt_id ...). 16 modules write state.running directly (58 write sites: pause_resume 17, reconciler 10, push_routing 6, state 4, lifecycle_fence 4, ...). Missing-key bugs such as orch-b-02 follow directly, and State.find_issue_id_for_ref/2 uses a single-clause fn that raises on any entry without :ref.
findings.recommendation: Introduce %RunningEntry{} with @enforce_keys for identity/runtime fields and nested sub-structs per concern (control, blocker pause, budget pause, fallback, divergence, telemetry), and a RunningRegistry API (put/update/fetch_by_identifier) that is the only writer of state.running. Split State into per-subsystem sub-structs (poll, capacity, ci, comments, alerts, control) owned by the module that mutates them.

findings.title: Every Codex update runs a full dashboard projection, ETS copy and PubSub broadcast inside the Orchestrator
findings.description: handle_codex_worker_update/3 calls StatusReport.notify_dashboard/1 for every streamed agent event. notify_dashboard builds snapshot_input/1 (Map.take + struct! + ControlLifecycle.snapshot_for + snapshot_queue_store, which calls AgentQueueStore.list_pending and list_visible_operator_messages for every running, polled and retrying identifier, i.e. the whole backlog), inserts it into ETS (a full copy), then builds running_summaries/1 over all polled issues plus running entries and broadcasts it. SnapshotPublisher then calls :ets.tab2list every 250 ms, copying the whole input out of ETS before comparing versions, even when nothing changed. Comments in the unit cite Orchestrator mailbox backlogs (#1549, #1684, #1837) - this is the busiest message type feeding that mailbox.
findings.recommendation: Coalesce: mark the state dirty on codex updates and publish on a timer (the publisher already exists) instead of projecting per event; broadcast per-entry token deltas instead of full running summaries; store the version in a separate ETS key (or use :ets.lookup_element on the version position) so the publisher only copies the input when it changed. Measure with the mailbox depth metric SnapshotStore already records before and after.

findings.title: Waiting-for-human sync rebuilds full CLI status rows inside the Orchestrator twice per poll
findings.description: sync_waiting_for_human_episodes/2 calls agent_statuses/1, which calls RepoBase.status (100 ms budget), reads the durable dispatch-budget file (Dispatcher.dispatch_latch_statuses), resolves Config, and makes one SubscriptionStore call per row, all in the Orchestrator process, at the start and at the end of every poll - only to find rows whose waiting_reason is :waiting_for_human. snapshot_payload's own comment says these rows were deliberately removed from the per-change path because they are too expensive to pay continuously (#1837).

findings.title: SnapshotStore rewrites a large :persistent_term value on every projection and on stale reads
findings.description: put_snapshot/4 calls :persistent_term.put with the full snapshot plus the full projected source_state on every completed projection (publisher cadence 250 ms + 50 ms coalescing). Updating an existing persistent_term key triggers a global scan of all processes for references to the old value, which is the documented reason persistent_term is meant for rarely-changing data. maybe_log_timeout/2 and maybe_log_initial_timeout/2 also put on the read path, and publish_global_pause writes another key.
findings.recommendation: Store the snapshot in a protected ETS table (read_concurrency) owned by SnapshotStore; keep persistent_term only for the generation token. Measure GC count/time before and after with :erlang.statistics(:garbage_collection).

findings.title: Every control-lifecycle change does a locked file load/merge/write inside the Orchestrator; failures are only logged
findings.description: persist_control_lifecycle/1 (12 call sites in PauseResume, plus RetryEngine and Lifecycle) calls ControlLifecycleStore.save, which takes a file lock with Process.sleep retries (up to 5 s), loads the journal, merges, and writes JSON - synchronously in the Orchestrator for every request/accept/apply/reject/expire. save/1 always returns :ok and reports lock or write failures with Logger.warning only, so the `:ok =` match at the call sites asserts nothing and a lost control journal is invisible.
findings.recommendation: Persist asynchronously from a dedicated writer process (latest-wins coalescing), return {:error, reason} from save and raise an operator alert on persistent failure. Remove the redundant persist on the {:ignored, _} branches (pause_resume.ex:1818, 1847).

findings.title: PauseResume is a 2,471-line module with 77 public clauses and at least eight responsibilities

findings.title: StatusReport builds dashboard rows and CLI rows with two parallel sets of builders that have drifted
findings.description: running_snapshot/5 vs running_status/4, retry_snapshot/4 vs retry_statuses/1, and idle_issue_snapshot/6 vs idle_status/5 build the same ticket rows for the dashboard and for `aiur status`/`watch`. Both running builders call WaitingReason.for_running with identical attrs; the shapes differ (snapshot rows carry progress, activity_stage, ci_result, backend and priority but no `reason`; status rows carry `reason`, tracker_state and complexity; retry_snapshot has no tracker_paused/pause_reason). Dead parameters remain (idle_issue_snapshot `_terminal_states`, idle_statuses `_running_by_identifier`, and agent_statuses_raw builds running_by_identifier only to pass it there); agent_statuses_and_state/1 returns the state unchanged. idle_reason/2 places WaitingReason atoms in the StatusReason `reason` field, mixing two vocabularies. AGENTS.md requires surfaces the docs call equivalent to agree.
findings.recommendation: Build one canonical row per ticket (Row.running/retry/idle) and derive the dashboard and CLI shapes by projection; move the API client functions out (orch-b-05) and the human-wait alerting out (orch-b-15). Target: StatusReport under 500 lines.

findings.title: PRHealthScanner and ReworkRequeue duplicate their worker scaffolding, including a 304 adapter that reads as 'no reviews'

findings.title: ReworkRequeue alert names the thread-clearance gate as the cause of every re-queue failure

findings.title: Ticket identifier matching uses five different rules
findings.description: State.find_running_by_identifier/2 and find_running_key_by_identifier/2 require `to_string(identifier) == target`. PauseResume.find_issue_id_by_identifier/2 and PushRouting use Issue.identifier_matches?/3, which also accepts a bare number for an identifier ending in '#N'. PriorityControl matches identifier or id with ==; TrackerHealth matches issue_id or identifier; PushRouting.blocker_fetch_identifier/1 splits on '#'. findings.title: Issue-state normalization is reimplemented in at least 12 places with 5 different semantics; the schema's default active_states hits the divergence

The GitHub poller and webhook compare active states through StatePolicy ('In Progress' -> 'in-progress'), but DispatchPolicy.active_state_set uses normalize_issue_state ('in progress'). The schema default active_states is ["Todo", "In Progress"], which is exactly the display-name trap AGENTS.md warns about.

Make the config defaults slug-form (["todo", "in-progress"]), or normalize configured states to slugs at parse time. Add one property test that the poller, webhook, dispatch policy and config validators agree for display names and slugs.

findings.title: Upgrade registry passes an unknown option (timeout:) to Req, which raises; the fail-open rescue turns every version check into 'no notice'
findings.description: Req 0.7.2 (mix.lock) validates options in Req.merge/2 and raises ArgumentError for unregistered ones. The registered list (deps/req/lib/req/steps.ex register_options) has :receive_timeout, :pool_timeout and :request_timeout, but no :timeout. fetch_dist_tags/2 therefore always raises. The rescue returns {:error, %ArgumentError{}}, and by the documented 'fail-open by contract' the notice is suppressed. The upgrade notice has never fired in production. The tests inject a fake transport, so they cannot see this. Blast radius is small (a notice), but the feature is dead and nothing reports it.
findings.recommendation: Use receive_timeout: timeout_ms (plus connect_options: [timeout: ...]) and retry: false. Add one test that calls Transport.Req.fetch_dist_tags against a Req.Test plug or bypass, so the real transport's option handling is exercised. Log (and count) the fail-open error class instead of discarding it.

The rescue returns {:error, %ArgumentError{}}, and by the documented 'fail-open by contract' the notice is suppressed. The upgrade notice has never fired in production. The tests inject a fake transport, so they cannot see this. Blast radius is small (a notice), but the feature is dead and nothing reports it.
claim.evidence: registry.ex:15 `case Req.get(url, timeout: timeout_ms, headers: [accept: "application/json"]) do`; registry.ex:28-29 `rescue error -> {:error, error}`; deps/req/lib/req/request.ex:1124-1129 `raise ArgumentError, "unknown option #{inspect(name)}..."`.
claim.recommendation: Use receive_timeout: timeout_ms (plus connect_options: [timeout: ...]) and retry: false. Add one test that calls Transport.Req.fetch_dist_tags against a Req.Test plug or bypass, so the real transport's option handling is exercised. Log (and count) the fail-open error class instead of discarding it.
claim.refactor_hint: Upgrade package: small and self-contained; good first carve once its transport is tested.

verification.reconciliation_reason: The registry sends timeout: to Req.get and rescues a request error, so an unsupported option can suppress upgrade notices. The dependency option contract was not executed at this snapshot, and the impact is confined to notices.

findings.title: Core current-run projections depend on the web layer (AiurWeb.OperatorControlCenter.UnitsRow/UnitsPolicy, AiurWeb.ObservabilityPubSub)
findings.description: The run summary and outcome read models, which CLIs and status reports also use, compute their unit rows with AiurWeb.OperatorControlCenter.UnitsRow.snapshot/1. They classify rows with AiurWeb.OperatorControlCenter.UnitsPolicy (in_scope?, condition?) and subscribe to AiurWeb.ObservabilityPubSub. Business rules (which unit is live, unfinished or queued) therefore live in the web namespace, and core cannot compile without aiur_web. Across src/lib/aiur, 16 files reference AiurWeb.* (for example alerts.ex, agent_pubsub.ex, orchestrator/snapshot_store.ex, recent_merge_store.ex).
findings.recommendation: Move UnitsRow.snapshot and UnitsPolicy into a core module (for example Aiur.RunUnits) that both the projections and the OCC presenter call. Replace the ObservabilityPubSub subscription with a core PubSub topic that the web layer re-broadcasts. Add a boundary check (the `boundary` library or an xref CI check) that forbids Aiur.* -> AiurWeb.* references.

findings.title: Ownership.Waiter.wait blocks its caller with an unbounded receive; the orchestrator calls it inline on one path
findings.description: Waiter.wait spawns an unlinked, unmonitored subscriber and then does `receive {:workspace_waiter_ready, ^waiter, result} -> result end` with no after clause. If the subscriber crashes (for example Registry.lookup raising because the registry is gone), the caller blocks forever. While the guardian is slow (blocked in Ownership.Store.put, see platform-misc-04), the subscriber resubscribes every 100 ms and the caller keeps waiting. RetryEngine.synchronize_workspace_wait's fallback clause calls it from the Orchestrator process, although the clause above it says 'so the Orchestrator never blocks on a guardian'. OrphanedWorkers already knows it blocks and runs it in a spawned process.
findings.recommendation: Monitor the subscriber and add a deadline to Waiter.wait that returns {:error, :timeout}. Make the orchestrator path always asynchronous (the OrphanedWorkers pattern), with the answer arriving as a message.

findings.title: Daemon-private state paths: 7 copy-pasted leaf helpers, about 13 ad-hoc leaf computations, and AIUR_BG_STATE_DIR with 3 different fallbacks
findings.description: current_run_membership_state_dir, progress_retention_state_dir, usage_ledger_state_dir, usage_aggregate_state_dir, usage_compaction_state_dir, takeover_alert_state_dir and balance_baseline_state_dir are the same 8-line function with a different app-env key and leaf. The root is misnamed decision_state_dir/0, although it is the root for all daemon state, and runtime_state_dir/0 returns that root itself with no leaf. This contradicts the stated 'own leaf so it can never be mistaken for decision state' rule. Other stores compute leaves themselves: ownership store 'workspace-ownership', ci_approval_store, pr_ready_ledger_store, executor_command_attention, dispatch_budget_store, metrics, recent_merge_store, tool_call_ledger/storage, branch_ref_store, resource_store, global_pause_store, webhooks/delivery_log. AIUR_BG_STATE_DIR falls back to `File.cwd!()/.aiur-state` in Paths, to '~/.config/aiur' in the Env schema default, and to $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/aiur in Upgrade.State. The live checkout shows an untracked .aiur-state/ created by the cwd fallback.
findings.recommendation: Replace the 7 functions with one `state_dir(leaf_atom)` backed by a single registry map (leaf name plus app-env override key). Rename decision_state_dir to daemon_state_root. Give decision and runtime state their own leaves (with a one-time migration). Make every store resolve through the registry. Make the AIUR_BG_STATE_DIR fallback single-sourced from Env.Schema.

findings.title: The atom-or-string map key accessor is reimplemented 48 times in 42 files with two different semantics, although two shared helpers exist
findings.description: A regex census of src/lib found 48 definitions or inline uses of 'get key as atom, else as string' across 42 files, for example decision_answer, decision_event, decision_history, decision_revision, decision_sanitizer, decision_store (3), decision_validation, executor_listener, issue_log, usage_envelope (4 variants), run_telemetry sampler (3) and writer, token_accounting, control_lifecycle, and several aiur_web presenters. There are two semantics. `Map.get(m,k) || Map.get(m,str)` falls through when the atom key holds false or nil (Snapshot.row_value, MapAccess.get, ExecutorListener, TokenAccounting). `Map.get(m,k, Map.get(m,str))` respects a present false or nil (Value.get, most decision modules). For boolean fields such as tracker_paused this changes the answer. CurrentRunProjection.Value.get is duplicated byte-for-byte in aiur_web/.../units_row/value.ex:8. TicketObservation uses String.to_atom(key) for the reverse direction.
findings.recommendation: Keep one helper (Aiur.Protocol.MapAccess.fetch/3 with explicit present-false semantics) and delete the rest. Better: normalize external payloads to atom keys once at the boundary (JSON decode or ingress) so internal code never needs dual-key reads.

findings.title: Every workspace operation is implemented twice (Elixir local and SSH shell remote), and the pairs have already drifted
findings.description: Readiness, ready marker, recreate, remove, before_remove hook and git-metadata probing each exist as an Elixir function for local and as an inline shell script for remote. Examples of drift: (a) the ready marker path is the @workspace_ready_marker constant locally but is hard-coded twice in shell ('$workspace/.claude/.aiur-workspace-ready', provisioner.ex:570 and :599); (b) local remove checks Layout.validate_workspace_path before rm -rf, remote remove runs `rm -rf "$workspace"` unchecked; (c) the remote before_remove hook interpolates the raw command (`"  #{command}"`) with no AgentEnvironment.scrub_shell_command and no hook_env, while Hooks.remote_hook_command scrubs and exports env; (d) git-dir containment uses PathSafety locally and `pwd -P` case matching remotely.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a WorkspaceHost behaviour (Local, Ssh) with one operation per verb (readiness, mark_ready, recreate, remove, run_hook, probe_git). Generate the remote scripts from shared constants, and route every remote hook through Hooks.remote_hook_command. Add a parity test per verb that runs the same scenario against Local and a local-sh 'remote' shim.

findings.title: Path containment is implemented four ways; git-dir expansion and discovery are duplicated between GitMetadata and CodexSandboxPolicy
findings.description: Layout.validate_workspace_path does canonicalize plus String.starts_with?(ws <> "/", root <> "/"). GitMetadata.ensure_git_dir_inside_workspace does the same with its own error shapes. CodexSandboxPolicy.path_inside?/2 is a third string-prefix check. Paths and Reconstruction use PathSafety.contained?/2. GitMetadata.local_git_metadata_dir plus expand_git_dir and CodexSandboxPolicy.local_git_metadata_root plus expand_git_dir run the same two `git rev-parse` calls and the same expansion code.
findings.recommendation: Route every containment check through PathSafety.contained?/2 and map its results to domain errors at the call site. Move git-dir discovery into one Aiur.Git.dir/1 used by GitMetadata and the sandbox policy.

findings.title: Provisioner keeps test-only legacy arities whose readiness logic differs from production; readiness is recomputed about 7 times per dispatch with 3 git subprocesses each
findings.description: Production calls only ensure_workspace/5 (workspace.ex:71) and recreate/4 (refresh.ex:80). ensure_workspace/2 (local clause), /3 and /4 and recreate/2 (local clause) have no production callers, yet provisioner_test.exs exercises ensure_workspace(ws, nil) at 179, 192, 209, 223, 239 and 361. The readiness cond appears three times with different outcomes: ensure_workspace/5 and /2 return {:ok, ws, false} for 'dir with .git but not a valid checkout', while workspace_readiness/1 returns {:error, {:workspace_ambiguous, ..., :invalid_git_checkout}}. Checkout.valid_workspace?/1 runs `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `git rev-parse --verify HEAD` and a full `git status --porcelain` (only its exit code is used). One create plus before_run reaches it from ensure_workspace, ensure_workspace_usable, mark_workspace_ready, Refresh.refresh_workspace_readiness, run_before_run_command and ensure_dispatch_ready.
findings.recommendation: Delete the legacy arities and move the tests to ensure_workspace/5. Collapse the three conds into workspace_readiness/1 plus an explicit 'interrupted init tolerated' option. Replace `git status --porcelain` with `git rev-parse --git-dir` (validity) and compute readiness once per dispatch, passing it down instead of re-probing.

findings.title: Two implementations of the $VAR env-reference grammar with different trimming; the one that claims to be the 'single home' is mostly unused
findings.description: Config.EnvRef's moduledoc says it is the 'Single home for the `$VAR` env-reference resolution grammar', but its resolve/2 and reference_name/1 have no production callers. Only normalize_secret/1 is used, by Linear.Config. Schema.finalize_settings and Config use Config.Schema.EnvResolver, which reimplements resolve_env_value, reference_name (env_reference_name) and the regex. Semantics differ: EnvRef.normalize_secret trims, EnvResolver.normalize_secret_value does not, so the same secret with trailing whitespace resolves differently depending on the path.
findings.recommendation: Keep one module (EnvRef), move EnvResolver's path-token helper into it, delete the duplicate, and decide on trimming once (trim secrets).

findings.title: Ticket activity stage/progress vocabulary and phase parsing are copied across 6 modules, and TicketActivity re-sanitizes what TicketObservation already normalized
findings.description: The stage list brainstorm/plan/work/review appears 7 times in 6 files (as atoms and as strings). The progress event names ["progress","progress.checkin","progress.phase"] appear in 3 files. The 'phase.<stage>.<transition>' parser exists 3 times (Projection.phase_source, TicketObservation.parse_stage, TicketHistoryNormalizer.topic_kind). TicketObservation.new already normalizes source, attributes and provenance into safe shapes; TicketActivity.Projection then re-applies safe_source, safe_attributes and safe_provenance to the same struct. findings.recommendation: Create an Aiur.AgentPhase vocabulary module (stages/0, transitions/0, progress_event_names/0, parse_phase_topic/1) and use it everywhere. Let TicketActivity trust the TicketObservation contract (or assert it) instead of re-sanitizing.

findings.title: Membership Reconciler.Snapshot keeps a hand-copied waiting-reason list that has drifted from Orchestrator.WaitingReason, and uses a fixed precedence chain
findings.description: Snapshot.@waiting_reasons has 12 atoms. WaitingReason.t has 20. Reasons not in the copy include :run_paused, :paused_operator, :paused_transient, :provider_limited, :latched_lifetime and :claim_released. A row with such a reason and no matching work_state falls through the lifecycle_for_row precedence chain to the bucket default (:running for running rows, :queued for idle rows). So a provider-limited or lifetime-latched ticket is recorded in durable membership as running. The cancelled-state vocabulary also differs: Snapshot treats only cancelled/canceled as :cancelled, while CurrentRunSummary.Facts also counts not_planned/notplanned.
findings.recommendation: Have WaitingReason export waiting_reasons/0 (or a lifecycle_for/1 mapping) and use it in Snapshot. Put cancelled-state detection in the shared TrackerState module (platform-misc-10). Add a test that every WaitingReason value maps to a deliberate membership lifecycle.

A row with such a reason and no matching work_state falls through the lifecycle_for_row precedence chain to the bucket default (:running for running rows, :queued for idle rows). So a provider-limited or lifetime-latched ticket is recorded in durable membership as running. The cancelled-state vocabulary also differs: Snapshot treats only cancelled/canceled as :cancelled, while CurrentRunSummary.Facts also counts not_planned/notplanned.
claim.evidence: snapshot.ex:7-20 `@waiting_reasons [:waiting_for_human, ..., :unresponsive]` (12 entries); waiting_reason.ex:13-33 @type t lists 20 values; snapshot.ex:105 `if(normalize_state(state) in ["cancelled", "canceled"], ...)` vs facts.ex:8 `@cancelled_states ~w(cancelled canceled not_planned notplanned)`.
claim.recommendation: Have WaitingReason export waiting_reasons/0 (or a lifecycle_for/1 mapping) and use it in Snapshot. Put cancelled-state detection in the shared TrackerState module (platform-misc-10). Add a test that every WaitingReason value maps to a deliberate membership lifecycle.
claim.refactor_hint: Orchestrator <-> membership boundary: the mapping from orchestrator status to membership lifecycle should be owned by one side and exported.

findings.title: Health and freshness are collapsed to wrong or unknown causes: a read-only but intact DecisionStore reads as 'data unavailable', and there is no single health type
findings.description: StoreReader.health/1 maps :writable to available, {:corrupt,_,_} to partial, and everything else to unavailable_health() ('Retained Decision data unavailable'). DecisionStore goes read-only with its in-memory data intact for {:repair, reason} and {:lifecycle_append_failed, type, reason}. Surfaces then label complete data as unavailable while still returning it (read_one returns {:ok, decision, unavailable_health}). CurrentRunProjection.Value.health/1 has a `_ -> :unavailable` catch-all, and health and freshness travel as bare atoms, tagged tuples and maps depending on the source (SourceFallback writes {:unavailable, :read_failed} for membership, :unavailable for status, %{status: :stale} or :stale for freshness). This forces every reader to accept all shapes.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit read-only-intact state (for example :read_only with a reason list) to StoreReader and render it as 'complete, not writable'. Define one Health struct (status, reasons, observed_at) and one Freshness struct for all current-run and decision sources, and replace the catch-all with :unknown per the AGENTS.md collapsed-cause rule.

findings.title: Linear client duplicates its GraphQL selection, silently truncates blockers at 50, re-queries the viewer on every poll, and ships test seams in production
findings.description: (a) @query and @query_by_ids repeat the same 34-line issue selection; use a GraphQL fragment. (b) inverseRelations(first: $relationFirst) is fetched with relationFirst: 50 and no pageInfo, so blockers beyond 50 are dropped silently (fix-by-limit family). (c) With assignee 'me', routing_assignee_filter runs resolve_viewer_assignee_filter, a viewer GraphQL request, on every fetch_candidate_issues and fetch_issue_states_by_ids call; the result is never cached. (d) Four public *_for_test functions. (e) Config access is split: Linear.Config (trims project_slug, has its own endpoint default), Client (reads settings.tracker.linear.* raw) and Workspace.Layout.repo_segment (raw project_slug) disagree on whitespace. (f) The api_key/project_slug cond is duplicated in fetch_candidate_issues and fetch_issues_by_states.
findings.recommendation: Use a shared fragment; paginate relations or at least flag truncation when hasNextPage; cache the viewer id per api_key; move test seams behind an injected graphql_fun option; route all Linear config reads through Linear.Config.

findings.title: Memory tracker keeps state in Application env with non-atomic read-modify-write and inconsistent mutation semantics, so tests cannot reach real behaviours
findings.description: The in-memory tracker used by tests and local development keeps issues in Application.get_env(:aiur, :memory_tracker_issues) and mutates them with get_env then put_env, which races under concurrent callers. The mutations are also inconsistent: update_issue_state/2 only sends an event and does not change state, update_issue_state/3 with expected_state does change it, add_label only sends an event, and remove_label mutates. A test that adds a label and then polls never sees the label, which is a fixture that cannot reach the behaviour under test.
findings.recommendation: Back the memory tracker with an Agent or ETS table owned by a test-started process, make every write mutate state consistently (state and labels), and send the notification after the mutation.

findings.title: Config.Schema.Agent is a 45-field grab-bag in a file that also defines Codex, Claude and Rtk, with fields and cast list maintained by hand
findings.description: agent.ex (476 lines) defines 4 modules. The Agent section mixes dispatch routing, the load governor (max_load_average, target_load_average, load_ramp_step, run_queue_threshold, min_free_memory_mb), the build gate (max_concurrent_builds, build_gate_*), GitHub budget-broker alerting (budget_broker_*), the saturation log and turn limits. Its 38 permitted keys are a second hand-maintained copy of the field list (see platform-misc-01), plus 24 validate_number lines. The Codex-specific CodexSandboxPolicy (347 lines) lives in Config, shells out to git and writes probe files into configured roots at config validation time.
findings.recommendation: Split the agent section by owner (agent.routing, agent.limits, load_governor, build_gate, github.budget_broker) with key aliases for compatibility. One module per file. Move CodexSandboxPolicy to the Codex backend package and make config validation pure (probe roots at dispatch, not parse).

findings.title: Guardian is a hand-rolled spawn/receive loop with 12 near-identical call clauses; one bad receipt halts the Reconciler and with it daemon boot
findings.description: Guardian (759 lines, the largest file in the unit) uses bare spawn/1, not proc_lib or GenServer, so it has no sys debugging, no supervision and no crash reports. Its message loop repeats `{reply, next} = f(state, gen); reply(from, ref, reply); loop(next)` for 12 message kinds, with a separate client-side timeout table in Ownership.timeout_result. The positive-pid predicate `is_integer(&1) and &1 > 0` over descendant_pids is written 5 times (lines 319, 358, 377, 671, 752). Ownership.Reconciler is a GenServer whose only work is init; if any receipt fails Guardian.restore (for example {:invalid_workspace_receipt, _} from a missing key) the reduce_while halts and init returns {:stop, ...}, failing the supervision tree start. AlertFeed.Backfill is the same pattern: a GenServer that starts one unobserved task and then idles forever.
findings.recommendation: Convert Guardian to a :gen_statem (explicit states provisioning/active/reaping/retained) started under a DynamicSupervisor with restart: :temporary. Make the Reconciler quarantine an unrestorable receipt (log and alert) instead of halting boot, and use Task children (restart: :transient) for one-shot boot work.

findings.title: current_run_projections stores its checkpoint inside CurrentRunMembership.Store, copies helpers three ways, and swallows UnitsRow failures without a log
findings.description: The projection 'checkpoint' (full summary and outcome snapshots plus up to 1,000 entries per source) is kept in the Membership Store GenServer's state through put_projection_checkpoint/_fenced, so another subsystem's process holds foreign state so that it survives the projection's restart. Store's API therefore has three projection-only calls. start_task/2 and safe_supervised_start/2 are duplicated in SourceCollector and CheckpointPersistence, both silently falling back to unsupervised Task.start/1. restore_canonical/1 exists in Projector (twice, as canonical_state and restore_canonical with identical bodies) and in CheckpointPersistence. UnitsBuilder.safe_snapshot rescues and catches everything from UnitsRow.snapshot and returns an empty unit set with no log.
findings.recommendation: Give the projection checkpoint its own small holder (an ETS table owned by a supervisor-level process, or a durable file) instead of borrowing Membership.Store. Extract one TaskStarter helper that fails loudly when the task supervisor is missing. Log and count UnitsRow failures.

findings.title: The init wizard bypasses the GitHub transport, and runtime env precedence depends on the init namespace, with a different .env precedence than runtime
findings.description: Init.GitHub.fetch_label_names issues raw Req.get calls to https://api.github.com/repos/.../labels, bypassing Aiur.GitHub.Transport and the budget guard that the same file says the rest of init uses (#2353 comment at 289-292). Aiur.GitHub.Labels already owns label REST access. The runtime module Aiur.Env reads .env files through Aiur.Init.Dotenv.parse/1, so runtime depends on the wizard namespace. Init.Dotenv.load only reads ./.env, while AGENTS.md defines runtime precedence as env, then ./.env, then ~/.aiur/.env with GitHub credentials resolved as a group. `aiur init` can therefore report 'GITHUB_TOKEN not set' when the daemon would find it in ~/.aiur/.env.
findings.recommendation: Move Dotenv to a shared Aiur.Dotenv and have init use Aiur.Env's precedence resolver. Route label listing through GitHub.Labels/Transport.

findings.title: after_run and before_remove hook failures and timeouts are discarded, visible only in Logger output that is off without --debug
findings.description: run_after_run and both maybe_run_before_remove_hook clauses pipe the result into ignore_hook_failure/1, which maps {:error, _} to :ok. The only record is Logger.warning in handle_hook_command_result (and Logger.warning on timeout), which AGENTS.md notes is written nowhere without --debug. A broken after_run (for example one that uploads artifacts or releases external resources) fails on every run with no alert, counter or status field. Remove.remove_issue_workspaces also returns :ok whatever remove/2 returns.
findings.recommendation: Keep the non-fatal semantics but record failures: emit a (rate-limited) warning alert per hook name and ticket, and count failures in run telemetry so the status report shows 'after_run failing N/N'.

findings.title: A terminal membership member ignores every later lifecycle, so a reopened ticket stays 'completed' for the rest of the run
findings.description: Projection.apply_event returns {:ignored, :terminal, state} for any event on a member whose terminal? is true. If a ticket completes (for example it is closed by merge) and is then reopened or moved back to rework in the same run, the reconciler's :running observations are all ignored. The Reconciler counts {:ok, %{status: :terminal}} as success, so the summary keeps reporting the unit as successful_terminal while an agent works it. If this is intended ('first outcome wins'), it is undocumented and has no reopen path.
findings.recommendation: Decide the rule explicitly. If reopen should count, accept a non-terminal event that is newer than the terminal one and record a :reopened transition. Either way document it and add a test.

claim.evidence: Source-contract counterexample: parent timestamp100, cursor200, reply300. Selecting only parents after200 cannot select that parent for reply expansion. No Slack API response or live missed message was observed.
claim.recommendation: Specify a complete reply-discovery strategy independent of the parent's creation timestamp, with bounded pagination and overlap/dedup semantics.
claim.refactor_hint: Make ingestion completeness, processing backlog and resolution evidence separate explicit contracts.
claim.limits: This is an incomplete retrieval recipe, not proof every possible connected Slack tool misses such replies. A tool that directly returns new replies could satisfy the broader contract.

findings.title: Sweep closes a report on landing evidence alone
findings.description: Fix verification accepts a claimed PR merged into the default branch or a claimed commit's ancestry and then closes the feedback item. Neither condition establishes that the change addresses the reported symptom, although closed is documented as resolved and verified.
findings.recommendation: Record landing separately from symptom resolution; require report-specific evidence before resolved close-out and fetch the exact merge identity for the durable record.

findings.title: Media retry states are outside the next run's new-item loop
findings.description: Acknowledgment advances the source cursor before media analysis. Media work is then limited to new items; failures become needs_download or needs_analysis, but no step adds these persisted states back to the next run's media workset despite the promised three attempts across runs.
findings.recommendation: Build the media workset from new items plus retryable persisted states, with explicit attempt accounting and deduplication.

findings.title: Run-telemetry reduction exists three times (Dataset.build, Dataset.merge, Python analytics/reduce.py) and the dedupe/ordering rules have already diverged
findings.description: Summaries calls the Python reducer 'canonical' and the dashboard merges its run-summary.json output via Dataset.merge, while the live boot is reduced by Dataset.build. The three paths disagree: (1) Dataset.build dedupes lifecycle records by event_key including carried segment-roll points (dispatch/pr_opened/pr_merged, #2603) and silences their warnings; Python's _lifecycle_event_key only keys records with source_id/operation_id, so carried internal dispatch points are never deduped and GitHub-anchored ones warn; (2) Dataset.merge dedupes only by record_id and never re-applies the event-key dedupe, so carried replicas coming from summaries survive into re-derived intervals; (3) Elixir orders lifecycle pairing by source_line within one stream (causal_pair_order) while Python sorts by (timestamp_ms, boot_id, sequence). The carried-point constant and lifecycle pair key are also copied between Writer and Dataset.
findings.recommendation: Choose one reducer. Either make the Python package consume Elixir-produced summaries (Summaries writes the Dataset map directly on segment roll) or make Elixir call the Python reducer for every path; in either case move dedupe into a single function used by build and merge. Extract `RunTelemetry.Schema` (record kinds, carried point events, pair key, event-key rule) shared by Writer and Dataset, and add a golden-file test that runs both reducers over the same NDJSON and compares intervals.

findings.title: Dependency cycle between the CodingAgent registry and the usage/telemetry/meter modules, much of it at compile time
findings.description: Usage, pricing, meter and account-generation modules read provider families, backends, pricing policies and adapter lists from Aiur.CodingAgent, several via module attributes evaluated at compile time. In the other direction, Aiur.CodingAgent's registry embeds references to Aiur.Usage.PriceTable.Window, the headless usage adapters, RunTelemetry.Lifecycle decoders and ProviderMeterProbe. Any CodingAgent change recompiles the usage/meter modules, and neither side can be extracted into a package without the other.
findings.recommendation: Invert the dependency: define a small `ProviderSpec` behaviour/struct in a leaf package (families, backends, pricing policy, account-generation policy) that CodingAgent implements and the usage/meter/telemetry packages receive at runtime (config or registration at boot). Move adapter lists and telemetry decoders out of CodingAgent into the usage and telemetry packages, which register themselves per provider. Replace compile-time @providers attributes with runtime lookups or a generated catalog.

findings.title: Process-global mutable state across would-be packages: persistent_term churn and process-dictionary bindings
findings.description: Continuity stores every active account-generation binding for every service in one :persistent_term key and rewrites it (inside a cluster-wide :global.trans lock) on every retain/forget, i.e. on every agent session bind/recover/clear. Replacing a persistent term triggers a global scan of all processes, so this is a known BEAM anti-pattern for data that changes per session. Bindings themselves live in the caller's process dictionary (Context), which the meter events module documents as the reason daemon-internal consumers cannot address them. RunTelemetry.Writer publishes its admission atomics in its own process dictionary and callers read the whole dictionary with Process.info/2 on every cast; Lifecycle stores in-flight build/test operation classes in the caller's dictionary keyed by tracker pid and never clears keys whose completion never arrives.
findings.recommendation: Move Continuity into the Owner GenServer's state plus an ETS table owned by a long-lived heir process (survives Owner restarts without persistent_term churn); pass bindings explicitly in the session struct instead of the process dictionary; register the Writer admission counter in a named ETS/`:persistent_term` written once per boot; keep Lifecycle operation state in the session state or an explicit bounded map.

findings.title: RunTelemetry.Writer silently drops records whenever its admission counter is not discoverable (including the whole init window)
findings.description: enqueue_cast/2 is a `with` without an else: if server_pid/1 returns nil or admission_counter/1 returns :unavailable, the record is dropped with no cast, no overflow count and no log. GenServer registers the Writer's name before init/1 runs, and init runs Retention.prune (a full-file scan, see telemetry-usage-13) before it calls Process.put(@admission_key, ...). Every record emitted while a Writer is (re)starting, e.g. lifecycle events from running agents after a Writer crash, is therefore lost without trace, unlike queue overflow which is counted and surfaced as a warning record.
findings.recommendation: Create the atomics before any slow work (first line of init, or in the supervisor and pass it in), move boot-time pruning to handle_continue, and count 'writer unavailable' drops in the same atomics so the drained writer emits one warning record for them.

findings.title: Writer.terminate/2 shutdown materialization never runs on shutdown and blocks restarts for up to 30 s on crashes
findings.description: The Writer never calls Process.flag(:trap_exit, true), so a supervisor shutdown kills it without invoking terminate/2; the documented 'best-effort shutdown materialization' of run summaries does not happen on daemon stop. terminate/2 does run when a callback raises, and then it runs Summaries.materialize/0 synchronously with a 30 s timeout before the supervisor can restart the writer (Task.shutdown(:brutal_kill) kills only the Erlang task; the external `analytics/reduce` OS process started by System.cmd is not signalled and may keep running).
findings.recommendation: Decide the intent: if shutdown materialization matters, trap exits and give the child an explicit shutdown timeout, or move materialization to an Application prep_stop hook; otherwise delete terminate/2 and rely on segment-roll materialization. Never run the reducer on the crash path.

findings.title: Telemetry retention and tail reading JSON-decode every line, on the Writer's own process
findings.description: Retention.read_boot_groups streams the entire telemetry file and calls Jason.decode/1 on every line just to find restart markers. It runs inside the Writer GenServer at boot and every prune_interval_bytes (max_bytes/8, min 1 MiB) of appends, so the single writer stalls for a full-file decode repeatedly while callers' casts queue (and overflow is dropped). The current-session tail reader in Dataset decodes each tail line up to three times (boot_id_from_line, segment_boundary_line?, then parse_line).
findings.recommendation: Pre-filter with a cheap binary match (`:binary.match(line, "\"kind\":\"restart\"")`) before decoding, or maintain a sidecar index of group offsets written at each restart/segment marker; run pruning in a supervised Task that hands back the new offset rather than on the Writer; decode each tail line once and reuse the map.

findings.title: Segment-roll summary materialization spawns unbounded, untimed external reducer processes
findings.description: Every segment roll calls Summaries.materialize_async/0, which Task.start's an unsupervised System.cmd of `analytics/reduce --all --all-builds` with no timeout and no guard against a previous run still in progress. Rolls can happen every max_bytes/8 bytes on a busy boot, so concurrent reducers can overlap, each re-reading the whole telemetry stream and rewriting the same summary files. The reducer directory is also looked up relative to the daemon's cwd (`Path.expand("analytics")`), and failures are only Logger.warning.
findings.recommendation: Run materialization in a single supervised worker that coalesces requests (at most one running, one pending), enforces a timeout that kills the OS process (Port with :exit_status / MuonTrap-style), and resolves the reducer path from configuration rather than cwd.

claim.title: Segment-roll summary materialization spawns unbounded, untimed external reducer processes
claim.description: Every segment roll calls Summaries.materialize_async/0, which Task.start's an unsupervised System.cmd of `analytics/reduce --all --all-builds` with no timeout and no guard against a previous run still in progress. Rolls can happen every max_bytes/8 bytes on a busy boot, so concurrent reducers can overlap, each re-reading the whole telemetry stream and rewriting the same summary files. The reducer directory is also looked up relative to the daemon's cwd (`Path.expand("analytics")`), and failures are only Logger.warning.
claim.evidence: summaries.ex:111 `{:ok, {script, args}} -> Task.start(fn -> run_reduce_background(script, args) end)`; :119 `System.cmd(script, args, stderr_to_stdout: true)` (no timeout); :185 `[Path.join(RepoBase.base_path(repo_url()), "analytics"), Path.expand("analytics")] |> Enum.reject(&is_nil/1)` (the reject is a no-op); writer.ex:324 `Summaries.materialize_async()`.
claim.recommendation: Run materialization in a single supervised worker that coalesces requests (at most one running, one pending), enforces a timeout that kills the OS process (Port with :exit_status / MuonTrap-style), and resolves the reducer path from configuration rather than cwd.

findings.title: Sampler (841 lines) and Writer (628 lines) GenServers each bundle four responsibilities
findings.description: Sampler mixes tick scheduling/scan supervision, fleet and build-gate pressure probing with its own bounded Task.async_stream, process-tree attribution (daemon/ticket/operator), and per-process rate math, plus three separate rescue/catch wrappers (safe_sample, safe_call, record). Writer mixes admission control over atomics, retention/segment-roll policy, open-lifecycle and carried-point bookkeeping, and envelope encoding with three private timestamp validators. findings.title: ISO-8601 timestamp parsing re-implemented at ten sites in this unit (three inside Writer alone)
findings.description: Each site wraps DateTime.from_iso8601/1 with a different failure policy: Writer falls back to the lifecycle fallback in one helper, to DateTime.utc_now() in another (ignoring its injectable clock), and returns :error in a third; Dataset returns :error; Summaries raises ArgumentError; Sampler returns nil; DecisionMetrics returns nil or {:error, :invalid_timestamp}. findings.title: Every usage append rewrites and fsyncs the whole ledger checkpoint, and every ledger notification rewrites the whole aggregate checkpoint
findings.description: Store.persist/4 builds a checkpoint containing the full CounterPolicy dump (sorting the ever-growing idempotency list) and overwrites + fsyncs it on every append; capacity/4 JSON-encodes the record once more than the append path; Record.new re-runs admit/1 (full Codec.encode + regex scan of every string) already run by CounterPolicy.apply, and round-trips the delta through encode/decode; CounterPolicy.delta recomputes each entry key (term_to_binary + base64) a second time. Duplicate appends scan the whole in-memory record queue re-hashing each record. The aggregate then writes a checksummed JSON checkpoint of every cell (cap 32 MiB) with fsync on every notification. Per-append cost therefore grows with lifetime volume on a synchronous GenServer.call path.
findings.recommendation: Checkpoint on a cadence (every N appends or T ms) since the fsynced segment is already authoritative for recovery; keep encoded idempotency keys in insertion order so dump is O(1) amortized; admit once; index records by idempotency key; debounce aggregate checkpoints.

findings.title: Claude headless adapter drops imprecise provider cost without the coverage reason its docs promise
findings.description: The moduledoc says the decoded float cost is 'only ever a lossy fallback recorded as bounded coverage', and ExactMoney supports `coverage: :unknown, unknown_reason: :imprecise`, but cost/2 maps both :imprecise and :absent to `{nil, []}`. The second tuple element (cost_reasons) is therefore always [], so an imprecise-only cost vanishes from the envelope with no coverage reason and the aggregate reports full coverage for that turn.
findings.recommendation: On :imprecise emit a cost with `coverage: :unknown, unknown_reason: :imprecise` (or add an `:imprecise_cost` coverage reason), and add a test that feeds a float-only cost with raw nil and asserts the envelope's coverage is not :full.

findings.title: Provider meter input validation collapses every specific cause, and callers relabel all ingest errors as :malformed
findings.description: Input.normalize/1 computes precise reasons (:invalid_numeric_fact, :invalid_coverage_facts, :invalid_window, :unexpected_key, ...) and then discards them with `_ -> {:error, :invalid_provider_meter_update}`; windows/1 likewise collapses per-window reasons. The Store returns either that atom or :unknown_account_generation, and both callers outside this unit (claude/account_meters.ex:37-44, codex/account_generation.ex:265-277) map any error to a :malformed failure, so a generation-binding problem is recorded as provider malformation - the 'collapsed cause names a specific cause' pattern AGENTS.md forbids.
findings.recommendation: Return `{:error, {:invalid_provider_meter_update, reason}}` preserving the first failing check, keep :unknown_account_generation distinct at the callers (it is not provider malformation), and add the reason to the failure snapshot's health so the dashboard can show it.

findings.title: Provider account-generation transitions refused for validation or authority reasons return 'unavailable' with no log, metric or reason
findings.description: bind/replace/invalidate/retire/confirm all return Snapshot.unavailable(provider, backend) (reason :owner_unavailable) when valid_observation?/authorized? fail, whether the cause is an untrusted source, an unsupported auth mode, a stale authority or an invalid invalidation reason. findings.recommendation: Return {:error, reason} (untrusted_source | unsupported_auth_mode | unauthorized | invalid_reason) from State and have Owner reply with it; count refusals per reason in the snapshot or a telemetry counter.

findings.title: Decision metrics keeps two copies of the same bounded projection in two processes
findings.description: The DecisionMetrics collector holds samples + a seen Window and bounds them with Collector.bound/1; the Writer independently holds samples + records + its own seen Window, re-decodes every record the collector just built (Log.decode_record) and bounds them with a second function, bound_projections/1. Both call Window.recent/2, which fully sorts all samples every time the map exceeds the limit, i.e. on every event at steady state (twice per event across the two processes).
findings.recommendation: Make the Writer a dumb batch appender that receives already-bounded snapshots (records keyed by decision_id) and compacts from them; keep the projection only in the collector; replace Window.recent's full sort with an ordered structure (gb_trees keyed by last_observed_at) or evict incrementally.

findings.title: GitHub enrichment lists every PR in the repo and fails wholesale past 2,000; per-ticket N+1 endpoint fan-out
findings.description: enrich/3 fetches `/pulls?state=all&per_page=100` for the whole repository and only then filters to the requested tickets; with @max_pages 20 any repository with more than 2,000 PRs returns {:error, :pagination_limit} and the report gets zero GitHub anchors (a 'fix by raising a limit' cap). Comment fetches then fan out to 1 request per ticket plus 3 per matched PR, each paginated, sequentially. Results accumulate with `items ++ body` / `events ++ normalized` (quadratic). Dashboard.enrich_dataset also re-parses all telemetry inputs a second time (Dataset.build twice) to merge the anchors.
findings.recommendation: Query PRs by head branch per ticket (search API or `head=owner:branch`) or use the daemon's cached issue/PR graph instead of listing all PRs; run endpoint fetches with bounded concurrency; accumulate with prepend+reverse; pass the already-built dataset into enrichment and append records instead of rebuilding.

findings.title: About 22 bare assert_receive calls wait up to the 100 ms default for a message that another process must forward or produce
findings.description: test_helper.exs does not configure assert_receive_timeout, so the 100 ms ExUnit default applies. The unit has 326 assert_receive calls in 30 files, and 86 of them in 11 files have no explicit timeout. Most bare calls follow a synchronous call whose message is already in the mailbox, so they are safe. The listed ones are not. In orchestrator_status_test, the orchestrator sends to a spawned operator_message_probe, which then re-sends to the test process. The reconciler test waits on a 10 ms timer-driven reconciler process. extensions_test:202 waits for WorkflowStore to handle :poll, read the file, parse the YAML and broadcast. run_telemetry_test:226 waits for a sampler that writes and flushes a file before it sends. On a loaded CI box each of these can exceed 100 ms.
findings.recommendation: Set a suite-wide assert_receive_timeout (for example 1_000) in ExUnit.start/1, or use one @async_assert_timeout attribute, as current_run_membership_store_test already does. For forwarded messages, use receive_barrier/1 from TestSupport, which has no wall-clock bound.

findings.title: About 25 Process.sleep calls are used for synchronization, and several tests assert wall-clock bounds in the 25-700 ms range
findings.description: The unit has 59 Process.sleep calls in 15 files. About 25 of them sleep and then assert, instead of waiting on a barrier. ExecutorWakeInbox has no injectable clock or flush trigger. Its tests sleep 1_100 ms twice to outlast a 1_000 ms debounce, and assert that a waiter is served in under 700 ms. SnapshotStore freshness tests sleep 200, 80, 30 and 150 ms against a 50 ms timeout, and one yields a Task for only 25 ms. The DaemonLifecycle tests assert 200 < elapsed < 2_500 ms and give two concurrently booting elixir VMs 5 s. The extensions_test transient-parse test depends on a 75 ms writer landing inside WorkflowStore's private 3 x 50 ms retry window, which leaves a 25 ms margin. open_ticket_source_test:247 sleeps 100 ms and then asserts that nothing happened, so it passes without testing anything when the host is slow. Where the sleep precedes :sys.get_state (1483, 1520), it is redundant, because the system message is already ordered after the send.
findings.recommendation: Inject a clock and a flush trigger into ExecutorWakeInbox (send(:flush) or a debounce_fun) and into SnapshotStore (now_fun). Replace sleep-then-assert with receive_barrier or :sys.get_state ordering. Replace negative sleeps with an explicit processed-event acknowledgement. Remove the redundant sleeps at 1483 and 1520. Give WorkflowStore a parse-retry hook so the test can release the writer at a known attempt.

findings.title: Tests mutate VM-global production singletons, so no package can be tested without booting the whole :aiur app
findings.description: Configuration reaches code only through the VM-global WorkflowStore. In this unit, 146 write_workflow_file! calls in 12 files rewrite YAML and wait up to 15 s for the singleton to reload. Other tests change the running application directly. They terminate supervisor children (Supervisor.terminate_child(Aiur.Supervisor, WorkflowStore | ResourceStore | Aiur.Orchestrator), 5 sites) and kill WorkflowStore. They replace the state of the global Aiur.Orchestrator and TicketActivity, and suspend TicketActivity. They unregister the Aiur.Orchestrator name and register a fake. They flip the default Webhooks ModeRegistry, restoring it inline rather than in on_exit, so a failed assertion leaks webhook mode to later cases. They reconfigure the global :logger handler. TestSupport's #589/#780 comments describe the cascades this caused. All of this means the tests depend on one shared application tree.
findings.recommendation: Give each package an explicit config dependency: pass settings or a config-server name into GenServers and functions instead of reading the global WorkflowStore. Start named per-test instances (the pattern CurrentRunProjections and DecisionStore already use). Do not terminate app children; test restart behaviour on private supervised instances. Move webhook-mode flips into on_exit.
