findings.title: Polling helpers are re-implemented in 40 test files with different time budgets
findings.description: TestSupport has no shared eventually helper. In this unit alone there are 14 hand-written loops, and their budgets differ widely. extensions_test uses 20 x 25 ms = 500 ms. executor_events uses 50 x 10 ms = 500 ms. orchestrator_status's eventually? uses 100 x 25 ms, and its wait_for_snapshot defaults to 200 ms. current_run_projections uses 1000 x 5 ms. Some return false, some flunk and some return the value. The tight budgets (500 ms, 200 ms) are the ones that turn into flakes under load.
findings.recommendation: Add Aiur.TestSupport.eventually!(fun, timeout_ms \\ 5_000) with deadline semantics that returns the last value or flunks with a description, plus an await_state!(server, predicate) wrapper. Replace the local copies.

findings.title: Tests read and write host state outside their sandbox: the real HOME, the checkout, shared /tmp paths and the operator's live .aiur/config
findings.description: provider_meter_probe_workspace_test creates directories under System.user_home!()/.cache and File.cwd!()/.verification (inside the repository checkout). The src/config/config.exs test block, which is not in the snapshot, says System.user_home!/0 is cached by the VM, so this is the developer's real home. config_paths_test deletes the suite-global :log_file that config.exs sets to keep app-child writes out of <cwd>/log, so during that test app children write into the checkout's src/log. It also points :log_file at the fixed shared path /tmp/aiur_paths_test. ssh_test compares a glob of System.tmp_dir!()/aiur-ssh-script-*.sh before and after, and that directory is shared with other VMs and a live daemon. dogfood_hooks_test and workspace_and_config_test assert on the operator-editable .aiur/config and .aiur/hooks (base_branch == "main"). The live checkout currently shows `M .aiur/config`, so a local operator edit can fail CI-equivalent runs.
findings.recommendation: Route HOME-relative expansion through an injectable home option or Application env and point it at tmp_root!. Test the <cwd>/log fallback through a pure function that takes cwd. Give SSH.with_script a staging-dir option. Snapshot the dogfood files into test fixtures, or move the dogfood agreement check to a repo-level lint script that is allowed to read operator files.

findings.title: Tests change VM-global PATH, HOME and cwd while application children are running
findings.description: async: false only stops other tests from running at the same time. The shared :aiur application's children (pollers, stores, TaskSupervisor jobs that shell out) keep running. ssh_test sets PATH to one empty directory (System.put_env("PATH", test_root)), so any child process spawned in that window fails to find its executables. workflow_test calls File.cd!/2 seven times, and File.cd! changes the cwd of the whole OS process, which the Paths default log root and relative workspace roots depend on. The unit has 15 PATH writes in 5 files, 2 HOME writes and 7 cwd changes; 13 files repo-wide use File.cd.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit seams: executable path options for SSH, git and gh (some modules already take git_path or cmd_fun), and cwd and home arguments for Workflow.config_path_candidates/1. Then tests pass values instead of mutating process-global state.

findings.title: Unit tests depend on external tools and extra OS processes without skip tags, and one passes vacuously when its tool is missing
findings.description: agent_environment_test runs `bash -lc "mise exec -- elixir -e ..."`, which needs mise and a full Elixir boot and fails on any host without mise. daemon_lifecycle_test boots three child `elixir` VMs with the test code paths, two of them concurrently. workspace_and_config_test's sandbox test runs its main assertion only `case System.find_executable("bwrap") do nil -> :ok`, so it passes without asserting anything on hosts without bwrap. The completed-runner fixtures set hook_before_run to a shell loop that polls a release file every 10 ms until on_exit touches it, which leaves real sh processes spinning during the test.
findings.recommendation: Tag these tests (:external_tool / :bwrap / :subprocess_vm) and compute skip reasons the way pgrep_skip_reason/0 does, so a missing tool is reported rather than passed silently. Replace the spin-wait hook with a fake runner seam.

findings.title: Tests use three different strategies to make the global Aiur.PubSub available, and they conflict
findings.description: Some tests start a globally named Aiur.PubSub under their own test supervisor when the app's copy is missing. provider_account_generation_test does it in setup_all, so the global name belongs to that module's lifetime. Others call TestSupport.ensure_pubsub_running/0, which restarts the application child. application_test states that 'a bare {Phoenix.PubSub, name: Aiur.PubSub} restarts into its own dying partitions'. Repo-wide, 18 test files use the bare start and 14 sites call ensure_pubsub_running.
findings.recommendation: Use TestSupport.ensure_pubsub_running/0 everywhere, or better, pass a per-test pubsub name (as CurrentRunProjections does with its :pubsub option). Remove the bare global starts.

findings.title: 75% of the tests in this unit run serialized, mostly because pure-function tests use the heavy Aiur.TestSupport case
findings.description: `use Aiur.TestSupport` expands to `use ExUnit.Case` with no async option. Overall, 48 of the 74 files (918 of 1,217 tests, 29.7k of 35.3k lines) run synchronously.
findings.recommendation: Add a lightweight async case for pure tests, and let TestSupport accept `async:` only after config injection (tests-1c-13) makes that safe. Move pure-reducer tests to async modules first.

findings.title: DecisionExpiry's default sweep path writes real alerts into the VM-global ledger, so every test must opt out

findings.title: Global webhook delivery-mode state leaks between tests; only the reader side defends
findings.description: view_state_sweep_test writes 'owner/repo' into the default app-singleton Aiur.Webhooks.ModeRegistry (configure + record_delivery) and never cleans it up. Almost every GitHub test uses 'owner/repo' as its tracker repo. Read-cache TTLs depend on the mode, so a webhook-backed record turns a 31-second aging test into a cache hit. TestSupport.reset_global_state!/0 resets ResourceStore, AuthPreflight, PollCadence and DispatchAuthorization, but not ModeTable/ModeRegistry. Two reader files (read_cache_test, transport_read_cache_test) now delete the mode entry themselves, and read_cache_test's comment names the leak. Every new reader has to know to do the same.
findings.recommendation: Add ModeTable/ModeRegistry reset to TestSupport.reset_global_state!/0. Fix the writer too: view_state_sweep_test should start a private ModeRegistry (it already accepts `server`/`name`, as read_cache_test:1223 shows) and pass it to ViewStateSweep. Then remove the reader-side ModeTable.delete workarounds.

findings.title: Read-cache readiness helper duplicated and diverged; read_cache_test keeps the pattern #2397 retired
findings.description: There are three ways to 'make sure the shared ReadCache is up'. TestSupport.ensure_read_cache_running/1 restarts the app-owned child without timing. transport_read_cache_test uses it, and its comment says why the old approach was wrong: a wall-clock poll, or a start_supervised! replacement that dies at module end (#2397). read_cache_test, the main ReadCache suite with 82 tests, still has the old copy. It polls with Process.sleep(10) up to 100 times and then falls back to start_supervised!({ReadCache, ...}). That fallback registers a temporary ReadCache under the global name, and it dies when the test ends.
findings.recommendation: Delete read_cache_test's await_read_cache/1 and call Aiur.TestSupport.ensure_read_cache_running/0, as transport_read_cache_test does. Better, per tests-2-01: start a private ReadCache instance per test.

findings.title: GITHUB_TOKEN and GitHub.Config token-cache setup copied into 22 files in 3 diverged variants
findings.description: 22 unit files set GITHUB_TOKEN in setup. Variant A (8 files: agent_marker_wiring, app_identity, app_token_refresher, ci_poll_batch, client_events, code_owners, comment_poll_batch, mutation_write_through) sets only the env var. Variant B (12 files: comments, dependencies_api, human_review_gate, issue_state, issues, pull_requests, reply, repo_events, resolution, review_threads, teams, transport) also saves, erases and restores the private persistent_term key {Aiur.GitHub.Config, :resolved_token}. Variant C (2 files: auth_preflight, config_test) also handles {Config, :resolved_token_source}. Config.token/0 prefers the cached resolved token over GITHUB_TOKEN, and token_source/0 reads the source key. So variant A files depend on no earlier case leaving a cached token behind, and variant B files leave the source key stale. TestSupport does not reset this cache. Across the unit, tests reference private persistent_term keys 84 times: @token_cache_key 56, @source_cache_key 10, @origin_cache_key 8, @cache_key 6, {Aiur.Boot, :run_id} 4.
findings.recommendation: Add a public `Aiur.GitHub.Config.reset_token_cache/0` that erases both the token and source keys. Add a `with_github_token(token)` helper to TestSupport that sets the env var, resets the cache and registers the restore. Call it from reset_global_state!/0 and replace all 22 setup blocks with one line.

findings.title: Source-scanning 'architecture' tests use hard-coded relative paths into lib/ and will break or silently narrow after the carve
findings.description: Four unit files assert structure by reading production source text: 25 files suite-wide use `../../../lib`, `@lib_root` or `Application.app_dir(:aiur)`. graphql_cost_test runs a regex over every `lib/**/*.ex` for `Transport.github_graphql(` call sites that lack `caller:`. After a carve, @lib_root covers only the package the test lives in, so call sites in other packages drop out of the check. The `found >= 10` guard might still pass. budget_ledger_test and quota_history_test read one file by a path relative to __DIR__. view_state_sweep_test builds a path from `Application.app_dir(:aiur)/../../../..` + 'lib/' + the module name. quota_history_test's `refute code =~ "token"` fails on any comment that contains the word.
findings.recommendation: Move these checks into one repo-level check with explicit roots, such as a mix task or the existing scripts/ lint job, that scans every package's lib/. Or turn them into behavioral tests: for example, run QuotaHistory with a request_fun that flunks. Keep the found-count guard, and make it per package.

findings.title: Most of the unit runs serially; heavy TestSupport setup and async: false used without a stated need
findings.description: 1,258 of the unit's 1,958 tests (64%) run serially: 38 files (767 tests) use `use Aiur.TestSupport`, which is async: false, and 27 files (491 tests) declare async: false. Each TestSupport test does a lot of setup: it writes a workflow file, force-reloads WorkflowStore (15s timeout), sets about 10 Application env keys, resets 7 globals, checks runtime children and stops the HTTP server. 12 TestSupport files (314 tests) never write their own workflow (resource_store 102, dispatch_authorization 36, cache_inspector 34, resource_events 32, resource_fetch 29, view_state_sweep 22, quota_caller_attribution 14, poll_snapshots 12, delivered_pull_request 10, agent_cache_bridge 8, request_log 8, cache_history 7). They use TestSupport mainly for the global reset. In 4 files I verified that async: false has no reason. usage_ledger/recovery.ex, paths.ex and checkpoint.ex touch no Application env, persistent_term, ETS or registered names. CycleFetchCache is per-process (Process.put plus a private ETS table). AgentList.App with `name: nil, subscribe?: false` touches no global state in init (app.ex:99-111).
findings.recommendation: Make recovery_test, cycle_fetch_cache_test, app_phase_tracking_test and app_progress_ratchet_test async: true. Split TestSupport into a light `Aiur.TestSupport.GlobalReset`, which resets state and needs no workflow, and a heavy `Aiur.TestSupport.Workflow` for cases that need config. Every async: false should carry a one-line reason comment, as config_test does.

findings.title: No shared GitHub HTTP double: 289 hand-written request_fun routers in 30 files plus Req.Test stubs in 4 files
findings.description: Every GitHub test builds its own fake for the GitHub API as an inline `fn %{url: url} -> cond do String.ends_with?(url, ...)`. The largest counts are ci_readiness_test 39, pull_requests_test 26, issues_test 24, ci_poll_batch_test 20, comment_poll_batch_test 19, dispatch_authorization_test 18, transport_test 15 and issue_state_test 15; 289 in total. A second, separate mechanism, Req.Test plugs, is used in auth_preflight, transport_quota, transport_read_cache and transport. findings.title: Bare assert_receive (100 ms default) waits on an asynchronous sender in several files
findings.description: Counts across the unit: 220 assert_receive (153 without an explicit timeout) in 52 files, and 92 refute_receive (46 bare) in 35 files. Most bare sites follow a synchronous call or use a GenServer.call barrier, which is correct; quota_test calls snapshot/1 after each cast observe. findings.title: Negative assertions based on sleep or Task.yield timing pass vacuously when the system is slow
findings.description: These tests prove that something did NOT happen by waiting a fixed time. agent_cache_bridge_test sleeps 120 ms and then refutes a marker file that the asynchronous bridge would write. If the bridge takes longer than 120 ms under load, the refute passes even with the production change reverted, which breaks the AGENTS.md rule that tests must fail without the change. budget_test asserts `Task.yield(waiter, 80) == nil` to show the waiter is blocked. Budget.acquire spawns a python3 broker subprocess that can take longer than 80 ms to start, so a broken ceiling can also read as 'still blocked'. That file already records load-sensitivity flakes (#2286, comment at 1236-1241).
findings.recommendation: Replace fixed sleeps with a synchronous barrier on the process that would act. Examples: a :sys.get_state/1 or GenServer.call after the triggering deposit, or a positive control deposit in the same test that must produce its marker first, so the negative is ordered after it. For budget_test, have the broker report 'held' (an observable hold state or telemetry event) and assert on that.

findings.title: Wall-clock race test with 200-500 ms margins and a python broker in the loop
findings.description: 'starts the HTTP request deadline after local budget admission' sets github_request_deadline_ms to 1_500. The Req stub sleeps 1_000 ms, and the test sleeps 700 ms before it releases the lease. The assertion holds only if about 700 ms of admission wait plus 1_000 ms of request stays under the 1_500 ms deadline measured from admission. That leaves about 500 ms of slack in which the python3 budget broker subprocess (github_budget_enabled? = true) must admit the waiter. The test takes at least 1.7 s of real time.
findings.recommendation: Inject a clock or deadline function into Transport's deadline computation, so the test can assert when the deadline starts without sleeping. Or assert on a recorded `deadline_started_at` compared with `admitted_at` instead of racing real time.

findings.title: Tests rewrite or unregister the live CodeOwners singleton because production reads it by registered name
findings.description: issues_test uses :sys.replace_state on the app-supervised Aiur.GitHub.CodeOwners to inject an allowlist, then puts the captured state back in on_exit. If the singleton restarts meanwhile (see tests-2-01), the restore writes stale state into a new process. github_enricher_test calls Process.unregister(CodeOwners) on the live process to force the fallback path, and re-registers it in on_exit. Any app process that calls CodeOwners during the test gets :noproc. If the supervisor has started a new registered CodeOwners in the meantime, Process.register in on_exit raises. The same pattern runs suite-wide: Process.unregister against Orchestrator, Quota and ActiveTurns appears in 7 other files.
findings.recommendation: Add an injectable `codeowners:` / `allowed_users_fun:` option to Issues.fetch_issue_states_by_ids_conditional/3 and GitHubEnricher.enrich/3 (DispatchAuthorization.authorize already takes `allowed_users:`). Remove the replace_state and unregister calls.

findings.title: VM-global mutations beyond Application env: PATH, cwd, global trace patterns, code purge
findings.description: With the whole :aiur application running, several tests change process-global OS or VM state. config_test prepends a fake `gh` to PATH, and with_empty_path sets PATH to an empty directory. The comment at 758-762 admits that other code may shell out during the window. workspace_before_remove_test sets PATH to "" via with_path([]). Four files call File.cd!: store_test, pr_body_check_test, specs_check_task_test and workspace_before_remove_test. cwd is VM-wide, and app children that resolve relative paths (for example <cwd>/log) follow it. store_test calls `:erlang.trace(:new, true, ...)`, which traces every new process in the VM. resource_store_test sets a :global trace_pattern on :erlang.send_after/3. If the assert_receive fails, it never turns off the per-process trace, because that call is not in on_exit. cache_inspector_test runs :code.purge and :code.delete on a production module (ResourceStoreSource) that the app's CacheHistory sampler may be running.
findings.recommendation: Add seams to production: HostCommand already takes :wrapper_dir (host_command_test is the model), so add a `gh_path`/`find_executable_fun` option to Config.keyring_token and the workspace_before_remove task, and a `cwd:` option to the mix tasks. Replace the global trace with an injected `boot_fun` spy. Move all PATH, cwd and trace mutation behind one TestSupport helper that asserts the test module is async: false and restores the value in on_exit.

findings.title: quota_test creates and deletes a directory in the developer's real $HOME
findings.description: To test tilde-form workspace roots, the test creates `Path.join(System.user_home!(), "aiur-quota-test-<n>")`, writes an agent-requests.tsv under it, and removes it in on_exit. findings.recommendation: Give Layout/Quota an injectable home directory (a `home_fun:` or `:home_dir` app env), or run the test with HOME pointed at a tmp_root! for its duration (async: false already).

findings.title: Tests age and inspect private ETS entry maps directly (ResourceStore.Table, read-cache tables); six copies of 'age' helpers
findings.description: ResourceStore and ReadCache have no injectable clock, so tests move time by rewriting private fields in the ETS entry (:fetched_at_ms, :recorded_at_ms, :processed_at_ms, :data_version, and the {key, response, deposited_at} tuple shape). resource_store_test has 37 direct ResourceStore.Table operations. The 'age' helper exists 6 times: age_mark! in resource_store_test and view_state_sweep_test, age_body! in resource_fetch_test, and age_entries_by in read_cache_test and transport_read_cache_test, plus age_markers_by. The retention constant 72h is written out as a literal (`73 * 60 * 60 * 1000` and similar) 15 times in 3 files. That is deliberate in resource_store_test, where the literals pin the value.
findings.recommendation: Add a `clock:`/`now_ms_fun` option to ResourceStore and ReadCache, following Quota's `clock:`, and a test-only `ResourceStore.inspect_entry/1`. Then aging means advancing the clock, and the tests stop depending on the ETS layout. Keep the pinned-literal bound tests, but express them as clock advances.

findings.title: budget_test injects rows into the broker's private SQLite schema with inline python and runs real python3 brokers
findings.description: budget_test.exs is async: false and has 45 tests. It drives the real python3 budget broker for every acquire and release. It also writes to the broker's SQLite tables with python -c scripts: insert_stale_policy, create_legacy_budget_database, bump_broker_version and insert_lease_less_admission. The last one DROPs the admissions_require_lease trigger to insert a legacy row. lock_database opens a python process that holds `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` for 30 s. The Elixir tests therefore depend on the broker's private table and column names, and each python3 spawn adds load-dependent latency, which is behind the #2286 flakes the file mentions.
findings.recommendation: Move schema fixtures into the broker's own test suite (python) or into a `broker fixture` subcommand, so the Elixir side does not hard-code SQL. Keep a small end-to-end contract suite with the real broker and tag it (:broker_integration). Test Budget's Elixir logic against a fake broker behaviour.

findings.title: Production code reads 41 test-seam keys from the shared :aiur application env; tests in this unit set 40 distinct keys 197 times
findings.description: Dependency injection for tests is done through VM-global `Application.put_env(:aiur, ...)`, read by production at call time. Any test touching one of these keys must be `async: false`, must save/restore by hand, and still leaks into application processes that run concurrently. Across this unit tests set 40 distinct keys in 197 put_env calls in 27 files (top: loadavg_source_override 17, build_order_planning_pack 17, file_descriptor_sample_override 15, memory_tracker_issues 14, global_pause_store_path 10). findings.title: assert_receive with the 100 ms default waits on messages sent by other processes (≈70 verified sites); 257 bare assert_receive in 39 files overall
findings.description: Parsed count across the unit: 366 assert_receive (257 without a timeout, in 39 files) and 112 refute_receive (61 without a timeout, 17 files). Most bare sites follow a synchronous call and are harmless, but several families wait on a different process with only 100 ms: the dispatcher's runner runs inside `Task.Supervisor.start_child(Aiur.TaskSupervisor, ...)`, so every `assert_receive {:agent_runner_run, ...}` races the task start (9 bare sites in dispatcher_test, 2 in dispatcher_blocked_by_cost_test, 1 in dispatcher_stale_blocked_by_test); dispatcher_test:648 waits 1_000 ms for the same message, so the file is inconsistent with itself. `start_initial_ci_readiness_check` and `maybe_warn_ci_readiness` spawn the readiness scan (dispatcher_test 867-868, 981). realtime_test has 44 bare waits on the session process (its moduledoc says the suite runs 'without a clock', but each is a 100 ms clock); tts_test has 9 on the spawned TTS process; retry_engine_test 1163/1187 wait on the Ownership guardian.
findings.recommendation: For cross-process messages use the existing `receive_barrier/1` from TestSupport (no wall clock) or an explicit monitor/`:DOWN`; for messages produced synchronously use `assert_received`. Do not fix this by raising ExUnit's global assert_receive_timeout. Add a Credo check or grep gate: bare `assert_receive` after a call that spawns (Task.Supervisor, Realtime.start, TTS.start) must use receive_barrier.

findings.title: Process.sleep used for synchronization and to age records past wall-clock TTLs (42 sites in 16 files)
findings.description: dispatcher_blocked_by_cost_test sets `:blocked_by_max_age_ms` to 100 and sleeps 150 ms three times to make a real ResourceStore record stale, and sleeps 2 ms three times so two monotonic-millisecond timestamps differ; both depend on scheduler timing and silently change meaning if production reads a different clock. slot_test (4 sites) and session_writer_test (1) build a 'dead pid' with `spawn(fn -> :ok end); Process.sleep(10)`, which is not guaranteed under load (slot_test:68-70 does not even check liveness). slot_policy_test:327 proves 'nothing started' by sleeping 100 ms. server_test polls a real sqlite db and OS processes at 100 ms × 40.
findings.recommendation: Inject a clock (`now_ms_fun`) into ResourceStore/BoundedBlockedBy freshness checks instead of sleeping past a TTL; for strict ordering pass explicit timestamps. Replace sleep-based dead pids with one shared `dead_pid/0` (monitor + `:DOWN`). Replace negative sleeps with a synchronous probe (`:sys.get_state/1` after the broadcast is processed).

findings.title: refute_receive on a 60-second self-timer can never fail; the tests do not check the timer was cancelled
findings.description: Two tests schedule `Process.send_after(self(), msg, 60_000)`, hand the ref to production code that should cancel it, then `refute_receive msg` with the 100 ms default. findings.recommendation: Assert `Process.read_timer(ref) == false` (cancelled) instead of refuting the message, and mutation-check both tests by deleting the production `Process.cancel_timer` call.

findings.title: Tests reach internals: @doc false public seams, direct GenServer callback calls, :sys.get_state field reads

findings.title: async comment_wake_test depends on the global tracker config and the global Logger, and asserts through log text
findings.description: The module is `async: true`, yet several tests only pass because the ambient tracker 'fails the write' (comments: 'The unset tracker fails the write (permanently, here a 404)') and they assert `log =~ "rework transition skipped"` as proof the write was attempted. The file itself notes it 'cannot be swapped for a recording fake without serialising the file' because `Tracker.update_issue_state/2` is hard-wired at comment_wake.ex:1425 while the other seams ride inside the event map (`:issue_state_fetcher`, `:open_pr_fetcher`, `:unresolved_threads_fetcher`, `:emit_alert_fun`). `capture_log/1` captures the VM-global Logger (planning_source_test.exs:846-848 documents this, #1747), so in an async module 27 `assert log =~` and 14 `refute log =~` on generic strings can be satisfied or broken by a concurrent test.
findings.recommendation: Add an `:update_issue_state_fun` seam to the rework path (the merged-PR path already has one at comment_wake.ex:56-57), move test seams out of the event map into an opts keyword, and assert on the recorded write instead of log text. Keep log assertions only for unique sentinel strings.

findings.title: Tests read the real checkout and real environment: Config.repo() git-origin fallback; GITHUB_TOKEN deleted and not restored
findings.description: planning_source_test (no TestSupport, so no configured repo) calls `Config.repo()` 8 times; `repo/0` falls back to `Aiur.Git.origin_repo()`, i.e. the git remote of the directory `mix test` runs in. On a checkout without an origin (a tarball, a fresh `git init`, some CI caches) it returns nil and `String.replace(@pack, "acme/widgets", nil)` raises, so the tests pass or fail on the host rather than the code. init/github_test deletes GITHUB_TOKEN (and on_exit deletes it again) in 6 tests without saving the previous value, so an operator or CI token present at suite start is gone for every later test in the VM.
findings.recommendation: Pin the repository in planning_source_test (configure `tracker.github.repo` or use `Config.repo(origin_fun: fn -> "owner/repo" end)`). In github_test save and restore GITHUB_TOKEN with the shared `put_system_env!` helper (tests-3-09).

findings.title: VM-global cwd, PATH and XDG/OPENCODE env mutated while application processes run
findings.description: `File.cd!/2` changes the working directory of the whole BEAM; it is used 9 times in 4 init test files because the production functions read the cwd implicitly (Dotenv.load/0, Scaffold.ensure_env/1, GitHub.detect_repo/0, Runtime.detect_toolchain/0, Runtime.setup_repo_state/1). server_test prepends a stub `opencode` directory to PATH and sets OPENCODE_CONFIG/OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT/XDG_* for the VM. The modules are sync, but supervised application processes (WorkflowStore reloads, Git origin resolution, any slot/prewarm spawn) keep running and resolve relative paths or spawn `opencode` during those windows. server_test's prepare_serve_root/0 also builds its tmp dir without System.pid, contrary to TestSupport.tmp_root!/1's documented cross-VM collision.
findings.recommendation: Give the init functions a `cwd:`/`root:` option and pass the tmp dir; give Opencode.Server an `env:`/`executable:` option so tests pass the stub path and XDG dirs to the Port instead of mutating the VM env. Use tmp_root!/1 for all tmp dirs.

findings.title: Untagged tests need real binaries and OS processes (opencode, bash, pgrep, ps, git) with 15-40 s waits
findings.description: server_test boots a real `opencode serve` (Server.start_link -> `exec opencode serve --port 0`), talks HTTP to it and reads its sqlite db; it waits up to 40 s for startup. retry_engine_test spawns `bash -c 'sleep 600 & wait'` and polls `pgrep -P` to find the child. github_test runs `git init`/`git remote add` and ignores the exit status. orphaned_workers_test runs real AgentRunner tasks on the app TaskSupervisor with 15 s waits. None are tagged, while test_helper only excludes `:external`, `:perf_regression`, `:quarantine` and `:real_proc` (on hosts without /proc), so on a host without opencode on PATH these fail rather than skip, and they dominate suite wall time.
findings.recommendation: Tag these `@tag :real_proc` (or a new `:needs_opencode`) and skip with a clear reason when the binary is absent; assert on System.cmd exit codes. Keep one integration test per behaviour and cover the rest with the stub executable approach already used at server_test.exs:298-352.

findings.title: GitHub HTTP double setup copied between the two blocked_by regression files and reaching into a private persistent_term key
findings.description: Both files repeat the same ~45-line setup: ensure :req started, save 3-4 app keys, start a private Quota, point `:github_transport_test_options` at Req.Test, disable the budget, erase the cached token, put GITHUB_TOKEN, write a github workflow, reset ResourceStore, and restore everything. findings.title: An empty monitor mailbox does not prove tick completion
findings.description: wait_for_mailbox_drained returns as soon as the monitor has consumed the tick message, even while its snapshot callback is still executing. Callers can advance the clock or assert absence of alerts without waiting for the prior operation to finish. Record existence and already-true last_alert predicates elsewhere also are not whole-tick barriers, although their downstream effects require separate analysis.
findings.recommendation: Use a completion barrier on the monitor after sending each tick before changing fixture inputs or making negative assertions. Keep checks of durable state as separate behavior assertions.

findings.title: 24 test files assert on production source text or hard-coded repo-relative paths; the carve will break them en masse
findings.description: Census across the unit: 24 files contain Path.expand("../../../lib/..."), "../../../../packaging/...", ".aiur/...", "log/..." or @lib_root; at least 43 tests read a production .ex (or the 4179-line bash engine) with File.read! and assert regex/substring presence, ordering of substrings (pos!/2), or literal module-attribute values. Examples: opencode_slots_test asserts `@poll_death_threshold 3` in slot/state.ex; convo_paint_test pins `@convo_paint_poll_interval_ms 100`; compile_time_paths_test keeps a 40-line allowlist keyed by `aiur/<file>.ex` paths and literal source lines; progress_renderer_boundary_test keeps a call-site census keyed by src/lib-relative path. Any module move, rename or split during the carve fails these regardless of behaviour, and many of them (substring order, attribute literals) cannot detect a behavioural regression that keeps the text.
findings.recommendation: Before the carve: (1) convert architectural censuses (compile_time_paths, progress_renderer_boundary, deposit reader_sites) to key on module names via Code.fetch_docs/beam chunks or `mix xref` output instead of file paths; (2) replace substring-order characterization tests (opencode_slots, warm_*, enter_opens_new_pane, done_agent_detach, multi_pane_open, preseed_models, time_to_paint, chat_pane_loads_session, shutdown_cleanup) with behavioural tests against the GenServers (several already have behavioural siblings in the same file) or delete them; (3) centralise any remaining source reads behind one helper (e.g. Aiur.TestSupport.source!(Module)) resolving via Module.__info__(:compile)[:source] so moves do not break paths.

findings.title: Tests mutate shared application singletons: the live Orchestrator, Aiur.Supervisor children, registered names and CodeOwners state
findings.description: Across the unit there are 117 :sys.get_state/:sys.replace_state sites in 12 files, most against app-global processes. orchestrator_blocking_http_test rewrites the shared Aiur.Orchestrator's state in setup and parks the real Orchestrator inside a hanging HTTP request executed via :sys.replace_state (lines 146-157) so later cleanup must wait for it to answer again. deposit_test, webhook_poll_reconciliation_test and subscription_store_test terminate and restart children of Aiur.Supervisor by child id; github_webhook_test unregisters the Aiur.Orchestrator name and registers a probe under it, restoring it in on_exit with `rescue ArgumentError -> :ok`, so a failed re-register silently leaves the application without a registered Orchestrator for every later test. ensure_codeowners!/stop_codeowners overwrite the app CodeOwners allowlist in place. All of this assumes one monolithic supervision tree with fixed registered names, which is precisely what the carve splits.
findings.recommendation: Give every singleton a name/registry option and have tests start_supervised! their own instance (Orchestrator already supports name: + initial_poll?: false, used at orchestrator_blocking_http_test.exs:556). Replace the default-wake global name lookup in GithubWebhook with an injected wake target so the name hijack is unnecessary. Where the app instance must be used, fail loudly (flunk) if the name cannot be restored instead of rescuing.

findings.title: 'control queries add nothing to the orchestrator mailbox' can never fail: it traces the wrong process
findings.description: The test calls :erlang.trace(pid, true, [:send]) on the Orchestrator. The :send flag reports messages sent BY the traced process ({:trace, Orchestrator, :send, Msg, To}). sends_from_self/2 then counts only {:trace, ^me, :send, _, ^pid}, i.e. trace messages whose traced process is the test process, which is never traced. The count is therefore 0 before and 0 after, and `assert sends_from_self(pid, me) == before` is 0 == 0 whatever AgentControlCLI does. In addition flush_trace/3's catch-all `_other_trace ->` consumes every message in the test mailbox, not only trace messages. The #1837 property it names is only guarded indirectly by the neighbouring CLI-budget tests.
findings.recommendation: Trace the test process instead (:erlang.trace(self(), true, [:send]) and count {:trace, ^me, :send, _, ^pid}), or trace the Orchestrator with [:receive] and match on the message shape. Restrict the flush clause to {:trace, _, _, _, _} tuples. Then revert the read-model change locally and confirm the test fails, per AGENTS.md.

findings.title: Bare assert_receive/refute_receive (100 ms default): 163 + 41 sites; a subset waits on genuinely asynchronous senders
findings.description: Parsed census (arguments counted, comments excluded): 558 assert_receive calls, 163 without a timeout in 28 files; 176 refute_receive calls, 41 without a timeout in 9 files. No assert_receive_timeout override exists in test/test_helper.exs. Most bare sites follow a synchronous GenServer.call/closure whose sends happen before the reply, so they are really assert_received and only obscure intent; but some wait on other processes: queue_drain_test.exs:308/312/316/317 wait on messages produced by a Task.async and the FakeQueueOrchestrator it calls; all 36 tmux `assert_receive :ready` sites wait on a freshly spawned Task. Under CI scheduler contention a 100 ms window is the documented flake shape (#459 comment in ls_remote_ticker_test.exs:33-41). Worst files: queue_drain 28+21, coding_agent 26+4, checkpoint_delivery 22+5, tmux/layout 12, tmux/query 10.
findings.recommendation: Use assert_received/refute_received where the message is already in the mailbox (after a synchronous call), and an explicit, shared timeout constant (e.g. @receive_timeout 2_000 from test/support) where a sender is asynchronous. Add a credo/lint check that flags assert_receive with one argument.

findings.title: Process.sleep used as a synchronisation barrier where a real barrier exists or is documented
findings.description: 44 Process.sleep sites in 18 files. Several are pure timing guesses: shared_prewarm_e2e_test sleeps 20 ms after the asynchronous AttachPool.seed/2 six times, while its sibling opencode_slots_test uses the correct barrier `sync(pool)` (= :sys.get_state). agent_list_sort_test sleeps 50 ms and then calls :sys.get_state(app), which is itself the barrier. event_delivery_test sleeps 50 ms after SubscriptionStore.add_subscription/3 although subscription_store_test.exs:315 documents that bindings are ready synchronously. github_webhook_test sleeps a real 2.4 s to cross a debounce window. opencode_slots_test polls private state with sleep(50) in Enum.any?/2.
findings.recommendation: Replace with :sys.get_state barriers (as ls_remote_ticker_test's tick/1 does), explicit acknowledgement messages, or an injected clock for debounce windows (GithubWebhook already takes request_refresh_fun; add now_fun/monotonic_fun).

findings.title: Wall-clock duration assertions on a loaded CI host
findings.description: Tests assert elapsed wall time: exchange_test asserts a publish returns in under 100 ms while a slow subscriber sleeps; orchestrator_blocking_http_test asserts CLI status/agents finish in under 5 s and CommentPolling.start_async returns in under 1 s; orchestrator_lifecycle_test asserts a resumed entry's started_at is within 0..2 s of utc_now. findings.title: Five hand-written fake Orchestrators implement the raw queue call protocol, which itself has two parallel variants
findings.description: Agent-runner tests fake the Orchestrator by pattern-matching its private GenServer call tuples. FlakyRestoreQueueOrchestrator duplicates FakeQueueOrchestrator except one clause. The fakes reveal two coexisting queue protocols in production: per-identifier batch calls ({:claim_next_queue_item, id}, {:consume_delivered_queue_items, id}, {:restore_delivered_queue_items, id}, {:fail_delivered_queue_items, id, reason}) and per-item calls ({:claim_next_operator_queue_item, id}, {:claim_next_checkpoint_queue_item, id}, {:claim_blocker_critical_events_digest, id}, {:restore_queue_item_pending, item_id}, {:mark_queue_item_failed, item_id, reason}, {:acknowledge_queue_item_delivery, ...}); all ten atoms live in orchestrator.ex and orchestrator/operator_messages.ex. dashboard_live_test and agent_chat_broadcast_test (outside this unit) carry further fakes.
findings.recommendation: Define a behaviour (e.g. Aiur.AgentQueueOwner) with the queue operations as functions, have Orchestrator implement it, pass the implementation to AgentRunner, and ship one configurable in-memory fake in test support. Collapse the two protocols if the batch and per-item paths are the same state machine.

findings.title: Global persistent_term closure (Publisher.set_tracked_fn) installed by the Orchestrator and reset 31 times by tests
findings.description: The events Publisher's contamination filter is a function stored in :persistent_term and installed at runtime by Orchestrator.Lifecycle. Tests must reset it: 31 Publisher.set_tracked_fn calls in 11 files of this unit, on top of TestSupport.reset_global_state!/0 doing it for every TestSupport case. workspace_lifecycle_test documents the leak: 'The contamination filter's tracked_fn is process-global (:persistent_term) and can be left pointed at another test's narrow set'. findings.recommendation: Make the tracked-set a query the Publisher performs against an injected tracker/registry (or data kept in an ETS table owned by a process with a reset API), not a closure in persistent_term; pass it via publish opts in tests.

findings.title: fixture_server.exs: 2634-line script with 16 modules that re-implements DashboardLive handlers, already diverged

findings.title: Run-summary strip tests pin stale and unavailable readings as indistinguishable from fresh ones
findings.description: AGENTS.md ('Computed ages and collapsed causes', and the unknown-path mutation rule) requires that an unavailable/stale rendering path fail a test when replaced with a plausible default. Here the tests assert the opposite: 'the models pane renders stale and unavailable readings without labels' (Kimi 'reported nothing at all ... the row is just the empty bar'), 'a card standing stale or partial renders windows without qualifiers', 'a stale-stamped window renders its percentage without qualifiers', and 'a credit window past its freshness horizon keeps its balance without a stale label'. The test named 'names unavailable values instead of presenting synthetic zeroes' contains no positive assertion that anything is named; it only refutes '$0.00', 'N/A', 'Tokens' and CSS classes, so rendering an empty bar or 0% for an unavailable reading passes.
findings.recommendation: Surface the contradiction to the operator: either the strip carries a cause-neutral marker for stale/unavailable (with a test that fails when the branch is replaced by a default) or AGENTS.md records an explicit exception for this surface. At minimum, assert a distinguishing attribute (data-freshness="stale" / aria-label) so the value behind the render is constrained.

findings.title: Tombstone refutes: 21 refutes of removed labels in run_summary_strip_test, which pass on any rename
findings.description: The file has 53 tests, 158 html =~ assertions of which 83 are refutes. 21 refutes target strings of features that were removed ('Tokens', 'Spend', 'rs-spend', 'rs-token-*', 'Top consumer', 'Attributed', 'N/A'), and whole tests exist only to refute them ('spend figures are removed for every account', 'token glyphs are removed from the model rows', three 'omits attribution and coverage context' tests). findings.title: Provider 'keyed' credential check duplicated in RunSummaryStrip (reads System env at render) and ProviderMeterProbe (injectable) — forces async:false tests
findings.description: Both modules decide whether an OpenAI-compatible provider is 'keyed' by reading management_api_key_env || api_key_env from CodingAgent.backends(). The probe takes an :api_key_fetcher option; the strip calls System.get_env/1 directly inside a function component's render path. The copies already differ for non-compat providers (strip returns true, probe returns false). Because the component reads process-global env, run_summary_strip_test must be async: false, delete four credential env vars in setup, and carry three near-identical with_deepseek_key/with_kimi_key/with_openrouter_key helpers (lines 25-56) plus nested with_*_key blocks.
findings.recommendation: Compute 'keyed?' once in the provider registry (e.g. Aiur.OpenAICompat.Registry.keyed?(provider, fetcher)) and pass the result into the component via assigns (the presenter), so rendering is pure and the test can be async with a parameter instead of env mutation.

findings.title: Sandbox-isolation tests silently pass when bwrap is absent
findings.description: 'real command sandbox cannot read a host sibling' and two budget-sharing sandbox tests branch on System.find_executable("bwrap") and return :ok when it is missing, so on any host without bubblewrap the suite reports these security-relevant tests green without executing them. test_helper.exs already has the right pattern for environment-dependent tests (the :real_proc tag excluded when /proc is absent).

findings.title: Launcher control-protocol markers are a cross-language contract defined only by string literals in bash and Elixir
findings.description: The control RPC protocol between the bash launcher (packaging/npm/aiur-cli/libexec/aiur-engine.sh) and Aiur.AgentControlCLI is the marker strings __AIUR_CONTROL_EXIT__:, __AIUR_CONTROL_ERROR__:, __AIUR_CONTROL_READY__ and __AIUR_CONTROL_NOT_READY__. findings.title: TestSupport setup discards the result of every shared-child recovery, so a missing app child fails later and elsewhere
findings.description: The ensure_*_running/0 family returns :ok | :error, but the per-case setup and reset_global_state!/0 ignore it. reset_global_state! calls ensure_resource_store_running() and then GitHubResourceStore.reset(). The module's own doc says that reset is a no-op when the store is down and 'cannot distinguish an empty store from a missing one'. So when recovery fails, the reset is skipped without a signal and state leaks into the next case. The setup at 346 has the same problem, and on_exit at 371-373 ignores the result of Application.ensure_all_started(:aiur). This harness is shared by 194 test modules, and its own comments cite the flakes this pattern produced (#589, #780, #2397).
findings.recommendation: Make setup fail fast and name the child: `:ok = ensure_runtime_children_running()` should return {:error, {:child_down, name}}, which setup turns into a flunk that names the child. Make reset_global_state! assert that the resource store is running before it resets.

findings.title: Aiur.TestSupport is a 1,663-line god module that couples all 194 users to the full Aiur.Supervisor tree and forces them to run synchronously
findings.description: One module holds six jobs. (1) The ExUnit case template and per-case setup (228-379). (2) App-env capture, restore and global persistent_term resets (61-226). (3) Recovery of about 8 supervisor children, about 350 lines (788-1143). (4) Endpoint ownership (602-711). (5) A hand-written YAML workflow fixture generator, about 520 lines (1145-1662). (6) Miscellany: pgrep probe, tmp_root!, safe_stop, receive_barrier. `defmacro __using__(_opts)` expands to a bare `use ExUnit.Case`, so the options are thrown away and every user runs async: false. 7 callers pass `async: false`, which is discarded without a signal, and an `async: true` would be dropped the same way. Every case writes a workflow file, force-reloads WorkflowStore (15 s timeout), checks the application supervisor and stops HttpServer, whether or not it needs any of that.
findings.recommendation: Split it into: Aiur.TestSupport.AppCase (the case template; it passes opts through to ExUnit.Case and makes app isolation opt-in), Aiur.TestSupport.AppEnv (capture, restore, put_app_env!/put_system_env!), Aiur.TestSupport.AppChildren (one generic ensure_child_running/2), Aiur.TestSupport.WorkflowFixture (the YAML builder), Aiur.TestSupport.Endpoint and Aiur.TestSupport.Tmp. Pure tests should `use ExUnit.Case, async: true` and import only what they need.

findings.title: 17 sites start a temporary Aiur.PubSub under the ExUnit supervisor, the pattern TestSupport documents as the #2397 cause; a shared helper repeats it
findings.description: If Aiur.PubSub is missing, these sites start a replacement Phoenix.PubSub named Aiur.PubSub under the test or setup_all supervisor. The replacement dies when the test or module ends, and the shared name is left unregistered for every later module. TestSupport.ensure_pubsub_running/1 exists to prevent this, and its doc names the failure. Two helpers now do the same job in different ways: Aiur.Claude.MeterTestSupport.ensure_pubsub/0 and Aiur.TestSupport.ensure_pubsub_running/1. ticket_history_provider_test is the worst case: it does this in a per-test `setup`, not in setup_all.
findings.recommendation: Replace all 17 sites with `:ok = Aiur.TestSupport.ensure_pubsub_running()`. Delete MeterTestSupport.ensure_pubsub/0 or make it delegate. Add a lint test that rejects `start_supervised!({Phoenix.PubSub, name: Aiur.PubSub}`. Tests that need isolation should keep using a uniquely named PubSub, as current_run_projections_test does.

findings.title: github_graph_test mostly tests a copy of production GitHubGraph (97 of 104 calls), and the copy has already diverged
findings.description: Aiur.BuildOrder.GitHubGraph.TestAdapter rewrites fetch_catalog/1 and fetch_selected_root/2 against the internal Pager, Result and Settings modules. It has its own repository/limits validation, with copied @member_limit/@max_page_budget/@max_call_budget constants, valid_limits? and page_size. The test file aliases the adapter as `GitHubGraph`. Production wiring (Settings.authority/1 reading config, the member_labels? plumbing) is only reached by the 7 calls in the 'public repository authority' describe. The check order has already drifted. The adapter checks repository, then token, then limits. Production checks Settings.authority (repository plus limits from config), then token. So with invalid bounds and a missing token, the two return different errors.
findings.recommendation: Give production an explicit seam: Settings.authority/1 accepts an `:authority` override of {repository, limits} that is still validated by valid_limits?, or a `:config` reader function. Then point every test at Aiur.BuildOrder.GitHubGraph and delete the adapter.

findings.title: flunk sentinels inside callbacks that run in other processes cannot fail the test
findings.description: start_cache/1 runs the coordinator's reader under a Task.Supervisor that the test does not link to or await. A `reader: fn _ -> flunk("...") end` guard raises ExUnit.AssertionError in the task, not in the test process, so the test passes even when the reader is called. In 'restart loses in-memory detail until a new demand succeeds' the only real check is the return value of current/2, so 'current must not fetch' is not enforced. In 'rejects another repository before cache admission' the fallback check `%{entries: %{}}` matches any map (see tests-6-08), so neither guard can fail.
findings.recommendation: Use `fn _ -> send(parent, :unexpected_read); ... end` with `refute_received :unexpected_read` after a synchronous barrier (cache_barrier/1 already exists), or count calls with :counters and assert 0.

findings.title: 36 redaction/leak guards use `refute inspect(x) =~ secret`, which Inspect truncation and custom Inspect impls can make pass without checking
findings.description: inspect/1 truncates by default (limit: 50 elements per collection, printable_limit: 4096 bytes) and follows any custom Inspect implementation. None of the 36 sites passes limit: :infinity. financial_data_access_test:295 runs `refute inspect(socket) =~ sentinel` on a %Phoenix.LiveView.Socket{}, and that struct derives Inspect with `only: [:id, :endpoint, :router, :view, :parent_pid, :root_pid, :assigns, :transport_pid, :sticky?]`. So the `private` map, where FinancialDataAccess keeps its state (asserted at 294), is never part of the string being checked. These guards protect credential and payload redaction, a security property.
findings.recommendation: Add Aiur.TestSupport.refute_term_contains(term, needle), which walks maps, lists, tuples and structs (via Map.from_struct), or at least uses `inspect(term, limit: :infinity, printable_limit: :infinity, structs: false)`. Replace all 36 sites with it.

findings.title: 75 bare assert_receive/refute_receive sites use the 100 ms default; 297 others hard-code timeouts, mostly 2_000
findings.description: A parser count over the unit's 143 files (multi-line calls handled) found 47 assert_receive and 28 refute_receive calls with no timeout, in 16 files. Most follow a synchronous call and should be assert_received/refute_received, which states that intent. Some cross asynchronous hops and can flake under load: streamdeck_channel_test 1075/1126 (`push` goes to the channel process, then GenServer.cast to the fake session, then `send` to the observer, with no reply awaited), 1081 (commit cast), voice_channel_test 212/274 (`push("speak")` then the TTS fun), and usage_aggregate/store_test 158 (a publish during aggregate boot). The explicit timeouts are 260x `2_000`, 14x 200, 14x 100, 9x 500, 9x 5_000, 7x @async_assert_timeout, plus others, all hard-coded per call.
findings.recommendation: Convert post-synchronous-call sites to assert_received/refute_received. Put one shared `@receive_timeout` (from the case template or an env var for slow CI) on the rest, and ban bare assert_receive with a Credo check.

findings.title: Wall-clock quiescence windows and sleeps stand in for barriers; several can pass a regression under load
findings.description: (1) count_selected_reads/4 counts reads until the mailbox has been quiet for 500 ms. The 'costs exactly one selected read' / 'costs no selected read' tests (902, 917, 957) therefore miss any extra read that arrives after 500 ms, which is the regression they exist to catch. The burst test (924-938) depends on a real 2,000 ms debounce timer and 10 x 20 ms windows, so it is slow and sensitive to timing. (2) await_reconciliation_idle polls :sys.get_state with Process.sleep(10) x 200. (3) ad_hoc_source_test sleeps 100 ms and then asserts that nothing happened, which passes whenever processing is slower than 100 ms. (4) shared_resource_store_test sleeps 5 ms to age a body past `freshness_ms: 1` on the real clock. (5) ownership_test sleeps 150 ms before asserting fail-closed. (6) presenter_test asserts exact `held_for_seconds: 12, sample_age_seconds: 4`, computed from System.monotonic_time/DateTime.utc_now at test time, so it breaks if more than 1 s passes before the presenter runs.
findings.recommendation: Inject a clock (clock_ms/now funs already exist on GraphProjection) and timer scheduling (a send_after fun) so debounce and backoff advance deterministically. Count reads with a synchronous projection call as the barrier, not silence. For negative checks, deposit a positive sentinel after the negative case and wait for it. Give Presenter a `now` option.

findings.title: github_webhook_delivery_test await_deliveries/1 waits on the global Aiur.TaskSupervisor and gives up with :ok
findings.description: The helper polls Task.Supervisor.children(Aiur.TaskSupervisor), the app-wide supervisor that other subsystems also use, every 5 ms for up to 200 tries. When the tries run out it returns :ok, and it also returns :ok on any exit. An unrelated long-running task keeps it spinning for the full budget. A delivery that never finishes is reported as finished, and the assertions after it run against partial state.
findings.recommendation: Wait on the specific delivery: have the delivery path accept a completion callback or task supervisor option, or monitor the returned task pid. Flunk on timeout.

findings.title: Tests read and write private GenServer state, private message shapes, private function traces and private :persistent_term keys
findings.description: This unit has 89 :sys.get_state/replace_state calls in 13 files (760 in 87 files suite-wide). The worst are presenter_test (16), financial_data_test (16), graph_projection_recovery_test (15), ticket_detail_coordinator_test (13) and graph_projection_test (12). presenter_test replaces and suspends the state of the application singleton TicketActivity (`%{state | projection: ...}`). catalog_on_demand_test sets a local-call trace on the private GraphProjection.no_schedule?/3. recovery_test sends the internal `{:graph_projection_due, scope, token}` timer message. ticket_detail_test erases and restores the private :persistent_term key {Aiur.GitHub.Config, :resolved_token} but never restores the companion :resolved_token_source key that config.ex writes alongside it.
findings.recommendation: Add narrow test seams: an introspection function (e.g. GraphProjection.debug_state/1 returning a documented map), a public `fire_due/2`, and GitHub.Config.reset_token_cache/0 that clears both keys. Give Presenter and Orchestrator a way to take an injected snapshot instead of having tests replace Orchestrator state. Keep :sys state reads for last-resort cases, and wrap them in one helper per module.

findings.title: presenter_test starts Orchestrators that begin polling immediately against the default Linear fixture, and its on_exit cleanup does nothing
findings.description: Three tests call `Orchestrator.start_link(name: ...)` without `initial_poll?: false`. Lifecycle then calls schedule_tick(state, 0), so a real poll cycle starts at once. It runs against the TestSupport default tracker (kind linear, endpoint https://api.linear.app/graphql, api_key "token"), and presenter_test does not override :linear_client_module. That poll races the :sys.replace_state these tests apply next. Separately, all 12 on_exit blocks call `Process.exit(pid, :normal)`. Orchestrator traps exits (lifecycle.ex:83), so this only delivers a message and never stops the process. Cleanup actually happens through the start_link link.
findings.recommendation: Pass initial_poll?: false at every Orchestrator start in presenter tests, or make the TestSupport default tracker `memory`. Replace `Process.exit(pid, :normal)` with Aiur.TestSupport.safe_stop(pid), or start through start_supervised.

findings.title: streamdeck_projection_test points the global :workflow_file_path at a config file it never writes (the #589 shape)
findings.description: Three tests set `Application.put_env(:aiur, :workflow_file_path, workflow_path)` where workflow_path is `<tmp>/config.yaml`, and never create that file. They only need the path to locate the ModelAvailability ledger next to it. TestSupport documents that the global config resolving to a missing file makes any Config.settings!/0 read raise missing_workflow_file while WorkflowStore reloads or restarts, and that this crash-looped Aiur.Supervisor (#589). The module is not a TestSupport case, so nothing reloads or guards the store while the path is wrong.
findings.recommendation: Pass the ledger location to ModelAvailability.observe and StreamdeckProjection.provider_meters explicitly (a :ledger_path option). Otherwise, write a valid config first with write_workflow_file_atomic!/2 and use Workflow.set_workflow_file_path/1, which is pinned per process.

findings.title: Pure render/presenter tests take the heavy TestSupport setup and run synchronously; one 1,781-line module is async: false because of one describe block
findings.description: Seven modules totalling 2,889 lines `use Aiur.TestSupport` but contain no reference to config, WorkflowStore, Application env, PubSub, the filesystem or registered processes. They are pure render_component and presenter calls. Every case still writes a workflow file, force-reloads WorkflowStore, checks the supervisor tree and stops HttpServer, and the whole module is forced to run synchronously. github_graph_test is async: false for 66 tests because the 'public repository authority' describe block (3 tests) sets the global :workflow_file_path directly and reloads the shared WorkflowStore, bypassing TestSupport.
findings.recommendation: Switch the 7 modules to `use ExUnit.Case, async: true`. Move the 3 authority tests of github_graph_test into their own sync module (or a TestSupport case), and make the other 63 async.

findings.title: Oversized test modules, and a component test that relies on loose HTML substring checks
findings.description: github_graph_test has 66 tests mixing catalog, selected-root, dependency-endpoint, envelope and authority concerns. operator_control_center_components_test has 52 tests over 14 components (BuildOrderGraph, DecisionCard, DecisionInbox, History, FleetTable, ...), with 293 `html =~` substring assertions against 27 LazyHTML queries. Substring checks match class names and duplicates: line 50 asserts `class="bo-node is-merged"`, then line 52 asserts `html =~ "merged"`, which the class already satisfies. `"agent live"` is asserted twice (53 and 64). streamdeck_channel_test (57 tests) mixes socket auth, logs, Commands, control, say and voice. The in-file test doubles FakeDecisionStore, FakeVoiceSession and UnconfiguredVoiceSession are defined inside it.
findings.recommendation: Split per component or per concern: components into one file per component; github_graph_test into catalog / selected_root / dependency_endpoints / envelope / authority; streamdeck_channel_test into auth / commands / control / voice, with shared doubles in support. In component tests prefer LazyHTML selectors that assert element and attribute, not substrings.

findings.title: TestSupport's workflow fixture is a 215-line function around a hand-written YAML emitter, with copied helpers and duplicate or dead config
findings.description: workflow_content/1 merges about 55 defaults, pulls about 45 of them into locals one Keyword.get at a time, then emits YAML by string concatenation through about 15 section helpers and a custom yaml_value/1. Every schema key has to be mirrored here. Specific defects: (a) dead bindings silenced with `_ = {agent_turn_timeout_ms, agent_read_timeout_ms, agent_stall_timeout_ms}`; (b) alerts_line/3, pr_watch_line/3 and decisions_line/3 are identical; (c) @isolated_app_env_keys lists :github_cache_inspector_source twice; (d) setup puts :global_pause_store_path at 308 and then overwrites it with a different path at 334-338, so the first write is dead.
findings.recommendation: Build a nested map (defaults deep-merged with overrides), drop nil or absent optional sections, and encode it with the project's YAML writer, or a small generic map-to-YAML function. Collapse the three *_line helpers into optional_section(name, overrides, mapping). Remove the duplicate key and the dead put_env.

findings.title: Six hand-copied ensure/restart families for app children have diverged in retry semantics
findings.description: ensure_branch_ref_store_running, ensure_resource_store_running, ensure_workflow_store_running, ensure_pubsub_running, ensure_subscription_store_supervisor_running and ensure_read_cache_running each come with their own restart_X, restart_X_child (a try/catch around Supervisor.restart_child) and sometimes an X_status. The copies differ. ensure_pubsub_running/1 does not call ensure_aiur_supervisor_running first, but the others do. The workflow, branch-ref and resource-store restarts end with `{:error, _} -> whereis-check`, while pubsub, subscription-store and read-cache fall through to `_ -> X_status()`. Some retry by recursing into ensure_X_running(retries - 1), others into restart_X(retries - 1).
findings.recommendation: Replace them with one `ensure_app_child_running(registered_name, child_id, retries \\ 1)` and a table of {name, child_id}. ensure_runtime_children_running/0 then becomes Enum.reduce_while over the table and returns the first failure by name (see tests-6-01).

findings.title: Temp paths shared across VMs: the default fixture workspace root and 6 hand-built tmp roots in this unit (19 suite-wide)
findings.description: TestSupport.tmp_root!/1 explains that System.unique_integer is only unique within a node, and that two concurrent `mix test` VMs routinely pick the same name (measured at 60 shared names in 2 x 320 draws). Even so, the default workflow fixture sets workspace.root to the shared `/tmp/aiur_workspaces`, so any case that does not override it writes workspaces there across VMs and cases. This is the path the #2287 regression comment in workspace_and_config_test names. Six roots in this unit are still built as `System.tmp_dir!() <> unique_integer` without System.pid. remote_test compares a glob of the shared tmp dir (`aiur-ssh-script-*.sh`) before and after, which another VM staging a script can break.
findings.recommendation: Default the fixture workspace root to Path.join(workflow_root, "workspaces") inside the per-case root. Replace the 19 hand-built roots with tmp_root!/1. Have Remote stage scripts under an injectable dir so remote_test can use a private one.

findings.title: GitHub GraphQL payload builders (connection/pageInfo/graphql_response) are copied across 14 test files
findings.description: The GraphQL connection envelope (nodes/totalCount/pageInfo{hasNextPage,endCursor}), the issue-node shape and the rateLimit envelope are rebuilt by hand in each file. Two `defp connection` copies already differ in arity and options: github_graph_test takes opts with has_next?/cursor, and reconciliation_test hard-codes hasNextPage false. Five `graphql_response` variants take different arguments. Parsing GitHub payload shapes in more than one place is a known bug family in this codebase. Hand-built fixtures that drift from the real query shape have caused cost regressions before, as the #1766 comments in github_graph_test show.
findings.recommendation: Create Aiur.TestSupport.GitHubFixtures with connection/3, issue_node/2, graphql_ok/2 (with an optional rateLimit) and queued_request_fun/1, derived where possible from recorded real responses under test/fixtures. Use it for every GraphQL test.

findings.title: Core daemon and five CLIs depend on AiurWeb.OperatorControlCenter projection/policy modules (core -> web inversion)
findings.description: Several modules in this unit are not web code at all: they are the domain truth for Units rows, Units scope/condition policy, row presentation, the decision read facade, the build-order grid model and the analytics model. The daemon-owned current-run summary (Aiur.CurrentRunSummary.Facts) counts live/remaining units with the web module's UnitsPolicy, the current-run projection state builds its snapshot with AiurWeb...UnitsRow.snapshot/1, and every CLI (`aiur units`, `aiur commands`, `aiur analytics`, `aiur build-orders`, agent control) reaches into AiurWeb.OperatorControlCenter. `aiur units` even goes through PayloadLoader, which imports Phoenix.Component.assign/3 and resolves services via AiurWeb.Endpoint.config/1, so a CLI read depends on Phoenix endpoint configuration.
findings.recommendation: Move the non-rendering modules into a core projections package (e.g. Aiur.Projections.Units: UnitsRow, UnitsRow.*, UnitsPolicy, UnitsControlPolicy, UnitsPresentation; Aiur.Projections.Decisions: DecisionProvider, DecisionPresenter; Aiur.BuildOrder.GridModel; Aiur.Analytics.{Presenter, LatestRun, ScopeResolver}). Split PayloadLoader into a pure `load/1` (core, takes an explicit provider struct instead of Endpoint.config) and a socket-side scheduler (web). The web layer and CLIs then both depend on core, never the reverse.
findings.merge_reason: One core-to-web dependency inversion; SnapshotStore is an instance of the broader cross-layer dependency.

findings.title: Three diverged row classifiers (UnitsPolicy, UnitsControlPolicy, FleetFilters) plus a fourth reason list decide paused/queued/blocked/finished differently for the same row
findings.description: The same Units row facts are classified by independent predicate sets that have already drifted. UnitsPolicy (filter chips/counts, and via web-occ-01 the daemon summary) treats a row as paused when `Map.get(row, :tracker_paused?) == true` or a pause reason is present; UnitsControlPolicy (which control button renders) requires `running_ish?(row)` and only reads `runtime.tracker_paused?`. UnitsPolicy counts `lifecycle in [:queued, :retrying, :waiting]` or waiting_reason in @queue_reasons as queued; UnitsControlPolicy counts only `runtime_bucket == :queued or lifecycle in [:queued, :waiting]`. FleetFilters classifies `:waiting_for_dependency` as blocked while UnitsPolicy's @queue_reasons classifies it as queued, and FleetFilters decides finished by parsing tracker state strings (`["done", "closed", "cancelled", "canceled"]`) instead of the `terminal?` fact. Fields has its own @blocking_reasons list including :waiting_for_ci/:waiting_for_review that FleetFilters lacks. The comment in UnitsControlPolicy ("Mirror UnitsPolicy's flat-key fallback so both policies classify a row the same way") shows the intent; only the accessor was mirrored, not the predicates. UnitsPresenter.normalize_condition also hard-codes its own copy of the condition list.
findings.recommendation: Make one row-classification module the only truth (e.g. Aiur.Projections.Units.Classify) exposing `lifecycle_class/1 :: :active | :paused | :queued | :blocked | :stuck | :finished` plus the reason lists, and derive UnitsPolicy conditions, UnitsControlPolicy affordance gates, and (if kept) FleetFilters from it. Add a property test that enumerates row fixtures and asserts filter-chip class and control affordance agree. UnitsPresenter.normalize_condition should call UnitsPolicy.conditions/0.

findings.title: Ticket search indexes only the first 8 unique words of each title and description (index reuses the 8-term query cap)
findings.description: `words/1`, which builds the per-ticket index for title and body, calls `terms/1`, and `terms/1` truncates to `@max_terms` (8) because it was written to bound the operator's query. The index is therefore capped too: a title word after the eighth unique word, and every description word after the eighth unique word of the 1,000-character excerpt (OpenTicketSource @body_excerpt_chars), can never match. The moduledoc promises matching against "title words, and a bounded excerpt of its description" and the panel hint says "Matches ticket titles, descriptions, and IDs". Live correctness defect, scoped to the Tickets panel filter; the existing test only asserts the query cap (`length(TicketSearch.terms(...50 terms...)) == 8`) and no test searches for a late word.
findings.recommendation: Split the tokenizer from the cap: `tokenize/1` (NFC, downcase, split, uniq) used by `index/1`, and `terms/1 = tokenize |> Enum.take(@max_terms)` for queries only. Bound index cost by the excerpt length (already bounded) rather than by the query cap. Add a test that finds a word beyond position 8 in both title and body and fails with the current code.

findings.title: Host memory silently defaults to 32 GiB off Linux, and 'cores' is scheduler count; both render as measured facts
findings.description: host_mem_bytes/0 reads /proc/meminfo and returns @default_host_mem_bytes (32 GiB) on any failure, including every macOS host (the npm packaging ships darwin platforms: packaging/scripts/platforms.mjs). The memory chart then draws a 'host 32.0 GB' ceiling and the `mem_headroom_pct` KPI is computed against that invented denominator, with no marker that it is a default. `cores` is `System.schedulers_online()`, which is the BEAM +S setting, not the host core count, yet the CPU chart labels `cores * 100` as the "machine ceiling". This is the 'plausible default for an unknown' pattern AGENTS.md asks reviewers to reject.
findings.recommendation: Return `nil` host memory when unknown (or read it portably via :memsup / `sysctl hw.memsize` on darwin) and render 'host memory unknown' with no headroom KPI; use `:erlang.system_info(:logical_processors_available)` for cores. Keep the defaults out of the model.

findings.title: "stale" is rendered as "Healthy"/"Available" in 9 places across 6 modules whose own docs promise stale stays visibly distinct
findings.description: A product decision to stop telling the operator that data is out of date was implemented by editing each label table independently: `freshness_label(:stale)`, `health_label(:stale)`, `status_label(:stale)` and `window_freshness_label(:stale)` all return "Healthy", BuildOrderStatus returns "Available", and the stale messages became "Open tickets are shown below." / "Build Orders are listed below." The moduledocs still claim the opposite (e.g. RunSummaryPresenter: "keeps the distinct states (unknown, partial coverage, stale, unavailable, zero, exact) visibly separate"; ProviderMetersPresenter: "Each meter window keeps its ... standing, freshness, and reset distinct"), and Analytics.Presenter.cap_label still prints "stale, 5m old" for the same kind of reading, so two surfaces now disagree. Tests assert the collapsed label (usage_summary_presenter_test.exs:331 `assert degraded.freshness.label == "Healthy"`), so it is deliberate, but it is scattered and undocumented.
findings.recommendation: Decide the policy once and encode it in a single `AiurWeb.StateLabels` module (freshness/health/status -> label) used by every presenter; update the moduledocs to match. If stale is intentionally hidden, keep the age available (AGENTS.md: a surface that computes an age renders it) and make the Analytics cap label follow the same rule.

findings.title: Analytics.Charts and GithubCache.Charts copy the same SVG primitives verbatim; the chart skeleton is repeated in 11 functions and both stylesheets duplicate the palette
findings.description: `stacked_areas/4`, `poly/1`, `line/1`, `x_axis`, `y_grid/5`, `svg`, `text/4`, `fmt_elapsed/1` and `r2/1` exist in both chart modules with identical bodies (GithubCache.Charts' moduledoc even says it uses "the same" house style). Every chart function re-declares `h`, `{ml, mr, mt, mb}`, `pw = @w - ml - mr`, `ph = h - mt - mb`, `xf = fn t -> ml + (t - t0) / max(t1 - t0, 1) * pw end`, `yf = fn v -> mt + ph - v / vmax * ph end`. Analytics.Charts also has two different elapsed formatters (`elapsed/1` floors minutes, `fmt_elapsed/1` rounds seconds first). The two Styles modules hard-code overlapping categorical hex palettes (#3987e5, #d95926, #199e70, #c98500, #d55181 and the light-theme variants appear in both).
findings.recommendation: Extract AiurWeb.Charts.Svg (path builders, axes, text with mandatory escaping, time_svg/svg wrappers) and AiurWeb.Charts.Frame (a struct holding width/height/margins with xf/yf builders). Both chart modules keep only their chart-specific composition. Move the categorical palette into dashboard.css as shared tokens and have both scoped stylesheets reference them.

findings.title: Analytics.Charts interpolates model names, actor keys and ticket ids unescaped into SVG that is rendered with Phoenix.HTML.raw; the sibling chart module escapes
findings.description: text/4 embeds its body raw (`>#{body}</text>`), and callers pass data-derived strings: `"##{r.id}"` (ticket id from telemetry), `a.label` (actor label; any key not prefixed ticket: or _daemon/_operator is passed through verbatim), and `entry.label` / `model_label(entry.label)` in model_tokens_timeline (model ids from the usage snapshot, i.e. strings reported by providers or requested via ticket model labels) inside both `<title>` and `<text>`. The output is inserted with `Phoenix.HTML.raw` in UsageSummary, BuildOrderAnalytics and AnalyticsLive. A label containing `<` or `&` breaks the SVG; a hostile one injects markup into an authenticated dashboard that can answer Commands and pause agents. GithubCache.Charts already escapes its data labels (`escape(band.label)`), so the safer pattern exists in the unit.

findings.title: Current-run outcomes, run-summary and provider-meter announcements are computed on every update but never rendered
findings.description: DashboardLive subscribes to current-run outcome snapshots, debounces them on a 250 ms timer, reconciles and presents them, and assigns `current_run_outcomes` plus an announcement, but nothing renders `@current_run_outcomes` (the CurrentRunOutcomes component is dead, web-occ-13). Inside the presenter, `finished_this_run?` is computed and never read by any renderer, and `heading/3` ignores its arguments and always returns the neutral heading, while the moduledoc says the region "is labelled `Finished this run` only when ...". `run_summary_announcement` and `provider_meters_announcement` are likewise assigned and never rendered. findings.recommendation: Either render the region again (and make heading/3 honour finished_this_run?) or remove the subscription, flush timer, presenter and announcements. Do not carry the pipeline into the carved package unrendered.

findings.title: The Units table Remote Control link can never render: no producer emits remote_control_url and the projection strips it
findings.description: UnitsTable renders the remote-control anchor only when `row.live_conversation.remote_control_url` or `row.remote_control_url` is present, and UnitsPresentation.command/1 reports `remote_control: :available` on the same keys. grep over src/lib finds no code that sets `remote_control_url`: the daemon models the session as `remote_control: %{status: :on, session_url: url}` (agent_list/rc_pane_borders.ex:49, agent_runner/session_lifecycle.ex:70), Projection.row/5 never copies either key onto the row, and public_live_conversation/1 `Map.take`s only [:generation_handle, :state, :health, :freshness, :observed_at, :reason]. findings.title: Seventeen duration/age formatters and five timestamp renderers with three timezone conventions; TimeFormat exists but is used twice
findings.description: The same quantity renders differently by surface. 90 seconds is "1m 30s" (UnitsPresentation.age_label), "1 minute old" (ProviderMetersPresenter), "1m" (Analytics humanize_age, RunSummaryStrip duration), "1m ago" (BuildOrderStatus, DecisionCard, TicketContext); under a minute is "under 1m" (RunSummaryPresenter), "0m" (UnitsPresentation.format_duration, FleetTable), "just now" (TicketContext, DecisionCard) or "Observed 42s ago" (BuildOrderStatus.health_age, which never scales to minutes). UnitsPresentation.age_label's doc even says stale surfaces "must carry their age in one shape wherever they appear". Absolute times use viewer timezone (TimeFormat in History, ProviderMeters), ISO-8601 UTC (ConversationDrawer, CurrentRunOutcomes, DecisionDetail, TicketDetailModal), `%H:%M:%SZ` (BuildOrderGraph) or `%H:%M UTC` (BuildOrderCatalog). TicketContext computes relative time with `DateTime.utc_now()` at render, the exact 'ages on screen without re-render' problem History's comment (289-291) explains avoiding.
findings.recommendation: Create AiurWeb.Format.Time with `duration/1`, `age/2` (with explicit style: :compact | :ago | :sentence) and a single `<.timestamp value time_zone style>` component, and route every site through it. Pass `now` and `time_zone` from the LiveView instead of calling DateTime.utc_now in components.

findings.title: complexity:/build-lane: label parsing duplicated in UnitsRow.Fields with different validity rules than Aiur.BuildOrder.Metadata
findings.description: UnitsRow.Fields parses `complexity:N` as any positive integer (`Integer.parse`, `integer > 0`) and `build-lane:X` as any trimmed non-empty string, taking the first matching label. Aiur.BuildOrder.Metadata accepts complexity only as a single digit 1..5 and lanes only matching `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`, and reports ambiguity when two labels conflict. BuildOrderGridModel, Analytics.Presenter and AgentRoutingPreview each re-declare the 1..5 range. So a ticket labelled `complexity:12` shows `Cx:12` and a HIGH priority pill in the Units table (UnitsPresentation.priority: complexity >= 4 -> HIGH) while the build order treats it as invalid, and `build-lane: Foo Bar` shows a lane pill that Metadata rejects.
findings.recommendation: Have Fields call Aiur.BuildOrder.Metadata.parse/1 (or a smaller Aiur.Labels.complexity/1 / lane/1 it exposes) and expose `Metadata.complexity_range/0` for the other four sites.

findings.title: Source health/freshness normalization implemented three times with different mappings

Rename the StatusReport source key from `:status` to `:fleet` to remove the status/status collision. Replace catalog_status's clause chain with a table over (membership health, fleet degraded?, rows empty?).
