findings.title: DecisionCommands and RevisionCommands duplicate their socket-state and store plumbing; 'unavailable Command counts' exists three times
findings.description: answer_content/1, selected_decision/2, decision_identity/1, update_state/put_state, decision_store/0, the `ensure_*_key` idempotency helper and the conflict/store error copy are duplicated between the two command adapters (7 near-identical `safe_*` wrappers catching :exit). confirmation_required?/1 is duplicated between the server adapter and the DecisionRevisionAction component. The 'counts unavailable' map is defined in AwaitingCommands, PayloadLoader and DashboardLive, and has already diverged (PayloadLoader adds `scope`, `partial?`, `reason`); both AwaitingCommands and PayloadLoader implement counts via `{:ok, counts} = DecisionProvider.counts(...)` with rescue-on-MatchError.

Put `requires_confirmation?/1` and `unavailable_counts/0` on DecisionProvider (or core DecisionQuery) and reuse everywhere.

findings.title: Open agent-log modal re-reads and re-parses the whole agent log on every payload reload, and renders every message
findings.description: DashboardLive.reload_payload/2 calls AgentLogModal.refresh/2 on every payload reload (debounced to at most one per ~400 ms). refresh rebuilds from the running entry, which calls Aiur.AgentLog.read_workspace/1: `File.read` of the entire logs/agent.ndjson (or agent.md) followed by a full parse. These logs grow for the life of a session. The modal then renders every parsed message with no cap; the conversation drawer's log (via agent_log_composer) does the same. This is blocking file I/O and O(log size) work in the LiveView process at payload cadence.
findings.recommendation: Tail-read with a byte/line bound and remember the file offset per modal (incremental append), refresh only when the file mtime/size changed, and render a bounded window with a 'load earlier' control.

findings.title: Payload loads run inside the ControlCenterCache GenServer with :infinity, serializing every dashboard; the callers' exit fallback cannot fire on a slow load
findings.description: PayloadLoader passes `fn -> load_uncached(providers) end` to ControlCenterCache.fetch/fetch_event, which runs the loader inside handle_call with a `:infinity` caller timeout. load_uncached performs an orchestrator snapshot (15 s tolerance), DecisionQuery.counts, membership and activity reads, the open-ticket snapshot and one AgentRoutingPreview per ticket. While one load runs, every other LiveView's payload fetch waits behind it. The `catch :exit -> load_uncached(providers)` fallback in PayloadLoader only fires if the cache process is dead; a slow loader never triggers it, and a crashing loader takes the cache down and is then retried in every caller.
findings.recommendation: Keep single-flight but run the loader in a Task owned by the cache, reply to waiters when it completes, give callers a finite timeout with a stale-payload fallback, and rescue loader exceptions inside the task.

findings.title: durable_percent_entry/1 uses a single-clause guarded anonymous function; a durable window without used/limit crashes the Units page render
findings.description: `Enum.map(fn {_window, %{"used" => used, "limit" => limit}} when is_number(used) and is_number(limit) and limit > 0 -> ... end)` has no fallback clause, so any hourly/weekly/monthly entry lacking `used` or `limit`, or with limit 0, raises FunctionClauseError inside a `with` clause head (not rescued) during render. ModelAvailability.normalize_window/1 drops nil keys (`Map.reject(fn {_key, value} -> is_nil(value) end)`), so a provider window that reports only a reset time is persisted as `%{"reset_at" => ...}`. Census of the live .aiur/model-usage.json on 2026-09-26: 1 window (codex weekly), 1 of 1 has used/limit, 0 would raise, so this is latent.
findings.recommendation: Use `Enum.flat_map` with a catch-all clause returning [], and move the whole durable-observation read out of the component (web-occ-22). Add a test with a window `%{"reset_at" => ...}` that currently raises.

findings.title: LatestRun's ETS cache never evicts superseded entries and is owned by whichever process called first
findings.description: Each new or regenerated run summary changes the cache identity (it folds in every summary's size and mtime), and cache_put/2 inserts the new decoded dataset list without deleting the previous key. The moduledoc claims the design avoids "retaining one key per boot forever", but nothing ever deletes old keys; in a long-lived LiveView (Build Order pane refreshes every 30 s) each materialization adds a full copy of every decoded prior dataset. The table is a public named table created by the first caller; when that process exits, every other caller silently loses the cache.
findings.recommendation: Store a single entry (`:latest`) holding `{identity, value}` and replace it on miss, or `:ets.delete_all_objects` before insert. Own the table from a supervised process (or use a small GenServer/Cachex) instead of the first LiveView.

findings.title: A browser-supplied time zone reaches DateTime.shift_zone!/2 unvalidated
findings.description: The LiveSocket connect params carry `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`; DashboardLive accepts any non-empty string and TimeFormat.format/iso8601 call `DateTime.shift_zone!/2`, which raises for a zone the bundled Tz database does not know (a spoofed param, or a zone name newer than the database). The History table render then crashes and the LiveView reconnects with the same param, looping.
findings.recommendation: Validate at intake (`DateTime.shift_zone(DateTime.utc_now(), zone)` succeeds, else "Etc/UTC") and make TimeFormat use the non-bang shift with a UTC fallback.

findings.title: StreamdeckKeyFaceContract reads the TypeScript sidecar's JSON from packages/streamdeck at compile time
findings.description: The Elixir app embeds ../../../packages/streamdeck/src/key-face-contract.json via File.read! in a module attribute and raises at compile time if its shape changes. StreamdeckLive also builds CSS from it at compile time, and StreamdeckLogs derives @directions from it. Compiling src/ therefore requires the sibling TS package checkout at a fixed relative path. That blocks moving the Stream Deck sidecar to its own repository, and blocks building the Elixir app from a tree without packages/.
findings.recommendation: Make the Elixir side the owner of the contract (priv/streamdeck/key-face-contract.json, served over the channel or an HTTP endpoint), have the sidecar fetch or vendor it with a version check, and keep the compile-time validation against the priv copy.

findings.title: Control-failure reason taxonomy hand-maintained in the REST controller and the CLI, already diverged
findings.description: The REST API decides 409 (conflict) versus 503 (failure) from a hand-written list of 22 atoms plus 5 tuple clauses. The CLI keeps its own message table for the same Orchestrator.pause_agent/resume_agent reasons. They disagree. thrash_circuit_open, lifetime_dispatch_latch, dispatch_not_started, below_active_count, unknown_issue and agent_finished are named in the CLI but fall to the API's 503 'control_failed' catch-all, although they are conflicts, not outages. already_inactive, control_request_conflict, globally_paused and stale_generation appear only in the API list. Every new orchestrator decline reason is added by hand, one incident at a time, to at most one of them. The Stream Deck emulator shows inspect(reason) instead.
findings.recommendation: Create Aiur.Orchestrator.ControlReason with classify/1 -> :conflict | :invalid | :unavailable and message/1, owned next to pause_resume.ex. Use it from the API, CLI, StreamdeckLive/Channel and AgentLogModal.format_error. Add a test that enumerates every reason the orchestrator can return.

findings.title: Presenter's workspace path fallback drifted from Workspace.Layout, so /api/v1/:issue reports a wrong path for idle issues
findings.description: issue_payload_body falls back to Path.join(workspace.root, issue_identifier) whenever the running and retry rows lack :workspace_path. That is always true for idle-only issues, because idle rows carry no workspace_path. The real layout (AGENTS.md and Workspace.Layout.issue_workspace_path) is <root>/<repo-segment>/<issue-id>, with the identifier sanitized through Paths.sanitize. For a GitHub or Linear tracker the API therefore returns a directory that does not exist, and an unsanitized one.
findings.recommendation: Call Aiur.Workspace.Layout.issue_workspace_path(root, Layout.safe_identifier(id)), or better, have the orchestrator snapshot carry workspace_path for idle rows too, and delete the fallback.

findings.title: Protected usage-summary pipeline copied across DashboardLive, BuildOrder.UsageRuntime and AnalyticsLive (about 300 lines, already diverging)
findings.description: The following are copied in DashboardLive and UsageRuntime: authorized_context/1 (also in AnalyticsLive), usage_aggregate_generation/0 (also in AnalyticsLive), open_usage_drill/page_usage_drill/refresh_open_drill, usage_drill_dimension with the same @usage_drill_dimensions list, parse_cursor/1, the tier_facts stub returning %{}, apply/demote-to-locked, and the stash/flush debounce. findings.title: DashboardLive.render eagerly re-projects units and tickets on every render (every 1 s tick) through Map.put_new fallbacks
findings.description: render/1 starts with 40 Map.put_new calls whose default values are evaluated eagerly even when the key exists. Each render therefore runs UnitsPresenter.project over the whole units catalog (policy filter plus counts), TicketsPresenter.normalize and TicketsPresenter.search over the whole backlog (TicketSearch.filter when a query is set), CapacityPresenter.present, three nil presenters, fallback_decision_page and RouteRegistry.current_route. The :runtime_tick handler assigns :now every 1_000 ms, so this happens every second for every open tab. mount already assigns almost every key; only :retained_counts and :capacity_view depend on the fallback.

Consider rendering the ticking clock in a small child component or JS hook so the whole page does not diff every second.

findings.title: GithubCacheLive rebuilds its entire model, including a filesystem glob and read of every agent-cache.tsv, on every cache write, with no coalescing
findings.description: Each {:github_resource_changed, _} (any ResourceStore write: every poll response and every webhook) calls load/1. load/1 re-projects the ETS store and re-reads the quota meter, cache history, quota history and agent cache metrics. It also calls BudgetMap.snapshot, which globs <root>/*/.aiur-runtime/github-quota/agent-cache.tsv, File.reads every matching file whole, and reads the broker ledger. All of this runs synchronously in the LiveView process, once per open tab per write. The only protection is the ETS projection ceiling. DashboardLive coalesces the same kind of event through PayloadLoader, but this page does not. The page promises 'zero GitHub requests', but its local I/O is unbounded and grows with workspace count and log size.
findings.recommendation: On a change event, only mark the row highlighted and schedule a debounced (e.g. 1 s) projection refresh. Refresh budget map, agent cache metrics and history only on their own sampler ticks (they already have :quota_history_sampled/:cache_history_sampled). Cache BudgetMap's file-derived parts in the sampler, not per view.

findings.title: AnalyticsLive shells out to rtk (5 s timeout) and parses telemetry synchronously in handle_params, twice per page load
findings.description: load_model/1 runs in handle_params, so once for the dead render and again for the connected mount, and on every range change. It calls rtk_panel/0 -> Aiur.Rtk.savings, which runs System.cmd under Task.yield with a 5_000 ms timeout. claim.title: The analytics page's rtk panel runs up to three sequential shell-outs and an uncached config parse on each render
claim.description: Rtk.savings/1 calls status/1, which reads `Aiur.Config.settings_uncached()` (a workflow load and schema parse) and then runs `rtk --version` and `rtk hook check` before `rtk gain -f json`. Each is a Task with a 5 s bound, and they run sequentially, so a slow or wedged rtk can stall the LiveView for up to 15 s. The comment on run/4 says the bound exists because savings/1 "is read from a LiveView mount", but three bounded calls in a row compound the bound.

findings.title: Agent control seams (send, pause, resume, capabilities) duplicated across four surfaces with inconsistent injection

findings.title: StreamdeckChannel queues tickets by calling the CLI module (AgentControlCLI.todo) and decoding exit codes
findings.description: The comment explains why queue rules must not be duplicated. The chosen reuse point, though, is the CLI command itself: it prints to stdout inside the channel process, and the channel translates integer exit codes (0 -> :ok, 1 -> :queue_failed). A web socket handler now depends on the CLI package and on its textual and exit-code protocol, and cannot get a structured refusal reason (terminal ticket, already queued, ...). Those reasons collapse to :queue_failed.
findings.recommendation: Extract the queue rules from AgentControlCLI.todo into a domain function (e.g. Aiur.Queue.todo(identifier) :: :ok | {:error, reason}) that both the CLI (for printing) and the channel call.

findings.title: Stream Deck logs feed loaded two ways, and only the emulator papers over the event-before-write race with fixed 50 ms retries
findings.description: StreamdeckLive.agent_event_feed/1 is a copy of StreamdeckLogs.load/1: the same AgentEventFeed.list(identifier, %{"limit" => 50}) and bus_events call. On each transcript, alert or control event the emulator re-reads the durable feed, then schedules two more re-reads 50 ms apart (@durable_feed_retry_attempts 2), evidently because the PubSub event can arrive before IssueLog has flushed. That is 3 disk reads per event, and still stale if the write takes more than 100 ms. The physical deck channel reads once per event with no retry, so the two renderers of 'the same document' behave differently. There are also four handle_info clauses with identical bodies (lines 268-299).
findings.recommendation: Have IssueLog (or AgentEventFeed) publish a 'feed appended' event after the durable write, and subscribe to that instead of the raw transcript event. Use StreamdeckLogs.load/1 (seam-injected) from both surfaces and drop the fixed-delay retry.

findings.title: ElevenLabs realtime session lifecycle duplicated in StreamdeckChannel and VoiceChannel; the copies differ on errors and on stale audio
findings.description: Both channels start Realtime with owner: self(), push audio, commit or stop, relay :elevenlabs_transcript/:elevenlabs_error/:elevenlabs_closed, and clean up in terminate. StreamdeckChannel mints session ids, monitors the session, drains stale messages and drops frames for a stale session. VoiceChannel does none of that. It handles {:elevenlabs_error, reason} only when reason is binary (other reasons fall to the catch-all and are silently dropped). Its handle_in("audio") dereferences socket.assigns.stt.pid, and stt is set to nil by release_stt on :elevenlabs_closed. An audio frame already in flight when the provider closes therefore crashes the channel (undefined function nil.pid/0) instead of being dropped.
findings.recommendation: Extract AiurWeb.VoiceSession (start/push/commit/stop, session-id fencing, drain on stop, message normalization) and use it from both channels; guard audio on a live session.

findings.title: GitHub cache page tells the operator that REST calls can never be attributed, but Transport tags REST requests with a caller
findings.description: The 'usage-rest-caveat' block, always shown for the core budget, asserts that the caller tag is attached only inside Transport.maybe_put_caller/2, which is called solely from the GraphQL path, so every REST request bills as unattributed. Transport.fetch_json_list, fetch_json_list_conditional and the request at line 744 call put_caller/2 on REST GETs. The UI therefore states a false limitation as fact. AGENTS.md treats a wrong doc as worse than a missing one. The text also references issue numbers (#2298, #2297) that go stale silently.
findings.recommendation: Derive the caveat from data (show it only when the core ranking has just one 'unattributed' row), or delete it. Move long-form explanations to website/docs-app/apis/github.md and link to it.

findings.title: Static assets are served by two mechanisms; Plug.Static shadows 12 router routes and the compile-time embedded copies
findings.description: The Endpoint runs Plug.Static with `only:` equal to StaticAssets.revalidated_static_paths (dashboard.css, all hooks, aiur-dom-svg-layout*, ...), long_lived_static_paths (aiur-logo.png, bungee.woff2) and provider_asset_paths, before the router. All of those files exist in src/priv/static at the snapshot commit (git ls-tree). The router routes for /dashboard.css, the 5 hook JS files, /aiur-dom-svg-layout-adapter.js, the loader and :module, /aiur-logo.png, /bungee.woff2 and /provider-assets/* are therefore reached only when a file is missing, in which case they 404 anyway. The compile-time embedded @dashboard_css and @dom_svg_layout_adapter copies (File.read! at compile) are never what the browser receives. layout_asset_urls/0 has no production caller; grep finds only test/aiur/extensions_test.exs.
findings.recommendation: Pick one path: keep Plug.Static for files under priv/static and the controller only for vendor Phoenix JS and content-addressed layout assets. Delete the shadowed routes, the embedded copies and layout_asset_urls/0 (or wire it into the page if intended).

findings.title: Stream Deck download descriptor hard-codes a dev build pinned to one commit, and the 'unpublished' branch is effectively test-only
findings.description: @streamdeck_package pins version 0.0.0-dev.0098e3ac86a2, a fixed commit, and a release URL. streamdeck_package/0 falls back to it whenever :streamdeck_package is unset. No production code sets that key (grep: only the test sets it to %{}). Every daemon, whatever its version, therefore offers the same stale dev sidecar tarball. The comment's intended behavior ('a daemon without a release artifact ... only the download link is dropped') is unreachable.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the package descriptor from a release manifest produced by the packaging pipeline (or from the Stream Deck repo's latest release) and default to 'unpublished' (%{}).

findings.title: FinancialData.Cache: infinite-timeout call plus unbounded loader time lets one hung load pin a pending slot and block the LiveView
findings.description: Cache.fetch uses GenServer.call(..., :infinity). The load worker has no deadline, and a pending entry is resolved only by the worker's result, its DOWN, or a configuration change. A loader that blocks (for example UsageAggregate.cells_snapshot waiting on a busy GenServer) therefore leaves every waiter's LiveView blocked forever. Because cache keys include the per-connection generation, up to @max_entries 8 distinct hung keys make every further key answer :provider_unavailable immediately, until restart. Nothing polls or expires a stuck pending entry.
findings.recommendation: Start a per-load deadline timer (Process.send_after(self(), {:load_timeout, ref}, ms)) that kills the worker and replies {:error, :provider_unavailable}. Give fetch/7 a finite call timeout.

findings.title: AiurWeb.Presenter builds the same row fields in five payload builders
findings.description: running_entry_payload, retry_entry_payload, idle_entry_payload, running_issue_payload and retry_issue_payload each restate waiting_reason, open_decision_count, open_decision_count_health, ci: ci_payload(...), review: review_status(...), worker_host, workspace_path, tag/title/url and maybe_put_tracker_identity, each with its own defaults. findings.title: Unreachable `false ->` branches, a never-produced error payload, and a validate! that cannot fail
findings.description: `true <- is_function(h, n) || {:error, atom}` can yield only `true` or `{:error, atom}`, so the four `false ->` else-clauses are unreachable. A handler that returns neither {:ok, _} nor {:error, _} (for example :ok) raises WithClauseError instead, and nothing handles it. Errors.payload(:custom_event_quota_exceeded) has no producer (EmitEvent enforces only the progress cap). Claude.Config.validate!/0 checks byte_size(String.trim(command())) > 0, but command/0 already substitutes "aiur-claude" for blank values.
findings.recommendation: Replace the `||` idiom with a small `require_fun(h, arity, err)` helper, add an `other -> Errors.payload({:unexpected_handler_result, other})` clause, and delete the dead error clause and validate! check.

findings.title: Shell single-quote escaping is re-implemented instead of using Aiur.Shell.escape
findings.description: Four private copies of POSIX single-quote escaping exist next to the canonical Aiur.Shell.escape/1 (which Codex's AppServerPort uses). They are equivalent today (`'\''` vs `'"'"'`), but security-relevant quoting should have one implementation.

findings.title: Three `kill -0` liveness probes with different failure semantics
findings.description: RemoteControl.os_process_alive?/1 (string pid) looks kill up with find_executable and returns true when it is missing. Reaper.os_pid_alive?/1 runs "kill" directly. ProcessIdentity.alive?/1 (integer pid) also runs "kill" directly. RemoteControl.process_alive?/1 already delegates to ProcessIdentity.alive?. graceful_kill/1 runs "kill" without find_executable and swallows every exception into :ok.
findings.recommendation: Use ProcessIdentity.alive?/1 everywhere, accepting strings through one parse helper, and delete the private copies.

findings.title: HookSettings writes a new /tmp settings file per RC spawn and never deletes it

findings.title: ReplAgent uses `session.identifier` as a hidden 'hooks injected' flag
findings.description: drive_turn/3 routes to HookTurn when session.identifier is a binary, and otherwise to TranscriptTurn. The launcher sets identifier only when hook settings were written, so a field named for the ticket identifier doubles as the transport-mode flag. A future change that always sets identifier (it is useful for logging) would silently switch every non-RC REPL to hook-driven detection with no hooks installed. Every turn would then end in :turn_timeout.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit `turn_detection: :hooks | :transcript` session field and always carry the identifier.

findings.title: The DynamicTool error catalog is 60 function clauses, and each handler repeats the same execute/envelope skeleton
findings.description: Errors.payload/1 has 60 clauses (430 lines), most of the form %{"error" => %{"message" => "..."}}. Every handler repeats `with {:ok, args} <- normalize, true <- is_function(h) || {:error, x}, {:ok, r} <- h.(args) do Response.build(true, Jason.encode!(%{"ok" => true, ...}, pretty: true)) else {:error, reason} -> Response.failure(Errors.payload(reason))`. Blockers and Subscriptions each map action -> {handler key, error atom} with twin case blocks. Args.string/3 and Args.alert_string/3 are the same function, and emit_alert_value/2 supports only three hard-coded keys.
findings.recommendation: Make the catalog data-driven (a map from atom to message, plus builders for the few tuple shapes). Add a Handler helper `run(normalize_fun, handler_key, arity, ok_fields)`, and merge Args.string with Args.alert_string.

findings.title: Misleading names, inconsistent finish reasons, and small quadratic or atom-leak spots
findings.description: The quirk local_concurrency_limit and Concurrency.with_slot only count in-flight requests; they never limit, and the 2_500 in MeterWindows is display-only. The TurnStream watchdog ends with finish_reason "timeout", while Sse.finish_reason_for/1 documents that every close must be "stop" to avoid opencode re-open loops. ToolCallParser gives ids 'fallback-1..N' that repeat every round. BoundedGlob.keep/2 calls length/1 on every insert, which is O(n^2) up to 2_000 matches. WarmthReport calls String.to_atom on log text. SessionWriter.pop_any converts the whole MapSet to a list on every event once over the cap and evicts an arbitrary element, not the oldest. ProviderTurnLedger.complete persists guards twice (retire_identified and then persist_guards), and retired_turn_ids grow for the life of the session.
findings.recommendation: Rename the quirk to local_in_flight_gauge, or implement admission. Use Sse.finish_reason_for(:watchdog). Include the round number in fallback ids. Track a count in BoundedGlob. Use String.to_existing_atom or keep phases as strings. Use a bounded queue for seen_event_ids. Persist guards once per transition.

findings.title: Live-conversation retention re-encodes the whole snapshot to JSON per message and per eviction; partials re-sanitize all fragments
findings.description: LiveConversation.persist_snapshot calls Retention.retain on every changed snapshot; trim_messages computes snapshot_bytes (public_fun + Jason.encode_to_iodata!) for the current list and again after each single-message eviction, so an over-limit snapshot costs O(n) full encodes. Compactor.append_bounded_partial calls Normalizer.compact_fragments, which re-joins every fragment and re-runs the URL/environment redaction regexes over the whole body (up to 128 fragments, 256 KB input) for each new fragment; insert_message re-sorts and re-indexes the full message list per insert.
findings.recommendation: Track an incremental byte estimate per message and evict until under budget, then verify once; sanitize each fragment once on arrival and concatenate sanitized fragments (re-checking only the join boundary).

Compactor.append_bounded_partial calls Normalizer.compact_fragments, which re-joins every fragment and re-runs the URL/environment redaction regexes over the whole body (up to 128 fragments, 256 KB input) for each new fragment; insert_message re-sorts and re-indexes the full message list per insert.

findings.title: PaneManager.State keeps four redundant indexes updated by partial transforms; close path polls every slot synchronously
findings.description: identifier_to_pane, pane_to_identifier, pane_to_slot and slot_panes (plus placeholder_panes and title_by_identifier) must be kept consistent by hand; forget_identifier_for_pane drops identifier_to_pane and the title but leaves pane_to_identifier, while forget_pane_by_identifier drops all. Close.slot_for_pane calls Slot.snapshot (2s GenServer.call) on every registered slot from inside the PaneManager callback although SlotRegistry already exposes an ETS lookup used by OpencodeOpen, and close_opencode_or_generic hard-matches `:ok = Slot.deselect(slot_pid)`. Placeholder's async attach Task is started unmonitored; if it dies without sending :placeholder_swap/:placeholder_failed, the 'Loading opencode...' pane (tail -f /dev/null) stays until the next reconcile, and wait_for_slot busy-polls acquire_slot_or_grow (N Slot.snapshot calls) every 150ms for up to 60s.
findings.recommendation: Store one map slot => %{pane_id, identifier, kind: :real | :placeholder} and derive the other lookups; use SlotRegistry's ETS for pane->slot; monitor the placeholder task (Task.Supervisor.async_nolink) and fail the placeholder on DOWN; replace polling with the existing :slot_ready broadcast that OpenQueue already consumes.

findings.recommendation: Delete the swap mode and activate_new_pane (keep one keybinding target), collapse the QueueDrain wrappers, move MockTransport under test/support, and repoint the agent_runner_test marker test to TurnStreams.

findings.title: Bare assert_receive (100ms default) on cross-process messages in tmux tests
findings.description: The mock tmux transport sends {:tmux_mock_out, cmd} from the Tmux GenServer after a Task calls it, so the test process waits on a message produced by two hops of other processes. Many of these waits use the default 100ms timeout while sibling assertions in the same files pass 1_000, which is the flaky-under-load pattern. Grep counts of assert_receive lines without an explicit timeout: tmux_test.exs about 20 of 42, tmux/layout_test.exs 12 of 26, tmux/query_test.exs 10 of 20, tmux/input_test.exs 6 of 13.
findings.recommendation: Use an explicit module attribute timeout (e.g. @mock_timeout 1_000) for every cross-process assert_receive, or make MockTransport synchronous with the test via a call.

findings.title: Renderer typespec and comment debt: 54 of 70 all-term() specs in src/lib; stale width comments
findings.description: The renderer modules carry 54 specs of the form '@spec f(term(), ...) :: term()' (chrome 14, cells 12, model 9, markers 6, table 6, help 6, layout 1) - 54 of the 70 such specs in all of src/lib - which document nothing and hide type errors. Comments claim a 16-column progress cell ('<bar 10> <eta 5>') while @progress_cell_width = @progress_bar_width = 10. The row width is summed by hand in three places (Layout.compute base_overhead, Table.render_row plain_visual, table_header_row), and Layout/Text.cell size by String.length while padding uses visual_width, so wide glyphs in titles misalign. App carries @dialyzer no_return/nowarn suppressions for init/1 and render/1.
findings.recommendation: Replace term() specs with real types (iodata(), Layout.t()), have Layout.compute return the column list that both header and row rendering iterate, and remove the dialyzer suppressions after fixing the reported issue.

findings.title: TUI hardcodes GitHub URLs and model-family parsing; colors synced with website CSS by comment
findings.description: Links builds https://github.com/<project>/issues/<id> and /pull/<n> from Tracker.project_identity for any tracker (Linear projects get GitHub links), with two slightly different issue URL builders (ticket_url validates a positive integer, issue_url does not). findings.title: No-op detection is coupled to prompt wording by regex; local workspace probe has no timeout
findings.description: TurnProgress.prompt_digest/1 strips the turn counter and the no-op bullet from the rendered prompt using two regexes that must match TurnPrompt's wording exactly; TurnPrompt carries a comment warning that changing the wording breaks the no-op cap. The local branch of workspace_digest runs git through System.cmd with no timeout inside the runner (the remote branch has a 15s timeout), so a hung git (index lock, network filesystem) blocks the turn loop indefinitely. TurnPrompt also repeats the same '--test blocked' bullet verbatim three times (lines 29, 100, 123) and inlines the planning-to-work text that planning_to_work_transition_bullet/1 already produces.
findings.recommendation: Have TurnPrompt return {prompt_text, digest_material} where digest_material excludes counter and self-referential lines structurally; run the local probe through the same timeout wrapper as the remote one.

findings.title: Provider pid extraction parsed three ways in SessionLifecycle with different leniency and key fallbacks
findings.description: headless_os_pid/1 accepts binary pids only, uses Integer.parse with {n, _} (so "123abc" -> 123) and reads provider_pid || claude_app_server_pid; process_group_id/1 and maybe_put_provider_pid/2 require {value, ""} and accept integers; session_provider/2 reads provider_pid || codex_app_server_pid || claude_app_server_pid. The value from headless_os_pid is what the orchestrator uses to tree-reap on abort, so it is the most lenient parser guarding the most destructive use.
findings.recommendation: Have backends put a normalized provider_os_pid (positive integer) in session metadata and read it through one ProviderPid.parse/1 that is strict.

findings.title: Small helpers are duplicated across the unit: provenance, field/map_value, relative age, stage/phase labels

findings.description: The following Application.get_env and Endpoint.config keys exist only so tests can swap collaborators at runtime: :build_order_planning_membership_snapshot, :build_order_pack_status_health_snapshot, :build_order_display_clock, :bo_usage_flush_timer and :build_order_workspace_directory. :build_order_planning_pack(s) is a demo override. findings.title: Minor complexity in GraphProjection demand bookkeeping
findings.description: add_demand/3 returns {state, identity} and passes back an identity it never changes. remove_demand_by_monitor/3 takes an unused pid. selected_scope/2 returns the sentinel {:selected, nil}, which is then used as a MapSet key. active_scope_in?/2 duplicates active_scope?/2 (1313-1320) over a different map. drop_member_due/2 duplicates clear_member_due/2. Event lists are built with `events ++ next_events` inside reduces (request_changed_selected_roots, admit_pending), which is quadratic in watched roots.
findings.recommendation: Fold these into the scope state machine extraction (build-order-09): one active?/1 on the entry, one cancel_member_due/2, and prepend-then-reverse for event lists.

findings.title: Build Order tests trace private functions and assert an absence after Process.sleep
findings.description: graph_projection_catalog_on_demand_test.exs :erlang.trace's the private GraphProjection.no_schedule?/3 and reads :sys.get_state. That is also the starting state, so the test passes against a server that ignores all events and cannot fail without the production behaviour. findings.recommendation: Replace the trace with a behavioural assertion (no reader call within the window) or delete it along with the dead branch (build-order-29). For the absence test, deposit a labelled issue first, relabel it, and assert that it disappears. Use a synchronous barrier (call the server) instead of sleeping.

findings.title: TicketHistoryProvider retries the Exchange subscription every 100 ms forever, with no backoff or log
findings.description: When Events.Exchange is down or subscribe fails, subscribe_exchange/1 and monitor_exchange/1 schedule :resubscribe_exchange after a fixed 100 ms, with no cap, no backoff and no log. During an Exchange restart storm the provider wakes 10 times a second, and a permanently failing subscribe loops for the life of the daemon without anyone knowing.
findings.recommendation: Use an exponential backoff capped at a few seconds, log once per transition, and report history_health :unavailable while unsubscribed.

findings.title: TakeoverAlert.Store hand-rolls a non-fsynced atomic write, rewrites the whole file for every ticket on every tick, and only logs write failures
findings.description: The rest of the unit uses JsonStore.write! (tmp file, fsync, rename). This store writes a tmp file and renames without fsync, and on failure logs a warning and returns :ok. observe/4 always sets last_seen_at = now, so `record == previous` is never true and every monitored ticket triggers a full-file rewrite on every 5-minute tick. A lost write can re-fire a 'first' alert after restart, which is exactly what the moduledoc says the store prevents.
findings.recommendation: Use JsonStore.write!. Persist last_seen_at at most once per tick (batch all observations into one write per tick). Surface persistent write failure as an alert.

findings.title: DeliveryLog sorts the entire entry map on every claim once past the ceiling
findings.description: Once live entries exceed max_entries (200,000), every record/4 overflows by one and drop_oldest/2 runs Enum.sort_by over the whole map, O(n log n) on 200k entries per webhook claim, inside the GenServer call path. findings.title: Exchange.publish scans every binding and re-splits every pattern string on every publish
findings.description: publish/3 folds over the whole duplicate_bag and calls Topic.matches?/2 for each row, and matches? runs String.split on both pattern and topic every time. Cost is bindings times segments per publish, and bindings grow with 7 universal topics per ticket plus auto and manual subscriptions. findings.title: Targeted review-thread reconcile is silently dropped when the Orchestrator is not registered, after the delivery was already claimed
findings.description: nudge_orchestrator for kind :review_thread sends to Process.whereis(Aiur.Orchestrator). When nil (during a restart or boot window) it returns :ok with no log. The outcome still reports status :reconciled, and DeliveryLog has already claimed the delivery id and event key, so GitHub's retry would be dropped as a duplicate. Recovery depends on the next unresolved-thread poll. That covers 'unresolved', but for a 'resolved' transition the wake that should stop work is simply lost.
findings.recommendation: Return :unavailable and report status :error or :deferred so it is visible. Log at warning, or queue the hint for delivery when the orchestrator registers.

findings.title: AuthPreflight diagnostics: triplicated message assembly, string-matching an inspect/1 output, and stringly-typed dispatch on display labels

A local hold is detected partly by String.contains?(error, "{:aiur, :locally_held,") on an inspect/1 string. human_auth_reason/1 is a 13-clause case keyed on a mix of :reason and :classification that grows per incident. findings.title: Budget: per-actor ceilings are tuned by raising static defaults, and a test-only PubSub broadcast runs on every production request

findings.title: CiReadiness.cached_result does file IO and hashing on every dispatch cycle, and its :persistent_term scope map grows with each config edit
findings.description: Dispatcher.reconcile_completed_ci_readiness and reset_ci_readiness_for_config_change call cached_result and readiness_scope on the orchestrator path. Each call reads and SHA-256s the whole workflow config file (config_fingerprint) and, even when the memory entry is fresh, reads and JSON-decodes ci-readiness.json (newest_assessment evaluates both sides). Every config edit changes the fingerprint and therefore the scope key. Old scope entries are never removed from the :persistent_term map (delete_cached_scope only touches the current scope), so each edit leaves a stale entry, and each put triggers a global GC scan.
findings.recommendation: Cache the fingerprint keyed by file mtime and size, consult the persisted file only on a memory miss, and store a single current-scope entry (replace, not accumulate).

findings.title: AppTokenRefresher does network acquisition in init/1, and current_token/0 serves a token past its expiry
findings.description: When the boot-time resolve did not cache a token, init/1 calls AppToken.acquire. That is a JWT exchange plus a /rate_limit probe, each bounded only by the request timeout, and it blocks supervisor start. During a refresh-failure streak (backoff capped at 5 minutes), current_token/0 keeps returning the cached token even after expires_at. Every request then 401s, and AuthPreflight re-proves auth each cycle rather than the daemon reporting "no valid App token".
findings.recommendation: Return {:ok, state, {:continue, :acquire}} and acquire in handle_continue. Have current_token/0 return nil (or {:expired, token}) after expires_at so callers surface a precise needs-attention reason.

findings.title: ExecutorListener loses wake records for non-executor topics when inbox enqueue fails, with only Logger.error
findings.description: For non-`executor.` topics, deliver/2 enqueues a projected wake record into ExecutorWakeInbox. An enqueue error becomes a MatchError on `:ok = deliver(...)`, which is rescued and only logged. There is no watermark or replay for those topics, so the wake is lost for good. (For executor.* topics a later event advances the watermark, so the only effect is a failed watermark write.)
findings.recommendation: Retry enqueue with a bounded ladder, and raise one deduplicated alert when wake delivery fails, since Executor waits depend on these records.

findings.recommendation: Add a catch-all that logs at warning with the message shape and returns {:noreply, state}.

findings.title: Build and CI tooling ships in the production namespace, and Upgrade reads the version from Mix at runtime
findings.description: Aiur.TestShard (CI shard assignment, whose discover/1 defaults to Mix.Project.config()) is compiled into the release under lib/aiur, although only Mix.Tasks.Aiur.TestShard uses it. Upgrade.installed_version/0 calls Mix.Project.config() at runtime as a fallback, while cli.ex and app_server/messages.ex capture the version at compile time with `@version Mix.Project.config()[:version]`. findings.title: DispatchBudgetStore re-reads the whole JSON file on every per-issue lookup, and callers disagree on its errors
findings.description: lifetime/1 does JsonStore.read of dispatch-budgets.json (read plus decode of the full map) for each issue the Orchestrator evaluates, inside the Orchestrator process. The same read error is handled two ways: dispatcher.persisted_lifetime treats it as lifetime 0 (latch disabled, fail-open), while issue_sync.persisted_latch_status returns :unknown.

findings.title: OperatorWaitLog leaks ETS entries for undelivered messages and does file I/O in the Orchestrator
findings.description: record_queued inserts {identifier, request_id} into a public ETS table, and only record_delivered removes it. A message that is never provider-confirmed (agent died, message withdrawn) leaves its row forever. record_delivered runs File.mkdir_p! plus an appending File.write! in the calling process, which is the Orchestrator (operator_messages.ex:1031), once per delivered Executor message.
findings.recommendation: Expire pending rows older than a horizon (sweep on a timer in the owning GenServer), and send the append to that GenServer (cast) so the Orchestrator never blocks on disk.

findings.title: SSH.run has no timeout, ConnectTimeout or BatchMode
findings.description: run/3 and run_staged_script call System.cmd("ssh", ...) with no timeout, and ssh_target_args sets neither `-o ConnectTimeout` nor `-o BatchMode=yes`. An unreachable or hung worker host blocks the caller (the agent runner's remote workspace/hook path) for the kernel TCP timeout or longer.
findings.recommendation: Add `-o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=<n>` by default and run through a bounded runner, so remote failures surface as {:error, :timeout}.

findings.title: PathSafety.canonicalize collapses '..' before resolving symlinks, and contained? collapses all errors to :unreadable
findings.description: canonicalize/1 runs Path.expand/1 (a lexical `..` collapse) before walking symlinks. For an input like root/sub/link/../../x, the result is root/x, while the kernel would resolve link first and land elsewhere. The current callers (DecisionArtifact, Config.Paths, ToolResultSpill) use the returned canonical path rather than the original, so no escape was found. But the name promises realpath semantics that a future caller could rely on. contained?/2 also maps symlink_cycle, too_many_symlinks and every I/O error to :unreadable.
findings.recommendation: Resolve `..` segment by segment after following symlinks (true realpath), or document the lexical semantics in the function name. Pass the specific failure reason through contained?/2.

findings.title: Asks reads take an EXCLUSIVE SQLite lock with a 30s busy timeout and replay the whole log; file name does not match module
findings.description: Asks.open/1 -> all/1 wraps a read in Store.with_lock (BEGIN EXCLUSIVE, busy_timeout 30_000), so every `aiur status` and `aiur watch` can block up to 30s behind a writer and always decodes the full append-only log. The after-block issues COMMIT even when BEGIN failed. The file asks_store.ex defines Aiur.Asks.Store, which breaks the path-mirrors-module convention used elsewhere.
findings.recommendation: Serve reads without the exclusive lock (the append protocol already tolerates a torn tail) or from an in-memory projection; move the file to asks/store.ex.

findings.title: AgentQueueStore state transitions are copy-pasted and unguarded: two claim functions, four reset-to-pending blocks with drift, and paired single/bulk consume/fail
findings.description: claim_next_deliverable/2 is claim_next_deliverable_matching/3 with a constant-true matcher, and the 20-line claim body is duplicated. Field-clearing to reset an item to :pending is written four times (restore_pending, restore_failed_pending using Map.put chains, restore_delivered, maybe_retry_failed). Only maybe_retry_failed also resets delivery_attempts, so the copies disagree. mark_consumed/mark_failed accept items in any status. mark_consumed on a :pending item leaves its id in pending_ids_by_target (next_pending_item filters by status, so the index goes stale rather than wrong).
findings.recommendation: Implement claim_next_deliverable/2 as claim_next_deliverable_matching(store, t, fn _ -> true end). Add one reset_to_pending(item, reset_attempts?: bool) and one transition(store, id, to_status) with an allowed-from table that also maintains pending_ids_by_target.

findings.title: TestReset's agent-workspace guard hard-codes the "/aiur-workspaces/" directory name, the reset branches are duplicated, and PR close runs after the branches are deleted

The two dispatch_reset/2 clauses are identical except for Enum.take(tickets, 1). reset_one/2 calls delete_remote_branch before close_open_pr. close_open_pr re-lists remote branches, which are now gone, so it falls back to the legacy branch name only, and PRs from readable-suffix branches are closed only because GitHub closes a PR whose head is deleted.

findings.title: ProgressRetention keeps every ticket forever, copies the whole map into ETS on each retain, and latches degraded once the checkpoint passes 4 MB
findings.description: No entry is ever evicted, including for closed tickets. put_retained/4 does :ets.insert(table, {:all, retained}), copying the full map into ETS on every progress update. When the encoded checkpoint exceeds @max_checkpoint_bytes, encode_checkpoint returns {:error, :record_too_large} on every flush from then on: health stays {:degraded, {:flush_failed, ...}} and nothing further persists, a latch whose only exits are manual deletion or ticket eviction, and eviction does not exist. The cap is a 'raise the limit' shape: 4 MB is large enough to be far away today.
findings.recommendation: Store one ETS row per key and read with :ets.tab2list or match. Evict entries whose ticket is terminal (or cap by count, oldest observed_at first) so the checkpoint cannot grow without bound.

findings.title: RepoBase copies cache sidecars while holding a cross-host exclusive lock, with a 300 s busy timeout sized to 'outlast a slow copy'
findings.description: Migration holds an SQLite BEGIN EXCLUSIVE transaction, and inside it merge_sidecar/2 runs File.cp_r over the hex/mix/npm caches, which the comment says can be gigabytes. The busy_timeout was raised to 300 s to cover the copy, so a second host blocks for up to 5 minutes and then fails with repo_base_migration_lock_failed. This is the 'fix by raising a limit' bug family.
findings.recommendation: Do the copy outside the lock into a temp sibling, then take the lock only for the final renames. Or drop the cache merge: the caches are regenerable, so the destination copy could win and the legacy copy be deleted.

findings.title: Unused parameters, pass-through wrappers and redundant state in small modules
findings.description: EventPublicationLog.write/2,3 keeps a workspace argument that is 'never used to resolve the destination path'. Issue.label_names/1 returns the field unchanged (8 callers). findings.title: Inconsistent defensive handling under set -u (HOME/USER), a wrong exit-code capture in session_cleanup, and scripts that contradict their stated exit policy
findings.description: aiur_project_root guards `${HOME:-}` ('so an unset HOME under set -u can't abort'), yet aiur_resolve_identity (281), load_dotenv (612), run_session (872) and resolve_tmux_conf (1094) use bare $HOME, so the guard buys nothing. Session names fall back to `${USER:-user}`, but node names, the cookie owner check and the legacy reap use bare ${USER}. session_cleanup does `local code=$?` after `_cleanup_ran=1`, so it always captures 0. report-known-flaky-tests.sh says 'Exits 0 always', but `grep -v | sed` under pipefail exits 1 when the list contains only comments. verify-install.sh discards npm install errors (`>/dev/null 2>&1 || true`). `aiur stop <anything>` silently ignores its arguments.
findings.recommendation: Resolve HOME and USER once at the top of the engine, falling back to `id -un` and getent. Capture $? on the first line of the trap. Make the flaky reporter `|| true` its grep. Surface npm install output on failure. Reject stop arguments.

findings.title: Erlang cookie creation races between concurrent first launches of different instances
findings.description: The launch lock is per instance (keyed slug), but the cookie file is shared per user. Two first-ever launches from different projects can both see no cookie, each write a temp file and `mv` it into place. The first BEAM then runs with a cookie that has since been overwritten, and every later control RPC to it fails authentication.
findings.recommendation: Create the cookie with `ln "$tmp" "$cookie"` (atomic create-if-absent, a pattern already used at 1548) and re-read it afterwards.

findings.title: Unused playback adapter can hang on sink failure and conceal exit errors
findings.description: A write that returns false waits only for drain. A subsequent stdin error or process exit marks the sink dead but never settles the pending write, so playEncodedAudio cannot reach its finally/close. Separately close resolves even for nonzero exit. No production caller was found for these helpers in the frozen repository, so this is a latent library defect rather than an observed device outage.
findings.recommendation: Before wiring this code into a product, reject pending writes on terminal failure and report failed exits. Decide whether the unused playback/TTS code belongs in the package at all before investing in its API.

claim.evidence: Injected sink returns false, then emits error and exit(1). After the event loop drains, playback remains pending and close has not run; only a synthetic drain unblocks it. claim.recommendation: Before wiring this code into a product, reject pending writes on terminal failure and report failed exits. Decide whether the unused playback/TTS code belongs in the package at all before investing in its API.

findings.title: Unused fetch adapter does not cancel a body when streaming stops
findings.description: Breaking the fetch adapter async iterator releases its reader lock without cancelling the body. The TTS contract promises cancellation when the iterator is abandoned, and playback documentation claims that ceasing to await its Promise guarantees release; neither is an implemented cancellation protocol. These helpers have no production callers in the frozen source, so no live provider or cost impact is claimed.
findings.recommendation: Use explicit abort/cancel ownership, cancel the response body when iteration ends early, and document the difference between breaking iteration and abandoning an awaited Promise. Test cancellation while reading and while writing if these helpers are retained.

claim.evidence: Using an actual local ReadableStream and synthetic fetch, the probe breaks after one chunk: cancel is never called, the body is unlocked, and more bytes remain enqueueable/readable. claim.recommendation: Use explicit abort/cancel ownership, cancel the response body when iteration ends early, and document the difference between breaking iteration and abandoning an awaited Promise. Test cancellation while reading and while writing if these helpers are retained.
claim.refactor_hint: A stream return value is not by itself a resource ownership contract.

findings.title: Token payload parsing repeats lookups and recursively scans every update for rate limits
findings.description: extract_token_usage/1 and extract_rate_limits/1 list the same lookup twice (update[:usage] and Map.get(update, :usage) are identical; likewise for :rate_limits). findings.recommendation: Normalise payloads once per backend adapter into a typed usage/rate-limit struct; drop the recursive scan; rename turn_count to session_count.

findings.title: Remote command timeouts are always labelled hook 'remote_command'; the per-hook timeout match clauses are unreachable
findings.description: run_bounded returns {:error, {:workspace_hook_timeout, "remote_command", timeout_ms}} whatever the caller was running. Hooks.run_hook matches {:workspace_hook_timeout, ^hook_name, _} and Remove matches {:workspace_hook_timeout, "before_remove", _}; neither can ever match. findings.recommendation: Pass the operation name into run_remote_command/4 so the timeout carries it, and delete the dead clauses.

findings.title: Reconstruction staging and backup directories use VM-local unique integers and are never swept after a crash

findings.title: Dataset current-session reader ignores the requested boot id and reports tail-relative line numbers
findings.description: requested_boot_id is threaded through read_tail_chunks/consume_tail_lines, but the only use is `chosen_boot_id = if boot_id == requested_boot_id, do: requested_boot_id, else: boot_id`, which always equals boot_id; callers (latest_run.ex:34, presenter.ex:118) pass the current boot and always get whatever boot wrote the last line. Line numbers assigned via Enum.with_index(1) over the tail lines are relative to the tail, so warning locations are wrong, and a :file.read error mid-scan silently returns the partial state with no warning.
findings.recommendation: Either honor the requested boot (stop at the requested boot's first segment, skip newer boots) or drop the parameter; carry byte offsets to report real positions; add a read_error warning.

findings.title: Compaction's byte-based retention bound is inert in production
findings.description: Policy.retire_watermark uses raw_bytes to decide whether to retire down to the minimum window, but the Coordinator's raw_bytes_fun defaults to `fn -> 0 end` and aiur.ex starts `Aiur.UsageCompaction.Coordinator` with no options, so over_bytes? is never true and max_retained_bytes (8 MiB default) never binds; only the position cap works.
findings.recommendation: Default raw_bytes_fun to the ledger segment size (the ledger already stats it in capacity/4) or remove max_retained_bytes from the policy.

findings.title: ProviderMeters.Store crashes on a PubSub error and never evicts projections for rotated generations
findings.description: maybe_store/4 hard-matches `:ok = Events.broadcast(snapshot)`; Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast can return {:error, term}, which would crash the Store and drop every in-memory meter projection (there is no persistence). projections is keyed by {provider, backend, generation} and nothing removes entries for generations that were rotated or retired, so the map grows with every account generation for the daemon's lifetime.
findings.recommendation: Treat broadcast failure as non-fatal (log/count it); subscribe to account-generation change events and drop projections for invalidated generations (keep last-known for display with a bounded LRU).

findings.title: Decision delivery and timeout fixtures use a non-terminating cleanup signal
findings.description: start_orchestrator! spawns an unlinked recursive worker probe. Its on_exit callback calls Process.exit(worker_pid, :normal), which does not terminate this non-trapping target when sent by another process. The full-restart test uses the same ineffective signal before creating its replacement worker. The probe has no stop message or parent monitor, so intended cleanup leaves a live receive loop. OperatorSendTimeoutTest repeats this unlinked recursive worker and normal-exit teardown pattern.
findings.recommendation: Own worker probes under the test supervisor or implement a stop protocol and monitor their exit; verify teardown and restart fixtures observe DOWN before proceeding.

findings.title: on_exit sends kill -KILL to a recorded OS pid after the test has already confirmed that process is dead, so a reused pid could be killed
findings.description: The timeout test waits until the child pid is dead (kill -0). Its on_exit then runs `kill -KILL <pid>` unconditionally. If the OS has reused the pid in between, an unrelated process on the host is killed. wait_dead/2 can also report a reused pid as alive.
findings.recommendation: In on_exit, kill only when the test did not reach assert wait_dead (track it in a flag), or kill the process group that the production timeout path owns.

findings.title: Renderer sub-module tests restate constants and bundle unrelated assertions into one test
findings.description: Several of the 14 renderer/*_test.exs files hold a single test that asserts 8-13 unrelated facts, and some of those facts are constants. layout_test asserts `Layout.min_id_width() == 4` and `{progress_bar_width, runtime_cell_width, max_latest_width} == {10, 7, 60}`. style_test asserts that each Style function equals its IO.ANSI counterpart (`Style.reset() == IO.ANSI.reset()`), which only restates the implementation. findings.recommendation: Replace constant assertions with behavioral ones (for example, a row at width N truncates Latest at 60 visible chars). Split the multi-fact tests so each has a descriptive name. Delete style_test or fold it into a rendering test.

It computes offsets from `ResourceStore.unversioned_suppression_ms()`, so it moves with the constant. It also range-asserts that the bound is between 5 minutes and 2 hours. resource_store_test's own comment says these view_state_sweep assertions 'cannot fail when the value changes', and it re-tests the bound with literals. The ViewStateSweep file tests ResourceStore internals, including its own copy of age_mark!.
findings.recommendation: Delete the ResourceStore-bound tests from view_state_sweep_test and keep the pinned ones in resource_store_test. view_state_sweep_test should assert only that the sweep calls claim/3 and recovers what claim reports as :marked.

findings.title: Tests share the global Publisher replay window by hand-assigned id bands
findings.description: mutation_write_through_test picks comment ids 'in a band no other suite uses', because Aiur.Events.Publisher's replay window is ETS owned by a long-lived process and TestSupport does not empty it. A delivery reusing another file's comment id would be deduplicated silently. Correctness depends on authors coordinating id ranges by hand across files.
findings.recommendation: Add a `Publisher.reset_replay_window/0` (test-only) to TestSupport.reset_global_state!/0, or scope the replay window per Publisher instance so tests can start their own.

findings.title: Type-only assertions where the value is the point
findings.description: There are 19 `assert is_binary/is_integer/is_map/is_list(...)` sites in 10 files. Some are fine: they are paired with a value check, or the value really is opaque. Others are the pattern AGENTS.md warns about. The lifecycle_test named 'records a sanitized lifecycle boundary with a stable event key' only asserts `is_binary(attributes.event_key)`, so a random key per call would pass. interrupts_test checks `is_integer(pending_interrupt_request_id)` but never that the id in the frame equals the stored id. budget_test checks `is_integer(actor.core.reset_at_ms)` and not its value.
findings.recommendation: Assert the relationships instead. Recording the same boundary twice should give the same event_key. The frame id should equal next_state.pending_interrupt_request_id. reset_at_ms should equal the pinned reset.

findings.title: TestSupport's isolated app-env key list contains :github_cache_inspector_source twice
findings.description: @isolated_app_env_keys lists :github_cache_inspector_source at lines 91 and 93. It does no harm, since capture and restore are idempotent, but it suggests the list is edited by incident without review, which matters because this list is the suite's main isolation mechanism. The key used by several tests in this unit, :github_budget_enabled?, is not in the list. Each file (budget_test, transport_quota_test, transport_read_cache_test, auth_preflight_test) restores it by hand. So do :github_transport_test_options, :github_quota_server and :github_read_cache_ttls.
findings.recommendation: Deduplicate the list. Add the GitHub transport keys (:github_budget_enabled?, :github_transport_test_options, :github_quota_server, :github_read_cache_ttls, :github_request_deadline_ms) and delete the per-file restore code.

findings.title: `@tag :not_async` is used 7 times but nothing reads it; ExUnit async is module-level
findings.description: The tag suggests per-test serialisation, but ExUnit decides concurrency per module (`use ExUnit.Case, async: ...`) and no test_helper/CI config filters on `:not_async`. Both modules happen to be sync because `use ExUnit.Case` defaults to async: false, so the tag is dead and would give false confidence if someone flips the module to async.
findings.recommendation: Delete the tags and write `use ExUnit.Case, async: false` explicitly with a one-line reason (env mutation).

findings.title: ≈11 s of guaranteed idle wait per run from negative receives, mostly after synchronous calls
findings.description: 61 `refute_receive` without a timeout (100 ms each) plus 51 with explicit timeouts summing 5,080 ms: about 11.2 s of pure waiting in this unit, most of it in sync modules that run serially. In files like merged_ticket_reconciler_test (15 bare refutes) and comment_wake_test (15) the callbacks are invoked synchronously in the test process, so `refute_received` is equivalent and instant; where the sender is asynchronous, a 100 ms refute cannot prove absence anyway.
findings.recommendation: Use `refute_received` (optionally after the issue_sync_test `mailbox_barrier/0` pattern) for synchronous producers; for asynchronous ones, synchronise on a positive completion signal first and then `refute_received`.

findings.title: Assertions run inside a spawned production process in tts_test
findings.description: The injected `request` function runs inside the process `TTS.start/3` spawns, and it contains `assert {:cont, {_request, _response}} = into.(...)`. A failed assertion there raises in the TTS process, not the test, so the test fails later on a missing message (100 ms bare assert_receive) with an unrelated error, or passes if the crash path still sends the expected messages.
findings.recommendation: Send the `into` results to the test process and assert there, and wait with an explicit timeout or monitor.

findings.title: webhook_mode_contract_test locates consumer tests by a relative path walk tied to the current tree layout
findings.description: The meta-test enforces that every `consumer_*_test.exs` uses the dual-mode harness by globbing `Path.expand("../../../test/aiur/webhooks", __DIR__)`. Moving the webhooks tests into a package changes the directory; the 'at least one consumer test file' test would then fail loudly (good), but the path climbs out of test/ and back in, so it silently couples to `src/` being the mix project root.
findings.recommendation: Use `Path.join(__DIR__, "consumer_*_test.exs")` so the check travels with the directory.

findings.title: Failed workspace-reaping test leaves its inside sleeper running
findings.description: The real-process fixture starts two300-second sleepers but registers fallback process cleanup only for the outside PID. If production reaping or the following assertion fails, directory cleanup does not stop the inside sleeper. tmp_root! only constructs a unique path; this ExUnit case does not install shared process teardown.
findings.recommendation: Register cleanup for each owned process immediately after it is created, before later fixture setup can fail, and make readiness exhaustion fail explicitly. Verify failure-path cleanup with an owned-process barrier.

claim.title: Failed workspace-reaping test leaves its inside sleeper running
claim.description: The real-process fixture starts two300-second sleepers but registers fallback process cleanup only for the outside PID. If production reaping or the following assertion fails, directory cleanup does not stop the inside sleeper. tmp_root! only constructs a unique path; this ExUnit case does not install shared process teardown.
claim.evidence: tooling/remote_control_fixture_cleanup_probe.exs extracts the actual two on_exit callbacks and sleeper/readiness helpers from the frozen AST. With reaping deliberately omitted to model failure, both callbacks run: outside stops, inside remains non-zombie after its directory is removed. An explicit owned-PID kill stops the inside sleeper as positive control. Four results, exit0; all owned children stopped.
claim.recommendation: Register cleanup for each owned process immediately after it is created, before later fixture setup can fail, and make readiness exhaustion fail explicitly. Verify failure-path cleanup with an owned-process barrier.
claim.refactor_hint: Test process fixtures should own teardown independently of the production cleanup behavior they are testing.
claim.limits: Isolated fixture failure-path probe only, not a full ExUnit or production reaper run. No live workspace sweep. Maximum ordinary leftover lifetime is the300-second sleep; no production leak alleged. Readiness exhaustion observed in source but not separately executed. Cross-unit deduplication pending.

findings.title: Shim signal tests accept explicitly ignored interrupt and terminate signals
findings.description: Both signal-cleanup tests await natural completion of a one-second fake release and inspect the final lock. They ignore signal-command status and shim exit status. These assertions also pass when the shim explicitly ignores INT and TERM while retaining ordinary EXIT and success-path lock cleanup.
findings.recommendation: Define the intended interrupted-build behavior and assert an observable signal-path effect with confirmed delivery and owned-process cleanup. Do not infer interrupted completion from a lock absent after a normally finishing build; takeover ownership should be checked separately.

claim.title: Shim signal tests accept explicitly ignored interrupt and terminate signals
claim.description: Both signal-cleanup tests await natural completion of a one-second fake release and inspect the final lock. They ignore signal-command status and shim exit status. These assertions also pass when the shim explicitly ignores INT and TERM while retaining ordinary EXIT and success-path lock cleanup.
claim.evidence: tooling/shim_signal_oracle_probe.exs extracts the actual two tests and their fixture helpers into an isolated ExUnit module. A private original shim copy passes2/2; a private mutant changes all four combined cleanup traps to EXIT-only cleanup plus ignored INT/TERM and also passes2/2. Fake compiler/release/engine come from the source fixtures; original checkout never changes.
claim.recommendation: Define the intended interrupted-build behavior and assert an observable signal-path effect with confirmed delivery and owned-process cleanup. Do not infer interrupted completion from a lock absent after a normally finishing build; takeover ownership should be checked separately.
claim.refactor_hint: A final-state cleanup assertion cannot distinguish interrupt cleanup from ordinary success cleanup.
claim.limits: Two selected fixture tests only, not the full suite or real release build. No held-build control establishing an immediate-unlock or nonzero-exit contract: Bash can defer traps during foreground work, and the current trap does not itself exit. This finding establishes oracle insensitivity, not a production signal-handling bug or required abort semantics. Cross-unit deduplication pending.

findings.title: Engine test helpers isolate the node name but not HOME / AIUR_BG_STATE_DIR; git helpers inherit the user's global git config
findings.description: run_sourced_engine/2 pins AIUR_RELEASE_NODE when the caller omits it but leaves HOME and AIUR_BG_STATE_DIR to each caller; the engine defaults AIUR_BG_STATE_DIR to ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/aiur (cookie, instance records) and load_dotenv reads $HOME/.aiur/.env. Most callers pass AIUR_BG_STATE_DIR (21 occurrences), but the reap tests and instance_identity_test's identity/1 run with the real HOME, so isolation is by convention. Similarly the git!/1 helpers run `git commit` with the developer's ~/.gitconfig (commit signing, hooks, templates) in effect.
findings.recommendation: Make run_sourced_engine default HOME and AIUR_BG_STATE_DIR to a per-test tmp root (callers may override), and set GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 in a shared git helper.

findings.title: ToolExecutor.build/5 exposes 13 injection seams plus four positional arguments
findings.description: Tests configure ToolExecutor.build(issue, workspace, worker_host, session, opts) with up to seven closures at once; across the file the distinct option keys are coordination_enqueuer (21 uses), blocker_subscriber (10), dependency_declarer (9), event_publication_recorder (7), event_bus_publisher (7), dependency_present (6), coordination_runner (6), attention_opener (5), blocker_unsubscriber (4), dependency_unblocker (3), ticket_state_writer (2), attention_resolver (2), decision_lifecycle_recorder (1), plus decision_requester. The executor spans blocker coordination, event publication/recording, attention/decision projection and ticket state writes — several responsibilities behind one closure.
findings.recommendation: Group the seams into 3-4 behaviours (Coordination, Dependencies, EventSink, Decisions) passed as modules/structs, and split ToolExecutor per tool family so each test configures only its collaborator.

findings.title: The missing-credentials test in ticket_detail_test depends on ambient GITHUB_APP_* env
findings.description: 'maps missing production GitHub credentials to an auth failure' deletes GITHUB_TOKEN and erases the cached token. findings.title: receive_barrier/1 is an unbounded receive (156 uses); a missing message hangs until ExUnit's per-test timeout
findings.description: The macro deliberately has no `after` clause. When the expected message never arrives, the test hangs for the whole ExUnit timeout (60 s by default), and the failure names neither the pattern nor the mailbox contents. With 156 call sites, one regression can burn minutes of CI time per case with little diagnostic value.
findings.recommendation: Keep the no-wall-clock intent, but add a generous safety bound (e.g. 30 s, configurable) that flunks with the pattern and `Process.info(self(), :messages)`.

findings.title: Tests that depend on the host OS: GNU-only stat -c and real kill -0 on a recycled pid
findings.description: ownership_runner_test reads inodes with `stat -c %d:%i`, which only GNU coreutils supports, so it fails on macOS dev machines that the pgrep_skip_reason machinery otherwise accommodates. host_lock_test builds a 'dead pid' by running `sh -c 'echo $$'` and then probes it with the real `kill -0`. Its comment says 'Nothing else on the host can have taken it in between', but on a busy fleet host a recycled pid owned by the same user makes the probe say alive and the test fail.
findings.recommendation: Use File.stat!/1 (inode and major_device) instead of shelling out to stat. For the dead-pid case, inject alive_fun returning false and keep one :real_proc-tagged test for the real probe.

findings.title: max_turns_by_complexity_test writes the active workflow non-atomically and bypasses the WorkflowStore contract
findings.description: setup writes the config with plain File.write! and repoints Workflow at it. TestSupport documents that a truncate-then-write lets the WorkflowStore poll read an empty intermediate file and commit it as last-known-good (#1635), and provides write_workflow_file_atomic!/2 for this case. The test uses neither the atomic writer nor the TestSupport case.
findings.recommendation: Use Aiur.TestSupport.write_workflow_file_atomic!/2, or better, test Config against a parsed Schema struct without touching the global WorkflowStore.

findings.title: Unreachable branches and unused public functions in live modules
findings.description: DecisionAction: `acknowledgeable? = ... status == :open and ... not dismissible?` while `dismissible? = status in [:open, :deferred]`, so it is always false and the Acknowledge button never renders. AddAgentModal handles `{:ok, labels}`, `{:partial, ...}`, `{:error, :no_labels}` and non-binary `{:error, reason}` results, but DashboardLive only ever assigns `nil` or `{:error, message}` with a binary message. No caller in lib or test: TicketSearch.score/2, ConversationDrawer.Presenter.participation_notice/0, ProviderMeterSource.subscribe/1, UnitsURL.version/0, BuildOrderEpicIcon.planning_lanes/0; test-only: ProviderMeterSource.reload/3, RouteRegistry.route/2 and active?/2. RouteRegistry.routes/1 takes an `analytics` argument only to pass it to a no-op `resolve_runtime_availability/2`, and document?/1 can never be true (no route has type :document). UnitsPresenter.load/2's fallback clause calls `load(%{})`, discarding the caller's test seams.
findings.recommendation: Delete the dead branches and functions; fix the acknowledge condition if the button is still wanted; drop the unused `analytics` parameter from RouteRegistry.routes/1 and the :document route type.

findings.title: Directory/namespace mismatch, pure models under components/, inline JS hooks and CSS-in-Elixir
findings.description: Both src/lib/aiur_web/components/operator_control_center/ and src/lib/aiur_web/operator_control_center/ define modules in the same AiurWeb.OperatorControlCenter namespace, so a module's file location does not say whether it renders. BuildOrderGridModel (a pure projection used by build_orders_cli) lives under components/. Layouts.root embeds ~240 lines of JavaScript (AgentLogPanel, NavToggle, UsageWatch, ThemeToggle, CopyToClipboard hooks) in a HEEx string while seven other hooks are shipped as static files. Two stylesheets (466 lines) live in Elixir heredocs and are injected with `Phoenix.HTML.raw("<style>" <> Styles.css() <> "</style>")` by each component that needs them (twice on the Build Order page: analytics pane and usage summary).
findings.recommendation: During the carve: namespace components as AiurWeb.Components.OCC.* and presenters/models as AiurWeb.OCC.* (or move models to core per web-occ-01); move the inline hooks into static JS files like the others; move the scoped stylesheets into dashboard.css (or static css files) so they are cached and linted with the rest.

findings.title: Service injection via AiurWeb.Endpoint.config/1 in production code paths, with a second DI mechanism in Analytics
findings.description: 19 lookups in this unit (58 in src/lib) read `Endpoint.config(:decision_store) || DecisionStore`, `:orchestrator`, `:add_agent_fun`, `:units_membership_fun`, `:control_center_reload_timer` and similar at call time. These are test seams living in the endpoint's application env, so production code in presenters and command adapters depends on the Phoenix endpoint (and the CLI inherits it via PayloadLoader). Analytics uses a different mechanism (keyword opts `:orchestrator`, `:snapshot_timeout_ms` defaulting to a raw 15_000, while PayloadLoader wraps the same 15_000 in PollCadence.snapshot_tolerance_ms), and ScopeResolver uses `Application.get_env(:aiur, :build_order_data_source, ...)`. AddAgentSubmission's default even dispatches by function name: `&apply(Tracker, &3, [&1, &2])`.

findings.title: Very long render functions and presenter logic embedded in components
findings.description: ConversationDrawer.conversation_drawer/1 is one 214-line function (drawer, metadata, message list, agent log, voice composer). findings.title: TicketDetailModal renders the tracker URL as an href without the URL validation every other surface applies; operator-facing errors show inspect/1 of internal terms
findings.description: `<a :if={@ticket.url} ... href={@ticket.url}>` uses the raw tracker URL, while Units, Fleet, outcomes and build-order surfaces validate scheme/host first (a plain `<a href>` is not scheme-checked the way `<.link href>` is). AddAgentSubmission.message/1 and AgentLogModal.format_error/1 fall back to `inspect(error)`, putting tuples such as `{:tracker_exception, "..."}` or `{:exit, ...}` in operator copy.
findings.recommendation: Route the modal URL through the shared SafeUrl helper (web-occ-18) and map unknown errors to a generic sentence plus a logged detail.

findings.title: BuildOrderPresenter and BuildOrderViewModel sit at the aiur_web root beside an AiurWeb.BuildOrder.* namespace; six structs share one file
findings.description: The Build Order web code lives in two namespaces (AiurWeb.BuildOrderPresenter/BuildOrderViewModel versus AiurWeb.BuildOrder.ContextRuntime/SourceRuntime/...). build_order_view_model.ex defines 6 modules (Edge, Node, Capability, Group, Relationships, BuildOrderViewModel). build_node/4 filters all edges per node and selected_relationships filters all edges twice, so a render is O(nodes × edges). That is fine at current sizes, but it is the pattern to avoid if Build Orders grow.
findings.recommendation: Move to Aiur.BuildOrder.ViewModel.{Edge,Node,...} (one file per struct), and pre-index edges by target_key/source_key once in render/4.

findings.title: Unreachable or drifted handlers in DashboardLive and StreamdeckChannel
findings.description: (1) handle_info(:observability_updated) handles a bare atom that nothing sends; ObservabilityPubSub only broadcasts {:observability_updated, event_id}. (2) handle_event("toggle-fleet-filter") is a no-op for a button rendered only by Overview.fleet_overview, whose only caller is FleetTable.fleet_table, which has no callers. The component chain and the "fleet" entry in @table_sort_columns are dead. (3) DashboardLive.unavailable_retained_counts/0 is a drifted copy of PayloadLoader's version: it lacks scope and health.partial?/reason, and PayloadLoader always sets :retained_counts, so it is only a fallback. (4) The unauthorized clauses for implement/say/voice_start in StreamdeckChannel are unreachable, because join/3 refuses any socket without streamdeck_authenticated: true and that assign never changes.
findings.recommendation: Delete the bare-atom clauses, the fleet filter button chain (Overview.fleet_overview, FleetTable, FleetFilters if otherwise unused) and the no-op handler, the drifted unavailable_retained_counts, and the unreachable channel clauses.

findings.title: Small helpers copied across the unit, some already drifted
findings.description: relative_time/1 exists in StreamdeckLogs and StreamdeckStrip, and has drifted: the Logs version takes an injected now and truncates a non-ISO stamp to 6 characters, while the Strip version uses utc_now and returns the raw stamp, which can overflow the face. ISO-8601 parse helpers appear 4 times in this unit (two in StreamdeckProjection alone). Dual atom/string key getters appear 3 times (value/3, field/2, get_value/3). secure_equal?/2 is copied in Proof and StreamdeckAuth. transcript_flush_ms/0 is copied in StreamdeckLive and StreamdeckChannel with the same default of 250. The 'answerable' status list ["open", "deferred"] is repeated in StreamdeckLive (1132, 1173, 1187), StreamdeckChannel (550) and the TS client. The snapshot_timeout_ms expression PollCadence.snapshot_tolerance_ms(Endpoint.config(:snapshot_timeout_ms) || 15_000, ...) is repeated in 6 places, and the `Endpoint.config(:orchestrator) || Aiur.Orchestrator` seam in 8.
findings.recommendation: Collect into AiurWeb.Support.{Time, Maps, Crypto} and one AiurWeb.Runtime.snapshot_opts/0. Put the answerable-status predicate on Aiur.Decision (Decision.answerable?/1) and export it to the TS client through the channel payload.

findings.title: Stream Deck pushes read the orchestrator snapshot twice per event and may pair fleet and grid from different snapshots
findings.description: handle_info(:streamdeck_snapshot) builds snapshot() (fleet() reads the snapshot) and then grid() (a second read). running_changed and status_changed do the same with fleet() plus grid(). The two halves of one pushed message can therefore describe different orchestrator generations. status_changed fires on agent-list pane visibility changes, which are not fleet changes, so each pane open or close costs every connected deck two snapshot reads plus provider meter normalization.
findings.recommendation: Read the snapshot once per push and derive fleet and grid from it. Ignore status_changed messages whose status is pane visibility.

findings.title: Retry due_at is computed from wall-clock now instead of the snapshot's capture time
findings.description: due_at_iso8601/1 adds due_in_ms to DateTime.utc_now(). due_in_ms is relative to when the orchestrator built the snapshot, and dashboard_snapshot may return a :stale snapshot within the configured tolerance (polling-interval scaled). The reported due_at is therefore later than the real retry time by the snapshot's age.
findings.recommendation: Have the orchestrator publish an absolute due_at (or the snapshot's captured_at) and render that.

findings.description: The financial-data rest_for_one tree also starts VoiceSessionLimiter, so a financial-data Generation restart also resets all voice leases.
